q: The fundamental frequency of an open organ pipe is equal to the third harmonic of a closed organ pipe. If the length of the closed organ pipe is 20 cm, the length of the open organ pipe is
why: Open pipe fundamental = v/(2L); closed pipe third harmonic = 3v/(4×20). Equating, 2L = 80/3 cm, so L ≈ 13·3 cm, nearest 13·2 cm.

q: At what temperature will the rms speed of oxygen molecules become just sufficient for escaping from the Earth's atmosphere ? (Given : Mass of oxygen molecule (m) = 2·76 × 10⁻²⁶ kg, Boltzmann's constant k_B = 1·38 × 10⁻²³ J K⁻¹)
The efficiency of an ideal heat engine working between the freezing point and boiling point of water, is
A carbon resistor of (47 ± 4·7) kΩ is to be marked with rings of different colours for its identification. The colour code sequence will be
why: 47 kΩ = 47 × 10³: yellow (4), violet (7), orange (10³). Tolerance 4·7/47 = 10% corresponds to silver.

q: A set of 'n' equal resistors, of value 'R' each, are connected in series to a battery of emf 'E' and internal resistance 'R'. The current drawn is I. Now, the 'n' resistors are connected in parallel to the same battery. Then the current drawn from battery becomes 10 I. The value of 'n' is
why: Series: I = E/(nR+R) = E/((n+1)R). Parallel: 10I = E/(R/n+R) = nE/((n+1)R). So 10 = n.

q: Unpolarised light is incident from air on a plane surface of a material of refractive index 'μ'. At a particular angle of incidence 'i', it is found that the reflected and refracted rays are perpendicular to each other. Which of the following options is correct for this situation ?
opts: Reflected light is polarised with its electric vector perpendicular to the plane of incidence
Reflected light is polarised with its electric vector parallel to the plane of incidence
why: Perpendicular reflected and refracted rays means Brewster's angle, i = tan⁻¹μ. The reflected light is then plane polarised with its electric vector perpendicular to the plane of incidence.

q: In Young's double slit experiment the separation d between the slits is 2 mm, the wavelength λ of the light used is 5896 Å and distance D between the screen and slits is 100 cm. It is found that the angular width of the fringes is 0·20°. To increase the fringe angular width to 0·21° (with same λ and D) the separation between the slits needs to be changed to
why: Angular fringe width θ = λ/d, so θ ∝ 1/d. d' = 2 × 0·20/0·21 ≈ 1·9 mm.

q: An astronomical refracting telescope will have large angular magnification and high angular resolution, when it has an objective lens of
opts: large focal length and large diameter
large focal length and small diameter
small focal length and large diameter
small focal length and small diameter
why: Magnification = f₀/f_e is large for large f₀; resolving power ∝ D/λ is high for a large aperture diameter.

q: The ratio of kinetic energy to the total energy of an electron in a Bohr orbit of the hydrogen atom, is
why: In a Bohr orbit KE = −E (total energy), so KE : E = 1 : −1.

q: An electron of mass m with an initial velocity V = V₀ î (V₀ > 0) enters an electric field E = – E₀ î (E₀ = constant > 0) at t = 0. If λ₀ is its de-Broglie wavelength initially, then its de-Broglie wavelength at time t is
why: Force on the electron is +eE₀ î, so its speed grows: v = V₀ + eE₀t/m. λ = h/(mv) = λ₀ / (1 + eE₀t/(mV₀)).

q: For a radioactive material, half-life is 10 minutes. If initially there are 600 number of nuclei, the time taken (in minutes) for the disintegration of 450 nuclei is
why: 450 disintegrate so 150 remain = 600/4, i.e. two half-lives = 20 minutes.

q: When the light of frequency 2ν₀ (where ν₀ is threshold frequency), is incident on a metal plate, the maximum velocity of electrons emitted is v₁. When the frequency of the incident radiation is increased to 5ν₀, the maximum velocity of electrons emitted from the same plate is v₂. The ratio of v₁ to v₂ is
why: ½mv² = h(ν − ν₀): ½mv₁² = hν₀ and ½mv₂² = 4hν₀. So v₁²/v₂² = 1/4, v₁ : v₂ = 1 : 2.

q: In a p-n junction diode, change in temperature due to heating
opts: does not affect resistance of p-n junction
affects the overall V – I characteristics of p-n junction
why: Heating changes the number of thermally generated carriers, which changes both forward and reverse currents, so the whole V–I characteristic is affected.

q: An em wave is propagating in a medium with a velocity V = V î. The instantaneous oscillating electric field of this em wave is along +y axis. Then the direction of oscillating magnetic field of the em wave will be along
why: The wave travels along E × B. With E along +y and propagation along +x, we need ĵ × B̂ = î, and ĵ × k̂ = î, so B is along +z.

q: The refractive index of the material of a prism is √2 and the angle of the prism is 30°. One of the two refracting surfaces of the prism is made a mirror inwards, by silver coating. A beam of monochromatic light entering the prism from the other face will retrace its path (after reflection from the silvered surface) if its angle of incidence on the prism is
why: To retrace its path the ray must strike the silvered face normally, so r₂ = 0 and r₁ = A = 30°. Then sin i = μ sin r₁ = √2 × ½, so i = 45°.

q: An object is placed at a distance of 40 cm from a concave mirror of focal length 15 cm. If the object is displaced through a distance of 20 cm towards the mirror, the displacement of the image will be
why: Mirror formula with u = −40, f = −15 gives v = −24 cm. For u = −20, v = −60 cm. The image moves from 24 cm to 60 cm: 36 cm away from the mirror.

q: The magnetic potential energy stored in a certain inductor is 25 mJ, when the current in the inductor is 60 mA. This inductor is of inductance

An electron falls from rest through a vertical distance h in a uniform and vertically upward directed electric field E. The direction of electric field is now reversed, keeping its magnitude the same. A proton is allowed to fall from rest in it through the same vertical distance h. The time of fall of the electron, in comparison to the time of fall of the proton is
why: In both cases the electric force acts downward. The electron has a_e = g + eE/mₑ, hugely larger than a_p = g + eE/m_p. Since t = √(2h/a), the electron takes less time.

q: The electrostatic force between the metal plates of an isolated parallel plate capacitor C having a charge Q and area A, is
opts: proportional to the square root of the distance between the plates.
linearly proportional to the distance between the plates.
independent of the distance between the plates.
inversely proportional to the distance between the plates.
why: F = QE/2 = Q²/(2ε₀A). For fixed Q and A it does not depend on the plate separation.

q: A tuning fork is used to produce resonance in a glass tube. The length of the air column in this tube can be adjusted by a variable piston. At room temperature of 27°C two successive resonances are produced at 20 cm and 73 cm of column length. If the frequency of the tuning fork is 320 Hz, the velocity of sound in air at 27°C is
why: Successive resonances differ by λ/2: λ = 2 × (73 − 20) = 106 cm. v = fλ = 320 × 1·06 ≈ 339 m/s.

q: A pendulum is hung from the roof of a sufficiently high building and is moving freely to and fro like a simple harmonic oscillator. The acceleration of the bob of the pendulum is 20 m/s² at a distance of 5 m from the mean position. The time period of oscillation is
why: In SHM a = ω²x, so ω² = 20/5 = 4, ω = 2 rad/s and T = 2π/ω = π s.

q: A metallic rod of mass per unit length 0·5 kg m⁻¹ is lying horizontally on a smooth inclined plane which makes an angle of 30° with the horizontal. The rod is not allowed to slide down by flowing a current through it when a magnetic field of induction 0·25 T is acting on it in the vertical direction. The current flowing in the rod to keep it stationary is
why: Magnetic force BIL is horizontal; balance along the incline: BIL cos30° = mg sin30°. I = (m/L) g tan30°/B = 0·5 × 9·8 × 0·577/0·25 ≈ 11·3 A.

q: A thin diamagnetic rod is placed vertically between the poles of an electromagnet. When the current in the electromagnet is switched on, then the diamagnetic rod is pushed up, out of the horizontal magnetic field. Hence the rod gains gravitational potential energy. The work required to do this comes from
opts: the lattice structure of the material of the rod
the induced electric field due to the changing magnetic field
why: A static magnetic field does no work by itself; the energy supplied to the rod ultimately comes from the current source that establishes the field.

q: An inductor 20 mH, a capacitor 100 μF and a resistor 50 Ω are connected in series across a source of emf, V = 10 sin 314 t. The power loss in the circuit is
Current sensitivity of a moving coil galvanometer is 5 div/mA and its voltage sensitivity (angular deflection per unit voltage applied) is 20 div/V. The resistance of the galvanometer is
why: Voltage sensitivity = current sensitivity / G, so G = (5 div/mA) ÷ (20 div/V) = 0·25 V/mA = 250 Ω.

q: Three objects, A : (a solid sphere), B : (a thin circular disk) and C : (a circular ring), each have the same mass M and radius R. They all spin with the same angular speed ω about their own symmetry axes. The amounts of work (W) required to bring them to rest, would satisfy the relation
why: Work = rotational KE = ½Iω². I = (2/5)MR² (sphere), ½MR² (disk), MR² (ring), so W_C > W_B > W_A.

q: A moving block having mass m, collides with another stationary block having mass 4m. The lighter block comes to rest after collision. When the initial velocity of the lighter block is v, then the value of coefficient of restitution (e) will be
why: Momentum: mv = 4m V so V = v/4. e = (relative speed after)/(relative speed before) = (v/4 − 0)/v = 0·25.

q: Which one of the following statements is incorrect ?
opts: Frictional force opposes the relative motion.
Limiting value of static friction is directly proportional to normal reaction.
Rolling friction is smaller than sliding friction.
Coefficient of sliding friction has dimensions of length.
why: μ = f/N is a ratio of two forces, so it is dimensionless. The other statements are correct.

q: A toy car with charge q moves on a frictionless horizontal plane surface under the influence of a uniform electric field E. Due to the force qE, its velocity increases from 0 to 6 m/s in one second duration. At that instant the direction of the field is reversed. The car continues to move for two more seconds under the influence of this field. The average velocity and the average speed of the toy car between 0 to 3 seconds are respectively
why: a = 6 m/s². First 1 s: +3 m. Next 1 s decelerates to rest: +3 m. Last 1 s accelerates backwards: −3 m. Displacement 3 m in 3 s gives 1 m/s; distance 9 m gives 3 m/s.

q: The moment of the force, F = 4 î + 5 ĵ − 6 k̂ at (2, 0, − 3), about the point (2, − 2, − 2), is given by

A student measured the diameter of a small steel ball using a screw gauge of least count 0·001 cm. The main scale reading is 5 mm and zero of circular scale division coincides with 25 divisions above the reference level. If screw gauge has a zero error of – 0·004 cm, the correct diameter of the ball is
why: Reading = 0·5 cm + 25 × 0·001 cm = 0·525 cm. Correct value = reading − zero error = 0·525 − (−0·004) = 0·529 cm.

q: A solid sphere is rotating freely about its symmetry axis in free space. The radius of the sphere is increased keeping its mass same. Which of the following physical quantities would remain constant for the sphere ?
why: No external torque acts, so angular momentum is conserved. I increases, hence ω and the rotational KE (L²/2I) decrease.

q: If the mass of the Sun were ten times smaller and the universal gravitational constant were ten times larger in magnitude, which of the following is not correct ?
opts: Time period of a simple pendulum on the Earth would decrease.
Walking on the ground would become more difficult.
'g' on the Earth will not change.
why: g = GM_e/R² depends on G, which becomes ten times larger, so g on Earth would increase tenfold. The others follow from a larger g.

q: A solid sphere is in rolling motion. In rolling motion a body possesses translational kinetic energy (K_t) as well as rotational kinetic energy (K_r) simultaneously. The ratio K_t : (K_t + K_r) for the sphere is

A small sphere of radius 'r' falls from rest in a viscous liquid. As a result, heat is produced due to viscous force. The rate of production of heat when the sphere attains its terminal velocity, is proportional to
why: Rate of heat = F·v_t = 6πηr v_t². Terminal velocity v_t ∝ r², so the rate ∝ r × r⁴ = r⁵.

topic: Thermal radiation, Wien and Stefan laws
q: The power radiated by a black body is P and it radiates maximum energy at wavelength, λ₀. If the temperature of the black body is now changed so that it radiates maximum energy at wavelength (3/4)λ₀, the power radiated by it becomes nP. The value of n is
why: Wien's law: λ_m T = constant, so T' = (4/3)T. Stefan's law: P ∝ T⁴, so n = (4/3)⁴ = 256/81.

topic: Mechanical properties of solids, Young's modulus
q: Two wires are made of the same material and have the same volume. The first wire has cross-sectional area A and the second wire has cross-sectional area 3A. If the length of the first wire is increased by Δl on applying a force F, how much force is needed to stretch the second wire by the same amount ?
why: Same volume: the second wire has length l/3. F = YAΔl/l, so F₂/F₁ = (3A/(l/3))/(A/l) = 9. Force needed is 9F.

q: A sample of 0·1 g of water at 100°C and normal pressure (1·013 × 10⁵ Nm⁻²) requires 54 cal of heat energy to convert to steam at 100°C. If the volume of the steam produced is 167·1 cc, the change in internal energy of the sample, is
The correct order of N-compounds in its decreasing order of oxidation states is
why: Oxidation state of N: HNO₃ +5, NO +2, N₂ 0, NH₄Cl −3. So the decreasing order is HNO₃, NO, N₂, NH₄Cl.

q: Which one of the following elements is unable to form MF₆³⁻ ion?
why: Boron is in period 2 and has no vacant d-orbitals, so it cannot expand its covalency beyond 4. Al, Ga and In can form [MF₆]³⁻.

q: The correct order of atomic radii in group 13 elements is
why: Ga has a smaller radius than Al because of poor shielding by the 3d electrons (d-block contraction). Order: B < Ga < Al < In < Tl.

q: In the structure of ClF₃, the number of lone pairs of electrons on central atom 'Cl' is
why: Cl has 7 valence electrons; 3 are used in bonds with F, leaving 4 electrons, i.e. 2 lone pairs (T-shaped, sp³d).

q: Which of the following compounds can form a zwitterion?
why: A zwitterion needs both an acidic –COOH and a basic –NH₂ group in the same molecule. Glycine (an amino acid) has both and exists as ⁺H₃N–CH₂–COO⁻.

q: Nitration of aniline in strong acidic medium also gives m-nitroaniline because
opts: In absence of substituents nitro group always goes to m-position.
In electrophilic substitution reactions amino group is meta directive.
In spite of substituents nitro group always goes to only m-position.
In acidic (strong) medium aniline is present as anilinium ion.
why: In strong acid the –NH₂ group is protonated to –NH₃⁺ (anilinium ion), which is electron-withdrawing and meta directing, giving m-nitroaniline.

q: The difference between amylose and amylopectin is
opts: Amylose is made up of glucose and galactose
why: Amylose is an unbranched chain of α-D-glucose with 1→4 α-links. Amylopectin is branched, with 1→4 α-links in chains and 1→6 α-links at branch points.

q: A mixture of 2·3 g formic acid and 4·5 g oxalic acid is treated with conc. H₂SO₄. The evolved gaseous mixture is passed through KOH pellets. Weight (in g) of the remaining product at STP will be
why: HCOOH (0·05 mol) → CO + H₂O gives 0·05 mol CO. (COOH)₂ (4·5/90 = 0·05 mol) → CO + CO₂ + H₂O gives 0·05 mol CO and 0·05 mol CO₂. KOH absorbs CO₂, leaving 0·1 mol CO = 2·8 g.

q: Which of the following oxides is most acidic in nature?
why: Basic character of group 2 oxides increases down the group. BeO is amphoteric, the least basic (most acidic) of these; BaO, MgO and CaO are basic.

q: Which oxide of nitrogen is not a common pollutant introduced into the atmosphere both due to natural and human activity?
why: N₂O, NO and NO₂ are released by natural processes and by human activity. N₂O₅ is not a common atmospheric pollutant.

q: The compound A on treatment with Na gives B, and with PCl₅ gives C. B and C react together to give diethyl ether. A, B and C are in the order
why: A = C₂H₅OH; with Na gives B = C₂H₅ONa; with PCl₅ gives C = C₂H₅Cl. Williamson synthesis: C₂H₅ONa + C₂H₅Cl → C₂H₅OC₂H₅.

q: The compound C₇H₈ undergoes the following reactions: C₇H₈ → (3 Cl₂/Δ) A → (Br₂/Fe) B → (Zn/HCl) C. The product 'C' is
why: Toluene with 3 Cl₂/Δ gives benzotrichloride (C₆H₅CCl₃). The –CCl₃ group is meta directing, so Br₂/Fe gives m-bromobenzotrichloride. Zn/HCl reduces –CCl₃ to –CH₃, giving m-bromotoluene.

q: Hydrocarbon (A) reacts with bromine by substitution to form an alkyl bromide which by Wurtz reaction is converted to gaseous hydrocarbon containing less than four carbon atoms. (A) is
why: CH₄ → CH₃Br → (Wurtz) CH₃–CH₃ (2 carbons). Ethane would give C₂H₅Br → butane (4 carbons), and alkenes/alkynes would add bromine rather than substitute.

q: Which of the following molecules represents the order of hybridisation sp², sp², sp, sp from left to right atoms?
why: Carbons with a double bond are sp², with a triple bond are sp. In CH₂=CH–C≡CH the order is sp², sp², sp, sp.

q: Carboxylic acids have higher boiling points than aldehydes, ketones and even alcohols of comparable molecular mass. It is due to their
opts: more extensive association of carboxylic acid via van der Waals force of attraction
why: Carboxylic acids form strong intermolecular hydrogen bonds and exist as dimers, raising the boiling point.

q: Match the metal ions given in Column I with the spin magnetic moments of the ions given in Column II and assign the correct code: Column I: a. Co³⁺; b. Cr³⁺; c. Fe³⁺; d. Ni²⁺. Column II: i. √8 B.M.; ii. √35 B.M.; iii. √3 B.M.; iv. √24 B.M.; v. √15 B.M.
why: μ = √(n(n+2)). Co³⁺ (d⁶, 4 unpaired) = √24; Cr³⁺ (d³, 3) = √15; Fe³⁺ (d⁵, 5) = √35; Ni²⁺ (d⁸, 2) = √8. So a-iv, b-v, c-ii, d-i.

q: Which one of the following ions exhibits d-d transition and paramagnetism as well?
why: d-d transition and paramagnetism need a partly filled d subshell with unpaired electrons. MnO₄²⁻ has Mn(VI), d¹. The others (Mn(VII) and Cr(VI)) are d⁰.

q: Iron carbonyl, Fe(CO)₅ is
why: Fe(CO)₅ contains a single metal atom, so it is mononuclear.

q: The type of isomerism shown by the complex [CoCl₂(en)₂] is
why: [CoCl₂(en)₂] is of the type [M(AA)₂X₂] (octahedral) and shows cis and trans geometrical isomerism (the cis form is also optically active).

q: The geometry and magnetic behaviour of the complex [Ni(CO)₄] are
why: Ni(0) is 3d⁸4s². CO is a strong-field ligand, the electrons pair up to 3d¹⁰, and the complex is sp³ hybridised: tetrahedral and diamagnetic.

q: Following solutions were prepared by mixing different volumes of NaOH and HCl of different concentrations: a. 60 mL M/10 HCl + 40 mL M/10 NaOH; b. 55 mL M/10 HCl + 45 mL M/10 NaOH; c. 75 mL M/5 HCl + 25 mL M/5 NaOH; d. 100 mL M/10 HCl + 100 mL M/10 NaOH. pH of which one of them will be equal to 1?
why: For pH 1, [H⁺] must be 0·1 M. In c: 75×0·2 − 25×0·2 = 10 mmol H⁺ excess in 100 mL = 0·1 M, so pH = 1. (a gives 0·02 M, b gives 0·01 M, d is neutral.)

q: On which of the following properties does the coagulating power of an ion depend?
opts: Both magnitude and sign of the charge on the ion
The magnitude of the charge on the ion alone
The sign of the charge on the ion alone
why: By the Hardy-Schulze rule, coagulation is done by the ion carrying charge opposite to that of the sol, and its power increases with the magnitude of that charge. So both sign and magnitude matter.

q: Given van der Waals constant for NH₃, H₂, O₂ and CO₂ are respectively 4·17, 0·244, 1·36 and 3·59, which one of the following gases is most easily liquefied?
why: The constant 'a' measures intermolecular attraction. The largest 'a' (4·17 for NH₃) means the strongest attraction and the easiest liquefaction.

q: The solubility of BaSO₄ in water is 2·42 × 10⁻³ gL⁻¹ at 298 K. The value of its solubility product (K_sp) will be (Given molar mass of BaSO₄ = 233 g mol⁻¹)
In which case is the number of molecules of water maximum?
opts: 0·00224 L of water vapours at 1 atm and 273 K

q: The correct difference between first- and second-order reactions is that
opts: a first-order reaction can be catalyzed; a second-order reaction cannot be catalyzed
the half-life of a first-order reaction does not depend on [A]₀; the half-life of a second-order reaction does depend on [A]₀
the rate of a first-order reaction does not depend on reactant concentrations; the rate of a second-order reaction does depend on reactant concentrations
the rate of a first-order reaction does depend on reactant concentrations; the rate of a second-order reaction does not depend on reactant concentrations
why: For first order t½ = 0·693/k (independent of [A]₀); for second order t½ = 1/(k[A]₀), which depends on [A]₀.

q: Among CaH₂, BeH₂, BaH₂, the order of ionic character is
why: Ionic character increases as the metal's electropositivity increases down the group (Fajans' rule): BeH₂ < CaH₂ < BaH₂.

q: For the redox reaction MnO₄⁻ + C₂O₄²⁻ + H⁺ → Mn²⁺ + CO₂ + H₂O the correct coefficients of the reactants for the balanced equation are: MnO₄⁻, C₂O₄²⁻, H⁺
why: Mn changes by 5 e⁻ per MnO₄⁻, and each C₂O₄²⁻ gives 2 e⁻, so the ratio is 2 : 5. Balancing charge and H gives 16 H⁺: 2MnO₄⁻ + 5C₂O₄²⁻ + 16H⁺ → 2Mn²⁺ + 10CO₂ + 8H₂O.

q: Which one of the following conditions will favour maximum formation of the product in the reaction, A₂(g) + B₂(g) ⇌ X₂(g), Δ_rH = – X kJ?
why: The reaction is exothermic, so low temperature favours products. It reduces the moles of gas (2 → 1), so high pressure favours products (Le Chatelier).

q: When initial concentration of the reactant is doubled, the half-life period of a zero order reaction
why: For zero order, t½ = [A]₀/2k, which is directly proportional to [A]₀, so doubling [A]₀ doubles t½.

q: The bond dissociation energies of X₂, Y₂ and XY are in the ratio of 1 : 0·5 : 1. ΔH for the formation of XY is – 200 kJ mol⁻¹. The bond dissociation energy of X₂ will be
why: Let B.E.(X₂) = x. For ½X₂ + ½Y₂ → XY: ΔH = x/2 + 0·25x − x = −0·25x = −200, so x = 800 kJ mol⁻¹.

q: The correction factor 'a' to the ideal gas equation corresponds to
opts: electric field present between the gas molecules
forces of attraction between the gas molecules
why: In the van der Waals equation, 'a' corrects for the intermolecular forces of attraction; 'b' corrects for the volume of molecules.

q: Consider the following species: CN⁺, CN⁻, NO and CN. Which one of these will have the highest bond order?
why: By MO theory the bond orders are: CN⁺ (12 e⁻) 2; CN (13 e⁻) 2·5; NO (15 e⁻) 2·5; CN⁻ (14 e⁻) 3. CN⁻ is the highest.

q: Magnesium reacts with an element (X) to form an ionic compound. If the ground state electronic configuration of (X) is 1s² 2s² 2p³, the simplest formula for this compound is
why: X is nitrogen (forms X³⁻), Mg forms Mg²⁺. Balancing charges gives Mg₃X₂.

q: Iron exhibits bcc structure at room temperature. Above 900°C, it transforms to fcc structure. The ratio of density of iron at room temperature to that at 900°C (assuming molar mass and atomic radii of iron remains constant with temperature) is
why: bcc: Z = 2, a = 4r/√3. fcc: Z = 4, a = 2√2 r. Density ∝ Z/a³, so ratio = (2/4)·(a_fcc/a_bcc)³ = ½·(√6/2)³ = 3√6/8 = 3√3/(4√2).

q: Which one is a wrong statement?
opts: The electronic configuration of N atom is: 1s² (↑↓), 2s² (↑↓), 2pₓ¹ (↑), 2p_y¹ (↑), 2p_z¹ (↓)
An orbital is designated by three quantum numbers while an electron in an atom is designated by four quantum numbers.
Total orbital angular momentum of electron in 's' orbital is equal to zero.
The value of m for d_z² is zero.
why: In option (1) the three 2p electrons are shown with one spin reversed (↑, ↑, ↓), which violates Hund's rule; the correct configuration has all three parallel. The other statements are correct.

q: Oxygen is not produced during photosynthesis by
why: Green sulphur bacteria carry out anoxygenic photosynthesis using H₂S, not H₂O, so no O₂ is released. Cycas, Nostoc and Chara are oxygenic.

q: Double fertilization is
opts: Fusion of two male gametes with one egg
Fusion of one male gamete with two polar nuclei
Fusion of two male gametes of a pollen tube with two different eggs
why: One male gamete fuses with the egg (syngamy) and the other fuses with the two polar nuclei (triple fusion); together they make double fertilization.

q: Which one of the following plants shows a very close relationship with a species of moth, where none of the two can complete its life cycle without the other?
why: Yucca and the moth Pronuba show an obligate mutualism: the moth pollinates the flower and lays eggs in the ovary, where the larvae feed on seeds.

q: Pollen grains can be stored for several years in liquid nitrogen having a temperature of
why: Liquid nitrogen is at −196°C; pollen can be cryopreserved in it for years.

q: Which of the following elements is responsible for maintaining turgor in cells?
why: Potassium helps maintain turgor of cells (opening and closing of stomata, osmotic balance).

q: What is the role of NAD⁺ in cellular respiration?
opts: It is a nucleotide source for ATP synthesis.
It functions as an electron carrier.
It is the final electron acceptor for anaerobic respiration.
why: NAD⁺ accepts electrons and protons (becoming NADH) in glycolysis and the Krebs cycle, acting as an electron carrier.

q: In which of the following forms is iron absorbed by plants?
why: Plants absorb iron in the ferric (Fe³⁺) form.

q: Which of the following is commonly used as a vector for introducing a DNA fragment in human lymphocytes ?
why: Disarmed retroviruses integrate their genome into host animal cells and are used to deliver genes into human cells such as lymphocytes. λ phage and pBR322 are bacterial vectors; Ti plasmid is for plants.

q: Use of bioresources by multinational companies and organisations without authorisation from the concerned country and its people is called
why: Unauthorised use of bioresources and traditional knowledge of a country by companies is termed biopiracy.

q: In India, the organisation responsible for assessing the safety of introducing genetically modified organisms for public use is
opts: Council for Scientific and Industrial Research (CSIR)
why: GEAC, set up by the Indian Government, decides on the validity of GM research and the safety of introducing GM organisms for public services.

q: The correct order of steps in Polymerase Chain Reaction (PCR) is
why: Each PCR cycle: denaturation of double-stranded DNA, annealing of primers, then extension by Taq polymerase.

q: Select the correct match :
why: Ribozymes are catalytic RNA molecules, i.e. nucleic acid. F₂ × recessive parent is a test cross, Morgan worked on linkage, and transformation was shown by Griffith.

q: A 'new' variety of rice was patented by a foreign company, though such varieties have been present in India for a long time. This is related to
why: A US company obtained a patent on Basmati rice varieties that have long existed in India, a well-known case of biopiracy.

q: Which of the following pairs is wrongly matched ?
opts: Starch synthesis in pea : Multiple alleles
why: Starch synthesis in pea (gene B, seed shape) illustrates pleiotropy, not multiple alleles. The other pairs are correct.

q: Select the correct statement :
opts: Punnett square was developed by a British scientist.
Transduction was discovered by S. Altman.
why: Reginald C. Punnett, a British geneticist, developed the Punnett square. Spliceosomes act in splicing, linkage was coined by Morgan, and transduction was discovered by Zinder and Lederberg.

q: Which of the following flowers only once in its life-time ?
why: Bamboo species flower once in their lifetime (monocarpic) after many years and then die.

q: Offsets are produced by
why: Offsets are a means of vegetative propagation in aquatic plants like water hyacinth and arise by mitotic division.

q: Select the correct match :
opts: Matthew Meselson and F. Stahl – Pisum sativum
Alfred Hershey and Martha Chase – TMV
Francois Jacob and Jacques Monod – Lac operon
why: Jacob and Monod proposed the lac operon. Meselson–Stahl used E. coli, Hershey–Chase used bacteriophage, and Jeffreys developed DNA fingerprinting.

q: Which of the following has proved helpful in preserving pollen as fossils ?
why: Sporopollenin in the exine is extremely resistant to chemical and biological degradation, so pollen fossilises well.

q: Natality refers to
opts: Number of individuals leaving the habitat
Number of individuals entering a habitat
why: Natality is the birth rate: the number of births per unit population per unit time.

q: World Ozone Day is celebrated on
why: 16 September commemorates the Montreal Protocol (1987); 5 June is World Environment Day and 22 April is Earth Day.

q: Which of the following is a secondary pollutant ?
why: Ozone in the troposphere is formed by reactions of primary pollutants (NOx, hydrocarbons) in sunlight, so it is a secondary pollutant.

q: What type of ecological pyramid would be obtained with the following data ? Secondary consumer : 120 g; Primary consumer : 60 g; Primary producer : 10 g
why: Values are in grams (biomass) and increase from producer to top consumer, so the biomass pyramid is inverted.

q: In stratosphere, which of the following elements acts as a catalyst in degradation of ozone and release of molecular oxygen ?
why: Chlorine atoms released from CFCs by UV act as catalyst in breaking down ozone to O₂.

q: The two functional groups characteristic of sugars are
why: Sugars are polyhydroxy aldehydes or ketones, having carbonyl and hydroxyl groups.

q: Which among the following is not a prokaryote ?
why: Saccharomyces is a yeast (fungus, eukaryote); Nostoc and Oscillatoria are cyanobacteria and Mycobacterium is a bacterium.

q: The Golgi complex participates in
why: The Golgi apparatus packages materials and forms secretory vesicles.

q: Which of the following is not a product of light reaction of photosynthesis ?
why: Light reactions give ATP, NADPH and O₂; NADH is not produced.

q: Which of the following is true for nucleolus ?
opts: It takes part in spindle formation.
Larger nucleoli are present in dividing cells.
It is a site for active ribosomal RNA synthesis.
why: The nucleolus is a non-membranous site of rRNA synthesis; it disappears during division and larger nucleoli occur in cells making much protein.

q: Stomatal movement is not affected by
why: Stomata respond to light, temperature, CO₂ concentration and water status, but not to O₂ concentration.

q: The stage during which separation of the paired homologous chromosomes begins is
why: At diplotene the synaptonemal complex dissolves and homologous chromosomes begin to separate, remaining attached at chiasmata.

q: Stomata in grass leaf are
why: Grasses (monocots) have dumb-bell shaped guard cells; dicots have kidney shaped ones.

q: Secondary xylem and phloem in dicot stem are produced by
why: Vascular cambium cuts off secondary xylem inwards and secondary phloem outwards.

q: Pneumatophores occur in
why: Mangrove halophytes such as Rhizophora and Avicennia have pneumatophores for gas exchange in swampy soil.

q: Casparian strips occur in
why: Casparian strips of suberin are deposited on radial and tangential walls of endodermal cells.

q: Plants having little or no secondary growth are
why: Grasses are monocots, which generally lack a vascular cambium and show little or no secondary growth; conifers and dicot trees show extensive secondary growth.

q: Sweet potato is a modified
why: Sweet potato is a root tuber arising from adventitious roots; it has no nodes, unlike potato.

q: Which of the following statements is correct ?
opts: Selaginella is heterosporous, while Salvinia is homosporous.
Ovules are not enclosed by ovary wall in gymnosperms.
Stems are usually unbranched in both Cycas and Cedrus.
why: Gymnosperms have naked ovules. Horsetails are pteridophytes, both Selaginella and Salvinia are heterosporous, and Cedrus stems are branched.

q: Select the wrong statement :
opts: Pseudopodia are locomotory and feeding structures in Sporozoans.
Cell wall is present in members of Fungi and Plantae.
Mitochondria are the powerhouse of the cell in all kingdoms except Monera.
why: Sporozoans have no locomotory structures; pseudopodia belong to amoeboid protozoans. The other statements are correct.

q: After karyogamy followed by meiosis, spores are produced exogenously in
why: Agaricus is a basidiomycete in which meiosis in the basidium gives basidiospores borne exogenously; ascomycetes form spores endogenously in asci.

q: Match the items given in Column I with those in Column II and select the correct option given below : Column I: a. Herbarium; b. Key; c. Museum; d. Catalogue.  Column II: i. It is a place having a collection of preserved plants and animals; ii. A list that enumerates methodically all the species found in an area with brief description aiding identification; iii. Is a place where dried and pressed plant specimens mounted on sheets are kept; iv. A booklet containing a list of characters and their alternates which are helpful in identification of various taxa.
why: Herbarium holds dried pressed plants (iii), key lists contrasting characters (iv), museum holds preserved plants and animals (i), catalogue enumerates species of an area (ii).

q: Winged pollen grains are present in
why: Pinus pollen grains have two air bladders (wings) for wind dispersal.

q: Which one is wrongly matched ?
why: Polysiphonia is a red alga whose gametes are non-motile (no flagella). The other pairs are correct.

q: Which of the following options correctly represents the lung conditions in asthma and emphysema, respectively ?
opts: Increased respiratory surface; Inflammation of bronchioles
Increased number of bronchioles; Increased respiratory surface
Inflammation of bronchioles; Decreased respiratory surface
Decreased respiratory surface; Inflammation of bronchioles
why: Asthma involves inflammation of bronchi and bronchioles; emphysema damages alveolar walls and decreases respiratory surface.

q: Match the items given in Column I with those in Column II and select the correct option given below : Column I: a. Tricuspid valve; b. Bicuspid valve; c. Semilunar valve.  Column II: i. Between left atrium and left ventricle; ii. Between right ventricle and pulmonary artery; iii. Between right atrium and right ventricle.
why: Tricuspid guards right atrioventricular opening (iii), bicuspid the left (i), semilunar valves guard the pulmonary artery and aorta (ii).

q: Match the items given in Column I with those in Column II and select the correct option given below : Column I: a. Tidal volume; b. Inspiratory Reserve volume; c. Expiratory Reserve volume; d. Residual volume.  Column II: i. 2500 – 3000 mL; ii. 1100 – 1200 mL; iii. 500 – 550 mL; iv. 1000 – 1100 mL
why: TV is about 500 mL, IRV 2500–3000 mL, ERV 1000–1100 mL and RV 1100–1200 mL.

q: The transparent lens in the human eye is held in its place by
opts: smooth muscles attached to the iris
ligaments attached to the ciliary body
smooth muscles attached to the ciliary body
why: Suspensory ligaments connect the lens to the ciliary body and hold it in place.

q: Which of the following is an amino acid derived hormone ?
why: Epinephrine is derived from tyrosine; estradiol, estriol and ecdysone are steroids.

q: Which of the following hormones can play a significant role in osteoporosis ?
why: Estrogen deficiency after menopause and parathyroid hormone (which mobilises bone calcium) both affect bone mass and osteoporosis.

q: Which of the following structures or regions is incorrectly paired with its function ?
opts: Hypothalamus : production of releasing hormones and regulation of temperature, hunger and thirst.
Limbic system : consists of fibre tracts that interconnect different regions of brain; controls movement.
Medulla oblongata : controls respiration and cardiovascular reflexes.
Corpus callosum : band of fibers connecting left and right cerebral hemispheres.
why: The limbic system controls emotions, memory and motivation, not movement.

q: The amnion of mammalian embryo is derived from
why: The amnion is an extra-embryonic membrane formed from ectoderm and mesoderm.

q: Hormones secreted by the placenta to maintain pregnancy are
why: The placenta secretes hCG, hPL, estrogens and progestogens; relaxin comes from the ovary and oxytocin and prolactin from the pituitary.

q: The difference between spermiogenesis and spermiation is
opts: In spermiogenesis spermatozoa from sertoli cells are released into the cavity of seminiferous tubules, while in spermiation spermatozoa are formed.
In spermiogenesis spermatozoa are formed, while in spermiation spermatids are formed.
In spermiogenesis spermatids are formed, while in spermiation spermatozoa are formed.
In spermiogenesis spermatozoa are formed, while in spermiation spermatozoa are released from sertoli cells into the cavity of seminiferous tubules.
why: Spermiogenesis is the transformation of spermatids into spermatozoa; spermiation is their release from Sertoli cells into the tubule lumen.

q: The contraceptive ‘SAHELI’
opts: increases the concentration of estrogen and prevents ovulation in females.
blocks estrogen receptors in the uterus, preventing eggs from getting implanted.
why: Saheli (centchroman) is a non-steroidal once-a-week pill that acts as an estrogen receptor blocker in the uterus, preventing implantation.

q: Ciliates differ from all other protozoans in
opts: having a contractile vacuole for removing excess water
why: Ciliates such as Paramecium have a macronucleus and a micronucleus.

q: Identify the vertebrate group of animals characterized by crop and gizzard in its digestive system.
why: Birds have a crop for storing food and a gizzard for grinding it.

q: Which of the following features is used to identify a male cockroach from a female cockroach ?
opts: Presence of a boat shaped sternum on the 9th abdominal segment
why: Males have a pair of anal (caudal) styles on the 9th segment which females lack; both sexes have anal cerci.

q: Which one of these animals is not a homeotherm ?
why: Chelone is a turtle (reptile), a poikilotherm. Camelus and Macropus are mammals and Psittacula is a bird.

q: Which of the following animals does not undergo metamorphosis ?
why: Earthworm shows direct development. Moth, tunicate (tadpole larva) and starfish (bipinnaria larva) have larval metamorphosis.

q: Which of the following organisms are known as chief producers in the oceans ?
why: Diatoms are the chief producers in the oceans.

q: Which one of the following population interactions is widely used in medical science for the production of antibiotics ?
why: Antibiotics such as penicillin from Penicillium inhibit bacteria without affecting the fungus, an example of amensalism.

q: All of the following are included in ‘Ex-situ conservation’ except
why: Sacred groves are in-situ conservation; the others are ex-situ.

q: Match the items given in Column I with those in Column II and select the correct option given below : Column I: a. Eutrophication; b. Sanitary landfill; c. Snow blindness; d. Jhum cultivation.  Column II: i. UV-B radiation; ii. Deforestation; iii. Nutrient enrichment; iv. Waste disposal
why: Eutrophication is nutrient enrichment, landfill is waste disposal, snow blindness is caused by UV-B and jhum cultivation causes deforestation.

q: In a growing population of a country,
opts: reproductive and pre-reproductive individuals are equal in number.
reproductive individuals are less than the post-reproductive individuals.
pre-reproductive individuals are more than the reproductive individuals.
pre-reproductive individuals are less than the reproductive individuals.
why: A growing population has an age pyramid with a broad base, so pre-reproductive individuals outnumber reproductive ones.

q: Which part of poppy plant is used to obtain the drug “Smack” ?
why: Latex from unripe poppy capsules yields morphine, which is acetylated to heroin (smack).

q: All of the following are part of an operon except
why: An operon has structural genes, a promoter and an operator (plus a regulator gene); enhancers are not part of a bacterial operon.

q: A woman has an X-linked condition on one of her X chromosomes. This chromosome can be inherited by
why: A mother passes one of her X chromosomes to both sons and daughters.

q: According to Hugo de Vries, the mechanism of evolution is
why: De Vries proposed mutation as large single-step changes called saltation.

q: AGGTATCGCAT is a sequence from the coding strand of a gene. What will be the corresponding sequence of the transcribed mRNA ?
why: mRNA has the same sequence as the coding strand with U in place of T: AGGUAUCGCAU.

q: Match the items given in Column I with those in Column II and select the correct option given below : Column I: a. Proliferative Phase; b. Secretory Phase; c. Menstruation.  Column II: i. Breakdown of endometrial lining; ii. Follicular Phase; iii. Luteal Phase
why: Proliferative phase corresponds to the follicular phase, secretory to the luteal phase, and menstruation is breakdown of the endometrium.

q: Match the items given in Column I with those in Column II and select the correct option given below: Column I: a. Glycosuria; b. Gout; c. Renal calculi; d. Glomerular nephritis. Column II: i. Accumulation of uric acid in joints; ii. Mass of crystallised salts within the kidney; iii. Inflammation in glomeruli; iv. Presence of glucose in urine
why: Glycosuria is glucose in urine (iv); gout is uric acid deposition in joints (i); renal calculi are crystallised salt masses in the kidney (ii); glomerular nephritis is inflammation of glomeruli (iii).

q: Match the items given in Column I with those in Column II and select the correct option given below: Column I (Function): a. Ultrafiltration; b. Concentration of urine; c. Transport of urine; d. Storage of urine. Column II (Part of Excretory System): i. Henle's loop; ii. Ureter; iii. Urinary bladder; iv. Malpighian corpuscle; v. Proximal convoluted tubule
why: Ultrafiltration occurs in the Malpighian corpuscle, urine is concentrated in Henle's loop, carried by the ureter and stored in the urinary bladder.

q: Which of the following gastric cells indirectly help in erythropoiesis?
why: Parietal (oxyntic) cells secrete intrinsic factor, needed to absorb vitamin B₁₂, which is required for erythropoiesis.

q: Match the items given in Column I with those in Column II and select the correct option given below: Column I: a. Fibrinogen; b. Globulin; c. Albumin. Column II: i. Osmotic balance; ii. Blood clotting; iii. Defence mechanism
why: Fibrinogen is needed for blood clotting, globulins for defence (antibodies) and albumin for osmotic balance.

q: Which of the following is an occupational respiratory disorder?
why: Silicosis is caused by long exposure to silica dust in grinding and stone-breaking industries. Emphysema is mainly caused by smoking.

q: Calcium is important in skeletal muscle contraction because it
opts: detaches the myosin head from the actin filament.
activates the myosin ATPase by binding to it.
binds to troponin to remove the masking of active sites on actin for myosin.
prevents the formation of bonds between the myosin cross bridges and the actin filament.
why: Ca²⁺ binds troponin, shifting tropomyosin and exposing the myosin-binding active sites on actin so cross-bridges can form.

q: Nissl bodies are mainly composed of
why: Nissl granules in neurons are clusters of free ribosomes and rough endoplasmic reticulum involved in protein synthesis.

q: Which of these statements is incorrect?
opts: Glycolysis operates as long as it is supplied with NAD that can pick up hydrogen atoms.
Enzymes of TCA cycle are present in mitochondrial matrix.
Oxidative phosphorylation takes place in outer mitochondrial membrane.
why: Oxidative phosphorylation (ETS and ATP synthase) occurs in the inner mitochondrial membrane, not the outer membrane.

q: Select the incorrect match:
why: Polytene chromosomes occur in salivary glands of Drosophila; lampbrush chromosomes are found in amphibian oocytes.

q: Which of the following terms describe human dentition?
why: Human teeth are set in sockets (thecodont), appear twice (diphyodont) and are of different types (heterodont).

q: Which of the following events does not occur in rough endoplasmic reticulum?
why: Phospholipid (lipid) synthesis takes place in the smooth ER; the RER handles signal peptide cleavage, folding and glycosylation of proteins.

q: Many ribosomes may associate with a single mRNA to form multiple copies of a polypeptide simultaneously. Such strings of ribosomes are termed as
why: Several ribosomes translating the same mRNA form a polysome (polyribosome).

q: In which disease does mosquito transmitted pathogen cause chronic inflammation of lymphatic vessels?
why: Elephantiasis (filariasis) is caused by Wuchereria transmitted by Culex mosquitoes, causing chronic inflammation of lymphatic vessels.

q: Which of the following is not an autoimmune disease?
why: Alzheimer's is a neurodegenerative disorder; rheumatoid arthritis, psoriasis and vitiligo are autoimmune.

q: Among the following sets of examples for divergent evolution, select the incorrect option:
opts: Brain of bat, man and cheetah
Heart of bat, man and cheetah
Forelimbs of man, bat and cheetah
Eye of octopus, bat and man
why: The eyes of octopus and mammals evolved independently with similar function, so they are analogous (convergent evolution), not divergent.

q: Conversion of milk to curd improves its nutritional value by increasing the amount of
why: Lactic acid bacteria in curd increase vitamin B₁₂ content.

q: The similarity of bone structure in the forelimbs of many vertebrates is an example of
why: Similar structure with a common origin but different functions is homology, evidence of divergent evolution.

q: Which of the following characteristics represent 'Inheritance of blood groups' in humans? a. Dominance b. Co-dominance c. Multiple allele d. Incomplete dominance e. Polygenic inheritance
why: ABO blood groups show dominance (Iᴬ, Iᴮ over i), co-dominance (IᴬIᴮ) and multiple alleles (Iᴬ, Iᴮ, i).

q: Two particles A and B are moving in uniform circular motion in concentric circles of radii rA and rB with speed vA and vB respectively. Their time period of rotation is the same. The ratio of angular speed of A to that of B will be :
why: Angular speed ω = 2π/T. Both particles have the same time period, so their angular speeds are equal and the ratio is 1 : 1.

q: A parallel plate capacitor of capacitance 20 μF is being charged by a voltage source whose potential is changing at the rate of 3 V/s. The conduction current through the connecting wires, and the displacement current through the plates of the capacitor, would be, respectively :
why: Conduction current I = C dV/dt = 20×10⁻⁶ × 3 = 60 μA. Displacement current in the gap equals the conduction current, so it is also 60 μA.

q: A 800 turn coil of effective area 0.05 m² is kept perpendicular to a magnetic field 5×10⁻⁵ T. When the plane of the coil is rotated by 90° around any of its coplanar axis in 0.1 s, the emf induced in the coil will be :
why: Flux changes from NBA to 0. emf = NBA/t = 800 × 5×10⁻⁵ × 0.05 / 0.1 = 0.02 V.

q: The unit of thermal conductivity is :
why: From Q/t = K A ΔT/L, K = (Q/t)·L/(AΔT) has unit W m⁻¹ K⁻¹.

q: The displacement of a particle executing simple harmonic motion is given by y = A₀ + A sinωt + B cosωt. Then the amplitude of its oscillation is given by :
why: A sinωt + B cosωt = R sin(ωt + φ) with R = √(A² + B²); A₀ only shifts the mean position, so the amplitude is √(A² + B²).

q: A hollow metal sphere of radius R is uniformly charged. The electric field due to the sphere at a distance r from the centre :
opts: increases as r increases for r < R and for r > R
zero as r increases for r < R, decreases as r increases for r > R
zero as r increases for r < R, increases as r increases for r > R
decreases as r increases for r < R and for r > R
why: Inside a charged hollow conductor the field is zero. Outside, E = kQ/r², which decreases as r increases.

q: The work done to raise a mass m from the surface of the earth to a height h, which is equal to the radius of the earth, is :
why: W = GMm(1/R − 1/(R+h)) with h = R gives GMm/2R. Since GM = gR², W = ½ mgR.

q: An electron is accelerated through a potential difference of 10,000 V. Its de Broglie wavelength is, (nearly) : (mₑ = 9×10⁻³¹ kg)

In a double slit experiment, when light of wavelength 400 nm was used, the angular width of the first minima formed on a screen placed 1 m away, was found to be 0.2°. What will be the angular width of the first minima, if the entire experimental apparatus is immersed in water ? (μwater = 4/3)
why: Angular width θ = λ/d. In water λ becomes λ/μ, so θ' = 0.2° × 3/4 = 0.15°.

q: A body weighs 200 N on the surface of the earth. How much will it weigh half way down to the centre of the earth ?
why: Inside the earth g' = g(1 − d/R). At half the depth to the centre, d = R/2, so g' = g/2 and the weight is 100 N.

topic: Motion of charge in magnetic field
q: Ionized hydrogen atoms and α-particles with same momenta enters perpendicular to a constant magnetic field, B. The ratio of their radii of their paths rH : rα will be :
why: r = p/(qB). Same p and B, so r ∝ 1/q. qH = e and qα = 2e, giving rH : rα = 2 : 1.

q: Which of the following acts as a circuit protection device ?
why: A fuse melts when current exceeds a safe value and breaks the circuit, thereby protecting it.

q: Two parallel infinite line charges with linear charge densities +λ C/m and −λ C/m are placed at a distance of 2R in free space. What is the electric field mid-way between the two line charges ?
why: Each line gives λ/(2πε₀R) at the midpoint, and for opposite charges the fields point the same way, so the total is λ/(πε₀R).

q: A disc of radius 2 m and mass 100 kg rolls on a horizontal floor. Its centre of mass has speed of 20 cm/s. How much work is needed to stop it ?
why: Work = total KE = ½mv²(1 + k²/R²) = ½ × 100 × (0.2)² × 3/2 = 3 J for a disc.

q: α-particle consists of :
why: An α-particle is a helium nucleus, made of 2 protons and 2 neutrons.

q: Two point charges A and B, having charges +Q and −Q respectively, are placed at certain distance apart and force acting between them is F. If 25% charge of A is transferred to B, then force between the charges becomes :
why: After transfer A has 0.75Q and B has −0.75Q. Force ∝ product of charges, so F' = (3/4)² F = 9F/16.

q: Which colour of the light has the longest wavelength ?
why: In the visible spectrum red has the longest wavelength (about 700 nm) and violet the shortest.

q: When an object is shot from the bottom of a long smooth inclined plane kept at an angle 60° with horizontal, it can travel a distance x₁ along the plane. But when the inclination is decreased to 30° and the same object is shot with the same velocity, it can travel x₂ distance. Then x₁ : x₂ will be :
why: Distance up the plane x = v²/(2g sinθ), so x ∝ 1/sinθ. x₁ : x₂ = sin30° : sin60° = 1/2 : √3/2 = 1 : √3.

q: A particle moving with velocity V is acted by three forces shown by the vector triangle PQR. The velocity of the particle will :
opts: change according to the smallest force QR
why: Three forces forming a closed vector triangle sum to zero, so net force is zero and the velocity stays constant (Newton's first law).

q: At a point A on the earth's surface the angle of dip, δ = +25°. At a point B on the earth's surface the angle of dip, δ = −25°. We can interpret that :
opts: A and B are both located in the northern hemisphere.
A is located in the southern hemisphere and B is located in the northern hemisphere.
A is located in the northern hemisphere and B is located in the southern hemisphere.
A and B are both located in the southern hemisphere.
why: In the northern hemisphere the field points downward (positive dip) and in the southern hemisphere it points upward (negative dip). So A is north and B is south.

q: A force F = 20 + 10y acts on a particle in y-direction where F is in newton and y in meter. Work done by this force to move the particle from y = 0 to y = 1 m is :
A mass m is attached to a thin wire and whirled in a vertical circle. The wire is most likely to break when :
opts: the mass is at the highest point
the mass is at the lowest point
inclined at an angle of 60° from vertical
why: Tension T = mv²/r + mg cosθ is greatest at the lowest point where speed is maximum and gravity adds to the centripetal need.

q: A solid cylinder of mass 2 kg and radius 4 cm is rotating about its axis at the rate of 3 rpm. The torque required to stop after 2π revolutions is :
why: ω = 3 rpm = π/10 rad/s, θ = 2π × 2π = 4π² rad. α = ω²/(2θ) = 1/800 rad/s². I = ½mr² = 16×10⁻⁴ kg m². τ = Iα = 2×10⁻⁶ N m.

q: Body A of mass 4m moving with speed u collides with another body B of mass 2m, at rest. The collision is head on and elastic in nature. After the collision the fraction of energy lost by the colliding body A is :
why: vA = (4m − 2m)u/(6m) = u/3. Final KE is 1/9 of the initial, so the fraction lost is 1 − 1/9 = 8/9.

q: Average velocity of a particle executing SHM in one complete vibration is :
why: In one complete vibration the net displacement is zero, so the average velocity is zero.

q: Pick the wrong answer in the context with rainbow.
opts: When the light rays undergo two internal reflections in a water drop, a secondary rainbow is formed.
The order of colours is reversed in the secondary rainbow.
An observer can see a rainbow when his front is towards the sun.
Rainbow is a combined effect of dispersion, refraction and reflection of sunlight.
why: A rainbow is seen when the sun is behind the observer, so the observer's back (not front) must be towards the sun.

q: Two similar thin equi-convex lenses, of focal length f each, are kept coaxially in contact with each other such that the focal length of the combination is F₁. When the space between the two lenses is filled with glycerin (which has the same refractive index (μ = 1.5) as that of glass) then the equivalent focal length is F₂. The ratio F₁ : F₂ will be :
why: In contact, F₁ = f/2. Each lens has f = R (μ = 1.5). With glycerin of the same index the inner surfaces cancel, leaving the two outer surfaces: 1/F₂ = 0.5/R + 0.5/R = 1/R, so F₂ = f. Hence F₁ : F₂ = 1 : 2.

q: A soap bubble, having radius of 1 mm, is blown from a detergent solution having a surface tension of 2.5×10⁻² N/m. The pressure inside the bubble equals at a point Z₀ below the free surface of water in a container. Taking g = 10 m/s², density of water = 10³ kg/m³, the value of Z₀ is :
why: Excess pressure in a soap bubble is 4T/r = 4 × 2.5×10⁻² / 10⁻³ = 100 Pa. Setting ρgZ₀ = 100 gives Z₀ = 100/(10⁴) = 0.01 m = 1 cm.

q: In which of the following processes, heat is neither absorbed nor released by a system ?
why: An adiabatic process involves no heat exchange with the surroundings (Q = 0).

q: Increase in temperature of a gas filled in a container would lead to :
why: The average kinetic energy of gas molecules is proportional to absolute temperature, so it rises with temperature. Mass is unchanged and, in a rigid container, pressure increases.

q: Thiobacillus is a group of bacteria helpful in carrying out :
why: NCERT lists Pseudomonas and Thiobacillus as denitrifying bacteria that convert nitrate to nitrogen gas.

q: From evolutionary point of view, retention of the female gametophyte with developing young embryo on the parent sporophyte for some time, is first observed in :
why: In some pteridophytes (Selaginella, Salvinia) the zygote develops into a young embryo within the female gametophyte retained on the sporophyte, a precursor of the seed habit.

q: Which of the following is the most important cause for animals and plants being driven to extinction ?
why: Habitat loss and fragmentation is the most important cause of biodiversity loss according to NCERT (the evil quartet).

q: Xylem translocates :
opts: Water, mineral salts and some organic nitrogen only
Water, mineral salts, some organic nitrogen and hormones
why: NCERT states that xylem transports water, mineral salts, some organic nitrogen and hormones from roots to other parts.

q: Which of the following statements is correct ?
opts: Cornea is an external, transparent and protective proteinacious covering of the eye-ball.
Cornea consists of dense connective tissue of elastin and can repair itself.
Cornea is convex, transparent layer which is highly vascularised.
Cornea consists of dense matrix of collagen and is the most sensitive portion of the eye.
why: The cornea is a transparent, avascular tissue made of a dense collagen matrix and is richly supplied with nerve endings, so it is highly sensitive.

topic: Seed structure, sexual reproduction in plants
q: Persistent nucellus in the seed is known as :
why: Remnants of nucellus that persist in the seed, as in black pepper and beet, form the perisperm.

q: Select the correctly written scientific name of Mango which was first described by Carolus Linnaeus :
why: Binomial nomenclature: genus capitalised, species in lower case, both italicised, followed by the author's name abbreviated (Linn.) in roman type.

q: Expressed Sequence Tags (ESTs) refers to :
why: In the Human Genome Project, ESTs identified all genes that are expressed as RNA, as opposed to sequence annotation of the whole genome.

q: Grass leaves curl inwards during very dry weather. Select the most appropriate reason from the following :
opts: Shrinkage of air spaces in spongy mesophyll
why: Bulliform cells lose water and become flaccid in dry weather, causing the leaf to curl inwards and reduce water loss.

q: Which of the following muscular disorders is inherited ?
why: Muscular dystrophy is a genetic (X-linked) disorder causing progressive degeneration of skeletal muscle; tetany, myasthenia gravis and botulism are not inherited.

q: Under which of the following conditions will there be no change in the reading frame of following mRNA ? 5' AACAGCGGUGCUAUU 3'
opts: Insertion of A and G at 4th and 5th positions respectively
Deletion of GGU from 7th, 8th and 9th positions
why: Reading frame is kept only if a multiple of three nucleotides is added or removed. Deleting GGU (positions 7-9) removes exactly one codon; the other options add or remove one or two bases and cause a frameshift.

q: The shorter and longer arms of a submetacentric chromosome are referred to as :
why: By convention the shorter arm is the p-arm (petit) and the longer arm is the q-arm.

q: Select the correct option.
opts: 8th, 9th and 10th pairs of ribs articulate directly with the sternum.
11th and 12th pairs of ribs are connected to the sternum with the help of hyaline cartilage.
Each rib is a flat thin bone and all the ribs are connected dorsally to the thoracic vertebrae and ventrally to the sternum.
There are seven pairs of vertebrosternal, three pairs of vertebrochondral and two pairs of vertebral ribs.
why: Of 12 pairs of ribs, the first 7 are true (vertebrosternal), 8th-10th are vertebrochondral (false) and 11th-12th are floating (vertebral) ribs.

q: Which of the following sexually transmitted diseases is not completely curable ?
why: Genital herpes (a viral infection) can be managed but not completely cured; gonorrhoea and chlamydiasis are bacterial and curable with antibiotics. Genital warts are also viral, but herpes is the option the NCERT treats as not completely curable.

q: Which of the following statements is not correct ?
opts: The hydrolytic enzymes of lysosomes are active under acidic pH.
Lysosomes are formed by the process of packaging in the endoplasmic reticulum.
why: Lysosomes are formed by packaging of enzymes in the Golgi apparatus (enzymes synthesised in the rough ER), not packaging in the ER itself.

q: Which one of the following equipments is essentially required for growing microbes on a large scale, for industrial production of enzymes ?
why: Large-scale culture of microbes for industrial products such as enzymes is done in bioreactors (fermentors) that provide optimal growth conditions.

q: Which one of the following is not a method of in situ conservation of biodiversity ?
why: Botanical gardens conserve organisms outside their natural habitat, so they are ex situ; the others protect species in their natural habitat.

q: Consider following features : (a) Organ system level of organisation (b) Bilateral symmetry (c) True coelomates with segmentation of body. Select the correct option of animal groups which possess all the above characteristics.
why: Annelida, Arthropoda and Chordata are organ-system level, bilaterally symmetrical, true coelomates with metameric segmentation; Mollusca show no true segmentation.

q: The ciliated epithelial cells are required to move particles or mucus in a specific direction. In humans, these cells are mainly present in :
why: Ciliated columnar epithelium lines the bronchioles (moving mucus) and the fallopian tubes (moving the ovum); the other listed ducts are not ciliated.

q: What is the site of perception of photoperiod necessary for induction of flowering in plants ?
why: Leaves perceive the photoperiodic stimulus and send a flowering signal to the shoot apex.

q: Match the hominids with their correct brain size : (a) Homo habilis (b) Homo neanderthalensis (c) Homo erectus (d) Homo sapiens ; (i) 900 cc (ii) 1350 cc (iii) 650-800 cc (iv) 1400 cc. Select the correct option.
why: Homo habilis 650-800 cc, Neanderthal about 1400 cc, Homo erectus about 900 cc and Homo sapiens about 1350 cc.

q: In Antirrhinum (Snapdragon), a red flower was crossed with a white flower and in F1 generation, pink flowers were obtained. When pink flowers were selfed, the F2 generation showed white, red and pink flowers. Choose the incorrect statement from the following :
opts: This experiment does not follow the Principle of Dominance.
Pink colour in F1 is due to incomplete dominance.
Law of Segregation does not apply in this experiment.
why: Incomplete dominance gives a 1:2:1 F2 ratio because the alleles still segregate during gamete formation, so the Law of Segregation does apply.

q: Which of these following methods is the most suitable for disposal of nuclear waste ?
opts: Bury the waste under Antarctic ice-cover
Dump the waste within rocks under deep ocean
Bury the waste within rocks deep below the Earth's surface
why: After storage in suitable shielded containers, nuclear waste is buried within rocks about 500 m deep below the Earth's surface, as recommended in NCERT.

q: Drug called 'Heroin' is synthesized by :
why: Heroin (smack) is diacetylmorphine, formed by acetylation of morphine.

q: Use of an artificial kidney during hemodialysis may result in : (a) Nitrogenous waste build-up in the body (b) Non-elimination of excess potassium ions (c) Reduced absorption of calcium ions from gastro-intestinal tract (d) Reduced RBC production. Which of the following options is the most appropriate ?
why: Dialysis removes nitrogenous wastes and excess K⁺, but it cannot replace the endocrine functions of the kidney: lack of active vitamin D reduces calcium absorption and lack of erythropoietin reduces RBC production.

q: What is the genetic disorder in which an individual has an overall masculine development, gynaecomastia, and is sterile ?
why: Klinefelter's syndrome (XXY) gives masculine development with gynaecomastia and sterility; Turner's (XO) gives sterile females.

q: Which of the following statements is incorrect ?
opts: Morels and truffles are edible delicacies.
Claviceps is a source of many alkaloids and LSD.
Conidia are produced exogenously and ascospores endogenously.
Yeasts have filamentous bodies with long thread-like hyphae.
why: Yeasts are unicellular fungi and do not form hyphae; the other statements are correct.

q: Which of the following ecological pyramids is generally inverted ?
opts: Pyramid of biomass in a forest
Pyramid of biomass in a sea
why: In the sea, phytoplankton (producers) have a smaller standing crop than the zooplankton and fish they support, so the biomass pyramid is inverted. Energy pyramids are always upright.

q: Select the correct sequence for transport of sperm cells in male reproductive system.
opts: Testis → Epididymis → Vasa efferentia → Rete testis → Inguinal canal → Urethra
Seminiferous tubules → Rete testis → Vasa efferentia → Epididymis → Vas deferens → Ejaculatory duct → Urethra → Urethral meatus
Seminiferous tubules → Vasa efferentia → Epididymis → Inguinal canal → Urethra
Testis → Epididymis → Vasa efferentia → Vas deferens → Ejaculatory duct → Inguinal canal → Urethra → Urethral meatus
why: Sperm pass from seminiferous tubules to rete testis, vasa efferentia, epididymis, vas deferens, ejaculatory duct, urethra and out through the urethral meatus.

q: Which of the following protocols did aim for reducing emission of chlorofluorocarbons into the atmosphere ?
why: The Montreal Protocol (1987) was signed to control emission of ozone-depleting substances such as CFCs. Kyoto deals with greenhouse gases.

q: The correct sequence of phases of cell cycle is :
why: Interphase consists of G₁, S and G₂ in that order, followed by the M phase.

q: What is the fate of the male gametes discharged in the synergid ?
opts: One fuses with the egg, other(s) degenerate(s) in the synergid.
One fuses with the egg, other(s) fuse(s) with synergid nucleus.
One fuses with the egg and other fuses with central cell nuclei.
why: Double fertilization: one male gamete fuses with the egg (syngamy) and the other fuses with the two polar nuclei of the central cell (triple fusion).

q: Which of the following pair of organelles does not contain DNA ?
why: Mitochondria and chloroplasts have their own DNA, and the nucleus contains DNA; lysosomes and vacuoles are single-membrane organelles without DNA.

q: Which of the following glucose transporters is insulin-dependent ?
why: GLUT IV, present in muscle and adipose tissue, is the insulin-regulated glucose transporter.

q: Conversion of glucose to glucose-6-phosphate, the first irreversible reaction of glycolysis, is catalyzed by :
why: Hexokinase phosphorylates glucose to glucose-6-phosphate using ATP in the first step of glycolysis.

q: Variations caused by mutation, as proposed by Hugo de Vries, are :
why: De Vries's mutation theory held that mutations are sudden, large, random and directionless; Darwinian variations are small and directionless.

q: Which of the following statements regarding mitochondria is incorrect ?
opts: Outer membrane is permeable to monomers of carbohydrates, fats and proteins.
Enzymes of electron transport are embedded in outer membrane.
Inner membrane is convoluted with infoldings.
Mitochondrial matrix contains single circular DNA molecule and ribosomes.
why: The enzymes of the electron transport chain are embedded in the inner mitochondrial membrane (cristae), not the outer membrane.

q: Select the correct sequence of organs in the alimentary canal of cockroach starting from mouth :
opts: Pharynx → Oesophagus → Crop → Gizzard → Ileum → Colon → Rectum
Pharynx → Oesophagus → Gizzard → Crop → Ileum → Colon → Rectum
Pharynx → Oesophagus → Gizzard → Ileum → Crop → Colon → Rectum
Pharynx → Oesophagus → Ileum → Crop → Gizzard → Colon → Rectum
why: In cockroach the foregut is pharynx, oesophagus, crop and gizzard, followed by the midgut/ileum, then colon and rectum.

q: Select the hormone-releasing Intra-Uterine Devices.
why: Progestasert and LNG-20 release hormones (progestogen/levonorgestrel); Lippes Loop is non-medicated and Multiload 375 is copper releasing.

q: Concanavalin A is :
why: Concanavalin A is a carbohydrate-binding protein (lectin), listed among secondary metabolites in NCERT.

q: DNA precipitation out of a mixture of biomolecules can be achieved by treatment with :
why: In NCERT's isolation of genetic material, purified DNA precipitates as fine threads when chilled ethanol is added.

q: Which of the following factors is responsible for the formation of concentrated urine ?
opts: Maintaining hyperosmolarity towards inner medullary interstitium in the kidneys.
Secretion of erythropoietin by Juxtaglomerular complex.
why: The osmotic gradient (counter-current mechanism) with hyperosmolar inner medulla lets water be reabsorbed from the collecting duct, giving concentrated urine. Low ADH would give dilute urine.

q: What would be the heart rate of a person if the cardiac output is 5 L, blood volume in the ventricles at the end of diastole is 100 mL and at the end of ventricular systole is 50 mL ?
why: Stroke volume = 100 - 50 = 50 mL. Heart rate = cardiac output / stroke volume = 5000 mL / 50 mL = 100 beats per minute.

topic: Strategies for enhancement in food production
q: Select the incorrect statement.
opts: Inbreeding is essential to evolve purelines in any animal.
Inbreeding selects harmful recessive genes that reduce fertility and productivity.
Inbreeding helps in accumulation of superior genes and elimination of undesirable genes.
why: Continued inbreeding exposes harmful recessive genes and causes inbreeding depression; it does not select them. Selection then eliminates them, which is why the other statements are correct.

q: Match the following genes of the Lac operon with their respective products : (a) i gene (b) z gene (c) a gene (d) y gene ; (i) β-galactosidase (ii) Permease (iii) Repressor (iv) Transacetylase. Select the correct option.
why: i codes for the repressor, z for β-galactosidase, y for permease and a for transacetylase.

q: Which of the following features of genetic code does allow bacteria to produce human insulin by recombinant DNA technology ?
why: Because the code is nearly universal, the same codons specify the same amino acids in bacteria and humans, so bacteria can translate the human insulin gene.

q: Match the following hormones with the respective disease : (a) Insulin (b) Thyroxin (c) Corticoids (d) Growth Hormone ; (i) Addison's disease (ii) Diabetes insipidus (iii) Acromegaly (iv) Goitre (v) Diabetes mellitus. Select the correct option.
why: Insulin deficiency causes diabetes mellitus, thyroxin disorder gives goitre, corticoid deficiency gives Addison's disease and excess growth hormone in adults gives acromegaly.

q: Colostrum, the yellowish fluid, secreted by mother during the initial days of lactation is very essential to impart immunity to the newborn infants because it contains :
why: Colostrum is rich in antibodies, mainly IgA, which give passive immunity to the newborn.

q: Placentation, in which ovules develop on the inner wall of the ovary or in peripheral part, is :
why: In parietal placentation the ovules are borne on the inner wall (peripheral region) of a unilocular ovary, as in mustard and Argemone.

q: Respiratory Quotient (RQ) value of tripalmitin is :
why: For fats like tripalmitin, 2(C₅₁H₉₈O₆) + 145 O₂ → 102 CO₂ + 98 H₂O, so RQ = 102/145 ≈ 0.7.

q: Select the correct group of biocontrol agents.
opts: Bacillus thuringiensis, Tobacco mosaic virus, Aphids
why: Trichoderma (fungus), Baculovirus (NPV) and Bacillus thuringiensis (bacterium) are all used as biological control agents; tobacco mosaic virus and aphids are pests.

q: Match the Column-I with Column-II : Column-I: (a) P-wave (b) QRS complex (c) T-wave (d) Reduction in the size of T-wave ; Column-II: (i) Depolarisation of ventricles (ii) Repolarisation of ventricles (iii) Coronary ischemia (iv) Depolarisation of atria (v) Repolarisation of atria. Select the correct option.
why: P-wave is atrial depolarisation, QRS is ventricular depolarisation, T-wave is ventricular repolarisation, and a reduced T-wave suggests coronary ischemia.

q: Match the following structures with their respective location in organs : (a) Crypts of Lieberkühn (b) Glisson's Capsule (c) Islets of Langerhans (d) Brunner's Glands ; (i) Pancreas (ii) Duodenum (iii) Small intestine (iv) Liver. Select the correct option from the following :
why: Crypts of Lieberkühn are in the small intestine, Glisson's capsule covers the liver, islets of Langerhans are in the pancreas and Brunner's glands are in the duodenum.

q: Which of the following contraceptive methods do involve a role of hormone ?
why: Lactational amenorrhea (prolactin suppresses ovulation), oral pills and emergency contraceptives act through hormones; CuT and barrier methods do not.

q: Due to increasing air-borne allergens and pollutants, many people in urban areas are suffering from respiratory disorder causing wheezing due to :
opts: benign growth on mucous lining of nasal cavity.
proliferation of fibrous tissues and damage of the alveolar walls.
reduction in the secretion of surfactants by pneumocytes.
why: Asthma, characterised by wheezing, is caused by inflammation of the bronchi and bronchioles.

q: A gene locus has two alleles A, a. If the frequency of dominant allele A is 0.4, then what will be the frequency of homozygous dominant, heterozygous and homozygous recessive individuals in the population ?
why: p = 0.4, so q = 0.6. By Hardy-Weinberg, AA = p² = 0.16, Aa = 2pq = 0.48, aa = q² = 0.36.

q: How does steroid hormone influence the cellular activities ?
opts: Changing the permeability of the cell membrane.
Binding to DNA and forming a gene-hormone complex.
Activating cyclic AMP located on the cell membrane.
Using aquaporin channels as second messenger.
why: Steroid hormones are lipid soluble, enter the cell and bind intracellular receptors; the hormone-receptor complex interacts with DNA and regulates gene expression. Cyclic AMP and membrane receptors are used by protein hormones.

q: In some plants, the female gamete develops into embryo without fertilization. This phenomenon is known as :
why: Development of an embryo from an unfertilised egg is parthenogenesis. Parthenocarpy is fruit formation without fertilisation.

q: Which one of the following statements regarding post-fertilization development in flowering plants is incorrect ?
why: After fertilisation ovules develop into seeds, not into embryo sac (the embryo sac is present before fertilisation). The other three statements are correct.

q: Match the following organisms with the products they produce : List I: (a) Lactobacillus; (b) Saccharomyces cerevisiae; (c) Aspergillus niger; (d) Acetobacter aceti  List II: (i) Cheese; (ii) Curd; (iii) Citric Acid; (iv) Bread; (v) Acetic Acid. Select the correct option.
why: Lactobacillus turns milk into curd, yeast is used for bread, Aspergillus niger produces citric acid and Acetobacter aceti produces acetic acid.

q: Tidal Volume and Expiratory Reserve Volume of an athlete is 500 mL and 1000 mL respectively. What will be his Expiratory Capacity if the Residual Volume is 1200 mL ?
why: Expiratory capacity = tidal volume + expiratory reserve volume = 500 + 1000 = 1500 mL. Residual volume is not part of it.

q: Purines found both in DNA and RNA are :
why: Purines are adenine and guanine and both occur in DNA and RNA. Thymine and cytosine are pyrimidines.

q: The concept of "Omnis cellula-e cellula" regarding cell division was first proposed by :
why: Rudolf Virchow (1855) proposed that new cells arise from pre-existing cells, Omnis cellula-e cellula, modifying the cell theory.

q: Phloem in gymnosperms lacks :
opts: Both sieve tubes and companion cells
why: Gymnosperm phloem has sieve cells and albuminous cells. Sieve tubes and companion cells are found only in angiosperms.

q: Match the following organisms with their respective characteristics : List I: (a) Pila; (b) Bombyx; (c) Pleurobrachia; (d) Taenia  List II: (i) Flame cells; (ii) Comb plates; (iii) Radula; (iv) Malpighian tubules. Select the correct option from the following :
why: Pila (mollusc) has a radula, Bombyx (insect) has Malpighian tubules, Pleurobrachia (ctenophore) has comb plates and Taenia (flatworm) has flame cells.

q: It takes very long time for pineapple plants to produce flowers. Which combination of hormones can be applied to artificially induce flowering in pineapple plants throughout the year to increase yield ?
why: Auxins (such as NAA) and ethylene promote flowering in pineapple, so they can be used to induce flowering all year.

q: Which of the following pairs of gases is mainly responsible for green house effect ?
why: CO₂ and CH₄ are the major greenhouse gases that trap heat in the atmosphere.

q: Which of the following is true for Golden rice ?
opts: It is Vitamin A enriched, with a gene from daffodil.
It is pest resistant, with a gene from Bacillus thuringiensis.
It is drought tolerant, developed using Agrobacterium vector.
It has yellow grains, because of a gene introduced from a primitive variety of rice.
why: Golden rice is a transgenic rice rich in provitamin A (beta-carotene) carrying a gene from daffodil. It is not designed for pest or drought resistance.

q: Which of the following immune responses is responsible for rejection of kidney graft ?
why: Graft rejection is caused by the cell-mediated immune response (T-lymphocytes) against the foreign tissue.

q: Which of the statements given below is not true about formation of Annual Rings in trees ?
opts: Annual ring is a combination of spring wood and autumn wood produced in a year.
Differential activity of cambium causes light and dark bands of tissue - early and late wood respectively.
Activity of cambium depends upon variation in climate.
Annual rings are not prominent in trees of temperate region.
why: Annual rings are clearly marked in temperate trees because cambial activity varies with the seasons; they are not prominent in tropical trees. So statement 4 is false.

q: What is the direction of movement of sugars in phloem ?
why: Sugars move from source to sink, and since sources and sinks can be at either end, translocation in phloem is bi-directional.

q: Polyblend, a fine powder of recycled modified plastic, has proved to be a good material for :
why: Polyblend is mixed with bitumen to lay roads, increasing their durability and water resistance.

q: What map unit (Centimorgan) is adopted in the construction of genetic maps ?
opts: A unit of distance between two expressed genes, representing 10% cross over.
A unit of distance between two expressed genes, representing 100% cross over.
A unit of distance between genes on chromosomes, representing 1% cross over.
A unit of distance between genes on chromosomes, representing 50% cross over.
why: One map unit (centimorgan) corresponds to 1% recombination frequency between two genes on a chromosome.

q: Consider the following statements : (A) Coenzyme or metal ion that is tightly bound to enzyme protein is called prosthetic group. (B) A complete catalytic active enzyme with its bound prosthetic group is called apoenzyme. Select the correct option.
why: A tightly bound cofactor is a prosthetic group, so A is true. The complete active enzyme with its prosthetic group is the holoenzyme; the apoenzyme is the protein part alone, so B is false.

q: Which of the following can be used as a biocontrol agent in the treatment of plant disease ?
why: Trichoderma is a fungus used as a biocontrol agent against plant pathogens.

q: Pinus seed cannot germinate and establish without fungal association. This is because :
opts: it has obligate association with mycorrhizae.
it has very hard seed coat.
its seeds contain inhibitors that prevent germination.
