why: Pinus roots have an obligate mycorrhizal association that supplies minerals and water, so the seedling cannot establish without the fungus.

q: Which of the following is a commercial blood cholesterol lowering agent ?
why: Statins, produced from Monascus purpureus, inhibit the enzyme for cholesterol synthesis and lower blood cholesterol. Cyclosporin A is an immunosuppressant and streptokinase a clot buster.

q: Identify the correct pair representing the causative agent of typhoid fever and the confirmatory test for typhoid.
why: Typhoid is caused by Salmonella typhi and is confirmed by the Widal test.

q: Match Column - I with Column - II. Column - I: (a) Saprophyte; (b) Parasite; (c) Lichens; (d) Mycorrhiza  Column - II: (i) Symbiotic association of fungi with plant roots; (ii) Decomposition of dead organic materials; (iii) Living on plants or animals; (iv) Symbiotic association of algae and fungi. Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
why: Saprophytes feed on dead organic matter, parasites live on hosts, lichens are algae-fungus associations and mycorrhiza is a fungus-root association.

q: In a species, the weight of newborn ranges from 2 to 5 kg. 97% of the newborn with an average weight between 3 to 3.3 kg survive whereas 99% of the infants born with weights from 2 to 2.5 kg or 4.5 to 5 kg die. Which type of selection process is taking place ?
why: Individuals with the average phenotype survive while both extremes are eliminated, which is stabilizing selection.

q: Following statements describe the characteristics of the enzyme Restriction Endonuclease. Identify the incorrect statement.
opts: The enzyme cuts DNA molecule at identified position within the DNA.
The enzyme binds DNA at specific sites and cuts only one strand.
The enzyme cuts the sugar-phosphate backbone at specific sites on each strand.
The enzyme recognizes a specific palindromic nucleotide sequence in the DNA.
why: Restriction endonucleases cut the sugar-phosphate backbone of both strands at specific sites within a palindromic sequence, not just one strand.

q: Select the incorrect statement.
opts: In male grasshoppers, 50% of sperms have no sex-chromosome.
In domesticated fowls, sex of progeny depends on the type of sperm rather than egg.
Human males have one of their sex-chromosome much shorter than the other.
why: Fowls follow the ZW-ZZ system where the female is heterogametic, so the sex of progeny depends on the type of egg, not sperm.

q: Which of the following statements is incorrect ?
opts: Infective constituent in viruses is the protein coat.
Prions consist of abnormally folded proteins.
why: The infective constituent of a virus is its nucleic acid (genome), not the protein coat.

q: Identify the cells whose secretion protects the lining of gastro-intestinal tract from various enzymes.
why: Goblet cells secrete mucus that lubricates and protects the lining of the gastrointestinal tract from enzymes and acid.

q: The Earth Summit held in Rio de Janeiro in 1992 was called :
opts: to reduce CO₂ emissions and global warming.
for conservation of biodiversity and sustainable utilization of its benefits.
to assess threat posed to native species by invasive weed species.
for immediate steps to discontinue use of CFCs that were damaging the ozone layer.
why: The 1992 Rio Earth Summit was convened to take urgent steps for conservation of biodiversity and sustainable use of its benefits.

q: What triggers activation of protoxin to active Bt toxin of Bacillus thuringiensis in boll worm ?
why: The Bt protoxin crystals are solubilised and activated by the alkaline pH of the insect gut.

q: Which part of the brain is responsible for thermoregulation ?
why: The hypothalamus contains the thermoregulatory centre that controls body temperature.

q: Match the Xenon compounds in Column - I with its structure in Column - II and assign the correct code : Column - I: (a) XeF₄; (b) XeF₆; (c) XeOF₄; (d) XeO₃  Column - II: (i) pyramidal; (ii) square planar; (iii) distorted octahedral; (iv) square pyramidal.
why: XeF₄ is square planar (sp³d²), XeF₆ is distorted octahedral, XeOF₄ is square pyramidal and XeO₃ is pyramidal.

q: Which is the correct thermal stability order for H₂E (E = O, S, Se, Te and Po) ?
why: Thermal stability of hydrides decreases down the group as the E-H bond weakens, so H₂O is most stable and H₂Po least.

q: Enzymes that utilize ATP in phosphate transfer require an alkaline earth metal (M) as the cofactor. M is :
why: ATP-dependent phosphate transfer enzymes (kinases) use Mg²⁺ as the cofactor.

q: Which of the following reactions are disproportionation reaction ? (a) 2Cu⁺ → Cu²⁺ + Cu⁰  (b) 3MnO₄²⁻ + 4H⁺ → 2MnO₄⁻ + MnO₂ + 2H₂O  (c) 2KMnO₄ → K₂MnO₄ + MnO₂ + O₂  (d) 2MnO₄⁻ + 3Mn²⁺ + 2H₂O → 5MnO₂ + 4H⁺. Select the correct option from the following :
why: In (a) Cu⁺ goes to Cu²⁺ and Cu⁰ and in (b) Mn(+6) goes to +7 and +4, so both are disproportionation. In (c) Mn(+7) is only reduced (O is oxidised) and in (d) Mn(+7) and Mn(+2) both go to +4 (comproportionation).

q: The method used to remove temporary hardness of water is :
why: Clark's method adds lime to precipitate calcium and magnesium bicarbonates as carbonates and hydroxides, removing temporary hardness only.

q: For the chemical reaction N₂(g) + 3H₂(g) ⇌ 2NH₃(g) the correct option is :
why: Rate = −d[N₂]/dt = −(1/3) d[H₂]/dt = +(1/2) d[NH₃]/dt; reactants decrease and products increase, so only option 3 is right.

q: For a cell involving one electron E°cell = 0.59 V at 298 K, the equilibrium constant for the cell reaction is : [Given that 2.303RT/F = 0.059 V at T = 298 K]
The manganate and permanganate ions are tetrahedral, due to :
opts: The π-bonding involves overlap of p-orbitals of oxygen with d-orbitals of manganese
The π-bonding involves overlap of p-orbitals of oxygen with p-orbitals of manganese
The π-bonding involves overlap of d-orbitals of oxygen with d-orbitals of manganese
why: Oxygen has no d-orbitals in its valence shell; the π bonds in MnO₄²⁻ and MnO₄⁻ arise from pπ-dπ overlap between O and Mn.

q: The number of moles of hydrogen molecules required to produce 20 moles of ammonia through Haber's process is :
why: N₂ + 3H₂ → 2NH₃, so 3 mol H₂ give 2 mol NH₃; for 20 mol NH₃ we need 20 × 3/2 = 30 mol H₂.

q: A gas at 350 K and 15 bar has molar volume 20 percent smaller than that for an ideal gas under the same conditions. The correct option about the gas and its compressibility factor (Z) is :
opts: Z > 1 and attractive forces are dominant
Z > 1 and repulsive forces are dominant
Z < 1 and attractive forces are dominant
Z < 1 and repulsive forces are dominant
why: Z = Vreal/Videal = 0.8, which is less than 1, indicating attractive forces dominate.

q: Which will make basic buffer ?
opts: 50 mL of 0.1 M NaOH + 25 mL of 0.1 M CH₃COOH
100 mL of 0.1 M CH₃COOH + 100 mL of 0.1 M NaOH
100 mL of 0.1 M HCl + 200 mL of 0.1 M NH₄OH
100 mL of 0.1 M HCl + 100 mL of 0.1 M NaOH
why: A basic buffer needs a weak base and its salt. 10 mmol HCl + 20 mmol NH₄OH leaves 10 mmol NH₄OH and forms 10 mmol NH₄Cl, giving a buffer.

q: If the rate constant for a first order reaction is k, the time (t) required for the completion of 99% of the reaction is given by :
Conjugate base for Brönsted acids H₂O and HF are :
why: A conjugate base is formed by loss of H⁺: H₂O gives OH⁻ and HF gives F⁻.

q: Which of the following species is not stable ?
why: Silicon cannot accommodate six large Cl⁻ ions around it because of steric crowding, so [SiCl₆]²⁻ does not exist, whereas the small F⁻ forms stable [SiF₆]²⁻.

q: Which one is malachite from the following ?
why: Malachite is the basic copper carbonate ore CuCO₃·Cu(OH)₂. CuFeS₂ is copper pyrites and Fe₃O₄ is magnetite.

q: Which of the following is incorrect statement ?
opts: GeX₄ (X = F, Cl, Br, I) is more stable than GeX₂
why: PbF₄ is ionic, not covalent (Pb in +4 state with highly electronegative F). SiCl₄ hydrolyses easily, Ge(+4) is more stable than Ge(+2), and SnF₄ is ionic, so those statements are correct.

q: The non-essential amino acid among the following is :
why: Valine, leucine and lysine are essential amino acids that the body cannot synthesise. Alanine can be synthesised by the body, so it is non-essential.

q: Match the following : List I: (a) Pure nitrogen; (b) Haber process; (c) Contact process; (d) Deacon's process.  List II: (i) Chlorine; (ii) Sulphuric acid; (iii) Ammonia; (iv) Sodium azide or Barium azide. Which of the following is the correct option ?
why: Pure N₂ is obtained by thermal decomposition of sodium or barium azide; Haber process gives NH₃; Contact process gives H₂SO₄; Deacon's process gives Cl₂.

q: Among the following, the narrow spectrum antibiotic is :
why: Penicillin G is effective mainly against a limited range of bacteria (narrow spectrum). Ampicillin and amoxycillin are semi-synthetic broad spectrum, and chloramphenicol is broad spectrum.

q: Which of the following is an amphoteric hydroxide ?
why: Be(OH)₂ reacts with both acids and bases, so it is amphoteric. The hydroxides of Mg, Ca and Sr are basic.

q: Which of the following diatomic molecular species has only π bonds according to Molecular Orbital Theory ?
why: C₂ has 12 electrons with configuration ...(π2p)⁴ filling both π orbitals with no net σ bond, so its two bonds are both π. N₂ and O₂ have a σ bond, and Be₂ has bond order zero.

q: The biodegradable polymer is :
why: Nylon 2-nylon 6 is a copolymer of glycine and aminocaproic acid, a biodegradable polymer. Nylon-6,6, nylon-6 and Buna-S are not biodegradable.

q: The number of sigma (σ) and pi (π) bonds in pent-2-en-4-yne is :
opts: 13 σ bonds and no π bond
why: Pent-2-en-4-yne is CH₃–CH=CH–C≡CH. It has 4 C–C σ bonds and 6 C–H σ bonds = 10 σ bonds, and 1 (double bond) + 2 (triple bond) = 3 π bonds.

q: What is the correct electronic configuration of the central atom in K₄[Fe(CN)₆] based on crystal field theory ?
why: Fe is in the +2 state (d⁶). CN⁻ is a strong field ligand, so the complex is octahedral low spin with all six electrons paired in t₂g: t₂g⁶ e_g⁰.

q: Among the following, the one that is not a green house gas is :
why: N₂O, CH₄ and O₃ all absorb infrared radiation and act as greenhouse gases. SO₂ is an acidic pollutant and not counted as a greenhouse gas.

q: A compound is formed by cation C and anion A. The anions form hexagonal close packed (hcp) lattice and the cations occupy 75% of octahedral voids. The formula of the compound is :
why: For N anions in hcp there are N octahedral voids. Cations fill 75% = 0.75N, so C : A = 0.75 : 1 = 3 : 4, giving C₃A₄.

q: For an ideal solution, the correct option is :
opts: Δmix S = 0 at constant T and P
Δmix V ≠ 0 at constant T and P
Δmix H = 0 at constant T and P
Δmix G = 0 at constant T and P
why: An ideal solution has no heat change and no volume change on mixing: Δmix H = 0 and Δmix V = 0. Δmix S is positive and Δmix G is negative.

q: The compound that is most difficult to protonate is :
why: In phenol the lone pair on oxygen is delocalised into the benzene ring, so it is least available to accept a proton. In water, methanol and dimethyl ether the lone pairs are localised (alkyl groups even increase availability).

q: 4d, 5p, 5f and 6p orbitals are arranged in the order of decreasing energy. The correct option is :
why: Using the (n + l) rule: 5f = 8, 6p = 7, 5p = 6 and 4d = 6. For equal (n + l), the higher n has higher energy, so 5p > 4d. Order: 5f > 6p > 5p > 4d.

q: The mixture that forms maximum boiling azeotrope is :
why: Water + nitric acid shows negative deviation from Raoult's law and forms a maximum boiling azeotrope. Ethanol–water and acetone–CS₂ show positive deviation, and heptane–octane is nearly ideal.

q: In which case change in entropy is negative ?
opts: Expansion of a gas at constant temperature
why: Entropy decreases when the number of gas particles falls. 2H(g) → H₂(g) reduces moles of gas, giving a negative ΔS, while the other processes increase disorder.

q: Which of the following series of transitions in the spectrum of hydrogen atom falls in visible region ?
why: The Balmer series (transitions to n = 2) lies in the visible region. Lyman is ultraviolet, while Paschen and Brackett are infrared.

q: Identify the incorrect statement related to PCl₅ from the following :
opts: Three equatorial P–Cl bonds make an angle of 120° with each other
Two axial P–Cl bonds make an angle of 180° with each other
Axial P–Cl bonds are longer than equatorial P–Cl bonds
why: PCl₅ is trigonal bipyramidal with 120° equatorial angles, 180° axial angle and longer axial bonds. Because of the weaker axial bonds it is highly reactive, so the claim that it is non-reactive is incorrect.

q: The most suitable reagent for the conversion of H₃C–C≡C–CH₃ to cis-2-butene is :
why: Partial hydrogenation with a poisoned catalyst (Lindlar's type: H₂, Pd/C, quinoline) gives the cis alkene. Na/liquid NH₃ gives the trans alkene, and Hg²⁺/H⁺ hydrates the alkyne to a ketone.

q: For the cell reaction 2Fe³⁺(aq) + 2I⁻(aq) → 2Fe²⁺(aq) + I₂(aq), E°cell = 0.24 V at 298 K. The standard Gibbs energy (ΔrG°) of the cell reaction is : [Given that Faraday constant F = 96500 C mol⁻¹]
why: n = 2 electrons. ΔG° = −nFE° = −2 × 96500 × 0.24 = −46320 J mol⁻¹ = −46.32 kJ mol⁻¹.

q: Which of the following is not an attribute of a population ?
why: Sex ratio, natality and mortality are population attributes. Species interaction occurs between different populations, so it is not an attribute of a single population.

q: The process of growth is maximum during :
why: In the sigmoid growth curve, the exponential (log) phase shows the maximum rate of growth.

q: The roots that originate from the base of the stem are :
why: In monocots the primary root is short-lived and is replaced by fibrous roots that arise from the base of the stem.

q: Match the following diseases with the causative organism and select the correct option. Column - I: (a) Typhoid; (b) Pneumonia; (c) Filariasis; (d) Malaria. Column - II: (i) Wuchereria; (ii) Plasmodium; (iii) Salmonella; (iv) Haemophilus.
why: Typhoid is caused by Salmonella, pneumonia by Haemophilus, filariasis by Wuchereria and malaria by Plasmodium.

q: In which of the following techniques, the embryos are transferred to assist those females who cannot conceive ?
why: ZIFT (zygote or early embryo up to 8 blastomeres into the fallopian tube) and IUT (embryo with more than 8 blastomeres into the uterus) transfer embryos. GIFT transfers gametes and ICSI injects a sperm into an ovum.

q: Identify the wrong statement with reference to the gene 'I' that controls ABO blood groups.
opts: A person will have only two of the three alleles.
When IA and IB are present together, they express same type of sugar.
Allele 'i' does not produce any sugar.
why: IA and IB are codominant: when together they each express their own sugar, so both types of sugar are produced (AB blood group). Hence statement 3 is wrong.

q: Choose the correct pair from the following :
opts: Ligases - Join the two DNA molecules
Polymerases - Break the DNA into fragments
Nucleases - Separate the two strands of DNA
Exonucleases - Make cuts at specific positions within DNA
why: DNA ligases join DNA fragments. Nucleases cut DNA (exonucleases remove nucleotides from the ends, endonucleases cut within), and polymerases synthesise DNA.

q: Select the correct match.
opts: Sickle cell anaemia - Autosomal recessive trait, chromosome-11
why: Sickle cell anaemia is an autosomal recessive disorder caused by a mutation on chromosome 11. Haemophilia is X linked, phenylketonuria is autosomal recessive and thalassemia is autosomal.

q: Match the following columns and select the correct option. Column - I: (a) Gregarious, polyphagous pest; (b) Adult with radial symmetry and larva with bilateral symmetry; (c) Book lungs; (d) Bioluminescence. Column - II: (i) Asterias; (ii) Scorpion; (iii) Ctenoplana; (iv) Locusta.
why: Locusta is a gregarious polyphagous pest, Asterias has a radial adult and bilateral larva, scorpions have book lungs and Ctenoplana (ctenophore) shows bioluminescence.

q: The infectious stage of Plasmodium that enters the human body is :
why: Plasmodium enters the human body as sporozoites through the bite of an infected female Anopheles mosquito.

q: Identify the substances having glycosidic bond and peptide bond, respectively in their structure :
why: Inulin is a polysaccharide (glycosidic bonds) and insulin is a protein (peptide bonds). Cholesterol, glycerol and lecithin are lipids.

q: The plant parts which consist of two generations - one within the other : (a) Pollen grains inside the anther; (b) Germinated pollen grain with two male gametes; (c) Seed inside the fruit; (d) Embryo sac inside the ovule
why: Pollen grains (gametophyte) inside the anther and embryo sac (gametophyte) inside the ovule are each a gametophyte within a sporophyte. A germinated pollen grain alone is only gametophyte, and seed inside fruit is sporophyte within sporophyte.

q: The product(s) of reaction catalyzed by nitrogenase in root nodules of leguminous plants is/are :
why: Nitrogenase catalyses N₂ + 8e⁻ + 8H⁺ + 16 ATP → 2NH₃ + H₂ + 16 ADP + 16 Pi, giving ammonia and hydrogen.

q: Identify the correct statement with regard to G₁ phase (Gap 1) of interphase.
opts: DNA synthesis or replication takes place.
Reorganisation of all cell components takes place.
Cell is metabolically active, grows but does not replicate its DNA.
why: In G₁ the cell is metabolically active and grows continuously but does not replicate DNA; replication occurs in the S phase.

q: Cuboidal epithelium with brush border of microvilli is found in :
why: The proximal convoluted tubule is lined by simple cuboidal brush border epithelium that increases the surface area for reabsorption.

q: Which of the following statements about inclusion bodies is incorrect ?
opts: They are not bound by any membrane.
These are involved in ingestion of food particles.
They lie free in the cytoplasm.
These represent reserve material in cytoplasm.
why: Inclusion bodies are membraneless reserve materials (phosphate granules, cyanophycean granules, glycogen granules) lying free in the cytoplasm; they do not ingest food particles.

q: Which is the important site of formation of glycoproteins and glycolipids in eukaryotic cells ?
why: Golgi bodies receive proteins and lipids from the ER and modify them, forming glycoproteins and glycolipids.

q: In gel electrophoresis, separated DNA fragments can be visualized with the help of :
why: DNA bands are stained with ethidium bromide and seen as orange-coloured bands under UV light.

q: Identify the wrong statement with reference to transport of oxygen.
opts: Binding of oxygen with haemoglobin is mainly related to partial pressure of O₂.
Partial pressure of CO₂ can interfere with O₂ binding with haemoglobin.
Higher H⁺ conc. in alveoli favours the formation of oxyhaemoglobin.
Low pCO₂ in alveoli favours the formation of oxyhaemoglobin.
why: In alveoli there is high pO₂, low pCO₂, lower H⁺ concentration and lower temperature, which favour oxyhaemoglobin formation. A higher H⁺ concentration would shift the curve right and favour dissociation.

q: Ray florets have :
why: In sunflower (Asteraceae) ray florets are pistillate and have an inferior ovary.

q: The specific palindromic sequence which is recognized by EcoRI is :
why: EcoRI recognises 5'-GAATTC-3' (complementary strand 3'-CTTAAG-5'), which reads the same in the 5'→3' direction on both strands. GGATCC is BamHI.

q: Which of the following is put into Anaerobic sludge digester for further sewage treatment ?
why: After secondary treatment, a small part of the activated sludge is returned to the aeration tank and the rest is pumped into anaerobic sludge digesters.

q: Select the correct events that occur during inspiration. (a) Contraction of diaphragm; (b) Contraction of external inter-costal muscles; (c) Pulmonary volume decreases; (d) Intra pulmonary pressure increases
why: During inspiration the diaphragm and external intercostal muscles contract, increasing pulmonary volume and decreasing intrapulmonary pressure so air enters.

q: If the head of cockroach is removed, it may live for few days because :
opts: the supra-oesophageal ganglia of the cockroach are situated in ventral part of abdomen.
the cockroach does not have nervous system.
the head holds a small proportion of a nervous system while the rest is situated along the ventral part of its body.
the head holds a 1/3rd of a nervous system while the rest is situated along the dorsal part of its body.
why: The cockroach nervous system is mostly a ventral nerve cord with segmental ganglia; the head ganglia are only a small part, so the body survives for some days.

q: Which of the following statements are true for the phylum-Chordata ? (a) In Urochordata notochord extends from head to tail and it is present throughout their life. (b) In Vertebrata notochord is present during the embryonic period only. (c) Central nervous system is dorsal and hollow. (d) Chordata is divided into 3 subphyla : Hemichordata, Tunicata and Cephalochordata.
why: In Urochordata the notochord is present only in the larval tail, so (a) is false. Subphyla are Urochordata, Cephalochordata and Vertebrata, so (d) is false. (b) and (c) are true.

q: Match the organism with its use in biotechnology. (a) Bacillus thuringiensis; (b) Thermus aquaticus; (c) Agrobacterium tumefaciens; (d) Salmonella typhimurium. (i) Cloning vector; (ii) Construction of first rDNA molecule; (iii) DNA polymerase; (iv) Cry proteins. Select the correct option from the following : (a) (b) (c) (d)
why: B. thuringiensis gives Cry proteins, Thermus aquaticus gives Taq DNA polymerase, Agrobacterium is a cloning vector, and Salmonella typhimurium plasmid was used to make the first rDNA molecule.

q: Match the following concerning essential elements and their functions in plants : (a) Iron; (b) Zinc; (c) Boron; (d) Manganese. (i) Photolysis of water; (ii) Pollen germination; (iii) Required for chlorophyll biosynthesis; (iv) IAA biosynthesis. Select the correct option : (a) (b) (c) (d)
why: Iron is needed for chlorophyll biosynthesis, zinc for IAA synthesis, boron for pollen germination and manganese for photolysis of water.

q: Identify the incorrect statement.
opts: Heart wood does not conduct water but gives mechanical support.
Sapwood is involved in conduction of water and minerals from root to leaf.
Sapwood is the innermost secondary xylem and is lighter in colour.
Due to deposition of tannins, resins, oils etc., heart wood is dark in colour.
why: Heartwood is the innermost, dark secondary xylem; sapwood is the outer, lighter-coloured xylem that conducts water. So statement 3 is incorrect.

q: Match the following : (a) Inhibitor of catalytic activity; (b) Possess peptide bonds; (c) Cell wall material in fungi; (d) Secondary metabolite. (i) Ricin; (ii) Malonate; (iii) Chitin; (iv) Collagen. Choose the correct option from the following : (a) (b) (c) (d)
why: Malonate is a competitive inhibitor of succinic dehydrogenase, collagen is a protein with peptide bonds, chitin forms fungal cell walls and ricin is a secondary metabolite.

q: Meiotic division of the secondary oocyte is completed :
opts: At the time of fusion of a sperm with an ovum
why: The secondary oocyte is arrested at metaphase II; meiosis II is completed only when a sperm penetrates it, forming the ovum and second polar body at the time of sperm-ovum fusion.

q: According to Robert May, the global species diversity is about :
why: Robert May estimated global species diversity at about 7 million (IUCN count is about 1.5 million described species).

q: The first phase of translation is :
why: Translation begins with activation of amino acids and their attachment to tRNA (aminoacylation) in the presence of ATP.

q: Which of the following regions of the globe exhibits highest species diversity ?
why: The Amazon rainforest of South America has the highest biodiversity on earth.

q: Which of the following statements is not correct ?
opts: In man insulin is synthesised as a proinsulin.
The proinsulin has an extra peptide called C-peptide.
The functional insulin has A and B chains linked together by hydrogen bonds.
Genetically engineered insulin is produced in E-Coli.
why: The A and B chains of functional insulin are linked by disulphide bonds, not hydrogen bonds.

q: The transverse section of a plant shows following anatomical features : (a) Large number of scattered vascular bundles surrounded by bundle sheath. (b) Large conspicuous parenchymatous ground tissue. (c) Vascular bundles conjoint and closed. (d) Phloem parenchyma absent. Identify the category of plant and its part :
why: Scattered, conjoint, closed vascular bundles with sheath, undifferentiated ground tissue and no phloem parenchyma are features of a monocot stem.

q: Match the following columns and select the correct option. Column - I: (a) 6 - 15 pairs of gill slits; (b) Heterocercal caudal fin; (c) Air Bladder; (d) Poison sting. Column - II: (i) Trygon; (ii) Cyclostomes; (iii) Chondrichthyes; (iv) Osteichthyes. (a) (b) (c) (d)
why: Cyclostomes have 6-15 pairs of gill slits, Chondrichthyes have a heterocercal tail, Osteichthyes have an air bladder and Trygon (sting ray) has a poison sting.

q: From his experiments, S.L. Miller produced amino acids by mixing the following in a closed flask :
opts: CH₄, H₂, NH₃ and water vapor at 800°C
CH₃, H₂, NH₄ and water vapor at 800°C
CH₄, H₂, NH₃ and water vapor at 600°C
CH₃, H₂, NH₃ and water vapor at 600°C
why: Miller used CH₄, H₂, NH₃ and water vapour at 800°C with electric discharge.

q: Embryological support for evolution was disapproved by :
why: Ernst Haeckel's recapitulation theory was disproved by Karl Ernst von Baer, who noted that embryos never pass through the adult stages of other animals.

q: The process responsible for facilitating loss of water in liquid form from the tip of grass blades at night and in early morning is :
why: Root pressure forces water out as droplets through hydathodes at leaf tips (guttation) when transpiration is low.

q: Secondary metabolites such as nicotine, strychnine and caffeine are produced by plants for their :
why: These alkaloids are secondary metabolites with no direct role in growth; they protect plants against herbivores and pathogens (defence).

q: The oxygenation activity of RuBisCo enzyme in photorespiration leads to :
opts: 1 molecule of 4-C compound and 1 molecule of 2-C compound
why: In oxygenation RuBP combines with O₂ to give one molecule of 3-C PGA and one molecule of 2-C phosphoglycolate, so of the options the one 3-C compound is the answer.

q: Bt cotton variety that was developed by the introduction of toxin gene of Bacillus thuringiensis (Bt) is resistant to :
why: The Bt toxin (Cry protein) kills specific insect larvae such as bollworms, giving resistance to insect pests.

q: Which of the following refer to correct example(s) of organisms which have evolved due to changes in environment brought about by anthropogenic action ? (a) Darwin's Finches of Galapagos islands. (b) Herbicide resistant weeds. (c) Drug resistant eukaryotes. (d) Man-created breeds of domesticated animals like dogs.
why: Herbicide-resistant weeds, drug-resistant eukaryotes and man-created breeds are due to human activity; Darwin's finches evolved naturally.

q: Identify the wrong statement with reference to immunity.
opts: When exposed to antigen (living or dead) antibodies are produced in the host's body. It is called "Active immunity".
When ready-made antibodies are directly given, it is called "Passive immunity".
Active immunity is quick and gives full response.
Foetus receives some antibodies from mother, it is an example for passive immunity.
why: Active immunity is slow and takes time to give a full response; passive immunity gives ready-made antibodies quickly.

topic: Strategies for enhancement in food production
q: By which method was a new breed 'Hisardale' of sheep formed by using Bikaneri ewes and Marino rams ?
why: Hisardale was developed by crossing superior males of one breed (Marino) with superior females of another (Bikaneri), which is cross breeding.

q: Identify the correct statement with reference to human digestive system.
opts: Serosa is the innermost layer of the alimentary canal.
Ileum is a highly coiled part.
why: The ileum is the highly coiled part of the small intestine and opens into the large intestine; serosa is the outermost layer and the appendix arises from the caecum.

q: Match the following columns and select the correct option. Column - I: (a) Clostridium butylicum; (b) Trichoderma polysporum; (c) Monascus purpureus; (d) Aspergillus niger. Column - II: (i) Cyclosporin-A; (ii) Butyric Acid; (iii) Citric Acid; (iv) Blood cholesterol lowering agent. (a) (b) (c) (d)
why: Clostridium butylicum gives butyric acid, Trichoderma polysporum gives cyclosporin-A, Monascus purpureus gives statins (cholesterol lowering) and Aspergillus niger gives citric acid.

q: Presence of which of the following conditions in urine are indicative of Diabetes Mellitus ?
why: In diabetes mellitus glucose (glycosuria) and ketone bodies (ketonuria) appear in the urine.

q: Floridean starch has structure similar to :
why: Floridean starch, the reserve food of red algae, is similar to amylopectin and glycogen in structure.

q: Select the option including all sexually transmitted diseases.
why: Gonorrhoea, syphilis and genital herpes are STDs; malaria, filaria and cancer are not.

q: Match the following with respect to meiosis : (a) Zygotene; (b) Pachytene; (c) Diplotene; (d) Diakinesis. (i) Terminalization; (ii) Chiasmata; (iii) Crossing over; (iv) Synapsis. Select the correct option from the following : (a) (b) (c) (d)
why: Synapsis occurs in zygotene, crossing over in pachytene, chiasmata are seen in diplotene and terminalization occurs in diakinesis.

q: Which of the following pairs is of unicellular algae ?
why: Chlorella and Spirulina are unicellular (Spirulina is used as single cell protein); Laminaria, Sargassum, Gelidium and Gracilaria are multicellular, Volvox is colonial.

q: Which of the following hormone levels will cause release of ovum (ovulation) from the graffian follicle ?
why: High estrogen from the mature follicle exerts positive feedback and triggers the LH surge that causes ovulation; low LH or FSH cannot do this and progesterone is high only after ovulation.

q: Match the following columns and select the correct option. Column - I: (a) Bt cotton; (b) Adenosine deaminase deficiency; (c) RNAi; (d) PCR. Column - II: (i) Gene therapy; (ii) Cellular defence; (iii) Detection of HIV infection; (iv) Bacillus thuringiensis. (a) (b) (c) (d)
why: Bt cotton uses Bacillus thuringiensis gene, ADA deficiency is treated by gene therapy, RNAi is a cellular defence against viral RNA, and PCR is used to detect HIV.

q: Montreal protocol was signed in 1987 for control of :
opts: Transport of Genetically modified organisms from one country to another
why: The Montreal Protocol (1987) was an international treaty to control emission of ozone depleting substances such as CFCs.

q: Which of the following is correct about viroids ?
opts: They have RNA with protein coat.
They have free RNA without protein coat.
They have DNA with protein coat.
They have free DNA without protein coat.
why: Viroids (discovered by T.O. Diener) are infectious agents consisting of free low molecular weight RNA without a protein coat.

q: The ovary is half inferior in :
why: Plum (like rose, peach) has perigynous flowers with a half inferior ovary. Brinjal and mustard have superior ovary; sunflower has inferior ovary.

q: The enzyme enterokinase helps in conversion of :
why: Enterokinase secreted by intestinal mucosa activates inactive trypsinogen into active trypsin.

q:
Match the trophic levels with their correct species examples in grassland ecosystem.
List I: (a) Fourth trophic level; (b) Second trophic level; (c) First trophic level; (d) Third trophic level  List II: (i) Crow; (ii) Vulture; (iii) Rabbit; (iv) Grass
Select the correct option :
why: Grass is the producer (first level), rabbit the primary consumer (second), crow the secondary consumer (third) and vulture the tertiary consumer (fourth level).

q: How many true breeding pea plant varieties did Mendel select as pairs, which were similar except in one character with contrasting traits ?
why: Mendel selected 14 true-breeding pea varieties, i.e. 7 pairs, each pair differing in one character with contrasting traits.

q:
Match the following columns and select the correct option.
Column I: (a) Organ of Corti; (b) Cochlea; (c) Eustachian tube; (d) Stapes  Column II: (i) Connects middle ear and pharynx; (ii) Coiled part of the labyrinth; (iii) Attached to the oval window; (iv) Located on the basilar membrane
why: Organ of Corti lies on the basilar membrane; cochlea is the coiled part of the labyrinth; Eustachian tube connects middle ear to pharynx; stapes is attached to the oval window.

q: In water hyacinth and water lily, pollination takes place by :
why: Most aquatic plants such as water hyacinth and water lily emerge above water and are pollinated by insects or wind, not by water.

q: Name the plant growth regulator which upon spraying on sugarcane crop, increases the length of stem, thus increasing the yield of sugarcane crop.
why: Gibberellins cause elongation of internodes; spraying sugarcane with gibberellin increases stem length and yield.

q: In light reaction, plastoquinone facilitates the transfer of electrons from :
why: Electrons from PS-II are passed to plastoquinone, which transfers them to the Cytb₆f complex, then plastocyanin carries them to PS-I.

q: Which of the following is not an inhibitory substance governing seed dormancy ?
why: Abscisic acid, phenolic acids and para-ascorbic acid inhibit germination, whereas gibberellic acid promotes germination and breaks dormancy.

q: Name the enzyme that facilitates opening of DNA helix during transcription.
why: During transcription RNA polymerase itself opens the DNA helix locally; no separate helicase is used as in replication.

q: Which of the following would help in prevention of diuresis ?
opts: More water reabsorption due to undersecretion of ADH
Reabsorption of Na⁺ and water from renal tubules due to aldosterone
Decrease in secretion of renin by JG cells
why: Aldosterone increases reabsorption of Na⁺ and water from distal tubules, reducing urine volume. ADH undersecretion, or less renin (so less aldosterone), would cause diuresis.

q: In relation to Gross primary productivity and Net primary productivity of an ecosystem, which one of the following statements is correct ?
opts: Gross primary productivity is always less than net primary productivity.
Gross primary productivity is always more than net primary productivity.
Gross primary productivity and Net primary productivity are one and same.
There is no relationship between Gross primary productivity and Net primary productivity.
why: NPP = GPP − respiratory losses (R), so GPP is always greater than NPP.

q:
Match the following columns and select the correct option.
Column I: (a) Placenta; (b) Zona pellucida; (c) Bulbo-urethral glands; (d) Leydig cells  Column II: (i) Androgens; (ii) Human Chorionic Gonadotropin (hCG); (iii) Layer of the ovum; (iv) Lubrication of the Penis
why: Placenta secretes hCG; zona pellucida is a layer around the ovum; bulbo-urethral glands lubricate the penis; Leydig cells secrete androgens.

q: Strobili or cones are found in :
why: Equisetum (a pteridophyte) bears sporophylls aggregated into strobili or cones. Salvinia bears sporocarps, Pteris sori, and Marchantia is a bryophyte.

q: Some dividing cells exit the cell cycle and enter vegetative inactive stage. This is called quiescent stage (G₀). This process occurs at the end of :
why: Cells that do not divide further exit the cycle from the G₁ phase into the quiescent G₀ stage.

q: Flippers of Penguins and Dolphins are examples of :
why: Flippers of penguins and dolphins are analogous organs that evolved independently for swimming, an example of convergent evolution.

q: If the distance between two consecutive base pairs is 0.34 nm and the total number of base pairs of a DNA double helix in a typical mammalian cell is 6.6 × 10⁹ bp, then the length of the DNA is approximately :
why: Length = 6.6 × 10⁹ × 0.34 × 10⁻⁹ m = 2.244 m, approximately 2.2 m.

q: The QRS complex in a standard ECG represents :
why: The QRS complex represents ventricular depolarisation (onset of ventricular contraction); P wave is atrial depolarisation and T wave ventricular repolarisation.

q:
Match the following columns and select the correct option.
Column I: (a) Eosinophils; (b) Basophils; (c) Neutrophils; (d) Lymphocytes  Column II: (i) Immune response; (ii) Phagocytosis; (iii) Release histaminase, destructive enzymes; (iv) Release granules containing histamine
why: Eosinophils release histaminase and destructive enzymes; basophils release histamine granules; neutrophils are phagocytic; lymphocytes mediate immune response.

q: Which of the following statements is correct ?
opts: Adenine pairs with thymine through two H-bonds.
Adenine pairs with thymine through one H-bond.
Adenine pairs with thymine through three H-bonds.
Adenine does not pair with thymine.
why: In DNA, adenine pairs with thymine by two hydrogen bonds, while guanine pairs with cytosine by three.

q: The sequence that controls the copy number of the linked DNA in the vector, is termed :
why: The origin of replication (ori) is the sequence from which replication starts and it controls the copy number of the linked DNA.

q: Identify the basic amino acid from the following.
why: Lysine has an extra amino group in its side chain, making it a basic amino acid; glutamic acid is acidic, tyrosine and valine are neutral.

q:
Match the following columns and select the correct option.
Column I: (a) Pituitary gland; (b) Thyroid gland; (c) Adrenal gland; (d) Pancreas  Column II: (i) Grave's disease; (ii) Diabetes mellitus; (iii) Diabetes insipidus; (iv) Addison's disease
why: ADH deficiency from pituitary gives diabetes insipidus; thyroid hyperfunction gives Grave's disease; adrenal cortex deficiency gives Addison's disease; insulin deficiency from pancreas gives diabetes mellitus.

q: Select the correct statement.
opts: Insulin acts on pancreatic cells and adipocytes.
why: Glucocorticoids such as cortisol stimulate gluconeogenesis. Glucagon causes hyperglycemia, insulin causes hypoglycemia and acts on hepatocytes and adipocytes.

q: Which one of the following is the most abundant protein in the animals ?
why: Collagen is the most abundant protein in the animal world (and RuBisCO in the biosphere).

q: Experimental verification of the chromosomal theory of inheritance was done by :
why: Sutton and Boveri proposed the chromosomal theory; Thomas Hunt Morgan and colleagues experimentally verified it using Drosophila.

q:
Match the following columns and select the correct option.
Column I: (a) Floating Ribs; (b) Acromion; (c) Scapula; (d) Glenoid cavity  Column II: (i) Located between second and seventh ribs; (ii) Head of the Humerus; (iii) Clavicle; (iv) Do not connect with the sternum
why: Floating ribs do not connect to the sternum; acromion articulates with the clavicle; scapula lies over the second to seventh ribs; glenoid cavity receives the head of the humerus.

q: The number of substrate level phosphorylations in one turn of citric acid cycle is :
why: Only the conversion of succinyl-CoA to succinate yields GTP (ATP) by substrate level phosphorylation, once per turn.

q: Dissolution of the synaptonemal complex occurs during :
why: Synaptonemal complex forms in zygotene, is complete at pachytene and dissolves during diplotene.

q: Bilaterally symmetrical and acoelomate animals are exemplified by :
why: Platyhelminthes are bilaterally symmetrical and acoelomate; Aschelminthes are pseudocoelomate, Annelida coelomate, and Ctenophora radially symmetrical.

q: The body of the ovule is fused within the funicle at :
why: The funicle (stalk) joins the body of the ovule at the hilum.

q: Goblet cells of alimentary canal are modified from :
why: Goblet cells, which secrete mucus, are unicellular glands modified from columnar epithelial cells lining the alimentary canal.

q: Snow-blindness in Antarctic region is due to :
opts: Freezing of fluids in the eye by low temperature
Inflammation of cornea due to high dose of UV-B radiation
High reflection of light from snow
Damage to retina caused by infra-red rays
why: Snow-blindness results from inflammation of the cornea caused by high doses of UV-B radiation (low ozone, reflection from snow).

q: Identify a molecule which does not exist.
why: In He₂ bond order = (2 − 2)/2 = 0, so it does not exist. Li₂ (bond order 1), C₂ (2) and O₂ (2) exist.

q: Find out the solubility of Ni(OH)₂ in 0.1 M NaOH. Given that the ionic product of Ni(OH)₂ is 2 × 10⁻¹⁵.

Identify the correct statements from the following :
(a) CO₂(g) is used as refrigerant for ice-cream and frozen food.
(b) The structure of C₆₀ contains twelve six carbon rings and twenty five carbon rings.
(c) ZSM-5, a type of zeolite, is used to convert alcohols into gasoline.
(d) CO is colorless and odourless gas.
why: (a) is wrong because solid CO₂ (dry ice), not the gas, is the refrigerant. (b) is wrong: C₆₀ has twenty six-membered and twelve five-membered rings. (c) and (d) are correct.

q:
Hydrolysis of sucrose is given by the following reaction.
Sucrose + H₂O ⇌ Glucose + Fructose
If the equilibrium constant (Kc) is 2 × 10¹³ at 300 K, the value of ΔrG⊖ at the same temperature will be :

Identify the incorrect match.
Name: (a) Unnilunium; (b) Unniltrium; (c) Unnilhexium; (d) Ununnunium IUPAC Official Name: (i) Mendelevium; (ii) Lawrencium; (iii) Seaborgium; (iv) Darmstadtium
why: Unnilunium = 101 Md, Unniltrium = 103 Lr, Unnilhexium = 106 Sg are correct. The name for Z = 111 (Unununium, close to the printed Ununnunium) corresponds to Roentgenium, not Darmstadtium (Z = 110, Ununnilium), so (d)-(iv) is incorrect.

q: An element has a body centered cubic (bcc) structure with a cell edge of 288 pm. The atomic radius is :
why: In bcc the body diagonal √3a = 4r, so r = (√3/4)a = (√3/4) × 288 pm.

q: Which of the following set of molecules will have zero dipole moment ?
opts: Boron trifluoride, hydrogen fluoride, carbon dioxide, 1,3-dichlorobenzene
Boron trifluoride, beryllium difluoride, carbon dioxide, 1,4-dichlorobenzene
why: BF₃ (trigonal planar), BeF₂ and CO₂ (linear) and 1,4-dichlorobenzene (symmetric) all have zero net dipole moment; NH₃, H₂O, HF, NF₃ and 1,3-dichlorobenzene are polar.

q: On electrolysis of dil. sulphuric acid using Platinum (Pt) electrode, the product obtained at anode will be :
why: With inert Pt electrodes and dilute H₂SO₄, water is oxidised at the anode (2H₂O → O₂ + 4H⁺ + 4e⁻), giving oxygen; hydrogen forms at the cathode.

q: Reaction between acetone and methylmagnesium chloride followed by hydrolysis will give :
why: Grignard reagent adds to a ketone to give a tertiary alcohol: (CH₃)₂CO + CH₃MgCl → (CH₃)₃C–OH (tert-butyl alcohol) after hydrolysis.

q: Which of the following oxoacid of sulphur has –O–O– linkage ?
why: Peroxodisulphuric acid (Marshall's acid), H₂S₂O₈, contains a peroxy –O–O– linkage between two sulphur atoms.

q: The calculated spin only magnetic moment of Cr²⁺ ion is :
why: Cr²⁺ is d⁴ with 4 unpaired electrons; μ = √[n(n+2)] = √24 ≈ 4.90 BM.

q: The correct option for free expansion of an ideal gas under adiabatic condition is :
why: Free expansion is against zero external pressure so w = 0; adiabatic so q = 0; hence ΔU = 0 and for an ideal gas ΔT = 0.

q: The freezing point depression constant (K_f) of benzene is 5.12 K kg mol⁻¹. The freezing point depression for the solution of molality 0.078 m containing a non-electrolyte solute in benzene is (rounded off upto two decimal places) :
The number of Faradays (F) required to produce 20 g of calcium from molten CaCl₂ (Atomic mass of Ca = 40 g mol⁻¹) is :
why: 20 g Ca = 0.5 mol. Ca²⁺ + 2e⁻ → Ca needs 2 F per mole, so 0.5 × 2 = 1 F.

q: Reaction between benzaldehyde and acetophenone in presence of dilute NaOH is known as :
why: Two different carbonyl compounds (benzaldehyde with no α-H and acetophenone with α-H) react in dilute base: this is a cross aldol (Claisen-Schmidt) condensation.

topic: Purification and characterisation of organic compounds
q: Paper chromatography is an example of :
why: In paper chromatography water held in the cellulose fibres is the stationary phase and the solvent the mobile phase; separation is by partition.

q: An increase in the concentration of the reactants of a reaction leads to change in :
why: More reactant concentration means more molecules per unit volume, so collisions per second increase. Activation energy, threshold energy and heat of reaction do not depend on concentration.

q: A mixture of N₂ and Ar gases in a cylinder contains 7 g of N₂ and 8 g of Ar. If the total pressure of the mixture of the gases in the cylinder is 27 bar, the partial pressure of N₂ is : [Use atomic masses (in g mol⁻¹) : N = 14, Ar = 40]
why: Moles of N₂ = 7/28 = 0.25; moles of Ar = 8/40 = 0.2. Mole fraction of N₂ = 0.25/0.45 = 5/9, so p(N₂) = 5/9 × 27 = 15 bar.

q: Identify the correct statement from the following :
opts: Wrought iron is impure iron with 4% carbon.
Blister copper has blistered appearance due to evolution of CO₂.
Vapour phase refining is carried out for Nickel by Van Arkel method.
Pig iron can be moulded into a variety of shapes.
why: Wrought iron has the least carbon (0.1-0.25%); blister copper's surface is due to SO₂ evolution; nickel is refined by the Mond process (Van Arkel is for Zr/Ti). Pig iron is cast (moulded) into various shapes.

q: A tertiary butyl carbocation is more stable than a secondary butyl carbocation because of which of the following ?
why: A tertiary carbocation has more α C-H bonds (9 versus 5-6), so hyperconjugation delocalises the positive charge more and stabilises it.

q: Which of the following is a cationic detergent ?
why: Cationic detergents are quaternary ammonium salts such as cetyltrimethylammonium bromide; the others are anionic.

q: Elimination reaction of 2-Bromo-pentane to form pent-2-ene is : (a) β-Elimination reaction (b) Follows Zaitsev rule (c) Dehydrohalogenation reaction (d) Dehydration reaction
why: Removal of H and Br from adjacent carbons is β-elimination (dehydrohalogenation) giving the more substituted alkene (Zaitsev). Dehydration means loss of water, so (d) is wrong.

q: The mixture which shows positive deviation from Raoult's law is :
why: Acetone breaks the hydrogen bonding of ethanol, so A-B interactions are weaker than A-A and B-B, giving positive deviation. Benzene+toluene and chloroethane+bromoethane are ideal; acetone+chloroform is negative.

q: Which of the following is a basic amino acid ?
why: Lysine has an extra amino group in its side chain (more NH₂ than COOH), so it is basic. Serine, alanine and tyrosine are neutral.

q: HCl was passed through a solution of CaCl₂, MgCl₂ and NaCl. Which of the following compound(s) crystallise(s) ?
why: Passing HCl raises the Cl⁻ concentration (common ion effect); NaCl is the least soluble of the three chlorides and crystallises, while CaCl₂ and MgCl₂ are very soluble.

q: Which of the following is a natural polymer ?
why: Natural rubber is cis-1,4-polyisoprene; the others are synthetic polymers/rubbers.

q: Which of the following is not correct about carbon monoxide ?
opts: It reduces oxygen carrying ability of blood.
The carboxyhaemoglobin (haemoglobin bound to CO) is less stable than oxyhaemoglobin.
It is produced due to incomplete combustion.
why: CO binds haemoglobin about 200-300 times more strongly than O₂, so carboxyhaemoglobin is more stable than oxyhaemoglobin; statement (3) is wrong.

q: Sucrose on hydrolysis gives :
why: Sucrose is formed from α-D-glucose and β-D-fructose joined through a glycosidic bond; hydrolysis returns these two.

q: The following metal ion activates many enzymes, participates in the oxidation of glucose to produce ATP and with Na, is responsible for the transmission of nerve signals.
why: Potassium ions activate many enzymes, take part in glucose oxidation, and with sodium maintain the nerve-signal gradient (Na⁺/K⁺ pump).

q: Which one of the followings has maximum number of atoms ?
opts: 1 g of Ag(s) [Atomic mass of Ag = 108]
1 g of Mg(s) [Atomic mass of Mg = 24]
1 g of O₂(g) [Atomic mass of O = 16]
1 g of Li(s) [Atomic mass of Li = 7]
why: Number of atoms ∝ moles of atoms = 1/atomic mass (times atomicity). 1/7 = 0.143 for Li is the largest (O₂ gives 2×1/32 = 0.0625).

q: The number of protons, neutrons and electrons in ¹⁷⁵₇₁Lu, respectively, are :
why: Protons = atomic number = 71; electrons = 71 for the neutral atom; neutrons = 175 - 71 = 104.

q: What is the change in oxidation number of carbon in the following reaction ? CH₄(g) + 4Cl₂(g) → CCl₄(l) + 4HCl(g)
why: In CH₄ carbon is -4 (H is +1); in CCl₄ carbon is +4 (Cl is -1). The change is -4 to +4.

q: Identify the incorrect statement.
opts: Cr²⁺(d⁴) is a stronger reducing agent than Fe²⁺(d⁶) in water.
The transition metals and their compounds are known for their catalytic activity due to their ability to adopt multiple oxidation states and to form complexes.
Interstitial compounds are those that are formed when small atoms like H, C or N are trapped inside the crystal lattices of metals.
The oxidation states of chromium in CrO₄²⁻ and Cr₂O₇²⁻ are not the same.
why: Chromium is +6 in both CrO₄²⁻ and Cr₂O₇²⁻, so statement (4) is incorrect. Cr²⁺ is indeed a stronger reductant than Fe²⁺ (Cr³⁺/Cr²⁺ E° = -0.41 V).

q: For the reaction, 2Cl(g) → Cl₂(g), the correct option is :
why: Bond formation releases energy (ΔH < 0) and two gas moles become one, so disorder falls (ΔS < 0).

q: Measuring Zeta potential is useful in determining which property of colloidal solution ?
why: Zeta potential is the potential difference across the fixed and diffuse layers of charge; a high value indicates strong repulsion and hence a stable colloid.

q: Urea reacts with water to form A which will decompose to form B. B when passed through Cu²⁺(aq), deep blue colour solution C is formed. What is the formula of C from the following ?
why: Urea + water gives ammonium carbonate (A), which decomposes to NH₃ (B). NH₃ with Cu²⁺ gives the deep blue complex [Cu(NH₃)₄]²⁺.

q: Match the following and identify the correct option. List I: (a) CO(g) + H₂(g); (b) Temporary hardness of water; (c) B₂H₆; (d) H₂O₂  List II: (i) Mg(HCO₃)₂ + Ca(HCO₃)₂; (ii) An electron deficient hydride; (iii) Synthesis gas; (iv) Non-planar structure
why: CO + H₂ is synthesis gas; temporary hardness is due to Mg and Ca bicarbonates; B₂H₆ is an electron-deficient hydride; H₂O₂ has a non-planar open-book structure.

topic: Classification of elements nature of oxides
q: Match the following. Oxide: (a) CO, (b) BaO, (c) Al₂O₃, (d) Cl₂O₇  Nature: (i) Basic, (ii) Neutral, (iii) Acidic, (iv) Amphoteric. Which of the following is correct option ?
why: CO is neutral, BaO is basic, Al₂O₃ is amphoteric and Cl₂O₇ is acidic.

q: The rate constant for a first order reaction is 4.606 × 10⁻³ s⁻¹. The time required to reduce 2.0 g of the reactant to 0.2 g is :
Which of the following alkane cannot be made in good yield by Wurtz reaction ?
why: Wurtz reaction gives good yield only for symmetrical alkanes (R-R from one halide). n-Heptane would need two different halides (propyl and butyl), giving a mixture; the others come from a single halide.

q: For which one of the following, Bohr model is not valid ?
why: Bohr's model works only for single-electron species (H, He⁺, deuterium). Ne⁺ has nine electrons.

q: The ratio of contributions made by the electric field and magnetic field components to the intensity of an electromagnetic wave is : (c = speed of electromagnetic waves)
why: Energy densities are equal: ½ε₀E² = B²/(2μ₀) (since E = cB), so their contributions to intensity are in the ratio 1 : 1.

q: The Brewsters angle i_b for an interface should be :
why: tan i_b = μ, and μ > 1 for a denser medium, so i_b > 45°; it is always less than 90°.

q: A cylinder contains hydrogen gas at pressure of 249 kPa and temperature 27°C. Its density is : (R = 8.3 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹)

A ray is incident at an angle of incidence i on one surface of a small angle prism (with angle of prism A) and emerges normally from the opposite surface. If the refractive index of the material of the prism is μ, then the angle of incidence is nearly equal to :
why: Normal emergence gives r₂ = 0, so r₁ = A. Snell's law for small angles: i = μr₁ = μA.

q: Two cylinders A and B of equal capacity are connected to each other via a stop cock. A contains an ideal gas at standard temperature and pressure. B is completely evacuated. The entire system is thermally insulated. The stop cock is suddenly opened. The process is :
why: The system is thermally insulated so no heat is exchanged (Q = 0): the free expansion is adiabatic.

q: The energy equivalent of 0.5 g of a substance is :
A body weighs 72 N on the surface of the earth. What is the gravitational force on it, at a height equal to half the radius of the earth ?
why: g' = g/(1 + h/R)² = g/(1.5)² = 4g/9, so the weight is 72 × 4/9 = 32 N.

q: The solids which have the negative temperature coefficient of resistance are :
why: In metals resistance rises with temperature; in insulators and semiconductors, more charge carriers are freed on heating, so resistance falls (negative coefficient).

q: The phase difference between displacement and acceleration of a particle in a simple harmonic motion is :
why: In SHM a = -ω²x, so acceleration is opposite to displacement: phase difference π rad.

q: A screw gauge has least count of 0.01 mm and there are 50 divisions in its circular scale. The pitch of the screw gauge is :
why: Least count = pitch / number of divisions, so pitch = 0.01 × 50 = 0.5 mm.

q: In a guitar, two strings A and B made of same material are slightly out of tune and produce beats of frequency 6 Hz. When tension in B is slightly decreased, the beat frequency increases to 7 Hz. If the frequency of A is 530 Hz, the original frequency of B will be :
why: B is 524 or 536 Hz. Reducing tension lowers B's frequency; the beats increase only if B moves further from A, i.e. B = 524 Hz (becomes 523, beats 7).

topic: System of particles centre of mass
q: Two particles of mass 5 kg and 10 kg respectively are attached to the two ends of a rigid rod of length 1 m with negligible mass. The centre of mass of the system from the 5 kg particle is nearly at a distance of :
why: x = (5×0 + 10×100)/(5+10) = 66.7 cm ≈ 67 cm from the 5 kg particle.

q: Find the torque about the origin when a force of 3ĵ N acts on a particle whose position vector is 2k̂ m.
Light with an average flux of 20 W/cm² falls on a non-reflecting surface at normal incidence having surface area 20 cm². The energy received by the surface during time span of 1 minute is :
why: Energy = flux × area × time = 20 × 20 × 60 = 24000 J = 24 × 10³ J.

q: A spherical conductor of radius 10 cm has a charge of 3.2 × 10⁻⁷ C distributed uniformly. What is the magnitude of electric field at a point 15 cm from the centre of the sphere ? (1/4πε₀ = 9 × 10⁹ N m²/C²)
In a certain region of space with volume 0.2 m³, the electric potential is found to be 5 V throughout. The magnitude of electric field in this region is :
why: E = -dV/dr; the potential is constant, so the field is zero.

q: The increase in the width of the depletion region in a p-n junction diode is due to :
opts: both forward bias and reverse bias
why: Reverse bias pulls majority carriers away from the junction, widening the depletion region; forward bias narrows it.

q: A 40 μF capacitor is connected to a 200 V, 50 Hz ac supply. The rms value of the current in the circuit, is nearly :
The mean free path for a gas, with molecular diameter d and number density n can be expressed as :
why: Mean free path λ = 1/(√2 π n d²).

q: For transistor action, which of the following statements is correct ?
opts: Base, emitter and collector regions should have same doping concentrations.
Base, emitter and collector regions should have same size.
Both emitter junction as well as the collector junction are forward biased.
The base region must be very thin and lightly doped.
why: For transistor action the base is thin and lightly doped so that most carriers from the emitter reach the collector; the emitter junction is forward and collector junction reverse biased, and the regions differ in doping and size.

q: Light of frequency 1.5 times the threshold frequency is incident on a photosensitive material. What will be the photoelectric current if the frequency is halved and intensity is doubled ?
why: After halving, the frequency is 0.75 of the threshold frequency, below threshold, so no photoelectrons are emitted regardless of intensity: current is zero.

q: When a uranium isotope ²³⁵₉₂U is bombarded with a neutron, it generates ⁸⁹₃₆Kr, three neutrons and :
why: Mass number: 235 + 1 = 89 + 3 + A gives A = 144; charge: 92 = 36 + Z gives Z = 56, which is ¹⁴⁴₅₆Ba.

q: The energy required to break one bond in DNA is 10⁻²⁰ J. This value in eV is nearly :
A wire of length L, area of cross section A is hanging from a fixed support. The length of the wire changes to L₁ when mass M is suspended from its free end. The expression for Young's modulus is :
why: Y = stress/strain = (Mg/A)/((L₁ - L)/L) = MgL/(A(L₁ - L)).

q: The average thermal energy for a mono-atomic gas is : (k_B is Boltzmann constant and T, absolute temperature)
why: A monatomic molecule has 3 translational degrees of freedom, each contributing ½k_BT, so the average energy is 3/2 k_BT.

q: In Young's double slit experiment, if the separation between coherent sources is halved and the distance of the screen from the coherent sources is doubled, then the fringe width becomes :
why: Fringe width β = λD/d. With d → d/2 and D → 2D, β' = λ(2D)/(d/2) = 4λD/d = 4β.

q: The capacitance of a parallel plate capacitor with air as medium is 6 μF. With the introduction of a dielectric medium, the capacitance becomes 30 μF. The permittivity of the medium is : (ε₀ = 8.85 × 10⁻¹² C² N⁻¹ m⁻²)
why: Dielectric constant K = 30/6 = 5, so permittivity ε = Kε₀ = 5 × 8.85 × 10⁻¹² = 44.25 × 10⁻¹² ≈ 0.44 × 10⁻¹⁰ C² N⁻¹ m⁻².

q: Dimensions of stress are :
why: Stress = force/area = [MLT⁻²]/[L²] = [ML⁻¹T⁻²].

q: Assume that light of wavelength 600 nm is coming from a star. The limit of resolution of telescope whose objective has a diameter of 2 m is :
why: Limit of resolution Δθ = 1.22λ/D = 1.22 × 600 × 10⁻⁹ / 2 = 3.66 × 10⁻⁷ rad.

q: A series LCR circuit is connected to an ac voltage source. When L is removed from the circuit, the phase difference between current and voltage is π/3. If instead C is removed from the circuit, the phase difference is again π/3 between current and voltage. The power factor of the circuit is :
why: Without L: tan(π/3) = X_C/R; without C: tan(π/3) = X_L/R. So X_L = X_C, the circuit is at resonance, the impedance equals R and the power factor is 1.

q: A short electric dipole has a dipole moment of 16 × 10⁻⁹ C m. The electric potential due to the dipole at a point at a distance of 0.6 m from the centre of the dipole, situated on a line making an angle of 60° with the dipole axis is : (1/4πε₀ = 9 × 10⁹ N m²/C²)
An iron rod of susceptibility 599 is subjected to a magnetising field of 1200 A m⁻¹. The permeability of the material of the rod is : (μ₀ = 4π × 10⁻⁷ T m A⁻¹)
A long solenoid of 50 cm length having 100 turns carries a current of 2.5 A. The magnetic field at the centre of the solenoid is : (μ₀ = 4π × 10⁻⁷ T m A⁻¹)
A charged particle having drift velocity of 7.5 × 10⁻⁴ m s⁻¹ in an electric field of 3 × 10⁻¹⁰ V m⁻¹, has a mobility in m² V⁻¹ s⁻¹ of :
why: Mobility μ = v_d/E = 7.5 × 10⁻⁴ / 3 × 10⁻¹⁰ = 2.5 × 10⁶ m² V⁻¹ s⁻¹.

q: The quantities of heat required to raise the temperature of two solid copper spheres of radii r₁ and r₂ (r₁ = 1.5 r₂) through 1 K are in the ratio :
why: Heat Q = mcΔT, and mass ∝ volume ∝ r³. So Q₁/Q₂ = (r₁/r₂)³ = 1.5³ = 27/8.

q: An electron is accelerated from rest through a potential difference of V volt. If the de Broglie wavelength of the electron is 1.227 × 10⁻² nm, the potential difference is :
why: For an electron λ = 1.227/√V nm. So √V = 1.227 / 1.227 × 10⁻² = 100, giving V = 10⁴ V.

q: Taking into account of the significant figures, what is the value of 9.99 m − 0.0099 m ?
why: The difference is 9.9801 m. In subtraction the result keeps the fewest decimal places of the inputs (9.99 has two), so it is 9.98 m.

q: A ball is thrown vertically downward with a velocity of 20 m/s from the top of a tower. It hits the ground after some time with a velocity of 80 m/s. The height of the tower is : (g = 10 m/s²)

A capillary tube of radius r is immersed in water and water rises in it to a height h. The mass of the water in the capillary is 5 g. Another capillary tube of radius 2r is immersed in water. The mass of water that will rise in this tube is :
why: Height h ∝ 1/r, and mass = πr²hρ ∝ r²·(1/r) = r. Doubling the radius doubles the mass to 10 g.

q: A resistance wire connected in the left gap of a metre bridge balances a 10 Ω resistance in the right gap at a point which divides the bridge wire in the ratio 3 : 2. If the length of the resistance wire is 1.5 m, then the length of 1 Ω of the resistance wire is :
why: X/10 = 3/2 so X = 15 Ω for 1.5 m of wire. Hence 1 Ω corresponds to 1.5/15 = 0.1 m = 1.0 × 10⁻¹ m.

q: A small block slides down on a smooth inclined plane, starting from rest at time t = 0. Let Sₙ be the distance travelled by the block in the interval t = n – 1 to t = n. Then, the ratio Sₙ/Sₙ₊₁ is :
why: Distance in the nth second from rest is Sₙ = (a/2)(2n – 1). Hence Sₙ/Sₙ₊₁ = (2n – 1)/(2n + 1).

q: A spring is stretched by 5 cm by a force 10 N. The time period of the oscillations when a mass of 2 kg is suspended by it is :

A convex lens 'A' of focal length 20 cm and a concave lens 'B' of focal length 5 cm are kept along the same axis with a distance 'd' between them. If a parallel beam of light falling on 'A' leaves 'B' as a parallel beam, then the distance 'd' in cm will be :
why: For a parallel beam to emerge parallel (afocal combination) the lenses must share a focus: d = f₁ + f₂ = 20 + (–5) = 15 cm.

q: Column - I gives certain physical terms associated with flow of current through a metallic conductor. Column - II gives some mathematical relations involving electrical quantities. Match Column - I and Column - II with appropriate relations. Column - I: (A) Drift Velocity; (B) Electrical Resistivity; (C) Relaxation Period; (D) Current Density. Column - II: (P) m/(ne²ρ); (Q) nev_d; (R) (eE/m)τ; (S) E/J.
why: v_d = (eE/m)τ; ρ = E/J; from ρ = m/(ne²τ) we get τ = m/(ne²ρ); J = nev_d. So A-R, B-S, C-P, D-Q.

q: The electron concentration in an n-type semiconductor is the same as hole concentration in a p-type semiconductor. An external field (electric) is applied across each of them. Compare the currents in them.
opts: current in n-type = current in p-type.
current in p-type > current in n-type.
current in n-type > current in p-type.
No current will flow in p-type, current will only flow in n-type.
why: Current ∝ carrier concentration × mobility. With equal concentrations, electrons have higher mobility than holes, so the n-type carries more current.

q: A radioactive nucleus ᴬ_Z X undergoes spontaneous decay in the sequence ᴬ_Z X → _{Z–1}B → _{Z–3}C → _{Z–2}D, where Z is the atomic number of element X. The possible decay particles in the sequence are :
why: Z → Z–1 is β⁺ emission; Z–1 → Z–3 is α emission (Z falls by 2); Z–3 → Z–2 is β⁻ emission (Z rises by 1). Sequence: β⁺, α, β⁻.

q: Water falls from a height of 60 m at the rate of 15 kg/s to operate a turbine. The losses due to frictional force are 10% of the input energy. How much power is generated by the turbine? (g = 10 m/s²)
why: Input power = (dm/dt)gh = 15 × 10 × 60 = 9000 W. After 10% loss, output = 0.9 × 9 kW = 8.1 kW.

topic: Dual nature of radiation and matter
q: The number of photons per second on an average emitted by the source of monochromatic light of wavelength 600 nm, when it delivers the power of 3.3 × 10⁻³ watt will be : (h = 6.6 × 10⁻³⁴ Js)
For a plane electromagnetic wave propagating in x-direction, which one of the following combination gives the correct possible directions for electric field (E) and magnetic field (B) respectively ?
why: E, B must be perpendicular and E × B must point along +x. For E = –ĵ + k̂ and B = –ĵ – k̂, E·B = 1 – 1 = 0 and E × B = 2î, which is along +x.

q: The effective resistance of a parallel connection that consists of four wires of equal length, equal area of cross-section and same material is 0.25 Ω. What will be the effective resistance if they are connected in series ?
why: Four equal resistors in parallel give R/4 = 0.25 Ω, so R = 1 Ω. In series: 4R = 4 Ω.

q: In a potentiometer circuit a cell of EMF 1.5 V gives balance point at 36 cm length of wire. If another cell of EMF 2.5 V replaces the first cell, then at what length of the wire, the balance point occurs ?
why: EMF ∝ balancing length: l₂ = 36 × (2.5/1.5) = 60 cm.

q: Polar molecules are the molecules :
opts: acquire a dipole moment only in the presence of electric field due to displacement of charges.
acquire a dipole moment only when magnetic field is absent.
having a permanent electric dipole moment.
why: Polar molecules have centres of positive and negative charge that do not coincide, so they possess a permanent electric dipole moment.

q: A parallel plate capacitor has a uniform electric field 'E' in the space between the plates. If the distance between the plates is 'd' and the area of each plate is 'A', the energy stored in the capacitor is : (ε₀ = permittivity of free space)
why: Energy density = ½ε₀E²; volume between plates = Ad, so U = ½ε₀E²Ad.

q: Consider the following statements (A) and (B) and identify the correct answer. (A) A zener diode is connected in reverse bias, when used as a voltage regulator. (B) The potential barrier of p-n junction lies between 0.1 V to 0.3 V.
why: A zener diode regulates voltage in reverse breakdown, so (A) is correct. The barrier potential is about 0.3 V for Ge and 0.7 V for Si, so the range 0.1–0.3 V in (B) is not correct.

topic: Work, energy and conservation of energy
q: A particle is released from height S from the surface of the Earth. At a certain height its kinetic energy is three times its potential energy. The height from the surface of earth and the speed of the particle at that instant are respectively :
why: Total energy = mgS. With KE = 3PE, PE = mgS/4 so h = S/4 and KE = 3mgS/4 = ½mv², giving v = √(3gS/2).

q: If E and G respectively denote energy and gravitational constant, then E/G has the dimensions of :
why: [E] = ML²T⁻², [G] = M⁻¹L³T⁻². E/G = M²L⁻¹T⁰.

q: Match Column - I and Column - II and choose the correct match from the given choices. Column - I: (A) Root mean square speed of gas molecules; (B) Pressure exerted by ideal gas; (C) Average kinetic energy of a molecule; (D) Total internal energy of 1 mole of a diatomic gas. Column - II: (P) (1/3) n m v̄²; (Q) √(3RT/M); (R) (5/2) RT; (S) (3/2) k_B T.
why: v_rms = √(3RT/M); P = (1/3)nmv̄²; average KE per molecule = (3/2)k_BT; U of one mole of a diatomic gas = (5/2)RT.

q: A body is executing simple harmonic motion with frequency 'n', the frequency of its potential energy is :
why: Potential energy ∝ x² ∝ sin²ωt = (1 – cos2ωt)/2, which oscillates at twice the frequency: 2n.

q: A cup of coffee cools from 90°C to 80°C in t minutes, when the room temperature is 20°C. The time taken by a similar cup of coffee to cool from 80°C to 60°C at a room temperature same at 20°C is :
why: Newton's law: Δθ/time = k(mean θ – 20). First: 10/t = k(85–20) = 65k. Second: 20/t′ = k(70–20) = 50k. Dividing gives t′ = (13/5)t.

q: A capacitor of capacitance 'C', is connected across an ac source of voltage V, given by V = V₀ sinωt. The displacement current between the plates of the capacitor, would then be given by :
why: Displacement current equals the conduction current in the circuit: I_d = C dV/dt = V₀ωC cosωt.

q: The half-life of a radioactive nuclide is 100 hours. The fraction of original activity that will remain after 150 hours would be :

topic: Photoelectric effect and de Broglie wavelength
q: An electromagnetic wave of wavelength 'λ' is incident on a photosensitive surface of negligible work function. If 'm' mass is of photoelectron emitted from the surface has de-Broglie wavelength λ_d, then :
why: With negligible work function, KE = hc/λ and λ_d = h/√(2m·KE), so λ_d² = hλ/(2mc). Hence λ = (2mc/h)λ_d².

q: The escape velocity from the Earth's surface is υ. The escape velocity from the surface of another planet having a radius, four times that of Earth and same mass density is :
why: v_e = √(2GM/R) = R√(8πGρ/3), so for the same density v_e ∝ R. Radius 4 times gives 4υ.

q: If force [F], acceleration [A] and time [T] are chosen as the fundamental physical quantities. Find the dimensions of energy.
why: Energy = force × length, and length has dimensions of acceleration × time² = [A][T²]. So energy = [F][A][T²].

q: Two conducting circular loops of radii R₁ and R₂ are placed in the same plane with their centres coinciding. If R₁ >> R₂, the mutual inductance M between them will be directly proportional to :
why: Field at the centre due to the large loop is B = μ₀I/(2R₁), roughly uniform over the small loop. Flux = B·πR₂², so M ∝ R₂²/R₁.

q: A series LCR circuit containing 5.0 H inductor, 80 μF capacitor and 40 Ω resistor is connected to 230 V variable frequency ac source. The angular frequencies of the source at which power transferred to the circuit is half the power at the resonant angular frequency are likely to be :
why: ω₀ = 1/√(LC) = 1/√(5 × 80×10⁻⁶) = 50 rad/s. Half-power points are at ω₀ ± R/(2L) = 50 ± 40/10 = 46 and 54 rad/s.

q: A car starts from rest and accelerates at 5 m/s². At t = 4 s, a ball is dropped out of a window by a person sitting in the car. What is the velocity and acceleration of the ball at t = 6 s ? (Take g = 10 m/s²)
why: At t = 4 s the car (and ball) has horizontal speed 5 × 4 = 20 m/s. After release the ball has no horizontal acceleration; in the next 2 s vertical speed = 10 × 2 = 20 m/s. Speed = √(20² + 20²) = 20√2 m/s and acceleration = g = 10 m/s².

q: A particle of mass 'm' is projected with a velocity υ = kVₑ (k < 1) from the surface of the earth. (Vₑ = escape velocity) The maximum height above the surface reached by the particle is :
why: Energy conservation: ½m(kVₑ)² – GMm/R = –GMm/(R + h), with ½Vₑ² = GM/R. This gives (1 – k²)/R = 1/(R + h), so h = Rk²/(1 – k²).

q: A particle moving in a circle of radius R with a uniform speed takes a time T to complete one revolution. If this particle were projected with the same speed at an angle 'θ' to the horizontal, the maximum height attained by it equals 4R. The angle of projection, θ, is then given by :
why: Speed v = 2πR/T. Max height H = v²sin²θ/(2g) = 4R gives sin²θ = 8gR/v² = 2gT²/(π²R). So θ = sin⁻¹(2gT²/(π²R))^(1/2).

topic: Moving charges in a magnetic field
q: In the product F = q(v × B) = q v × (Bₓî + B_yĵ + B₀k̂). For q = 1 and v = 2î + 4ĵ + 6k̂ and F = 4î – 20ĵ + 12k̂. What will be the complete expression for B ?
why: v × B = (4B₀ – 6B_y)î + (6Bₓ – 2B₀)ĵ + (2B_y – 4Bₓ)k̂ = 4î – 20ĵ + 12k̂. Testing the options, only Bₓ = –6, B_y = –6, B₀ = –8 satisfies all three components (e.g. 4(–8) – 6(–6) = 4 and 2(–6) – 4(–6) = 12).

q: A ball of mass 0.15 kg is dropped from a height 10 m, strikes the ground and rebounds to the same height. The magnitude of impulse imparted to the ball is (g = 10 m/s²) nearly :
why: Speed just before and after impact = √(2gh) = √200 ≈ 14.1 m/s. Impulse = change in momentum = 2mv = 2 × 0.15 × 14.1 ≈ 4.2 kg m/s.

topic: Magnetic dipole moment of a current loop
q: A uniform conducting wire of length 12a and resistance 'R' is wound up as a current carrying coil in the shape of, (i) an equilateral triangle of side 'a'. (ii) a square of side 'a'. The magnetic dipole moments of the coil in each case respectively are :
why: Triangle: perimeter 3a gives 4 turns, area √3a²/4, so m = 4·I·√3a²/4 = √3Ia². Square: perimeter 4a gives 3 turns, area a², so m = 3Ia².

q: Twenty seven drops of same size are charged at 220 V each. They combine to form a bigger drop. Calculate the potential of the bigger drop.
why: Charge is conserved: Q = 27q, and volume conservation gives R = 3r. V = kQ/R = 27kq/(3r) = 9 × 220 = 1980 V.

q: From a circular ring of mass 'M' and radius 'R' an arc corresponding to a 90° sector is removed. The moment of inertia of the remaining part of the ring about an axis passing through the centre of the ring and perpendicular to the plane of the ring is 'K' times 'MR²'. Then the value of 'K' is :
why: The removed 90° arc is one quarter of the ring, leaving mass 3M/4 all at distance R. I = (3M/4)R², so K = 3/4.

q: A step down transformer connected to an ac mains supply of 220 V is made to operate at 11 V, 44 W lamp. Ignoring power losses in the transformer, what is the current in the primary circuit ?
why: For an ideal transformer, input power = output power = 44 W. I_p = P/V_p = 44/220 = 0.2 A.

q: Dihedral angle of least stable conformer of ethane is :
why: The eclipsed conformer, with dihedral angle 0°, has maximum torsional strain and is the least stable; the staggered form (60°) is the most stable.

q: Noble gases are named because of their inertness towards reactivity. Identify an incorrect statement about them.
opts: Noble gases are sparingly soluble in water.
Noble gases have very high melting and boiling points.
Noble gases have weak dispersion forces.
Noble gases have large positive values of electron gain enthalpy.
why: Noble gases have only weak dispersion forces, so their melting and boiling points are very low, not very high. The other statements are correct.

q: The major product of the following chemical reaction is : (CH₃)₂CH–CH=CH₂ + HBr, in the presence of (C₆H₅CO)₂O₂ (peroxide) → ?
why: In the presence of peroxide, HBr adds to the alkene by the free-radical (anti-Markovnikov) route, so Br goes to the terminal carbon, giving (CH₃)₂CH–CH₂–CH₂–Br.

q: A particular station of All India Radio, New Delhi, broadcasts on a frequency of 1,368 kHz (kilohertz). The wavelength of the electromagnetic radiation emitted by the transmitter is : [speed of light, c = 3.0 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹]
The incorrect statement among the following is :
opts: Actinoid contraction is greater for element to element than Lanthanoid contraction.
Most of the trivalent Lanthanoid ions are colorless in the solid state.
Lanthanoids are good conductors of heat and electricity.
Actinoids are highly reactive metals, especially when finely divided.
why: Most trivalent lanthanoid ions are coloured (due to f-f transitions); only a few such as La³⁺, Lu³⁺, Ce³⁺, Gd³⁺ are colourless. The other statements are correct.

q: Right option for the number of tetrahedral and octahedral voids in hexagonal primitive unit cell are :
why: In hcp there are 6 atoms per unit cell; octahedral voids = number of atoms = 6 and tetrahedral voids = 2 × 6 = 12.

q: Which of the following reactions is the metal displacement reaction ? Choose the right option.
why: In a metal displacement reaction a more reactive metal (Al) displaces a less reactive metal (Cr) from its compound. Option 3 displaces hydrogen, not a metal.

q: Given below are two statements : Statement I : Aspirin and Paracetamol belong to the class of narcotic analgesics. Statement II : Morphine and Heroin are non-narcotic analgesics. In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below.
opts: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is false.
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is true.
why: Aspirin and paracetamol are non-narcotic analgesics, while morphine and heroin are narcotic analgesics, so both statements are false.

q: What is the IUPAC name of the organic compound formed in the following chemical reaction ? Acetone →(i) C₂H₅MgBr, dry Ether; (ii) H₂O, H⁺ → Product
why: Grignard reagent adds to the ketone C=O giving a tertiary alcohol: (CH₃)₂C(OH)CH₂CH₃, which is 2-methylbutan-2-ol.

q: Statement I : Acid strength increases in the order given as HF << HCl << HBr << HI. Statement II : As the size of the elements F, Cl, Br, I increases down the group, the bond strength of HF, HCl, HBr and HI decreases and so the acid strength increases. In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below.
opts: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is false.
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is true.
why: Down group 17 the H–X bond weakens as size increases, so the hydrogen halides become stronger acids: HF << HCl << HBr << HI. Both statements are true.

q: Which one among the following is the correct option for right relationship between C_P and C_V for one mole of ideal gas ?
why: Mayer's relation for one mole of an ideal gas: C_P − C_V = R.

q: Match List - I with List - II. List - I: (a) PCl₅; (b) SF₆; (c) BrF₅; (d) BF₃. List - II: (i) Square pyramidal; (ii) Trigonal planar; (iii) Octahedral; (iv) Trigonal bipyramidal. Choose the correct answer from the options given below.
why: PCl₅ is sp³d (trigonal bipyramidal), SF₆ sp³d² (octahedral), BrF₅ sp³d² with one lone pair (square pyramidal), BF₃ sp² (trigonal planar).

q: The following solutions were prepared by dissolving 10 g of glucose (C₆H₁₂O₆) in 250 ml of water (P₁), 10 g of urea (CH₄N₂O) in 250 ml of water (P₂) and 10 g of sucrose (C₁₂H₂₂O₁₁) in 250 ml of water (P₃). The right option for the decreasing order of osmotic pressure of these solutions is :
why: For equal volume and mass, osmotic pressure ∝ moles of solute = 10/M. Urea (M = 60) > glucose (180) > sucrose (342), so P₂ > P₁ > P₃.

q: Which one of the following methods can be used to obtain highly pure metal which is liquid at room temperature ?
why: The metal liquid at room temperature is mercury (a volatile metal), which is purified by distillation.

q: Tritium, a radioactive isotope of hydrogen, emits which of the following particles ?
why: Tritium (³H) has a high neutron to proton ratio and decays by β⁻ emission to ³He.

q: The correct option for the number of body centred unit cells in all 14 types of Bravais lattice unit cells is :
why: Body-centred lattices occur in cubic, tetragonal and orthorhombic systems only, giving 3.

q: The major product formed in dehydrohalogenation reaction of 2-Bromo pentane is Pent-2-ene. This product formation is based on ?
why: In dehydrohalogenation the more substituted (more stable) alkene is the major product, as stated by Saytzeff's rule.

q: The maximum temperature that can be achieved in blast furnace is :
why: In the blast furnace the temperature near the bottom (combustion zone) reaches about 2200 K.

q: The molar conductance of NaCl, HCl and CH₃COONa at infinite dilution are 126.45, 426.16 and 91.0 S cm² mol⁻¹ respectively. The molar conductance of CH₃COOH at infinite dilution is. Choose the right option for your answer.
why: Kohlrausch's law: Λ°(CH₃COOH) = Λ°(CH₃COONa) + Λ°(HCl) − Λ°(NaCl) = 91.0 + 426.16 − 126.45 = 390.71 S cm² mol⁻¹.

q: Ethylene diaminetetraacetate (EDTA) ion is :
opts: Hexadentate ligand with four "O" and two "N" donor atoms
Bidentate ligand with two "N" donor atoms
Tridentate ligand with three "N" donor atoms
