why: EDTA⁴⁻ binds through two nitrogen atoms and four carboxylate oxygen atoms, so it is hexadentate.

q: The structures of beryllium chloride in solid state and vapour phase, are :
why: Solid BeCl₂ has a polymeric chain structure with chloride bridges; in the vapour phase it exists as a chlorine-bridged dimer (becoming linear monomer only at very high temperature).

q: The right option for the statement "Tyndall effect is exhibited by", is :
why: Tyndall effect (scattering of light) is shown by colloids; starch solution is colloidal while the others are true solutions.

q: Which one of the following polymers is prepared by addition polymerisation ?
why: Teflon is made by addition polymerisation of tetrafluoroethene; Nylon-66, Novolac and Dacron are condensation polymers.

q: The RBC deficiency is deficiency disease of :
why: Deficiency of vitamin B₁₂ causes pernicious anaemia, a shortage of red blood cells.

q: The correct sequence of bond enthalpy of 'C–X' bond is :
opts: CH₃ – F < CH₃ – Cl < CH₃ – Br < CH₃ – I
CH₃ – F > CH₃ – Cl > CH₃ – Br > CH₃ – I
CH₃ – F < CH₃ – Cl > CH₃ – Br > CH₃ – I
CH₃ – Cl > CH₃ – F > CH₃ – Br > CH₃ – I
why: C–X bond strength falls as the halogen gets larger: C–F (452) > C–Cl (351) > C–Br (293) > C–I (234 kJ/mol).

q: An organic compound contains 78% (by wt.) carbon and remaining percentage of hydrogen. The right option for the empirical formula of this compound is : [Atomic wt. of C is 12, H is 1]
why: C: 78/12 = 6.5; H: 22/1 = 22. Ratio H:C = 22/6.5 ≈ 3.4, closest to CH₃ among the options.

q: Among the following alkaline earth metal halides, one which is covalent and soluble in organic solvents is :
why: Because of the very small size and high polarising power of Be²⁺, BeCl₂ is covalent and soluble in organic solvents.

q: BF₃ is planar and electron deficient compound. Hybridization and number of electrons around the central atom, respectively are :
why: Boron in BF₃ uses three bond pairs (sp² hybridisation, planar) and has only 6 electrons around it, hence electron deficient.

q: The pK_b of dimethylamine and pK_a of acetic acid are 3.27 and 4.77 respectively at T (K). The correct option for the pH of dimethylammonium acetate solution is :
why: For a salt of weak acid and weak base, pH = 7 + ½(pK_a − pK_b) = 7 + ½(4.77 − 3.27) = 7.75.

q: The compound which shows metamerism is :
why: Metamerism needs a polyvalent functional group such as an ether; C₄H₁₀O has metamers like CH₃OC₃H₇ and C₂H₅OC₂H₅. C₃H₈O can only give one ether (CH₃OC₂H₅).

q: Zr (Z = 40) and Hf (Z = 72) have similar atomic and ionic radii because of :
why: The poor shielding by 4f electrons causes lanthanoid contraction, making Hf (5d) nearly the same size as Zr (4d).

q: Match List - I with List - II. List - I: (a) [Fe(CN)₆]³⁻; (b) [Fe(H₂O)₆]³⁺; (c) [Fe(CN)₆]⁴⁻; (d) [Fe(H₂O)₆]²⁺. List - II: (i) 5.92 BM; (ii) 0 BM; (iii) 4.90 BM; (iv) 1.73 BM. Choose the correct answer from the options given below.
why: Fe³⁺ (d⁵) with strong CN⁻ has 1 unpaired electron (1.73 BM), with weak H₂O has 5 (5.92 BM). Fe²⁺ (d⁶) with CN⁻ has 0 (0 BM), with H₂O has 4 (4.90 BM).

q: From the following pairs of ions which one is not an iso-electronic pair ?
why: Fe²⁺ has 24 electrons while Mn²⁺ has 23, so they are not isoelectronic; the other pairs have 10, 10 and 23 electrons each.

q: The slope of Arrhenius Plot (ln k v/s 1/T) of first order reaction is −5 × 10³ K. The value of E_a of the reaction is. Choose the correct option for your answer. [Given R = 8.314 JK⁻¹mol⁻¹]
why: Slope = −E_a/R, so E_a = 5 × 10³ × 8.314 = 41570 J mol⁻¹ ≈ 41.5 kJ mol⁻¹.

q: For irreversible expansion of an ideal gas under isothermal condition, the correct option is :
why: Internal energy of an ideal gas depends only on temperature, so ΔU = 0 at constant T. An irreversible process increases total entropy, so ΔS_total ≠ 0 (> 0).

q: In which one of the following arrangements the given sequence is not strictly according to the properties indicated against it ?
opts: HF < HCl < HBr < HI : Increasing acidic strength
H₂O < H₂S < H₂Se < H₂Te : Increasing pK_a values
NH₃ < PH₃ < AsH₃ < SbH₃ : Increasing acidic character
CO₂ < SiO₂ < SnO₂ < PbO₂ : Increasing oxidising power
why: Acidity of hydrides increases down group 16, so pK_a values decrease from H₂O to H₂Te; the sequence given for increasing pK_a is therefore wrong.

q: The correct option for the value of vapour pressure of a solution at 45°C with benzene to octane in molar ratio 3 : 2 is : [At 45°C vapour pressure of benzene is 280 mm Hg and that of octane is 420 mm Hg. Assume Ideal gas]
why: Mole fractions: benzene 0.6, octane 0.4. P = 0.6 × 280 + 0.4 × 420 = 168 + 168 = 336 mm Hg (Raoult's law).

q: The molar conductivity of 0.007 M acetic acid is 20 S cm² mol⁻¹. What is the dissociation constant of acetic acid ? Choose the correct option. [Λ°(H⁺) = 350 S cm² mol⁻¹, Λ°(CH₃COO⁻) = 50 S cm² mol⁻¹]
CH₃CH₂COO⁻Na⁺ →(NaOH, + ? / Heat) CH₃CH₃ + Na₂CO₃. Consider the above reaction and identify the missing reagent/chemical.
why: Decarboxylation of a sodium carboxylate uses soda lime (NaOH + CaO) on heating, giving the alkane with one carbon less.

q: Which of the following molecules is non-polar in nature ?
why: SbCl₅ is symmetrical trigonal bipyramidal, so bond dipoles cancel and it is non-polar. POCl₃, CH₂O and NO₂ are polar.

q: Match List - I with List - II. List - I: (a) 2SO₂(g) + O₂(g) → 2SO₃(g); (b) HOCl(g) →(hν) •OH + •Cl; (c) CaCO₃ + H₂SO₄ → CaSO₄ + H₂O + CO₂; (d) NO₂(g) →(hν) NO(g) + O(g). List - II: (i) Acid rain; (ii) Smog; (iii) Ozone depletion; (iv) Tropospheric pollution. Choose the correct answer from the options given below.
why: SO₂ oxidation is a tropospheric pollution reaction; photolysis of HOCl releases Cl radicals that deplete ozone; sulphuric acid attacking carbonate stone is acid rain damage; photolysis of NO₂ drives photochemical smog.

q: Choose the correct option for the total pressure (in atm.) in a mixture of 4 g O₂ and 2 g H₂ confined in a total volume of one litre at 0°C is : [Given R = 0.082 L atm mol⁻¹K⁻¹, T = 273 K]
Which of the following plants is monoecious ?
why: Chara bears both antheridia and oogonia on the same plant, so it is monoecious. Carica, Marchantia and Cycas are dioecious.

q: Gemmae are present in :
why: Gemmae are green multicellular asexual buds formed in gemma cups of some liverworts such as Marchantia.

q: When the centromere is situated in the middle of two equal arms of chromosomes, the chromosome is referred as :
why: A median centromere giving two equal arms defines a metacentric chromosome.

q: Which of the following stages of meiosis involves division of centromere ?
why: Centromeres divide at the start of anaphase II so sister chromatids separate to opposite poles.

q: The first stable product of CO₂ fixation in sorghum is :
why: Sorghum is a C₄ plant; PEP carboxylase fixes CO₂ in mesophyll cells to give oxaloacetic acid as the first stable product.

q: The factor that leads to Founder effect in a population is :
why: Founder effect is a form of genetic drift in which a small group starting a new population carries only part of the original gene pool.

q: Which of the following is an incorrect statement ?
opts: Mature sieve tube elements possess a conspicuous nucleus and usual cytoplasmic organelles.
Microbodies are present both in plant and animal cells.
The perinuclear space forms a barrier between the materials present inside the nucleus and that of the cytoplasm.
Nuclear pores act as passages for proteins and RNA molecules in both directions between nucleus and cytoplasm.
why: Mature sieve tube elements lack a nucleus and most organelles; the other statements are correct.

q: Amensalism can be represented as :
why: In amensalism one species is harmed while the other is unaffected: (−, 0).

q: The amount of nutrients, such as carbon, nitrogen, phosphorus and calcium present in the soil at any given time, is referred as :
why: The amount of mineral nutrients present in the soil at a given time is called the standing state; standing crop refers to biomass of organisms.

q: Which of the following algae contains mannitol as reserve food material ?
why: Brown algae such as Ectocarpus store food as laminarin or mannitol. Red algae store floridean starch and green algae store starch.

q: Inspite of interspecific competition in nature, which mechanism the competing species might have evolved for their survival ?
why: Competing species avoid competition by resource partitioning, using resources in different ways or at different times.

q: Genera like Selaginella and Salvinia produce two kinds of spores. Such plants are known as :
why: Plants producing two kinds of spores (micro- and megaspores) are heterosporous.

q: The site of perception of light in plants during photoperiodism is :
why: Leaves perceive the photoperiod; the flowering stimulus is then transmitted to the shoot apex.

q: Plants follow different pathways in response to environment or phases of life to form different kinds of structures. This ability is called :
why: The ability of plants to form different structures in response to environment or life phase (e.g. heterophylly) is plasticity.

q: Match List - I with List - II. List - I: (a) Cristae; (b) Thylakoids; (c) Centromere; (d) Cisternae. List - II: (i) Primary constriction in chromosome; (ii) Disc-shaped sacs in Golgi apparatus; (iii) Infoldings in mitochondria; (iv) Flattened membranous sacs in stroma of plastids. Choose the correct answer from the options given below.
why: Cristae are infoldings of the inner mitochondrial membrane; thylakoids are flattened sacs in plastid stroma; the centromere is the primary constriction; cisternae are the disc-shaped sacs of the Golgi.

q: Match List - I with List - II. List I: (a) Cohesion; (b) Adhesion; (c) Surface tension; (d) Guttation  List II: (i) More attraction in liquid phase; (ii) Mutual attraction among water molecules; (iii) Water loss in liquid phase; (iv) Attraction towards polar surfaces. Choose the correct answer from the options given below.
why: Cohesion is mutual attraction among water molecules; adhesion is attraction towards polar surfaces; surface tension arises from greater attraction in the liquid phase; guttation is loss of water in liquid form.

q: DNA strands on a gel stained with ethidium bromide when viewed under UV radiation, appear as :
why: Ethidium bromide intercalates into DNA and fluoresces bright orange under UV light.

q: The term used for transfer of pollen grains from anthers of one plant to stigma of a different plant which, during pollination, brings genetically different types of pollen grains to stigma, is :
why: Xenogamy is transfer of pollen from anther of one plant to stigma of a different plant, bringing genetically different pollen.

q: Which of the following algae produce Carrageen ?
why: Carrageen is a hydrocolloid obtained from red algae such as Chondrus and Gigartina.

q: Which of the following statements is not correct ?
opts: Pyramid of biomass in sea is generally inverted.
Pyramid of biomass in sea is generally upright.
Pyramid of energy is always upright.
Pyramid of numbers in a grassland ecosystem is upright.
why: In the sea the biomass of phytoplankton is less than that of zooplankton and fish, so the biomass pyramid is generally inverted, not upright.

q: In the equation GPP - R = NPP. R represents :
why: Net primary productivity is gross primary productivity minus respiration losses (R).

q: Diadelphous stamens are found in :
why: Pea (Fabaceae) has stamens in two bundles (diadelphous); China rose is monadelphous and citrus is polyadelphous.

q: When gene targetting involving gene amplification is attempted in an individual's tissue to treat disease, it is known as :
why: Correcting a gene defect by delivering or amplifying a gene in an individual's tissues to treat disease is gene therapy.

q: Match List - I with List - II. List I: (a) Lenticels; (b) Cork cambium; (c) Secondary cortex; (d) Cork  List II: (i) Phellogen; (ii) Suberin deposition; (iii) Exchange of gases; (iv) Phelloderm. Choose the correct answer from the options given below.
why: Lenticels allow gas exchange; cork cambium is phellogen; secondary cortex is phelloderm; cork cells have suberin deposition.

q: Which of the following is a correct sequence of steps in a PCR (Polymerase Chain Reaction) ?
why: Each PCR cycle is denaturation of DNA, annealing of primers, then extension by Taq polymerase.

q: Mutations in plant cells can be induced by :
why: Gamma rays are ionising radiation and are mutagenic; kinetin and zeatin are cytokinins and infrared is non-ionising.

q: Match List - I with List - II. List I: (a) Protoplast fusion; (b) Plant tissue culture; (c) Meristem culture; (d) Micropropagation  List II: (i) Totipotency; (ii) Pomato; (iii) Somaclones; (iv) Virus free plants. Choose the correct answer from the options given below.
why: Protoplast fusion gives somatic hybrids like pomato; tissue culture rests on totipotency; meristem culture gives virus-free plants; micropropagation yields somaclones.

q: During the purification process for recombinant DNA technology, addition of chilled ethanol precipitates out :
why: Chilled ethanol precipitates DNA as fine threads; other biomolecules are removed by enzymes or remain in solution.

q: Complete the flow chart on central dogma. DNA (a: arrow looping back on DNA) → (b) → mRNA → (c) → (d)
why: Central dogma: DNA self-copies by replication, DNA to mRNA is transcription, mRNA to protein is translation.

q: Which of the following is not an application of PCR (Polymerase Chain Reaction) ?
why: PCR amplifies DNA and is used in diagnosis and mutation detection; it is not used to purify proteins.

q: The plant hormone used to destroy weeds in a field is :
why: 2,4-D is a synthetic auxin used as a selective weedicide against dicot weeds.

q: Match List - I with List - II. List I: (a) Cells with active cell division capacity; (b) Tissue having all cells similar in structure and function; (c) Tissue having different types of cells; (d) Dead cells with highly thickened walls and narrow lumen  List II: (i) Vascular tissues; (ii) Meristematic tissue; (iii) Sclereids; (iv) Simple tissue. Select the correct answer from the options given below.
why: Meristematic cells divide actively; simple tissue has one cell type; complex (vascular) tissue has several; sclereids are dead cells with thick walls and narrow lumen.

q: Which of the following are not secondary metabolites in plants ?
why: Amino acids and glucose are primary metabolites; the others are secondary metabolites.

q: Which of the following statements is incorrect ?
opts: During aerobic respiration, role of oxygen is limited to the terminal stage.
In ETC (Electron Transport Chain), one molecule of NADH + H⁺ gives rise to 2 ATP molecules, and one FADH₂ gives rise to 3 ATP molecules.
ATP is synthesized through complex V.
Oxidation-reduction reactions produce proton gradient in respiration.
why: NADH gives more ATP than FADH₂ (about 3 versus 2 in the textbook count), so the statement reversing them is incorrect.

q: Match Column - I with Column - II. Column I: (a) Nitrococcus; (b) Rhizobium; (c) Thiobacillus; (d) Nitrobacter  Column II: (i) Denitrification; (ii) Conversion of ammonia to nitrite; (iii) Conversion of nitrite to nitrate; (iv) Conversion of atmospheric nitrogen to ammonia. Choose the correct answer from options given below.
why: Nitrococcus oxidises ammonia to nitrite, Rhizobium fixes N₂ to ammonia, Thiobacillus denitrifies, and Nitrobacter oxidises nitrite to nitrate.

q: Match Column - I with Column - II. Column I (floral formulae): (a) %⚥ K(5) C1+2+(2) A(9)+1 G1; (b) ⊕⚥ K(5) C(5) A5 G2; (c) ⊕⚥ P(3+3) A3+3 G(3); (d) ⊕⚥ K2+2 C4 A2-4 G(2)  Column II: (i) Brassicaceae; (ii) Liliaceae; (iii) Fabaceae; (iv) Solanaceae. Select the correct answer from the options given below.
why: Zygomorphic, diadelphous flower is Fabaceae; K(5) C(5) A5 G2 is Solanaceae; P(3+3) A3+3 G(3) is Liliaceae; tetramerous with 4 petals and tetradynamous stamens is Brassicaceae.

q: Identify the correct statement.
opts: In capping, methyl guanosine triphosphate is added to the 3′ end of hnRNA.
RNA polymerase binds with Rho factor to terminate the process of transcription in bacteria.
The coding strand in a transcription unit is copied to an mRNA.
Split gene arrangement is characteristic of prokaryotes.
why: Capping is at the 5′ end; the template (not coding) strand is copied; split genes are eukaryotic; termination in bacteria involves Rho factor associating with RNA polymerase.

q: Which of the following statements is correct ?
opts: Fusion of two cells is called Karyogamy.
Fusion of protoplasms between two motile or non-motile gametes is called plasmogamy.
Organisms that depend on living plants are called saprophytes.
Some of the organisms can fix atmospheric nitrogen in specialized cells called sheath cells.
why: Plasmogamy is fusion of protoplasms of gametes; karyogamy is fusion of nuclei, saprophytes feed on dead matter, and nitrogen fixation occurs in heterocysts.

q: Select the correct pair.
opts: Large colorless empty cells in the epidermis of grass leaves - Subsidiary cells
In dicot leaves, vascular bundles are surrounded by large thick-walled cells - Conjunctive tissue
Cells of medullary rays that form part of cambial ring - Interfascicular cambium
Loose parenchyma cells rupturing the epidermis and forming a lens-shaped opening in bark - Spongy parenchyma
why: Medullary ray cells between vascular bundles become interfascicular cambium; the other pairs should be bulliform cells, bundle sheath and lenticels.

q: DNA fingerprinting involves identifying differences in some specific regions in DNA sequence, called as :
why: NCERT states DNA fingerprinting identifies differences in specific regions called repetitive DNA.

q: In some members of which of the following pairs of families, pollen grains retain their viability for months after release ?
why: Pollen of Poaceae (rice, wheat) loses viability in about 30 minutes, whereas some Rosaceae and Leguminosae pollen stays viable for months.

q: Which of the following statements is incorrect ?
opts: Both ATP and NADPH + H⁺ are synthesized during non-cyclic photophosphorylation.
Stroma lamellae have PS I only and lack NADP reductase.
Grana lamellae have both PS I and PS II.
Cyclic photophosphorylation involves both PS I and PS II.
why: Cyclic photophosphorylation involves only PS I.

q: What is the role of RNA polymerase III in the process of transcription in eukaryotes ?
why: RNA polymerase III transcribes tRNA, 5S rRNA and snRNAs; Pol I makes the large rRNAs and Pol II makes hnRNA.

q: In the exponential growth equation Nₜ = N₀eʳᵗ, e represents :
why: In the equation, e is the base of natural logarithms (about 2.718).

q: Now a days it is possible to detect the mutated gene causing cancer by allowing radioactive probe to hybridise its complimentary DNA in a clone of cells, followed by its detection using autoradiography because :
opts: mutated gene partially appears on a photographic film.
mutated gene completely and clearly appears on a photographic film.
mutated gene does not appear on a photographic film as the probe has no complimentarity with it.
mutated gene does not appear on a photographic film as the probe has complimentarity with it.
why: The probe pairs only with its complementary normal sequence, so the mutated gene lacks complementarity and gives no signal on the film.

q: Match List - I with List - II. List I: (a) Protein; (b) Unsaturated fatty acid; (c) Nucleic acid; (d) Polysaccharide  List II: (i) C=C double bonds; (ii) Phosphodiester bonds; (iii) Glycosidic bonds; (iv) Peptide bonds. Choose the correct answer from the options given below.
why: Proteins have peptide bonds, unsaturated fatty acids C=C bonds, nucleic acids phosphodiester bonds, polysaccharides glycosidic bonds.

q: Match List - I with List - II. List I: (a) S phase; (b) G₂ phase; (c) Quiescent stage; (d) G₁ phase  List II: (i) Proteins are synthesized; (ii) Inactive phase; (iii) Interval between mitosis and initiation of DNA replication; (iv) DNA replication. Choose the correct answer from the options given below.
why: DNA replicates in S; proteins for mitosis are made in G₂; the quiescent stage (G₀) is inactive; G₁ is the gap between mitosis and DNA replication.

q: Plasmid pBR322 has PstI restriction enzyme site within gene ampᴿ that confers ampicillin resistance. If this enzyme is used for inserting a gene for β-galactoside production and the recombinant plasmid is inserted in an E.coli strain
opts: it will not be able to confer ampicillin resistance to the host cell.
the transformed cells will have the ability to resist ampicillin as well as produce β-galactoside.
it will lead to lysis of host cell.
it will be able to produce a novel protein with dual ability.
why: Insertion at the PstI site inside ampᴿ inactivates that gene (insertional inactivation), so the host loses ampicillin resistance.

q: Identify the incorrect pair.
why: Ricin is a toxin, not a drug; codeine is an alkaloid, abrin a toxin and concanavalin A a lectin.

q: The fruit fly has 8 chromosomes (2n) in each cell. During interphase of Mitosis if the number of chromosomes at G₁ phase is 8, what would be the number of chromosomes after S phase ?
why: DNA content doubles in S phase but each chromosome still has two sister chromatids, so the chromosome number stays 8.

q: Match List - I with List - II. List I: (a) Metamerism; (b) Canal system; (c) Comb plates; (d) Cnidoblasts  List II: (i) Coelenterata; (ii) Ctenophora; (iii) Annelida; (iv) Porifera. Choose the correct answer from the options given below.
why: Metamerism is a feature of Annelida, canal system of Porifera, comb plates of Ctenophora, cnidoblasts of Coelenterata.

q: Match List - I with List - II. List I: (a) Vaults; (b) IUDs; (c) Vasectomy; (d) Tubectomy  List II: (i) Entry of sperm through Cervix is blocked; (ii) Removal of Vas deferens; (iii) Phagocytosis of sperms within the Uterus; (iv) Removal of fallopian tube. Choose the correct answer from the options given below.
why: Vaults are barriers blocking the cervix, IUDs promote phagocytosis of sperm in the uterus, vasectomy cuts the vas deferens and tubectomy the fallopian tubes.

q: If Adenine makes 30% of the DNA molecule, what will be the percentage of Thymine, Guanine and Cytosine in it ?
why: By Chargaff's rule A = T = 30%, so G + C = 40%, giving G = C = 20%.

q: Which of the following RNAs is not required for the synthesis of protein ?
why: mRNA, tRNA and rRNA take part in translation; siRNA is involved in RNA interference/gene silencing.

q: Which one of the following is an example of Hormone releasing IUD ?
why: LNG-20 releases the hormone levonorgestrel; CuT, Cu 7 and Multiload 375 are copper releasing.

q: Succus entericus is referred to as :
why: Succus entericus is the intestinal juice secreted by the small intestine.

q: Chronic auto immune disorder affecting neuro muscular junction leading to fatigue, weakening and paralysis of skeletal muscle is called as :
why: Myasthenia gravis is an autoimmune disorder affecting the neuromuscular junction.

q: With regard to insulin choose correct options. (a) C-peptide is not present in mature insulin. (b) The insulin produced by rDNA technology has C-peptide. (c) The pro-insulin has C-peptide. (d) A-peptide and B-peptide of insulin are interconnected by disulphide bridges. Choose the correct answer from the options given below.
why: Pro-insulin has the C-peptide, which is removed in mature insulin, whose A and B chains are joined by disulphide bridges; rDNA insulin is made as separate A and B chains without C-peptide.

q: Which one of the following belongs to the family Muscidae ?
why: The house fly (Musca domestica) belongs to family Muscidae.

q: Which is the "Only enzyme" that has "Capability" to catalyse Initiation, Elongation and Termination in the process of transcription in prokaryotes ?
why: In bacteria a single DNA-dependent RNA polymerase carries out initiation, elongation and termination of transcription.

q: Receptors for sperm binding in mammals are present on :
why: Sperm-binding receptors (ZP3) are on the zona pellucida of the ovum.

q: The centriole undergoes duplication during :
why: Centrioles duplicate during the S phase of interphase in the cell cycle.

q: Which one of the following organisms bears hollow and pneumatic long bones ?
why: Birds have pneumatic bones with air cavities; Neophron (vulture) is a bird, the others are a lizard and mammals.

q: Erythropoietin hormone which stimulates R.B.C. formation is produced by :
why: Juxtaglomerular cells of the kidney secrete erythropoietin in response to low oxygen.

q: Match the following : List I: (a) Physalia; (b) Limulus; (c) Ancylostoma; (d) Pinctada  List II: (i) Pearl oyster; (ii) Portuguese Man of War; (iii) Living fossil; (iv) Hookworm. Choose the correct answer from the options given below.
why: Physalia is Portuguese man-of-war, Limulus a living fossil, Ancylostoma the hookworm, Pinctada the pearl oyster.

q: During the process of gene amplification using PCR, if very high temperature is not maintained in the beginning, then which of the following steps of PCR will be affected first ?
why: Denaturation of double-stranded DNA needs high temperature (about 94 °C) and is the first step, so it is affected first.

q: Which of the following statements wrongly represents the nature of smooth muscle ?
opts: Communication among the cells is performed by intercalated discs
These muscles are present in the wall of blood vessels
why: Intercalated discs are a feature of cardiac muscle, not smooth muscle.

q: The organelles that are included in the endomembrane system are :
opts: Endoplasmic reticulum, Mitochondria, Ribosomes and Lysosomes
Endoplasmic reticulum, Golgi complex, Lysosomes and Vacuoles
Golgi complex, Mitochondria, Ribosomes and Lysosomes
Golgi complex, Endoplasmic reticulum, Mitochondria and Lysosomes
why: The endomembrane system comprises ER, Golgi complex, lysosomes and vacuoles; mitochondria and ribosomes are excluded.

q: Match List - I with List - II. List I: (a) Aspergillus niger; (b) Acetobacter aceti; (c) Clostridium butylicum; (d) Lactobacillus  List II: (i) Acetic Acid; (ii) Lactic Acid; (iii) Citric Acid; (iv) Butyric Acid. Choose the correct answer from the options given below.
why: Aspergillus niger gives citric acid, Acetobacter acetic acid, Clostridium butylicum butyric acid, Lactobacillus lactic acid.

q: For effective treatment of the disease, early diagnosis and understanding its pathophysiology is very important. Which of the following molecular diagnostic techniques is very useful for early detection ?
why: ELISA detects antigens or antibodies and is used for early detection of infections such as HIV.

q: Which of the following characteristics is incorrect with respect to cockroach ?
opts: A ring of gastric caeca is present at the junction of midgut and hind gut.
Hypopharynx lies within the cavity enclosed by the mouth parts.
In females, 7ᵗʰ-9ᵗʰ sterna together form a genital pouch.
10ᵗʰ abdominal segment in both sexes, bears a pair of anal cerci.
why: Gastric caeca lie at the junction of foregut and midgut; Malpighian tubules mark the midgut-hindgut junction.

q: Persons with 'AB' blood group are called as "Universal recipients". This is due to :
opts: Absence of antigens A and B on the surface of RBCs
Absence of antigens A and B in plasma
Presence of antibodies, anti-A and anti-B, on RBCs
Absence of antibodies, anti-A and anti-B, in plasma
why: AB plasma has neither anti-A nor anti-B antibodies, so it can accept blood of any ABO group.

q: Dobson units are used to measure thickness of :
why: Dobson units measure the thickness of the ozone layer in a column of air.

q: Read the following statements. (a) Metagenesis is observed in Helminths. (b) Echinoderms are triploblastic and coelomate animals. (c) Round worms have organ-system level of body organization. (d) Comb plates present in ctenophores help in digestion. (e) Water vascular system is characteristic of Echinoderms. Choose the correct answer from the options given below.
why: Metagenesis occurs in cnidarians, and comb plates are for locomotion, so (a) and (d) are wrong; (b), (c) and (e) are correct.

q: In a cross between a male and female, both heterozygous for sickle cell anaemia gene, what percentage of the progeny will be diseased ?
why: Aa × Aa gives AA : Aa : aa = 1 : 2 : 1, so only aa (25%) are diseased.

q: Which enzyme is responsible for the conversion of inactive fibrinogens to fibrins ?
why: Thrombin, formed from prothrombin, converts soluble fibrinogen to insoluble fibrin threads.

q: Select the favourable conditions required for the formation of oxyhaemoglobin at the alveoli.
opts: High pO₂, low pCO₂, less H⁺, lower temperature
Low pO₂, high pCO₂, more H⁺, higher temperature
High pO₂, high pCO₂, less H⁺, higher temperature
Low pO₂, low pCO₂, more H⁺, higher temperature
why: At alveoli, high pO₂, low pCO₂, lower H⁺ and lower temperature favour oxygen binding to haemoglobin.

q: Sphincter of oddi is present at :
opts: Junction of hepato-pancreatic duct and duodenum
why: The sphincter of Oddi guards the opening of the hepato-pancreatic duct into the duodenum.

q: Which stage of meiotic prophase shows terminalisation of chiasmata as its distinctive feature ?
why: Terminalisation of chiasmata occurs in diakinesis, the last substage of prophase I.

topic: Strategies for enhancement in food production
q: Which of the following is not an objective of Biofortification in crops ?
why: Biofortification aims to improve protein, vitamin, micronutrient and mineral content, not disease resistance.

q: The partial pressures (in mm Hg) of oxygen (O₂) and carbon dioxide (CO₂) at alveoli (the site of diffusion) are :
why: Alveolar air has pO₂ about 104 mm Hg and pCO₂ about 40 mm Hg.

q: Veneral diseases can spread through : (a) Using sterile needles (b) Transfusion of blood from infected person (c) Infected mother to foetus (d) Kissing (e) Inheritance. Choose the correct answer from the options given below.
why: STDs spread by contaminated blood transfusion and from infected mother to foetus; sterile needles, kissing and inheritance do not spread them.

q: A specific recognition sequence identified by endonucleases to make cuts at specific positions within the DNA is :
why: Restriction endonucleases recognise palindromic nucleotide sequences, which read the same on both strands in the 5′→3′ direction.

q: Which one of the following statements about Histones is wrong ?
opts: Histones are organized to form a unit of 8 molecules.
The pH of histones is slightly acidic.
Histones are rich in amino acids - Lysine and Arginine.
Histones carry positive charge in the side chain.
why: Histones are basic proteins rich in lysine and arginine, whose side chains carry positive charge. They form an octamer of 8 molecules. So calling them slightly acidic is wrong.

q:
During muscular contraction which of the following events occur ?
(a) 'H' zone disappears
(b) 'A' band widens
(c) 'I' band reduces in width
(d) Myosine hydrolyzes ATP, releasing the ADP and Pi
(e) Z-lines attached to actins are pulled inwards
Choose the correct answer from the options given below.
why: In the sliding filament mechanism the A band keeps its length, while the H zone vanishes and the I band shortens as actin is pulled inward by myosin heads using ATP. So (b) is false.

q:
Match List - I with List - II.
List I: (a) Scapula; (b) Cranium; (c) Sternum; (d) Vertebral column  List II: (i) Cartilaginous joints; (ii) Flat bone; (iii) Fibrous joints; (iv) Triangular flat bone
Choose the correct answer from the options given below.
why: Scapula is a triangular flat bone, cranial bones are united by fibrous joints (sutures), the sternum is a flat bone, and vertebrae are joined by cartilaginous joints.

q: Which of these is not an important component of initiation of parturition in humans ?
opts: Increase in estrogen and progesterone ratio
why: Parturition is initiated by foetal signals, a rise in the estrogen to progesterone ratio, prostaglandins and oxytocin release. Prolactin is concerned with lactation, not initiation of labour.

q:
Assertion (A) : A person goes to high altitude and experiences 'altitude sickness' with symptoms like breathing difficulty and heart palpitations.
Reason (R) : Due to low atmospheric pressure at high altitude, the body does not get sufficient oxygen.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below.
opts: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
why: Low atmospheric pressure at altitude lowers the partial pressure of oxygen, so the body gets too little oxygen (hypoxia), causing altitude sickness symptoms. R correctly explains A.

q:
Following are the statements with reference to 'lipids'.
(a) Lipids having only single bonds are called unsaturated fatty acids.
(b) Lecithin is a phospholipid.
(c) Trihydroxy propane is glycerol.
(d) Palmitic acid has 20 carbon atoms including carboxyl carbon.
(e) Arachidonic acid has 16 carbon atoms.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below.
why: Only single bonds means saturated, so (a) is false. Palmitic acid has 16 carbons and arachidonic acid has 20, so (d) and (e) are false. Lecithin is a phospholipid and glycerol is trihydroxy propane.

q: The Adenosine deaminase deficiency results into :
why: ADA deficiency impairs lymphocyte function and causes severe combined immunodeficiency (SCID), a dysfunction of the immune system.

q: Which of the following secretes the hormone, relaxin, during the later phase of pregnancy ?
why: Relaxin is secreted by the corpus luteum (ovary) in late pregnancy and relaxes the pelvic ligaments to ease childbirth.

q: Identify the types of cell junctions that help to stop the leakage of the substances across a tissue and facilitation of communication with neighbouring cells via rapid transfer of ions and molecules.
opts: Gap junctions and Adhering junctions, respectively.
Tight junctions and Gap junctions, respectively.
Adhering junctions and Tight junctions, respectively.
Adhering junctions and Gap junctions, respectively.
why: Tight junctions seal cells and prevent leakage of substances across a tissue. Gap junctions connect cytoplasm of adjacent cells for rapid transfer of ions and small molecules.

topic: Strategies for enhancement in food production
q: Which of the following is not a step in Multiple Ovulation Embryo Transfer Technology (MOET) ?
opts: Cow is administered hormone having LH like activity for super ovulation
Cow yields about 6-8 eggs at a time
Cow is fertilized by artificial insemination
Fertilized eggs are transferred to surrogate mothers at 8-32 cell stage
why: In MOET the cow is given hormone with FSH-like activity to induce super ovulation, not LH-like activity. The other steps are correct.

q:
Match List - I with List - II.
List I: (a) Filariasis; (b) Amoebiasis; (c) Pneumonia; (d) Ringworm  List II: (i) Haemophilus influenzae; (ii) Trichophyton; (iii) Wuchereria bancrofti; (iv) Entamoeba histolytica
Choose the correct answer from the options given below.
why: Filariasis is caused by Wuchereria bancrofti, amoebiasis by Entamoeba histolytica, pneumonia by Haemophilus influenzae and ringworm by Trichophyton.

q:
Match List - I with List - II.
List I: (a) Allen's Rule; (b) Physiological adaptation; (c) Behavioural adaptation; (d) Biochemical adaptation  List II: (i) Kangaroo rat; (ii) Desert lizard; (iii) Marine fish at depth; (iv) Polar seal
Choose the correct answer from the options given below.
why: Allen's rule (short extremities in cold) fits the polar seal. Kangaroo rat has physiological adaptation, desert lizard basks or burrows (behavioural), and marine fish at depth show biochemical adaptation.

q:
Match List - I with List - II.
List I: (a) Adaptive radiation; (b) Convergent evolution; (c) Divergent evolution; (d) Evolution by anthropogenic action  List II: (i) Selection of resistant varieties due to excessive use of herbicides and pesticides; (ii) Bones of forelimbs in Man and Whale; (iii) Wings of Butterfly and Bird; (iv) Darwin Finches
Choose the correct answer from the options given below.
why: Darwin's finches show adaptive radiation, butterfly and bird wings are analogous (convergent), forelimbs of man and whale are homologous (divergent), and herbicide resistance is anthropogenic.

q:
Statement I : The codon 'AUG' codes for methionine and phenylalanine.
Statement II : 'AAA' and 'AAG' both codons code for the amino acid lysine.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below.
opts: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is correct but Statement II is false
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is true
why: AUG codes only for methionine (phenylalanine is UUU and UUC), so Statement I is wrong. AAA and AAG both code for lysine, showing degeneracy of the code.

q:
Following are the statements about prostomium of earthworm.
(a) It serves as a covering for mouth.
(b) It helps to open cracks in the soil into which it can crawl.
(c) It is one of the sensory structures.
(d) It is the first body segment.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below.
why: The prostomium is a sensory lobe covering the mouth that helps push into soil cracks. It is not a segment; the peristomium is the first body segment.

q: The dimensions [MLT⁻²A⁻²] belong to the
why: From B = μ₀I/(2πr), μ₀ = force/(current²) = N A⁻², whose dimensions are [MLT⁻²A⁻²]. So it is magnetic permeability.

q: In half wave rectification, if the input frequency is 60 Hz, then the output frequency would be
why: A half wave rectifier conducts once in every input cycle, so the output has one pulse per cycle and the same frequency as the input, 60 Hz. (A full wave rectifier would give 120 Hz.)

q: If the initial tension on a stretched string is doubled, then the ratio of the initial and final speeds of a transverse wave along the string is
why: Wave speed v = √(T/μ), so v ∝ √T. With T doubled, v_initial : v_final = √T : √(2T) = 1 : √2.

q: A shell of mass m is at rest initially. It explodes into three fragments having mass in the ratio 2 : 2 : 1. If the fragments having equal mass fly off along mutually perpendicular directions with speed v, the speed of the third (lighter) fragment is
why: Let the masses be 2k, 2k, k. The two equal fragments have perpendicular momenta 2kv each, with resultant 2√2 kv. Momentum conservation gives k·v₃ = 2√2 kv, so v₃ = 2√2 v.

q: Two objects of mass 10 kg and 20 kg respectively are connected to the two ends of a rigid rod of length 10 m with negligible mass. The distance of the center of mass of the system from the 10 kg mass is
why: Taking the 10 kg mass as origin, x_cm = (10×0 + 20×10)/(10+20) = 200/30 = 20/3 m.

q: If a soap bubble expands, the pressure inside the bubble
opts: Is equal to the atmospheric pressure
why: Excess pressure inside a soap bubble is ΔP = 4S/r. As the radius r increases, the excess pressure and so the pressure inside decreases.

q: An electric lift with a maximum load of 2000 kg (lift + passengers) is moving up with a constant speed of 1.5 ms⁻¹. The frictional force opposing the motion is 3000 N. The minimum power delivered by the motor to the lift in watts is : (g = 10 ms⁻²)
why: At constant speed the motor force F = mg + friction = 20000 + 3000 = 23000 N. Power P = Fv = 23000 × 1.5 = 34500 W.

q: The angle between the electric lines of force and the equipotential surface is
why: Electric field lines are always perpendicular to equipotential surfaces, since there is no field component along an equipotential surface.

q: When two monochromatic lights of frequency, v and v/2 are incident on a photoelectric metal, their stopping potential becomes Vs/2 and Vs respectively. The threshold frequency for this metal is
why: eVs/2 = h(v − v₀) and eVs = h(v/2 − v₀). Dividing: (v/2 − v₀) = 2(v − v₀), which gives v₀ = 3v/2.

q: A long solenoid of radius 1 mm has 100 turns per mm. If 1 A current flows in the solenoid, the magnetic field strength at the centre of the solenoid is
In the given nuclear reaction, the element X is: ²²₁₁Na → X + e⁺ + ν
why: In β⁺ decay a proton becomes a neutron: the mass number stays 22 and the atomic number drops from 11 to 10. The element with Z = 10 is Ne, so X is ²²₁₀Ne.

q: Given below are two statements. Statement I : Biot-Savart law gives us the expression for the magnetic field strength of an infinitesimal current element (Idl) of a current carrying conductor only. Statement II : Biot-Savart law is analogous to Coulomb's inverse square law of charge q, with the former being related to the field produced by a scalar source, Idl while the latter being produced by a vector source, q. In light of above statements choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below
opts: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct and Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect and Statement II is correct
why: Biot-Savart law gives the field of a current element, so Statement I is correct. Statement II is wrong because Idl is a vector source and charge q is a scalar source, the reverse of what is stated.

q: The ratio of the radius of gyration of a thin uniform disc about an axis passing through its centre and normal to its plane to the radius of gyration of the disc about its diameter is
why: About the normal axis I = MR²/2, so k = R/√2. About a diameter I = MR²/4, so k = R/2. Ratio = (1/√2) : (1/2) = √2 : 1.

q: The peak voltage of the ac source is equal to
opts: The value of voltage supplied to the circuit
The rms value of the ac source
√2 times the rms value of the ac source
1/√2 times the rms value of the ac source
why: V_rms = V₀/√2, so the peak voltage V₀ = √2 V_rms.

q: The energy that will be ideally radiated by a 100 kW transmitter in 1 hour is

In a Young's double slit experiment, a student observes 8 fringes in a certain segment of screen when a monochromatic light of 600 nm wavelength is used. If the wavelength of light is changed to 400 nm, then the number of fringes he would observe in the same region of the screen is
why: Fringe width β = λD/d, so the number of fringes in a fixed region ∝ 1/λ. N = 8 × 600/400 = 12.

q: A square loop of side 1 m and resistance 1 Ω is placed in a magnetic field of 0.5 T. If the plane of loop is perpendicular to the direction of magnetic field, the magnetic flux through the loop is
why: Flux φ = BA cos0° = 0.5 × (1 × 1) = 0.5 Wb.

q: Two resistors of resistance 100 Ω and 200 Ω are connected in parallel in an electrical circuit. The ratio of the thermal energy developed in 100 Ω to that in 200 Ω in a given time is
why: In parallel the voltage is the same, so H = V²t/R ∝ 1/R. Ratio = (1/100) : (1/200) = 2 : 1.

q: The ratio of the distances travelled by a freely falling body in the 1st, 2nd, 3rd and 4th second
why: Distance in the nth second from rest = (g/2)(2n − 1), so the distances are in the ratio 1 : 3 : 5 : 7.

q: A body of mass 60 g experiences a gravitational force of 3.0 N, when placed at a particular point. The magnitude of the gravitational field intensity at that point is
why: Field intensity = F/m = 3.0 N / 0.060 kg = 50 N/kg.

q: A light ray falls on a glass surface of refractive index √3, at an angle 60°. The angle between the refracted and reflected rays would be
why: tan 60° = √3 = n, so 60° is Brewster's angle and the reflected and refracted rays are perpendicular: the angle between them is 90°. (Check: sin r = sin60°/√3 = 1/2, r = 30°; 180° − 60° − 30° = 90°.)

q: When light propagates through a material medium of relative permittivity εr and relative permeability μr, the velocity of light, v is given by (c-velocity of light in vacuum)
why: v = 1/√(με) = 1/√(μ₀ε₀μrεr) = c/√(μrεr).

q: Two hollow conducting spheres of radii R₁ and R₂ (R₁ >> R₂) have equal charges. The potential would be
opts: Dependent on the material property of the sphere
why: Potential of a conducting sphere V = kQ/R. For equal charge Q, the smaller radius gives the larger potential.

q: A copper wire of length 10 m and radius (10⁻²/√π) m has electrical resistance of 10 Ω. The current density in the wire for an electric field strength of 10 (V/m) is
why: A = πr² = 10⁻⁴ m². R = ρL/A gives ρ = RA/L = 10 × 10⁻⁴/10 = 10⁻⁴ Ω m. J = E/ρ = 10/10⁻⁴ = 10⁵ A/m².

q: Plane angle and solid angle have
why: Plane angle (radian) and solid angle (steradian) are ratios of lengths or areas, so they are dimensionless, but they still have units.

q: Let T₁ and T₂ be the energy of an electron in the first and second excited states of hydrogen atoms, respectively. According to the Bohr's model of an atom, the ratio T₁ : T₂ is
why: The first excited state is n = 2 and the second is n = 3. Energy (magnitude) ∝ 1/n², so T₁ : T₂ = (1/4) : (1/9) = 9 : 4.

q: Match List-I with List-II. List-I: (a) Gravitational constant (G); (b) Gravitational potential energy; (c) Gravitational potential; (d) Gravitational intensity.  List-II: (i) [L²T⁻²]; (ii) [M⁻¹L³T⁻²]; (iii) [LT⁻²]; (iv) [ML²T⁻²]. Choose the correct answer from the options given below
why: G = Fr²/m² gives [M⁻¹L³T⁻²]. Potential energy is [ML²T⁻²]. Potential (energy per unit mass) is [L²T⁻²]. Intensity (force per unit mass) is [LT⁻²].

q: Two pendulums of length 121 cm and 100 cm start vibrating in phase. At some instant, the two are at their mean position in the same phase. The minimum number of vibrations of the shorter pendulum after which the two are again in phase at the mean position is:
why: T ∝ √l, so T₁ : T₂ = 11 : 10 (longer : shorter). When the shorter completes n vibrations the longer completes n − 1: n × 10 = (n − 1) × 11, so n = 11.

q: The area of a rectangular field (in m²) of length 55.3 m and breadth 25 m after rounding off the value for correct significant digits is
why: 55.3 × 25 = 1382.5 m². The result can have only as many significant figures as the least precise value (25 has 2), so it rounds to 14 × 10².

q: A ball is projected with a velocity, 10 ms⁻¹, at an angle of 60° with the vertical direction. Its speed at the highest point of its trajectory will be
why: 60° with the vertical means 30° with the horizontal. At the highest point only the horizontal component remains: 10 cos30° = 5√3 ms⁻¹.

q: From Ampere's circuital law for a long straight wire of circular cross-section carrying a steady current, the variation of magnetic field in the inside and outside region of the wire is
opts: Uniform and remains constant for both the regions.
A linearly increasing function of distance upto the boundary of the wire and then linearly decreasing for the outside region.
A linearly increasing function of distance r upto the boundary of the wire and then decreasing one with 1/r dependence for the outside region.
A linearly decreasing function of distance upto the boundary of the wire and then a linearly increasing one for the outside region.
why: Inside (r < R) the enclosed current ∝ r², so B = μ₀Ir/(2πR²) ∝ r. Outside (r > R) the enclosed current is I, so B = μ₀I/(2πr) ∝ 1/r.

q: A series LCR circuit with inductance 10 H, capacitance 10 μF, resistance 50 Ω is connected to an ac source of voltage, V = 200sin(100t) volt. If the resonant frequency of the LCR circuit is ν₀ and the frequency of the ac source is ν, then
why: ω₀ = 1/√(LC) = 1/√(10 × 10⁻⁵) = 100 rad/s, and the source has ω = 100 rad/s. So ν₀ = ν = 100/2π = 50/π Hz.

q: Given below are two statements : One is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R). Assertion (A): The stretching of a spring is determined by the shear modulus of the material of the spring. Reason (R): A coil spring of copper has more tensile strength than a steel spring of same dimensions. In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below
opts: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
why: Stretching a coil spring twists its wire, so it is governed by the shear modulus: (A) is true. Steel has greater tensile strength than copper, so (R) is false.

q: A big circular coil of 1000 turns and average radius 10 m is rotating about its horizontal diameter at 2 rad s⁻¹. If the vertical component of earth's magnetic field at that place is 2 × 10⁻⁵ T and electrical resistance of the coil is 12.56 Ω, then the maximum induced current in the coil will be
why: Maximum emf = NBAω = 1000 × 2×10⁻⁵ × π(10)² × 2 = 12.56 V. Maximum current = 12.56/12.56 = 1 A.

q: The volume occupied by the molecules contained in 4.5 kg water at STP, if the intermolecular forces vanish away is
why: 4.5 kg = 4500 g of water = 4500/18 = 250 mol. With no intermolecular forces it behaves like an ideal gas: V = 250 × 22.4 L = 5600 L = 5.6 m³.

q: Two transparent media A and B are separated by a plane boundary. The speed of light in those media are 1.5 × 10⁸ m/s and 2.0 × 10⁸ m/s, respectively. The critical angle for a ray of light for these two media is
why: Refractive index n = c/v, so n_A is greater (slower medium A is denser). For total internal reflection from A to B, sin C = n_B/n_A = v_A/v_B = 1.5/2.0 = 0.75, so C = sin⁻¹(0.750).

q: A nucleus of mass number 189 splits into two nuclei having mass number 125 and 64. The ratio of radius of two daughter nuclei respectively is
why: Nuclear radius R = R₀A^(1/3). Ratio = (125/64)^(1/3) = 5/4, so 5 : 4.

q: Match List-I with List-II. List-I (Drug class): (a) Antacids; (b) Antihistamines; (c) Analgesics; (d) Antimicrobials. List-II (Drug molecule): (i) Salvarsan; (ii) Morphine; (iii) Cimetidine; (iv) Seldane. Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
why: Cimetidine is an antacid (H₂ receptor blocker), Seldane (terfenadine) is an antihistamine, morphine is a narcotic analgesic and salvarsan is an antimicrobial (antisyphilis) drug.

q: Match List-I with List-II. List – I (Hydrides): (a) MgH₂; (b) GeH₄; (c) B₂H₆; (d) HF. List – II (Nature): (i) Electron precise; (ii) Electron deficient; (iii) Electron rich; (iv) Ionic. Choose the correct answer from the options given below
why: MgH₂ is an ionic (saline) hydride, GeH₄ (group 14) is electron precise, B₂H₆ (group 13) is electron deficient and HF (group 17) has excess lone pairs, so it is electron rich.

q: The incorrect statement regarding enzymes is
opts: Like chemical catalysts enzymes reduce the activation energy of bio processes.
Enzymes are very specific for a particular reaction and substrate.
why: Enzymes are mostly globular proteins, not polysaccharides. They are biocatalysts that lower activation energy and are highly specific.

q: The IUPAC name of the complex- [Ag(H₂O)₂][Ag(CN)₂] is:
why: The cation [Ag(H₂O)₂]⁺ is diaquasilver(I) and the anion [Ag(CN)₂]⁻ is dicyanidoargentate(I); the cation is named first and Ag is +1 in both.

q: Gadolinium has a low value of third ionisation enthalpy because of
why: Removing the third electron from Gd (4f⁷5d¹6s²) gives Gd³⁺ with a stable half-filled 4f⁷ configuration, which has high exchange enthalpy, so the third ionisation enthalpy is low.

q: Amongst the following which one will have maximum ‘lone pair - lone pair’ electron repulsions?
why: XeF₂ has three lone pairs on the central atom (linear, lone pairs in the equatorial plane at 120°), more than ClF₃ (2), IF₅ (1) or SF₄ (1).

q: Which of the following statement is not correct about diborane?
opts: The four terminal B-H bonds are two centre two electron bonds.
The four terminal Hydrogen atoms and the two Boron atoms lie in one plane.
Both the Boron atoms are sp² hybridised.
why: In diborane each boron is sp³ hybridised (two sp³ orbitals form terminal 2c-2e bonds, the other two form the bridging 3c-2e bonds), so statement (4) is wrong.

q: Given below are two statements : Statement I : The boiling points of aldehydes and ketones are higher than hydrocarbons of comparable molecular masses because of weak molecular association in aldehydes and ketones due to dipole - dipole interactions. Statement II : The boiling points of aldehydes and ketones are lower than the alcohols of similar molecular masses due to the absence of H-bonding. In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the given below
opts: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
why: Carbonyl compounds are polar and show dipole-dipole attraction, so they boil higher than hydrocarbons; they cannot form intermolecular H-bonds like alcohols, so they boil lower than alcohols.

q: Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R). Assertion (A): In a particular point defect, an ionic solid is electrically neutral, even if few of its cations are missing from its unit cells. Reason (R): In an ionic solid, Frenkel defect arises due to dislocation of cation from its lattice site to interstitial site, maintaining overall electrical neutrality. In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
opts: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
why: Both statements are true: a Frenkel defect keeps the crystal neutral while a cation is displaced to an interstitial site. But the assertion refers to cations missing from the unit cell (as in Schottky-type vacancy), so R does not explain A.

q: Given below are two statements. Statement I: The boiling points of the following hydrides of group 16 elements increases in the order – H₂O < H₂S < H₂Se < H₂Te. Statement II: The boiling points of these hydrides increase with increase in molar mass. In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below :
opts: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
why: H₂O has the highest boiling point because of hydrogen bonding; the actual order is H₂S < H₂Se < H₂Te < H₂O. So the order in I is wrong and boiling points do not rise regularly with molar mass (II is wrong).

q: The incorrect statement regarding chirality is
opts: SN1 reaction yields 1 : 1 mixture of both enantiomers
The product obtained by SN2 reaction of haloalkane having chirality at the reactive site shows inversion of configuration
Enantiomers are superimposable mirror images on each other
A racemic mixture shows zero optical rotation
why: Enantiomers are non-superimposable mirror images, so statement 3 is incorrect. SN1 gives a racemic mixture (zero rotation) and SN2 gives inversion.

q: Identify the incorrect statement from the following.
opts: All the five 5d orbitals are different in size when compared to the respective 4d orbitals.
All the five 4d orbitals have shapes similar to the respective 3d orbitals.
In an atom, all the five 3d orbitals are equal in energy in free state.
The shapes of dxy, dyz and dzx orbitals are similar to each other; and dx²−y² and dz² are similar to each other.
why: dxy, dyz and dzx are alike (four lobes between axes) and dx²−y² has four lobes along the axes, but dz² has a different shape (two lobes along z with a doughnut ring), so the last statement is incorrect.

q: Choose the correct statement:
opts: Diamond and graphite have two dimensional network.
Diamond is covalent and graphite is ionic.
Diamond is sp³ hybridised and graphite is sp² hybridized.
Both diamond and graphite are used as dry lubricants.
why: Diamond has sp³ carbon in a 3D network; graphite has sp² carbon in layers. Both are covalent and only graphite is a dry lubricant.

q: Identify the incorrect statement from the following
opts: Alkali metals react with water to form their hydroxides.
The oxidation number of K in KO₂ is +4.
Ionisation enthalpy of alkali metals decreases from top to bottom in the group.
Lithium is the strongest reducing agent among the alkali metals.
why: K is always +1 in its compounds; KO₂ is a superoxide containing K⁺ and O₂⁻. So +4 is wrong.

q: Which one is not correct mathematical equation for Dalton's Law of partial pressure? Here p = total pressure of gaseous mixture
opts: pᵢ = χᵢp, where pᵢ = partial pressure of ith gas, χᵢ = mole fraction of ith gas in gaseous mixture
pᵢ = χᵢpᵢ°, where χᵢ = mole fraction of ith gas in gaseous mixture, pᵢ° = pressure of ith gas in pure state
why: pᵢ = χᵢpᵢ° is Raoult's law for a solution, not Dalton's law. Dalton's law gives p = Σpᵢ, with pᵢ = niRT/V = χᵢp.

q: Given below are two statements. Statement I: The acidic strength of monosubstituted nitrophenol is higher than phenol because of electron withdrawing nitro group. Statement II: o-nitrophenol, m-nitrophenol and p-nitrophenol will have same acidic strength as they have one nitro group attached to the phenolic ring. In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
opts: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.
why: The –NO₂ group withdraws electrons and stabilises the phenoxide, so nitrophenols are more acidic than phenol. But the effect depends on position (ortho and para show –R and –I, meta only –I), so their acidities differ.

q: At 298 K, the standard electrode potentials of Cu²⁺ / Cu, Zn²⁺ / Zn, Fe²⁺ / Fe and Ag⁺ / Ag are 0.34 V, –0.76 V, –0.44 V and 0.80 V, respectively. On the basis of standard electrode potential, predict which of the following reaction cannot occur?
why: A metal displaces another only if its E° is lower. Ag (0.80 V) is higher than Cu (0.34 V), so Ag cannot reduce Cu²⁺ (E°cell = 0.34 − 0.80 < 0).

q: Given below are two statements. Statement I: In the coagulation of a negative sol, the flocculating power of the three given ions is in the order Al³⁺ > Ba²⁺ > Na⁺. Statement II: In the coagulation of a positive sol, the flocculating power of the three given salts is in the order NaCl > Na₂SO₄ > Na₃PO₄. In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below
opts: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.
why: By the Hardy-Schulze rule, coagulating power increases with the charge of the oppositely charged ion. For a negative sol Al³⁺ > Ba²⁺ > Na⁺ (true); for a positive sol the anions act, so PO₄³⁻ > SO₄²⁻ > Cl⁻, the reverse of II.

q: Match List-I with List-II. List-I: (a) Li; (b) Na; (c) KOH; (d) Cs. List-II: (i) absorbent for carbon dioxide; (ii) electrochemical cells; (iii) coolant in fast breeder reactors; (iv) photoelectric cell. Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
why: Li is used in electrochemical cells, liquid Na as coolant in fast breeder reactors, KOH absorbs CO₂ and Cs is used in photoelectric cells.

q: Given below are two statements. Statement I: Primary aliphatic amines react with HNO₂ to give unstable diazonium salts. Statement II: Primary aromatic amines react with HNO₂ to form diazonium salts which are stable even above 300 K. In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below
opts: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.
why: Aliphatic diazonium salts are unstable and decompose to alcohols and N₂. Aromatic diazonium salts are stable only at 273–278 K and decompose above about 300 K, so II is incorrect.

q: Which statement regarding polymers is not correct?
opts: Elastomers have polymer chains held together by weak intermolecular forces
Thermoplastic polymers are capable of repeatedly softening and hardening on heating and cooling respectively
why: Thermosetting polymers (e.g. bakelite) are cross-linked, harden irreversibly on heating and cannot be remoulded, so they are not reusable.

q: In one molal solution that contains 0.5 mole of a solute, there is
why: Molality = moles of solute / kg of solvent, so 1 m = 0.5 mol / 0.5 kg, i.e. 500 g of solvent.

q: RMgX + CO₂ → (dry ether) Y → (H₃O⁺) RCOOH. What is Y in the above reaction?
why: The Grignard reagent adds to CO₂ to give the magnesium carboxylate salt RCOO⁻Mg⁺X, which on acid hydrolysis gives RCOOH.

q: Given below are half cell reactions: MnO₄⁻ + 8H⁺ + 5e⁻ → Mn²⁺ + 4H₂O, E°(Mn²⁺/MnO₄⁻) = –1.510 V; ½O₂ + 2H⁺ + 2e⁻ → H₂O, E°(O₂/H₂O) = +1.223 V. Will the permanganate ion, MnO₄⁻ liberate O₂ from water in the presence of an acid?
why: MnO₄⁻ is reduced (E° = +1.510 V) while water is oxidised to O₂ (E° = −1.223 V as oxidation), so E°cell = 1.510 − 1.223 = +0.287 V. A positive value means the reaction occurs.

q: What mass of 95% pure CaCO₃ will be required to neutralise 50 mL of 0.5 M HCl solution according to the following reaction? CaCO₃(s) + 2HCl(aq) → CaCl₂(aq) + CO₂(g) + 2H₂O(l) [Calculate upto second place of decimal point]
why: HCl = 0.05 L × 0.5 M = 0.025 mol, so CaCO₃ needed = 0.0125 mol = 1.25 g pure. For 95% purity mass = 1.25/0.95 = 1.32 g.

q: The pH of the solution containing 50 mL each of 0.10 M sodium acetate and 0.01 M acetic acid is [Given pKa of CH₃COOH = 4.57]
why: This is a buffer: pH = pKa + log([salt]/[acid]). Equal volumes dilute both equally, so the ratio stays 0.10/0.01 = 10 and pH = 4.57 + 1 = 5.57.

q: Match List-I with List-II. List – I (Products formed): (a) Cyanohydrin; (b) Acetal; (c) Schiff's base; (d) Oxime. List – II (Reaction of carbonyl compound with): (i) NH₂OH; (ii) RNH₂; (iii) alcohol; (iv) HCN. Choose the correct answer from the options given below
why: Carbonyl + HCN gives cyanohydrin, + alcohol gives acetal, + RNH₂ gives Schiff's base (imine), + NH₂OH gives oxime.

q: Which amongst the following is incorrect statement?
opts: The bond orders of O₂⁺, O₂, O₂⁻ and O₂²⁻ are 2.5, 2, 1.5 and 1, respectively
C₂ molecule has four electrons in its two degenerate π molecular orbitals
why: O₂⁺ has 15 electrons with one unpaired electron in π*2p, so it is paramagnetic. The bond orders listed in (1), the π(2p)⁴ of C₂ and the single electron of H₂⁺ are all correct.

q: Given below are two statements: Statement I: In Lucas test, primary, secondary and tertiary alcohols are distinguished on the basis of their reactivity with conc. HCl + ZnCl₂, known as Lucas Reagent. Statement II: Primary alcohols are most reactive and immediately produce turbidity at room temperature on reaction with Lucas Reagent. In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
opts: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
why: Lucas test does distinguish the three classes by reaction rate with conc. HCl/ZnCl₂. But tertiary alcohols react fastest (immediate turbidity); primary alcohols give no turbidity at room temperature.

q: If radius of second Bohr orbit of the He⁺ ion is 105.8 pm, what is the radius of third Bohr orbit of Li²⁺ ion?
For a first order reaction A → Products, initial concentration of A is 0.1 M, which becomes 0.001 M after 5 minutes. Rate constant for the reaction in min⁻¹ is
A 10.0 L flask contains 64 g of oxygen at 27°C. (Assume O₂ gas is behaving ideally). The pressure inside the flask in bar is (Given R = 0.0831 L bar K⁻¹ mol⁻¹)

The pollution due to oxides of sulphur gets enhanced due to the presence of: (a) particulate matter; (b) ozone; (c) hydrocarbons; (d) hydrogen peroxide. Choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
why: SO₂ is oxidised to SO₃ faster in the presence of particulate matter (catalytic surface) and oxidants such as ozone and hydrogen peroxide. Hydrocarbons do not enhance it.

q: Copper crystallises in fcc unit cell with cell edge length of 3.608 × 10⁻⁸ cm. The density of copper is 8.92 g cm⁻³. Calculate the atomic mass of copper.
The order of energy absorbed which is responsible for the color of complexes (A) [Ni(H₂O)₂(en)₂]²⁺ (B) [Ni(H₂O)₄(en)]²⁺ and (C) [Ni(en)₃]²⁺ is
why: Energy absorbed corresponds to the crystal field splitting Δ, which increases with more strong-field en ligands (en > H₂O). The number of en is C (3) > A (2) > B (1), so C > A > B.

q: Match List-I with List-II. List-I (Ores): (a) Haematite (b) Magnetite (c) Calamine (d) Kaolinite. List-II (Composition): (i) Fe₃O₄ (ii) ZnCO₃ (iii) Fe₂O₃ (iv) [Al₂(OH)₄Si₂O₅]. Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
why: Haematite is Fe₂O₃, magnetite is Fe₃O₄, calamine is ZnCO₃ and kaolinite is the aluminosilicate clay [Al₂(OH)₄Si₂O₅].

topic: d- and f-block KMnO4 oxidising action
q: In the neutral or faintly alkaline medium, KMnO₄ oxidises iodide into iodate. The change in oxidation state of manganese in this reaction is from
why: In neutral or weakly alkaline medium MnO₄⁻ is reduced to MnO₂, so Mn goes from +7 to +4.

q: Compound X on reaction with O₃ followed by Zn/H₂O gives formaldehyde and 2-methyl propanal as products. The compound X is
why: Ozonolysis cleaves C=C into two carbonyls: HCHO comes from =CH₂ and (CH₃)₂CHCHO from the other carbon. Joining them gives CH₂=CH–CH(CH₃)₂, i.e. 3-methylbut-1-ene.

q: 3O₂(g) ⇌ 2O₃(g). For the above reaction at 298 K, K_C is found to be 3.0 × 10⁻⁵⁹. If the concentration of O₂ at equilibrium is 0.040 M then concentration of O₃ in M is
Which of the following is not a method of ex situ conservation?
why: National Parks protect species in their natural habitat, so they are in situ conservation. The others are done outside the natural habitat.

q: Identify the correct set of statements: (a) The leaflets are modified into pointed hard thorns in Citrus and Bougainvillea (b) Axillary buds form slender and spirally coiled tendrils in cucumber and pumpkin (c) Stem is flattened and fleshy in Opuntia and modified to perform the function of leaves (d) Rhizophora shows vertically upward growing roots that help to get oxygen for respiration (e) Subaerially growing stems in grasses and strawberry help in vegetative propagation. Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
why: Thorns in Citrus and Bougainvillea are modified axillary buds, not leaflets, so (a) is wrong. Statements (b), (c), (d) and (e) are correct.

q: Given below are two statements: Statement I: Decomposition is a process in which the detritus is degraded into simpler substances by microbes. Statement II: Decomposition is faster if the detritus is rich in lignin and chitin. In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
opts: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
why: Statement I defines decomposition correctly. Detritus rich in lignin and chitin decomposes slowly; it is faster when rich in nitrogen and water-soluble sugars, so Statement II is wrong.

q: Hydrocolloid carrageen is obtained from:
why: Carrageen is obtained from red algae (Rhodophyceae). Algin comes from brown algae.

q: Which one of the following plants shows vexillary aestivation and diadelphous stamens?
why: Pisum sativum is a Fabaceae member with papilionaceous corolla showing vexillary aestivation and (9)+1 diadelphous stamens.

q: Which of the following is incorrectly matched?
why: Ulothrix is a green alga that stores starch; mannitol is a reserve food of brown algae. The other pairs are correct.

q: The process of translation of mRNA to proteins begins as soon as:
opts: The small subunit of ribosome encounters mRNA
The larger subunit of ribosome encounters mRNA
Both the subunits join together to bind with mRNA
The tRNA is activated and the larger subunit of ribosome encounters mRNA
why: Translation initiation starts when the small ribosomal subunit binds the mRNA; the large subunit joins afterwards at the start codon.

q: Match List-I with List-II. List-I: (a) Manganese (b) Magnesium (c) Boron (d) Iron. List-II: (i) Activates the enzyme catalase (ii) Required for pollen germination (iii) Activates enzymes of respiration (iv) Functions in splitting of water during photosynthesis. Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
why: Manganese is needed for water splitting, magnesium activates respiratory enzymes, boron is needed for pollen germination and iron activates catalase.

q: Which one of the following never occurs during mitotic cell division?
opts: Spindle fibres attach to kinetochores of chromosomes
Movement of centrioles towards opposite poles
Coiling and condensation of the chromatids
why: Pairing of homologous chromosomes (synapsis) occurs only in prophase I of meiosis, never in mitosis.

q: Given below are two statements: Statement I: The primary CO₂ acceptor in C₄ plants is phosphoenolpyruvate and is found in the mesophyll cells. Statement II: Mesophyll cells of C₄ plants lack RuBisCo enzyme. In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
opts: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
why: In C₄ plants PEP in mesophyll cells is the primary CO₂ acceptor, and RuBisCo is present only in bundle sheath cells, so both statements are correct.

q: Which one of the following is not true regarding the release of energy during ATP synthesis through chemiosmosis? It involves:
opts: Movement of protons across the membrane to the stroma
Reduction of NADP to NADPH₂ on the stroma side of the membrane
why: Energy for ATP synthesis comes from breakdown of the proton gradient as protons move through ATP synthase into the stroma. There is no 'electron gradient' being broken down, so option 2 is not true.

q: Habitat loss and fragmentation, over exploitation, alien species invasion and co-extinction are causes for:
why: These are the four major causes ('evil quartet') of biodiversity loss.

q: What is the net gain of ATP when each molecule of glucose is converted to two molecules of pyruvic acid?
why: Glycolysis produces 4 ATP and uses 2 ATP, so the net gain is 2 ATP per glucose.

q: "Girdling Experiment" was performed by Plant Physiologists to identify the plant tissue through which:
opts: for both water and food transportation
why: Removing a ring of bark (phloem) causes sugars to accumulate above the ring, showing that food is transported through phloem.

q: Which of the following is not observed during apoplastic pathway?
opts: Movement of water occurs through intercellular spaces and wall of the cells
The movement does not involve crossing of cell membrane
The movement is aided by cytoplasmic streaming
Apoplast is continuous and does not provide any barrier to water movement
why: Cytoplasmic streaming aids movement in the symplast, not in the apoplast, which runs through cell walls and intercellular spaces.

q: Which one of the following plants does not show plasticity?
why: Plasticity as heterophylly (different leaf forms) is shown by cotton, coriander and buttercup; maize does not show it.

topic: Human genome project and DNA fingerprinting
q: DNA polymorphism forms the basis of:
opts: Both genetic mapping and DNA finger printing
why: DNA polymorphism (variation in DNA sequence) is the basis of both genetic mapping and DNA fingerprinting.

q: XO type of sex determination can be found in:
why: In grasshoppers males have one X chromosome (XO) and females have XX. Drosophila and monkeys are XY, birds are ZW.

q: Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R). Assertion (A): Polymerase chain reaction is used in DNA amplification. Reason (R): The ampicillin resistant gene is used as a selectable marker to check transformation. In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
opts: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
why: PCR amplifies DNA, and ampicillin resistance is a selectable marker for transformants, so both are true. The marker has no role in explaining PCR amplification.

q: The gaseous plant growth regulator is used in plants to:
opts: promote root growth and root hair formation to increase the absorption surface
kill dicotyledonous weeds in the fields
why: Ethylene is the gaseous regulator; it promotes root growth and root hair formation. Gibberellin speeds malting and 2,4-D kills dicot weeds.

q: The device which can remove particulate matter present in the exhaust from a thermal power plant is:
why: An electrostatic precipitator charges particles and collects them on plates, removing over 99% of particulate matter from thermal plant exhaust.

topic: Sexual reproduction in flowering plants pollination
q: Given below are two statements: Statement I: Cleistogamous flowers are invariably autogamous. Statement II: Cleistogamy is disadvantageous as there is no chance for cross pollination. In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
opts: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
why: Cleistogamous flowers never open, so pollination is necessarily self (autogamy). With no cross pollination there is no genetic variation, which is a disadvantage.

q: Exoskeleton of arthropods is composed of:
why: The arthropod exoskeleton is made of chitin, a polymer of N-acetylglucosamine.

q: Read the following statements and choose the set of correct statements: (a) Euchromatin is loosely packed chromatin (b) Heterochromatin is transcriptionally active (c) Histone octomer is wrapped by negatively charged DNA in nucleosome (d) Histones are rich in lysine and arginine (e) A typical nucleosome contains 400 bp of DNA helix. Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
why: Heterochromatin is densely packed and transcriptionally inactive, and a nucleosome has about 200 bp of DNA, so (b) and (e) are wrong. (a), (c) and (d) are correct.

q: Which one of the following statements cannot be connected to Predation?
opts: It helps in maintaining species diversity in a community
It might lead to extinction of a species
Both the interacting species are negatively impacted
It is necessitated by nature to maintain the ecological balance
why: In predation one species (predator) benefits and the other (prey) is harmed, so both are not negatively impacted.

topic: Morphology of flowering plants flower symmetry
q: The flowers are Zygomorphic in: (a) Mustard (b) Gulmohar (c) Cassia (d) Datura (e) Chilly. Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
why: Gulmohar and Cassia (Caesalpinioideae) have zygomorphic flowers. Mustard, Datura and chilly have actinomorphic flowers.

q: Which one of the following produces nitrogen fixing nodules on the roots of Alnus?
why: Frankia, an actinomycete, forms nitrogen-fixing root nodules in Alnus.

topic: Sexual reproduction in flowering plants pollination
q: Identify the incorrect statement related to Pollination:
opts: Pollination by water is quite rare in flowering plants
Pollination by wind is more common amongst abiotic pollination
Flowers produce foul odours to attract flies and beetles to get pollinated
Moths and butterflies are the most dominant pollinating agents among insects
why: Bees are the most dominant pollinating agents among insects, not moths and butterflies.

q: Which one of the following statement is not true regarding gel electrophoresis technique?
opts: The process of extraction of separated DNA strands from gel is called elution.
The separated DNA fragments are stained by using ethidium bromide.
The presence of chromogenic substrate gives blue coloured DNA bands on the gel.
Bright orange coloured bands of DNA can be observed in the gel when exposed to UV light.
why: DNA bands are stained with ethidium bromide and appear bright orange under UV light. Chromogenic substrates are used for screening recombinants (blue colonies), not for colouring DNA bands.

q: Production of Cucumber has increased manifold in recent years. Application of which of the following phytohormones has resulted in this increased yield as the hormone is known to produce female flowers in the plants:
why: Ethylene promotes female flower formation in cucumber, increasing fruit yield.

q: What amount of energy is released from glucose during lactic acid fermentation?
why: In lactic acid fermentation less than 7% of the energy in glucose is released, and the rest remains in the products.

topic: Anatomy of flowering plants secondary growth
q: In old trees the greater part of secondary xylem is dark brown and resistant to insect attack due to: (a) secretion of secondary metabolities and their deposition in the lumen of vessels. (b) deposition of organic compounds like tannins and resins in the central layers of stem. (c) deposition of suberin and aromatic substances in the outer layer of stem. (d) deposition of tannins, gum, resin and aromatic substances in the peripheral layers of stem. (e) presence of parenchyma cells, functionally active xylem elements and essential oils. Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
why: Heartwood is the dark central part where secondary metabolites, tannins and resins are deposited in vessel lumens and central layers. Peripheral layers are sapwood, so (c), (d) and (e) do not describe heartwood.

topic: Cell cycle and cell division meiosis
q: The appearance of recombination nodules on homologous chromosomes during meiosis characterizes:
opts: Sites at which crossing over occurs
why: Recombination nodules appear during pachytene at the sites where crossing over occurs.

q: Given below are two statements: Statement I: Mendel studied seven pairs of contrasting traits in pea plants and proposed the Laws of Inheritance. Statement II: Seven characters examined by Mendel in his experiment on pea plants were seed shape and colour, flower colour, pod shape and colour, flower position and stem height. In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
opts: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
why: Mendel studied seven contrasting trait pairs: seed shape, seed colour, flower colour, pod shape, pod colour, flower position and stem height, so both statements are correct.

topic: Molecular basis of inheritance gene regulation
q: Transposons can be used during which one of the following?
