why: Transposons can insert into genes and disrupt them, so they are used as tools for gene silencing (insertional inactivation). They are not used in PCR, autoradiography or sequencing.

q: While explaining interspecific interaction of population, (+) sign is assigned for beneficial interaction, (–) sign is assigned for detrimental interaction and (0) for neutral interaction. Which of the following interactions can be assigned (+) for one specifies and (–) for another specifies involved in the interaction?
why: Predation is (+,–): predator gains and prey loses. Amensalism is (–,0), commensalism (+,0) and competition (–,–).

q: Match the plant with the kind of life cycle it exhibits. List-I: (a) Spirogyra (b) Fern (c) Funaria (d) Cycas. List-II: (i) Dominant diploid sporophyte vascular plant, with highly reduced male or female gametophyte (ii) Dominant haploid free-living gametophyte (iii) Dominant diploid sporophyte alternating with reduced gametophyte called prothallus (iv) Dominant haploid leafy gametophyte alternating with partially dependent multicellular sporophyte. Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
why: Spirogyra has a dominant haploid gametophyte, fern a dominant sporophyte with prothallus, Funaria a dominant leafy gametophyte, and Cycas a sporophyte with highly reduced gametophytes.

q: Match List-I with List-II. List-I: (a) Metacentric chromosome; (b) Acrocentric chromosome; (c) Submetacentric; (d) Telocentric chromosome. List-II: (i) Centromere situated close to the end forming one extremely short and one very long arms; (ii) Centromere at the terminal end; (iii) Centromere in the middle forming two equal arms of chromosomes; (iv) Centromere slightly away from the middle forming one shorter arm and one longer arm. Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
why: Metacentric: centromere in the middle (two equal arms). Acrocentric: centromere near one end (one very short, one very long arm). Submetacentric: slightly off-centre (one shorter, one longer arm). Telocentric: terminal centromere.

q: Addition of more solutes in a given solution will :
opts: not affect the water potential at all
why: Water potential of pure water is zero; dissolving solutes lowers it (solute potential becomes more negative).

q: Which of the following occurs due to the presence of autosome linked dominant trait ?
why: Myotonic dystrophy is an autosomal dominant disorder. Sickle cell anaemia and thalassemia are autosomal recessive; haemophilia is X-linked recessive.

q: Which one of the following will accelerate phosphorus cycle?
why: The natural reservoir of phosphorus is rock; weathering of rocks releases phosphates into soil and water, so it drives the cycle. It has no significant atmospheric component.

q: In the following palindromic base sequences of DNA, which one can be cut easily by particular restriction enzyme?
why: A palindromic sequence reads the same 5′→3′ on both strands. GAATTC (complement CTTAAG, which read 5′→3′ is GAATTC) is the EcoRI site.

q: Read the following statements on lipids and find out correct set of statements: (a) Lecithin found in the plasma membrane is a glycolipid (b) Saturated fatty acids possess one or more c = c bonds (c) Gingely oil has lower melting point, hence remains as oil in winter (d) Lipids are generally insoluble in water but soluble in some organic solvents (e) When fatty acid is esterified with glycerol, monoglycerides are formed. Choose the correct answer from the option given below:
why: Lecithin is a phospholipid, not a glycolipid, so (a) is wrong; saturated fatty acids have no C=C bonds, so (b) is wrong. (c), (d) and (e) are correct.

q: What is the role of large bundle sheath cells found around the vascular bundles in C₄ plants?
opts: To provide the site for photorespiratory pathway
To increase the number of chloroplast for the operation of Calvin cycle
To enable the plant to tolerate high temperature
To protect the vascular tissue from high light intensity
why: In C₄ plants the large bundle sheath cells contain many chloroplasts and are the site of the Calvin cycle, where CO₂ released from C₄ acids is fixed. C₄ plants lack photorespiration.

q: If a geneticist uses the blind approach for sequencing the whole genome of an organism, followed by assignment of function to different segments, the methodology adopted by him is called as :
why: In the Human Genome Project, ESTs identify expressed genes, whereas the blind approach sequences the whole genome and then assigns functions to segments, which is called sequence annotation.

q: Given below are two statements : one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R). Assertion (A) : Mendel's law of Independent assortment does not hold good for the genes that are located closely on the same chromosome. Reason (R) : Closely located genes assort independently. In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
opts: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
why: Closely linked genes tend to be inherited together (linkage), so independent assortment fails for them. The reason, that closely located genes assort independently, is false.

q: The anatomy of springwood shows some peculiar features. Identify the correct set of statements about springwood. (a) It is also called as the earlywood (b) In spring season cambium produces xylem elements with narrow vessels (c) It is lighter in colour (d) The springwood along with autumnwood shows alternate concentric rings forming annual rings (e) It has lower density. Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
why: Springwood (earlywood) is lighter, has lower density and wide-cavity vessels; with autumnwood it forms annual rings. Statement (b), narrow vessels, is false.

q: The entire fleet of buses in Delhi were converted to CNG from diesel. In reference to this, which one of the following statements is false?
opts: CNG burns more efficiently than diesel
The same diesel engine is used in CNG buses making the cost of conversion low
It cannot be adulterated like diesel
why: Diesel engines cannot run on CNG without modification, so conversion required engine changes and was not a low-cost reuse of the same engine. The other statements are true.

q: In-situ conservation refers to:
opts: Protect and conserve the whole ecosystem
why: In-situ conservation protects the whole ecosystem and its biodiversity in its natural habitat, for example national parks and sanctuaries.

q: In which of the following animals, digestive tract has additional chambers like crop and gizzard?
why: Crop and gizzard are found in the digestive tract of birds. Pavo (peacock), Psittacula (parrot) and Corvus (crow) are all birds; the other options include non-birds.

q: If the length of a DNA molecule is 1.1 metres, what will be the approximate number of base pairs?
why: Distance between two base pairs is 0.34 nm = 0.34 × 10⁻⁹ m. Number of bp = 1.1 / (0.34 × 10⁻⁹) ≈ 3.3 × 10⁹.

q: Given below are two statements : Statement I : Fatty acids and glycerols cannot be absorbed into the blood. Statement II : Specialized lymphatic capillaries called lacteals carry chylomicrons into lymphatic vessels and ultimately into the blood. In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
opts: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
why: Fatty acids and glycerol are insoluble, so they are incorporated into micelles and then chylomicrons, which enter lacteals and reach the blood via lymph. Both statements follow the NCERT account.

q: Given below are two statements: Statement I: Autoimmune disorder is a condition where body defense mechanism recognizes its own cells as foreign bodies. Statement II: Rheumatoid arthritis is a condition where body does not attack self cells. In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
opts: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
why: Autoimmunity is the body attacking its own cells, so Statement I is true. Rheumatoid arthritis is an autoimmune disease, so Statement II is false.

q: Which of the following statements are true for spermatogenesis but do not hold true for Oogenesis? (a) It results in the formation of haploid gametes (b) Differentiation of gamete occurs after the completion of meiosis (c) Meiosis occurs continuously in a mitotically dividing stem cell population (d) It is controlled by the Luteinising hormone (LH) and Follicle Stimulating Hormone (FSH) secreted by the anterior pituitary (e) It is initiated at puberty. Choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
why: Both processes yield haploid gametes and are controlled by LH and FSH. Only spermatogenesis has gamete differentiation (spermiogenesis) after meiosis, continuous meiosis from a dividing stem cell population, and initiation at puberty (oogenesis begins in the foetus).

q: Given below are two statements : one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R). Assertion (A): Osteoporosis is characterised by decreased bone mass and increased chance of fractures. Reason (R): Common cause of osteoporosis is increased levels of estrogen. In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below.
opts: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
why: Osteoporosis does reduce bone mass and raise fracture risk, but a common cause is decreased (not increased) oestrogen level with age.

q: Given below are two statements: Statement I: Restriction endonucleases recognise specific sequence to cut DNA known as palindromic nucleotide sequence. Statement II: Restriction endonucleases cut the DNA strand a little away from the centre of the palindromic site. In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
opts: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
why: Restriction enzymes recognise palindromic sequences and cut each strand slightly off the centre of the site, giving sticky ends. Both statements are true.

q: Lippe's loop is a type of contraceptive used as:
why: Lippes loop is a non-medicated intrauterine device; copper-releasing IUDs include CuT, Cu7 and Multiload 375.

q: Under normal physiological conditions in human being every 100 ml of oxygenated blood can deliver ________ ml of O₂ to the tissues.
why: Every 100 ml of oxygenated blood delivers about 5 ml of O₂ to the tissues under normal conditions (NCERT).

q: Given below are two statements : one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R). Assertion (A) : All vertebrates are chordates but all chordates are not vertebrates. Reason (R) : Notochord is replaced by vertebral column in the adult vertebrates. In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the option given below :
opts: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
why: All chordates have a notochord at some stage; in vertebrates it is replaced by the vertebral column, whereas urochordates and cephalochordates lack a vertebral column. So R explains A.

q: Which of the following is not a connective tissue?
why: Blood, adipose tissue and cartilage are connective tissues; neuroglia are supporting cells of nervous tissue.

q: Nitrogenous waste is excreted in the form of pellet or paste by :
why: Birds such as Pavo (peacock) are uricotelic and excrete uric acid as a pellet or paste with minimal water loss.

q: Regarding Meiosis, which of the statements is incorrect?
opts: There are two stages in Meiosis, Meiosis-I and II
DNA replication occurs in S phase of Meiosis-II
Pairing of homologous chromosomes and recombination occurs in Meiosis-I
Four haploid cells are formed at the end of Meiosis-II
why: DNA replicates only once, in the S phase before meiosis I; there is no S phase between meiosis I and II.

q: In an E. Coli strain i gene gets mutated and its product can not bind the inducer molecule. If growth medium is provided with lactose, what will be the outcome?
opts: Only z gene will get transcribed
z, y, a genes will be transcribed
z, y, a genes will not be translated
RNA polymerase will bind the promoter region
why: The mutant repressor cannot bind the inducer (allolactose), so it stays bound to the operator and blocks transcription of z, y and a. With no mRNA, these genes are not translated.

q: Which of the following is a correct match for disease and its symptoms?
opts: Tetany – High Ca²⁺ level causing rapid spasms.
Myasthenia gravis – Genetic disorder resulting in weakening and paralysis of skeletal muscle
Muscular dystrophy – An auto immune disorder causing progressive degeneration of skeletal muscle
why: Arthritis is inflammation of joints. Tetany is due to low Ca²⁺; myasthenia gravis is autoimmune; muscular dystrophy is genetic.

q: Identify the microorganism which is responsible for the production of an immunosuppressive molecule cyclosporin A :
why: Cyclosporin A, used as an immunosuppressant in organ transplants, is produced by the fungus Trichoderma polysporum.

q: Given below are two statements : Statement I : Mycoplasma can pass through less than 1 micron filter size. Statement II : Mycoplasma are bacteria with cell wall. In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below
opts: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
why: Mycoplasma are the smallest living cells and can pass through filters under 1 micron, but they completely lack a cell wall.

q: Which of the following functions is not performed by secretions from salivary glands?
why: Saliva contains lysozyme (antibacterial), mucus (lubrication) and salivary amylase (starch digestion). Disaccharides are digested by intestinal enzymes, not by saliva.

q: Given below are two statements : Statement I : The coagulum is formed of network of threads called thrombins. Statement II : Spleen is the graveyard of erythrocytes. In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below :
opts: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
why: The clot is a network of fibrin threads (thrombin is the enzyme that makes fibrin), so Statement I is wrong. The spleen destroys old RBCs, so Statement II is correct.

q: A dehydration reaction links two glucose molecules to product maltose. If the formula for glucose is C₆H₁₂O₆ then what is the formula for maltose?
why: Two glucose molecules give C₁₂H₂₄O₁₂; losing one H₂O in the dehydration (condensation) reaction gives C₁₂H₂₂O₁₁.

q: Which of the following statements with respect to Endoplasmic Reticulum is incorrect?
opts: RER has ribosomes attached to ER
In prokaryotes only RER are present
SER are the sites for lipid synthesis
why: Prokaryotes have no endoplasmic reticulum at all; ER is a eukaryotic organelle. The other statements are correct.

q: Which of the following is present between the adjacent bones of the vertebral column?
why: Cartilage forms the intervertebral discs between adjacent vertebrae. Intercalated discs belong to cardiac muscle.

q: Tegmina in cockroach, arises from
why: The forewings (tegmina) are opaque and arise from the mesothorax; the hindwings, which are membranous, arise from the metathorax.

q: Given below are two statements: Statement I : The release of sperms into the seminiferous tubules is called spermiation. Statement II : Spermiogenesis is the process of formation of sperms from spermatogonia. In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below :
opts: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
why: Spermiation is the release of sperms into the seminiferous tubule lumen. Spermiogenesis is the transformation of spermatids into sperms; formation of sperms from spermatogonia is spermatogenesis.

q: If '8' Drosophila in a laboratory population of '80' died during a week, the death rate in the population is ______ individuals per Drosophila per week.
why: Death rate = number died / population size = 8 / 80 = 0.1 per individual per week.

q: Natural selection where more individuals acquire specific character value other than the mean character value, leads to
why: When more individuals shift to one extreme of the character value, the population mean moves in that direction, which is directional selection.

q: Which of the following is not the function of conducting part of respiratory system?
opts: It clears inhaled air from foreign particles
Temperature of inhaled air is brought to body temperature
Provides surface for diffusion of O₂ and CO₂
why: The conducting part (nostrils to terminal bronchioles) filters, humidifies and warms air. Gas diffusion occurs only in the alveoli of the exchange part.

topic: Strategies for enhancement in food production
q: Breeding crops with higher levels of vitamins and minerals or higher proteins and healthier fats is called :
why: Breeding crops for higher nutrient content (vitamins, minerals, proteins, healthy fats) is biofortification.

q: In the taxonomic categories which hierarchical arrangement in ascending order is correct in case of animals?
opts: Kingdom, Phylum, Class, Order, Family, Genus, Species
Kingdom, Class, Phylum, Family, Order, Genus, Species
Kingdom, Order, Class, Phylum, Family, Genus, Species
Kingdom, Order, Phylum, Class, Family, Genus, Species
why: Only option 1 gives the correct sequence of categories (Kingdom, Phylum, Class, Order, Family, Genus, Species); the others misplace ranks. The question's wording (ascending) is loose, as this list runs from the highest rank down.

q: At which stage of life the oogenesis process is initiated?
why: Oogenesis starts in the foetal ovary, where oogonia form and enter meiosis I to become primary oocytes arrested at prophase I.

q: Identify the asexual reproductive structure associated with Penicillium :
why: Penicillium reproduces asexually by conidia. Zoospores are in algae, gemmules in sponges and buds in yeast and Hydra.

q: In gene therapy of Adenosine Deaminase (ADA) deficiency, the patient requires periodic infusion of genetically engineered lymphocytes because :
opts: Retroviral vector is introduced into these lymphocytes.
Gene isolated from marrow cells producing ADA is introduced into cells at embryonic stages
Lymphocytes from patient's blood are grown in culture, outside the body.
Genetically engineered lymphocytes are not immortal cells.
why: The engineered lymphocytes are short-lived (not immortal), so the patient needs periodic infusions unless the ADA gene is introduced into marrow stem cells.

q: Select the incorrect statement with reference to mitosis:
opts: All the chromosomes lie at the equator at metaphase
Spindle fibres attach to centromere of chromosomes
Splitting of centromere occurs at anaphase
why: Spindle fibres attach to the kinetochores (protein discs on the centromere), not to the centromere itself; the other statements are correct.

q: Detritivores breakdown detritus into smaller particles. This process is called:
why: Breakdown of detritus into smaller particles by detritivores such as earthworms is fragmentation, the first step of decomposition.

q: If a colour blind female marries a man whose mother was also colour blind, what are the chances of her progeny having colour blindness?
why: The man's X chromosome comes from his colour blind mother (XcXc), so he is XcY and colour blind. The colour blind woman is XcXc, so all sons (XcY) and all daughters (XcXc) are colour blind: 100%.

q: Select the incorrect statement with respect to acquired immunity.
opts: Primary response is produced when our body encounters a pathogen for the first time.
Anamnestic response is elicited on subsequent encounters with the same pathogen.
Anamnestic response is due to memory of first encounter.
Acquired immunity is non-specific type of defense present at the time of birth.
why: Acquired immunity is pathogen-specific and develops after exposure; the non-specific defence present at birth is innate immunity.

q: Which one of the following statements is correct?
opts: The atrio-ventricular node (AVN) generates an action potential to stimulate atrial contraction
The tricuspid and the bicuspid valves open due to the pressure exerted by the simultaneous contraction of the atria
Blood moves freely from atrium to the ventricle during joint diastole.
Increased ventricular pressure causes closing of the semilunar valves.
why: During joint diastole the AV valves are open and blood flows passively from atria to ventricles. The SAN (not AVN) initiates atrial contraction, and rising ventricular pressure closes the AV valves, not the semilunar valves.

q:
Match List-I with List-II
List-I (Biological Molecules): (a) Glycogen; (b) Globulin; (c) Steroids; (d) Thrombin
List-II (Biological functions): (i) Hormone; (ii) Biocatalyst; (iii) Antibody; (iv) Storage product
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
why: Glycogen is a storage polysaccharide, globulins include antibodies, steroids include hormones, and thrombin is an enzyme (biocatalyst).

q: Ten E.coli cells with ¹⁵N - dsDNA are incubated in medium containing ¹⁴N nucleotide. After 60 minutes, how many E.coli cells will have DNA totally free from ¹⁵N?
why: E. coli divides every 20 minutes, so 60 minutes is 3 generations: each cell gives 8 cells (80 in all). Semi-conservative replication leaves only 2 of the 8 cells per original cell with a ¹⁵N strand, so 6 × 10 = 60 cells have only ¹⁴N DNA.

q: The recombination frequency between the genes a & c is 5%, b & c is 15%, b & d is 9%, a & b is 20%, c & d is 24% and a & d is 29%. What will be the sequence of these genes on a linear chromosome?
why: Recombination frequency is proportional to distance. Order a-c-b-d gives a-c 5, c-b 15 (a-b 20), b-d 9 (c-d 24, a-d 29), which matches all the data.

q:
Which of the following are not the effects of Parathyroid hormone?
(a) Stimulates the process of bone resorption
(b) Decreases Ca²⁺ level in blood
(c) Reabsorption of Ca²⁺ by renal tubules
(d) Decreases the absorption of Ca²⁺ from digested food
(e) Increases metabolism of carbohydrates
Choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
why: PTH raises blood Ca²⁺ by stimulating bone resorption, increasing renal reabsorption and increasing absorption from food. So decreasing blood Ca²⁺, decreasing absorption and increasing carbohydrate metabolism are not its effects.

q: Which of the following is not a desirable feature of a cloning vector?
opts: Presence of single restriction enzyme site
Presence of two or more recognition sites
why: A cloning vector needs an origin of replication, a selectable marker and a single recognition site for the restriction enzyme. Two or more sites would cut the vector into fragments.

q: Which of the following statements is not true?
opts: Analogous structures are a result of convergent evolution
Sweet potato and potato is an example of analogy
Flippers of penguins and dolphins are a pair of homologous organs
why: Flippers of penguins and dolphins have different origins but similar function, so they are analogous (convergent evolution), not homologous.

q: Select the incorrect statement regarding synapses :
opts: The membranes of presynaptic and postsynaptic neurons are in close proximity in an electrical synapse.
Electrical current can flow directly from one neuron into the other across the electrical synapse.
Impulse transmission across a chemical synapse is always faster than that across an electrical synapse.
why: Electrical synapses transmit faster because current flows directly; chemical synapses are slower due to neurotransmitter release and diffusion.

q:
Match List-I with List-II
List-I: (a) Bronchioles; (b) Goblet Cell; (c) Tendons; (d) Adipose Tissue
List-II: (i) Dense Regular Connective Tissue; (ii) Loose Connective Tissue; (iii) Glandular Tissue; (iv) Ciliated Epithelium
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
why: Bronchioles are lined by ciliated epithelium, goblet cells are unicellular glands, tendons are dense regular connective tissue, and adipose tissue is a type of loose connective tissue.

q:
Match List-I with List-II with respect to methods of Contraception and their respective actions.
List-I: (a) Diaphragms; (b) Contraceptive Pills; (c) Intra Uterine Devices; (d) Lactational Amenorrhea
List-II: (i) Inhibit ovulation and Implantation; (ii) Increase phagocytosis of sperm within Uterus; (iii) Absence of Menstrual cycle and ovulation following parturition; (iv) They cover the cervix blocking the entry of sperms
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
why: Diaphragms cover the cervix; pills inhibit ovulation and implantation; IUDs increase phagocytosis of sperm in the uterus; lactational amenorrhea means no menstrual cycle or ovulation after parturition.

q: Which of the following is a correct statement?
opts: Cyanobacteria are a group of autotrophic organisms classified under kingdom Monera.
Slime moulds are saprophytic organisms classified under Kingdom Monera.
Mycoplasma have DNA, ribosome and cell wall.
why: Cyanobacteria are photosynthetic prokaryotes placed in Monera. Bacteria can be autotrophic or heterotrophic, slime moulds belong to Protista, and mycoplasma lack a cell wall.

q:
Given below are two statements:
Statements I : In a scrubber the exhaust from the thermal plant is passed through the electric wires to charge the dust particles.
Statement II : Particulate matter (PM 2.5) cannot be removed by scrubber but can be removed by an electrostatic precipitator.
In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below :
opts: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
why: Charging dust particles with electric wires is how an electrostatic precipitator works, not a scrubber, so Statement I is incorrect. A scrubber removes gases such as SO₂, while fine particulates are removed by an electrostatic precipitator, so Statement II is correct.

q: A full wave rectifier circuit consists of two p-n junction diodes, a centre-tapped transformer, capacitor and a load resistance. Which of these components remove the ac ripple from the rectified output?
why: The capacitor acts as a filter: it charges to the peak and discharges slowly through the load, smoothing out the ac ripple. The diodes rectify and the transformer supplies the two phases.

q: Light travels a distance x in time t₁ in air and 10x in time t₂ in another denser medium. What is the critical angle for this medium?
why: Speed in air c = x/t₁, in the medium v = 10x/t₂, so n = c/v = t₂/(10t₁). Critical angle: sin θc = 1/n = 10t₁/t₂.

q: Resistance of a carbon resistor determined from colour codes is (22000 ± 5%) Ω. The colour of third band must be :
why: 22000 Ω = 22 × 10³ Ω. The first two bands give 2 and 2 (red, red) and the third band is the multiplier 10³, which is orange.

q: Given below are two statements: Statement I : Photovoltaic devices can convert optical radiation into electricity. Statement II : Zener diode is designed to operate under reverse bias in breakdown region. In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below :
opts: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.
why: Solar cells and photodiodes (photovoltaic devices) convert optical radiation to electricity, and a Zener diode is designed to work in reverse-bias breakdown as a voltage regulator. Both statements are correct.

q: The magnetic energy stored in an inductor of inductance 4 μH carrying a current of 2 A is :
The angular acceleration of a body, moving along the circumference of a circle, is :
opts: along the radius, away from centre
along the radius towards the centre
along the tangent to its position
why: Angular acceleration α = dω/dt is an axial vector, directed along the axis of rotation (same line as ω).

q: A Carnot engine has an efficiency of 50% when its source is at a temperature 327° C. The temperature of the sink is :
why: η = 1 − T₂/T₁ gives 0.5 = 1 − T₂/600, so T₂ = 300 K = 27° C.

q: Two bodies of mass m and 9m are placed at a distance R. The gravitational potential on the line joining the bodies where the gravitational field equals zero, will be (G = gravitational constant) :
why: Field zero at distance x from m: m/x² = 9m/(R−x)², so R−x = 3x and x = R/4. Potential V = −Gm/(R/4) − 9Gm/(3R/4) = −4Gm/R − 12Gm/R = −16Gm/R.

q: A vehicle travels half the distance with speed ϑ and the remaining distance with speed 2ϑ. Its average speed is:
why: For equal distances, average speed = 2v₁v₂/(v₁+v₂) = 2·ϑ·2ϑ/(3ϑ) = 4ϑ/3.

q: The amount of energy required to form a soap bubble of radius 2 cm from a soap solution is nearly : (surface tension of soap solution = 0.03 N m⁻¹)
why: A soap bubble has two surfaces, so W = T × 2 × 4πr² = 0.03 × 8π × (0.02)² = 0.03 × 8π × 4×10⁻⁴ ≈ 3.01×10⁻⁴ J.

q: The minimum wavelength of X-rays produced by an electron accelerated through a potential difference of V volts is proportional to:
why: eV = hc/λmin, so λmin = hc/(eV) ∝ 1/V.

q: The half life of a radioactive substance is 20 minutes. In how much time, the activity of substance drops to (1/16)th of its initial value?
why: 1/16 = (1/2)⁴, so four half-lives are needed: 4 × 20 = 80 minutes.

q: A metal wire has mass (0.4 ± 0.002) g, radius (0.3 ± 0.001) mm and length (5 ± 0.02) cm. The maximum possible percentage error in the measurement of density will nearly be:

In a plane electromagnetic wave travelling in free space, the electric field component oscillates sinusoidally at a frequency of 2.0×10¹⁰ Hz and amplitude 48 V m⁻¹. Then the amplitude of oscillating magnetic field is : (Speed of light in free space = 3 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹)
The temperature of a gas is −50° C. To what temperature should the gas be heated so that the rms speed is increased by 3 times?
why: v_rms ∝ √T. Increased by 3 times means the new speed is 4 times the old one, so T₂ = 16 × 223 K = 3568 K = 3295° C.

q: An ac source is connected to a capacitor C. Due to decrease in its operating frequency :
why: Xc = 1/(2πfC) increases when f decreases, so the current in the circuit falls. Displacement current equals the conduction current, so it decreases.

q: For Young's double slit experiment, two statements are given below: Statement I : If screen is moved away from the plane of slits, angular separation of the fringes remains constant. Statement II : If the monochromatic source is replaced by another monochromatic source of larger wavelength, the angular separation of fringes decreases. In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
opts: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.
why: Angular fringe separation θ = λ/d does not depend on the screen distance, so I is true. It increases with λ, so II (decreases) is false.

q: In hydrogen spectrum, the shortest wavelength in the Balmer series is λ. The shortest wavelength in the Bracket series is :
why: Shortest wavelength corresponds to n → ∞: 1/λ = R/n². Balmer (n=2): λ = 4/R. Brackett (n=4): λ' = 16/R = 4λ.

q: The errors in the measurement which arise due to unpredictable fluctuations in temperature and voltage supply are :
why: Errors from unpredictable fluctuations in conditions such as temperature or voltage supply are random errors.

q: In a series LCR circuit, the inductance L is 10 mH, capacitance C is 1 μF and resistance R is 100 Ω. The frequency at which resonance occurs is :
The venturi-meter works on :
why: A venturi-meter measures fluid flow speed using the pressure difference between wide and narrow sections, which follows from Bernoulli's principle.

q: The ratio of frequencies of fundamental harmonic produced by an open pipe to that of closed pipe having the same length is :
why: Open pipe fundamental f = v/2L; closed pipe f = v/4L. Ratio = 2 : 1.

q: An electric dipole is placed at an angle of 30° with an electric field of intensity 2×10⁵ N C⁻¹. It experiences a torque equal to 4 N m. Calculate the magnitude of charge on the dipole, if the dipole length is 2 cm.
The net magnetic flux through any closed surface is :
why: Gauss's law for magnetism: magnetic monopoles do not exist, so the net flux through any closed surface is zero.

q: A bullet is fired from a gun at the speed of 280 m s⁻¹ in the direction 30° above the horizontal. The maximum height attained by the bullet is (g = 9.8 m s⁻², sin 30° = 0.5) :

Two thin lenses are of same focal lengths (f), but one is convex and the other one is concave. When they are placed in contact with each other, the equivalent focal length of the combination will be :
why: 1/F = 1/f + 1/(−f) = 0, so the combination has zero power and infinite focal length.

q: A bullet from a gun is fired on a rectangular wooden block with velocity u. When bullet travels 24 cm through the block along its length horizontally, velocity of bullet becomes u/3. Then it further penetrates into the block in the same direction before coming to rest exactly at the other end of the block. The total length of the block is :
why: With constant retardation a: (u/3)² = u² − 2a(24) gives a = u²/54. Total length L satisfies 0 = u² − 2aL, so L = u²/(2a) = 27 cm.

q: A horizontal bridge is built across a river. A student standing on the bridge throws a small ball vertically upwards with a velocity 4 m s⁻¹. The ball strikes the water surface after 4 s. The height of bridge above water surface is (Take g = 10 m s⁻²) :
why: Taking up as positive, displacement s = ut − ½gt² = 4×4 − 5×16 = −64 m. The bridge is 64 m above the water.

q: 10 resistors, each of resistance R are connected in series to a battery of emf E and negligible internal resistance. Then those are connected in parallel to the same battery, the current is increased n times. The value of n is :
why: Series: I₁ = E/(10R). Parallel: R_eq = R/10, I₂ = 10E/R. Ratio n = I₂/I₁ = 100.

q: A wire carrying a current I along the positive x-axis has length L. It is kept in a magnetic field B = (2î + 3ĵ − 4k̂) T. The magnitude of the magnetic force acting on the wire is :
why: F = IL î × B = IL(3 k̂ + 4 ĵ), since î×ĵ = k̂ and î×(−4k̂) = 4ĵ. Magnitude = IL√(3² + 4²) = 5IL.

q: A satellite is orbiting just above the surface of the earth with period T. If d is the density of the earth and G is the universal constant of gravitation, the quantity 3π/(Gd) represents :
why: For a near-surface orbit T² = 4π²R³/(GM) with M = (4/3)πR³d, giving T² = 3π/(Gd).

q: Calculate the maximum acceleration of a moving car so that a body lying on the floor of the car remains stationary. The coefficient of static friction between the body and the floor is 0.15 (g = 10 m s⁻²).
why: Friction supplies the acceleration: a_max = μg = 0.15 × 10 = 1.5 m s⁻².

q: The resistance of platinum wire at 0°C is 2 Ω and 6.8 Ω at 80°C. The temperature coefficient of resistance of the wire is :
The radius of inner most orbit of hydrogen atom is 5.3×10⁻¹¹ m. What is the radius of third allowed orbit of hydrogen atom?
why: rₙ ∝ n², so r₃ = 9 × 0.53 Å = 4.77 Å.

q: Which of the following reactions will NOT give primary amine as the product?
why: Hofmann bromamide gives CH₃NH₂, and LiAlH₄ reduces nitriles and amides to primary amines (CH₃CH₂NH₂). Reduction of an isocyanide CH₃NC gives the secondary amine CH₃NHCH₃.

q: Match List - I with List - II : List I: A. Coke; B. Diamond; C. Fullerene; D. Graphite  List II: I. Carbon atoms are sp³ hybridised.; II. Used as a dry lubricant; III. Used as a reducing agent; IV. Cage like molecules. Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
why: Coke is a reducing agent (III), diamond has sp³ carbons (I), fullerene is a cage-like molecule (IV), graphite is a dry lubricant (II). So A-III, B-I, C-IV, D-II.

q: Given below are two statements : one is labelled as Assertion A and the other is labelled as Reason R : Assertion A : Metallic sodium dissolves in liquid ammonia giving a deep blue solution, which is paramagnetic. Reason R : The deep blue solution is due to the formation of amide. In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below :
opts: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.
why: The blue paramagnetic solution is due to ammoniated electrons, e⁻(NH₃)ₓ, so A is true. Amide formation happens slowly on standing and does not cause the blue colour, so R is false.

q: In Lassaigne's extract of an organic compound, both nitrogen and sulphur are present, which gives blood red colour with Fe³⁺ due to the formation of -
why: When both N and S are present, sodium thiocyanate forms and gives the blood-red [Fe(SCN)]²⁺ complex with Fe³⁺.

q: The conductivity of centimolar solution of KCl at 25°C is 0.0210 ohm⁻¹ cm⁻¹ and the resistance of the cell containing the solution at 25°C is 60 ohm. The value of cell constant is -
why: Cell constant = κ × R = 0.0210 × 60 = 1.26 cm⁻¹.

q: Which one is an example of heterogenous catalysis?
opts: Oxidation of sulphur dioxide into sulphur trioxide in the presence of oxides of nitrogen.
Hydrolysis of sugar catalysed by H⁺ ions.
Decomposition of ozone in presence of nitrogen monoxide.
Combination between dinitrogen and dihydrogen to form ammonia in the presence of finely divided iron.
why: In heterogeneous catalysis the catalyst is in a different phase from the reactants. Solid iron with gaseous N₂ and H₂ (Haber process) fits; the others are all in a single phase.

q: The given compound C₆H₅–CH=CH–CH(X)–CH₂CH₃ (a benzene ring attached to CH=CH–CH(X)–CH₂CH₃) is an example of ________.
why: The halogen X is on an sp³ carbon next to a C=C double bond, which is an allylic halide.

q: Given below are two statements : one is labelled as Assertion A and the other is labelled as Reason R : Assertion A : Helium is used to dilute oxygen in diving apparatus. Reasons R : Helium has high solubility in O₂. In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below :
opts: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true and R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is false.
why: Helium is mixed with oxygen for divers because it has very low solubility in blood, so A is true. R (high solubility) is false.

q: A compound is formed by two elements A and B. The element B forms cubic close packed structure and atoms of A occupy 1/3 of tetrahedral voids. If the formula of the compound is AₓB_y, then the value of x + y is in option
why: ccp gives 4 B atoms and 8 tetrahedral voids per cell. A = (1/3) × 8 = 8/3, so A₈/₃B₄ = A₂B₃. x + y = 5.

q: Given below are two statements : Statement I : A unit formed by the attachment of a base to 1' position of sugar is known as nucleoside. Statement II : When nucleoside is linked to phosphorous acid at 5'-position of sugar moiety, we get nucleotide. In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below :
opts: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.
why: A base joined to the 1' carbon of the sugar is a nucleoside, so I is true. A nucleotide forms when the nucleoside is esterified with phosphoric acid (not phosphorous acid) at the 5' position, so II is false.

q: The relation between nₘ, (nₘ = the number of permissible values of magnetic quantum number (m)) for a given value of azimuthal quantum number (l), is
why: For a given l, m runs from −l to +l, so nₘ = 2l + 1. Rearranging gives l = (nₘ − 1)/2.

q: Amongst the following, the total number of species NOT having eight electrons around central atom in its outer most shell, is NH₃, AlCl₃, BeCl₂, CCl₄, PCl₅ :
why: NH₃ (3 bond pairs + 1 lone pair) and CCl₄ have an octet. AlCl₃ has 6, BeCl₂ has 4 and PCl₅ has 10 electrons, so 3 species do not have an octet.

q: The correct order of energies of molecular orbitals of N₂ molecule is :
opts: σ1s < σ*1s < σ2s < σ*2s < (π2pₓ = π2p_y) < σ2p_z < (π*2pₓ = π*2p_y) < σ*2p_z
σ1s < σ*1s < σ2s < σ*2s < σ2p_z < (π2pₓ = π2p_y) < (π*2pₓ = π*2p_y) < σ*2p_z
σ1s < σ*1s < σ2s < σ*2s < σ2p_z < σ*2p_z < (π2pₓ = π2p_y) < (π*2pₓ = π*2p_y)
σ1s < σ*1s < σ2s < σ*2s < (π2pₓ = π2p_y) < (π*2pₓ = π*2p_y) < σ2p_z < σ*2p_z
why: For N₂ (and other molecules up to N₂) s-p mixing makes the π2p orbitals lower in energy than σ2p_z. The order is σ2s < σ*2s < π2p < σ2p_z < π*2p < σ*2p_z.

q: The number of σ bonds, π bonds and lone pair of electrons in pyridine, respectively are:
why: Pyridine C₅H₅N has 5 C–H σ bonds plus 6 ring σ bonds = 11 σ bonds, 3 π bonds (alternate double bonds) and 1 lone pair on nitrogen.

q: Intermolecular forces are forces of attraction and repulsion between interacting particles that will include : A. dipole - dipole forces. B. dipole - induced dipole forces. C. hydrogen bonding. D. covalent bonding. E. dispersion forces. Choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below :
opts: B, C, D, E are correct.
A, B, C, D are correct.
A, B, C, E are correct.
A, C, D, E are correct.
why: Covalent bonding is an intramolecular force, not intermolecular. Dipole-dipole, dipole-induced dipole, hydrogen bonding and dispersion forces are intermolecular.

q: Which of the following statements are NOT correct? A. Hydrogen is used to reduce heavy metal oxides to metals. B. Heavy water is used to study reaction mechanism. C. Hydrogen is used to make saturated fats from oils. D. The H-H bond dissociation enthalpy is lowest as compared to a single bond between two atoms of any element. E. Hydrogen reduces oxides of metals that are more active than iron. Choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below :
why: The H-H bond enthalpy (435.88 kJ/mol) is the highest for a single bond between two atoms of any element, so D is wrong. Hydrogen does not reduce oxides of metals more active than iron, so E is wrong. A, B, C are correct.

q: Which amongst the following molecules on polymerization produces neoprene?
why: Neoprene is the polymer of chloroprene (2-chlorobuta-1,3-diene), H₂C=C(Cl)–CH=CH₂.

q: Some tranquilizers are listed below. Which one from the following belongs to barbiturates?
why: Veronal, luminal and seconal are barbiturates. Chlordiazepoxide and Valium are benzodiazepines, and meprobamate is a different tranquilizer.

topic: Periodic properties atomic and ionic radii
q: The element expected to form largest ion to achieve the nearest noble gas configuration is :
why: O²⁻, F⁻ and N³⁻ are isoelectronic with Na⁺ and all have 10 electrons; the one with the lowest nuclear charge (N³⁻, Z = 7) is the largest. Na forms a small cation.

q: Select the correct statements from the following : A. Atoms of all elements are composed of two fundamental particles. B. The mass of the electron is 9.10939 × 10⁻³¹ kg. C. All the isotopes of a given element show same chemical properties. D. Protons and electrons are collectively known as nucleons. E. Dalton's atomic theory, regarded the atom as an ultimate particle of matter. Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
why: Atoms have three fundamental particles (electron, proton, neutron), so A is wrong. Protons and neutrons are nucleons, so D is wrong. B, C and E are correct.

q: Consider the following reaction and identify the product (P). 3-Methylbutan-2-ol, CH₃–CH(CH₃)–CH(OH)–CH₃, reacts with HBr to give Product (P).
why: Protonation and loss of water give a secondary carbocation, which undergoes a 1,2-hydride shift to the more stable tertiary carbocation. Br⁻ then attacks to give 2-bromo-2-methylbutane.

q: The stability of Cu²⁺ is more than Cu⁺ salts in aqueous solution due to -
why: Cu²⁺ has a much more negative hydration enthalpy than Cu⁺, which more than compensates for the second ionisation enthalpy, so Cu²⁺(aq) is more stable.

q: Weight (g) of two moles of the organic compound, which is obtained by heating sodium ethanoate with sodium hydroxide in presence of calcium oxide is :
why: Soda-lime decarboxylation of CH₃COONa gives methane (CH₄, molar mass 16 g/mol). Two moles weigh 32 g.

q: Amongst the given options which of the following molecules / ion acts as a Lewis acid?
why: BF₃ has an incomplete octet (6 electrons on boron) and accepts an electron pair, so it is a Lewis acid. The others have lone pairs to donate.

topic: p-block elements group 13 inert pair effect
q: Taking stability as the factor, which one of the following represents correct relationship?
why: Because of the inert pair effect the +1 state becomes more stable down group 13. Tl(I) is more stable than Tl(III), so TlI > TlI₃, while Al(III) is more stable than Al(I).

q: Homoleptic complex from the following complexes is :
why: A homoleptic complex has only one kind of ligand. K₃[Al(C₂O₄)₃] has only oxalate ligands; the others carry two or more different ligands.

q: The right option for the mass of CO₂ produced by heating 20 g of 20% pure limestone is (Atomic mass of Ca = 40) CaCO₃ → (1200 K) CaO + CO₂
why: Pure CaCO₃ = 0.20 × 20 = 4 g = 0.04 mol. Each mole gives 1 mol CO₂, so mass = 0.04 × 44 = 1.76 g.

q: For a certain reaction, the rate = k[A]²[B], when the initial concentration of A is tripled keeping concentration of B constant, the initial rate would
opts: decrease by a factor of nine.
increase by a factor of six.
increase by a factor of nine.
increase by a factor of three.
why: Rate ∝ [A]², so tripling [A] multiplies the rate by 3² = 9.

q: Given below are two statements : one is labelled as Assertion A and the other is labelled as Reason R : Assertion A : In equation ΔrG = −nFE_cell, value of ΔrG depends on n. Reason R : E_cell is an intensive property and ΔrG is an extensive property. In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below :
opts: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true and R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.
why: E_cell is intensive while ΔrG is extensive; ΔrG scales with the number of electrons n (amount of reaction), so R correctly explains A.

q: Match List - I with List - II : List I (Oxoacids of Sulphur): A. Peroxodisulphuric acid; B. Sulphuric acid; C. Pyrosulphuric acid; D. Sulphurous acid.  List II (Bonds): I. Two S-OH, Four S=O, One S-O-S; II. Two S-OH, One S=O; III. Two S-OH, Four S=O, One S-O-O-S; IV. Two S-OH, Two S=O. Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
why: H₂S₂O₈ has a S-O-O-S peroxo link (III); H₂SO₄ has two S-OH and two S=O (IV); H₂S₂O₇ has an S-O-S bridge (I); H₂SO₃ has two S-OH and one S=O (II).

topic: d and f block elements oxides
q: Which of the following statements are INCORRECT? A. All the transition metals except scandium form MO oxides which are ionic. B. The highest oxidation number corresponding to the group number in transition metal oxides is attained in Sc₂O₃ to Mn₂O₇. C. Basic character increases from V₂O₃ to V₂O₄ to V₂O₅. D. V₂O₄ dissolves in acids to give VO₄³⁻ salts. E. CrO is basic but Cr₂O₃ is amphoteric. Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
why: Acidic (not basic) character increases with higher oxidation state from V₂O₃ to V₂O₅, so C is wrong. V₂O₄ dissolves in acids to give VO²⁺ salts, not VO₄³⁻, so D is wrong.

q: Which complex compound is most stable?
why: The complex containing the bidentate chelating ligand ethylenediamine (en) forms chelate rings, giving extra stability (chelate effect).

q: What fraction of one edge centred octahedral void lies in one unit cell of fcc?
why: Each edge-centred octahedral void in fcc is shared by 4 unit cells, so one unit cell contains 1/4 of it (12 edges × 1/4 = 3 voids).

q: Which amongst the following options is the correct relation between change in enthalpy and change in internal energy?
why: H = U + PV, so ΔH = ΔU + Δ(PV) = ΔU + ΔngRT for gases at constant temperature.

q: On balancing the given redox reaction, a Cr₂O₇²⁻ + b SO₃²⁻(aq) + c H⁺(aq) → 2Cr³⁺(aq) + b SO₄²⁻(aq) + (c/2) H₂O(l), the coefficients a, b and c are found to be, respectively -
why: Cr₂O₇²⁻ takes 6 electrons (2 Cr from +6 to +3); each SO₃²⁻ gives 2, so b = 3. Balancing charge gives c = 8 (and 4 H₂O): Cr₂O₇²⁻ + 3SO₃²⁻ + 8H⁺ → 2Cr³⁺ + 3SO₄²⁻ + 4H₂O.

q: The equilibrium concentrations of the species in the reaction A + B ⇌ C + D are 2, 3, 10 and 6 mol L⁻¹, respectively at 300 K. ΔG° for the reaction is (R = 2 cal / mol K)

Given below are two statements : Statement I : The nutrient deficient water bodies lead to eutrophication. Statement II : Eutrophication leads to decrease in the level of oxygen in the water bodies. In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below :
opts: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is false.
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is true.
why: Eutrophication results from nutrient-rich (not nutrient-deficient) water, so Statement I is false. The algal bloom and its decay reduce dissolved oxygen, so Statement II is true.

q: The reaction that does NOT take place in a blast furnace between 900 K to 1500 K temperature range during extraction of iron is :
why: In the blast furnace, Fe₂O₃ is reduced to FeO by CO in the lower temperature zone (500-800 K); in the 900-1500 K zone FeO is reduced to Fe and C + CO₂ → 2CO occurs, along with slag formation in the hot zone.

q: Given below are two statements : One is labelled as Assertion A and the other is labelled as Reason R : Assertion A : The first stage of gametophyte in the life cycle of moss is protonema stage. Reason R : Protonema develops directly from spores produced in capsule. In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below :
opts: Both A and R are correct and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are correct but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is correct but R is not correct.
A is not correct but R is correct.
why: In mosses the spores (formed in the capsule) germinate directly into the protonema, the first gametophytic stage. So R explains A.

q: In angiosperm, the haploid, diploid and triploid structures of a fertilized embryo sac sequentially are :
opts: Synergids, Primary endosperm nucleus and zygote
Antipodals, synergids, and primary endosperm nucleus
Synergids, Zygote and Primary endosperm nucleus
why: Synergids are haploid, the zygote (n+n) is diploid and the primary endosperm nucleus (n+n+n) is triploid.

q: Movement and accumulation of ions across a membrane against their concentration gradient can be explained by
why: Movement against a concentration gradient needs energy (ATP) and carrier pumps, which is active transport.

q: Large, colourful, fragrant flowers with nectar are seen in :
why: Insect-pollinated flowers attract pollinators with large size, colour, fragrance and nectar; wind-pollinated flowers are small and dull.

q: The phenomenon of pleiotropism refers to
opts: presence of several alleles of a single gene controlling a single crossover.
presence of two alleles, each of the two genes controlling a single trait.
a single gene affecting multiple phenotypic expression.
more than two genes affecting a single character.
why: Pleiotropy is when one gene influences several phenotypic traits, as in phenylketonuria.

q: Which hormone promotes internode/petiole elongation in deep water rice?
why: As per NCERT, ethylene promotes rapid elongation of internodes and petioles in deep-water rice so that leaves/upper parts stay above water.

q: Among 'The Evil Quartet', which one is considered the most important cause driving extinction of species?
why: Habitat loss and fragmentation is the most important cause of biodiversity loss and species extinction.

q: Upon exposure to UV radiation, DNA stained with ethidium bromide will show
why: Ethidium bromide-stained DNA fluoresces bright orange under UV light.

q: Which micronutrient is required for splitting of water molecule during photosynthesis?
why: Manganese is needed for the oxygen-evolving complex that splits water in photosystem II; magnesium is a macronutrient.

q: Axile placentation is observed in
why: China rose, petunia and lemon have axile placentation; mustard is parietal, primrose and Dianthus free central, beans/pea marginal.

q: The process of appearance of recombination nodules occurs at which sub stage of prophase I in meiosis?
why: Crossing over occurs in pachytene and is marked by recombination nodules.

q: The reaction centre in PS II has an absorption maxima at
why: The PS II reaction centre chlorophyll a is P680; PS I is P700.

q: Unequivocal proof that DNA is the genetic material was first proposed by
why: Hershey and Chase's bacteriophage experiment with radioactive 32P and 35S gave unequivocal proof that DNA is the genetic material.

q: Among eukaryotes, replication of DNA takes place in -
why: DNA replication occurs in the S (synthesis) phase of interphase.

q: In tissue culture experiments, leaf mesophyll cells are put in a culture medium to form callus. This phenomenon may be called as -
why: Mature differentiated cells regaining the ability to divide to form callus is dedifferentiation.

q: Cellulose does not form blue colour with iodine because
opts: It does not contain complex helices and hence cannot hold iodine molecules.
It breakes down when iodine reacts with it.
why: Starch forms a helical structure that holds iodine (blue colour); cellulose is a linear polymer without complex helices.

q: Spraying of which of the following phytohormone on juvenile conifers helps in hastening the maturity period, that leads to early seed production?
why: Gibberellins spray on juvenile conifers hastens maturity and so early seed production.

q: Given below are two statements : Statement I : The forces generated by transpiration can lift a xylem-sized column of water over 130 meters height. Statement II : Transpiration cools leaf surfaces sometimes 10 to 15 degrees, by evaporative cooling. In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below :
opts: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.
why: NCERT states transpiration pull can lift water to over 130 m and that evaporative cooling lowers leaf temperature by 10-15 degrees.

q: Family Fabaceae differs from Solanaceae and Liliaceae. With respect to the stamens, pick out the characteristics specific to family Fabaceae but not found in Solanaceae or Liliaceae.
why: Fabaceae has diadelphous stamens (9+1); Solanaceae has epipetalous and Liliaceae epiphyllous stamens, so diadelphous is specific to Fabaceae. Polyadelphous, monoadelphous monothecous and epiphyllous options do not fit Fabaceae.

q: Expressed Sequence Tags (ESTs) refers to
opts: All genes that are expressed as RNA.
All genes that are expressed as proteins.
All genes whether expressed or unexpressed.
why: In the Human Genome Project, ESTs identify all genes that are expressed as RNA.

q: Identify the correct statements : A. Detrivores perform fragmentation. B. The humus is further degraded by some microbes during mineralisation. C. Water soluble inorganic nutrients go down into the soil and get precipitated by a process called leaching. D. The detritus food chain begins with living organisms. E. Earthworms break down detritus into smaller particles by a process called catabolism. Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
why: A, B and C are correct. The detritus food chain begins with dead organic matter (D false), and earthworms fragment detritus, not catabolism (E false).

q: The thickness of ozone in a column of air in the atmosphere is measured in terms of :
why: Ozone thickness is measured in Dobson units (1 DU = 0.01 mm of pure ozone at STP).

q: Given below are two statements : One is labelled as Assertion A and the other is labelled as Reason R : Assertion A : Late wood has fewer xylary elements with narrow vessels. Reason R : Cambium is less active in winters. In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below :
opts: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.
why: In winter the cambium is less active and forms fewer xylem elements with narrow vessels (late wood), so R explains A.

q: Which of the following stages of meiosis involves division of centromere?
why: Centromeres split in anaphase II, separating sister chromatids; in meiosis I they do not divide.

q: The historic Convention on Biological Diversity, 'The Earth Summit' was held in Rio de Janeiro in the year :
why: The Earth Summit at Rio de Janeiro was held in 1992.

q: How many ATP and NADPH2 are required for the synthesis of one molecule of Glucose during Calvin cycle?
why: Fixing 6 CO2 into one glucose needs 18 ATP and 12 NADPH.

q: In the equation GPP - R = NPP. GPP is Gross Primary Productivity, NPP is Net Primary Productivity. R here is ________.
why: Net primary productivity is gross primary productivity minus respiratory losses (R).

q: What is the role of RNA polymerase III in the process of transcription in Eukaryotes?
opts: Transcription of tRNA, 5 srRNA and snRNA
why: RNA polymerase I makes 28S, 18S, 5.8S rRNAs, II makes hnRNA/mRNA precursor, and III makes tRNA, 5S rRNA and snRNAs.

q: What is the function of tassels in the corn cob?
why: The tassels/silky styles of the corn cob are feathery stigmas that trap wind-borne pollen grains.

q: Identify the pair of heterosporous pteridophytes among the following :
why: Selaginella and Salvinia produce two kinds of spores (micro and megaspores); Lycopodium, Psilotum, Equisetum are homosporous.

q: In gene gun method used to introduce alien DNA into host cells, microparticles of _________ metal are used.
why: In biolistics, DNA is coated on microscopic particles of gold or tungsten.

q: Given below are two statements : Statement I : Endarch and exarch are the terms often used for describing the position of secondary xylem in the plant body. Statement II : Exarch condition is the most common feature of the root system. In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below :
opts: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is false.
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is true.
why: Endarch and exarch describe the position of protoxylem in primary xylem, not secondary xylem, so I is wrong; roots have exarch xylem, so II is true.

q: Frequency of recombination between gene pairs on same chromosome as a measure of the distance between genes to map their position on chromosome, was used for the first time by
why: Alfred Sturtevant, Morgan's student, used recombination frequency as a measure of gene distance to construct the first genetic map.

q: Given below are two statements : One is labelled as Assertion A and the other is labelled as Reason R : Assertion A : ATP is used at two steps in glycolysis. Reason R : First ATP is used in converting glucose into glucose-6-phosphate and second ATP is used in conversion of fructose-6-phosphate into fructose-1-6-diphosphate. In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below :
opts: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.
why: Two ATP are consumed: hexokinase step and phosphofructokinase step; R names exactly these two steps.

q: Which one of the following statements is NOT correct?
opts: The micro-organisms involved in biodegradation of organic matter in a sewage polluted water body consume a lot of oxygen causing the death of aquatic organisms.
Algal blooms caused by excess of organic matter in water improve water quality and promote fisheries.
Water hyacinth grows abundantly in eutrophic water bodies and leads to an imbalance in the ecosystem dynamics of the water body.
The amount of some toxic substances of industrial waste water increases in the organisms at successive trophic levels.
why: Algal blooms deteriorate water quality and cause fish mortality, so statement 2 is incorrect.

q: How many different proteins does the ribosome consist of?
why: The ribosome consists of about 80 different proteins along with rRNAs.

q: Which of the following statements are correct about Klinefelter's Syndrome? A. This disorder was first described by Langdon Down (1866). B. Such an individual has overall masculine development. However, the feminine development is also expressed. C. The affected individual is short statured. D. Physical, psychomotor and mental development is retarded. E. Such individuals are sterile. Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
why: Klinefelter's (XXY) males are masculine with some feminine traits (gynaecomastia) and sterile. Langdon Down described Down syndrome, and Klinefelter individuals are tall, not short.

q: Match List I with List II : List I: A. Oxidative decarboxylation; B. Glycolysis; C. Oxidative phosphorylation; D. Tricarboxylic acid cycle  List II: I. Citrate synthase; II. Pyruvate dehydrogenase; III. Electron transport system; IV. EMP pathway. Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
why: Pyruvate dehydrogenase does oxidative decarboxylation, glycolysis is the EMP pathway, ETS gives oxidative phosphorylation, and citrate synthase starts the TCA cycle.

q: Given below are two statements : One is labelled as Assertion A and the other is labelled as Reason R : Assertion A : A flower is defined as modified shoot wherein the shoot apical meristem changes to floral meristem. Reason R : Internode of the shoot gets condensed to produce different floral appendages laterally at successive nodes instead of leaves. In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below :
opts: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.
why: A flower is a modified shoot with condensed internodes bearing floral appendages in place of leaves at successive nodes, which explains the assertion.

q: Given below are two statements : One is labelled as Assertion A and the other is labelled as Reason R : Assertion A : In gymnosperms the pollen grains are released from the microsporangium and carried by air currents. Reason R : Air currents carry the pollen grains to the mouth of the archegonia where the male gametes are discharged and pollen tube is not formed. In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below :
opts: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.
why: Gymnosperm pollen is wind-borne (A true), but a pollen tube is formed and carries male gametes to the archegonium, so R is false.

q: Which of the following combinations is required for chemiosmosis?
opts: membrane, proton pump, proton gradient, ATP synthase
membrane, proton pump, proton gradient, NADP synthase
proton pump, electron gradient, ATP synthase
proton pump, electron gradient, NADP synthase
why: Chemiosmosis needs a membrane, a proton pump, a proton gradient and ATP synthase.

q: Melonate inhibits the growth of pathogenic bacteria by inhibiting the activity of
why: Malonate (melonate) is a competitive inhibitor of succinic dehydrogenase, being similar to succinate.

q: Identify the correct statements : A. Lenticels are the lens-shaped openings permitting the exchange of gases. B. Bark formed early in the season is called hard bark. C. Bark is a technical term that refers to all tissues exterior to vascular cambium. D. Bark refers to periderm and secondary phloem. E. Phellogen is single-layered in thickness. Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
why: Lenticels allow gas exchange (A) and bark is periderm plus secondary phloem (D). Early bark is soft bark, bark is a non-technical term, and phellogen is a few layers thick, so B, C, E are wrong.

q: Match List I with List II : List I: A. M Phase; B. G2 Phase; C. Quiescent stage; D. G1 Phase  List II: I. Proteins are synthesized; II. Inactive phase; III. Interval between mitosis and initiation of DNA replication; IV. Equational division. Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
why: M phase is equational division, G2 involves protein synthesis, quiescent stage (G0) is inactive, and G1 is the interval between mitosis and DNA replication.

q: Match List I with List II : List I (Interaction): A. Mutualism; B. Commensalism; C. Amensalism; D. Parasitism  List II (Species A and B): I. +(A), O(B); II. -(A), O(B); III. +(A), -(B); IV. +(A), +(B). Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
why: Mutualism is +/+, commensalism +/0, amensalism -/0 and parasitism +/-.

q: Given below are two statements : Statement I : Gause's 'Competitive Exclusion Principle' states that two closely related species competing for the same resources cannot co-exist indefinitely and competitively inferior one will be eliminated eventually. Statement II : In general, carnivores are more adversely affected by competition than herbivores. In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below :
opts: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is false.
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is true.
why: Gause's principle is correctly stated; NCERT notes that herbivores and plants are more adversely affected by competition than carnivores in general.

q: Match List I with List II : List I: A. Iron; B. Zinc; C. Boron; D. Molybdenum  List II: I. Synthesis of auxin; II. Component of nitrate reductase; III. Activator of catalase; IV. Cell elongation and differentiation. Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
why: Iron activates catalase, zinc is needed for auxin synthesis, boron for cell elongation and differentiation, molybdenum is a component of nitrate reductase.

q: Match List I with List II. List I: A. Vasectomy; B. Coitus interruptus; C. Cervical caps; D. Saheli  List II: I. Oral method; II. Barrier method; III. Surgical method; IV. Natural method. Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
why: Vasectomy is surgical, coitus interruptus a natural method, cervical caps a barrier method and Saheli an oral pill.

q: Given below are two statements: Statement I: Vas deferens receives a duct from seminal vesicle and opens into urethra as the ejaculatory duct. Statement II: The cavity of the cervix is called cervical canal which along with vagina forms birth canal. In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
opts: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is false.
Statement I incorrect but Statement II is true.
why: The vas deferens joins the seminal vesicle duct to form the ejaculatory duct, and the cervical canal with the vagina forms the birth canal; both are NCERT facts.

q: Which of the following statements is correct?
opts: Eutrophication refers to increase in domestic sewage and waste water in lakes.
Biomagnification refers to increase in concentration of the toxicant at successive trophic levels.
Presence of large amount of nutrients in water restricts 'Algal Bloom'
why: Biomagnification is the increase in toxicant concentration along successive trophic levels. Eutrophication is nutrient enrichment, nutrients promote algal blooms and blooms increase fish mortality.

q: Which one of the following common sexually transmitted diseases is completely curable when detected early and treated properly?
why: Gonorrhoea is bacterial and curable with antibiotics; herpes, hepatitis-B and HIV are viral and not completely curable.

q: Match List I with List II. List I: A. Heroin; B. Marijuana; C. Cocaine; D. Morphine  List II: I. Effect on cardiovascular system; II. Slow down body function; III. Painkiller; IV. Interfere with transport of dopamine. Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
why: Heroin is a depressant slowing body function, marijuana affects the cardiovascular system, cocaine blocks dopamine transport, and morphine is a painkiller.

q: Match List I with List II. List I (Type of Joint): A. Cartilaginous Joint; B. Ball and Socket Joint; C. Fibrous Joint; D. Saddle Joint  List II (Found between): I. Between flat skull bones; II. Between adjacent vertebrae in vertebral column; III. Between carpal and metacarpal of thumb; IV. Between Humerus and Pectoral girdle. Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
why: Cartilaginous joints lie between vertebrae, ball and socket at the shoulder, fibrous joints between skull bones, and the saddle joint at the thumb's carpometacarpal.

q: Given below are two statements: Statement I: A protein is imagined as a line, the left end represented by first amino acid (C-terminal) and the right end represented by last amino acid (N-terminal). Statement II: Adult human haemoglobin, consists of 4 subunits (two subunits of α type and two subunits of β type.) In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
opts: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.
why: In a protein the left end is the N-terminal (first amino acid) and the right end is the C-terminal, so Statement I is reversed and false. Adult haemoglobin (HbA) has two α and two β subunits, so Statement II is true.

q: Which of the following are NOT considered as the part of endomembrane system? A. Mitochondria B. Endoplasmic Reticulum C. Chloroplasts D. Golgi complex E. Peroxisomes. Choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
why: The endomembrane system includes ER, Golgi complex, lysosomes and vacuoles. Mitochondria, chloroplasts and peroxisomes are not coordinated with it in function, so A, C and E are excluded.

topic: Molecular basis of inheritance and evolution
q: Given below are two statements: Statement I: RNA mutates at a faster rate. Statement II: Viruses having RNA genome and shorter life span mutate and evolve faster. In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
opts: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I false but Statement II is true.
why: RNA is less stable and has no proofreading, so it mutates faster. RNA viruses with short life spans therefore mutate and evolve faster. Both statements are true.

q: Match List I with List II. List I: A. CCK; B. GIP; C. ANF; D. ADH  List II: I. Kidney; II. Heart; III. Gastric gland; IV. Pancreas. Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
why: CCK acts on the pancreas (and gall bladder), GIP inhibits gastric secretion (gastric gland), ANF is released by the heart, ADH acts on the kidney. So A-IV, B-III, C-II, D-I.

q: Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion A and the other is labelled as Reason R. Assertion A: Endometrium is necessary for implantation of blastocyst. Reason R: In the absence of fertilization, the corpus luteum degenerates that causes disintegration of endometrium. In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
opts: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.
why: The endometrium receives the blastocyst, so A is true. Corpus luteum degeneration without fertilization breaks down the endometrium, so R is true, but it does not explain why the endometrium is needed for implantation.

q: Match List I with List II. List I: A. Ringworm; B. Filariasis; C. Malaria; D. Pneumonia  List II: I. Haemophilus influenzae; II. Trichophyton; III. Wuchereria bancrofti; IV. Plasmodium vivax. Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
why: Ringworm is caused by Trichophyton, filariasis by Wuchereria bancrofti, malaria by Plasmodium vivax and pneumonia by Haemophilus influenzae (among the listed).

q: Given below are two statements: Statement I: Low temperature preserves the enzyme in a temporarily inactive state whereas high temperature destroys enzymatic activity because proteins are denatured by heat. Statement II: When the inhibitor closely resembles the substrate in its molecular structure and inhibits the activity of the enzyme, it is known as competitive inhibitor. In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
opts: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.
why: Low temperature only inactivates enzymes temporarily while heat denatures them. A competitive inhibitor resembles the substrate and competes for the active site. Both are true.

q: Match List I with List II. List I: A. Taenia; B. Paramoecium; C. Periplaneta; D. Pheretima  List II: I. Nephridia; II. Contractile vacuole; III. Flame cells; IV. Urecose gland. Choose the correct answer from the options give below:
why: Taenia (a flatworm) has flame cells, Paramoecium a contractile vacuole, Periplaneta (cockroach) urecose glands along with Malpighian tubules, and Pheretima (earthworm) nephridia.

q: Match List I with List II. List I (Interacting species): A. A Leopard and a Lion in a forest/grassland; B. A Cuckoo laying egg in a Crow's nest; C. Fungi and root of a higher plant in Mycorrtizae; D. A cattle egret and a Cattle in a field  List II (Name of Interaction): I. Competition; II. Brood parasitism; III. Mutualism; IV. Commensalism. Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
why: Leopard and lion compete for prey, the cuckoo shows brood parasitism, mycorrhiza is mutualism, and the cattle egret benefits while the cattle are unaffected (commensalism).

q: Given below are two statements: Statement I: Ligaments are dense irregular tissue. Statement II: Cartilage is dense regular tissue. In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
opts: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.
why: Ligaments are dense regular connective tissue (attaching bone to bone), and cartilage is a specialised connective tissue, not dense regular tissue. Both statements are false.

topic: Cell and molecular basis of inheritance
q: Given below are two statements: Statement I: In prokaryotes, the positively charged DNA is held with some negatively charged proteins in a region called nucleoid. Statement II: In eukaryotes, the negatively charged DNA is wrapped around the positively charged histone octamer to form nucleosome. In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
opts: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is false.
Statement I incorrect but Statement II is true.
why: DNA is negatively charged and is held with some positively charged proteins in the nucleoid, so Statement I has the charges reversed. In eukaryotes negatively charged DNA wraps positively charged histone octamers, so Statement II is true.

q: Match List I with List II with respect to human eye. List I: A. Fovea; B. Iris; C. Blind spot; D. Sclera  List II: I. Visible coloured portion of eye that regulates diameter of pupil.; II. External layer of eye formed of dense connective tissue.; III. Point of greatest visual acuity or resolution.; IV. Point where optic nerve leaves the eyeball and photoreceptor cells are absent. Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
why: Fovea gives greatest visual acuity, the iris is the coloured part that regulates pupil diameter, the blind spot lacks photoreceptors where the optic nerve leaves, and the sclera is the outer dense connective tissue layer.

q: Select the correct group/set of Australian Marsupials exhibiting adaptive radiation.
opts: Mole, Flying squirrel, Tasmanian tiger cat
why: Numbat, spotted cuscus and flying phalanger are all Australian marsupials. The other sets include placental mammals (bobcat, mole, flying squirrel, lemur, anteater, wolf).

q: Which of the following statements are correct regarding female reproductive cycle? A. In non-primate mammals cyclical changes during reproduction are called oestrus cycle. B. First menstrual cycle begins at puberty and is called menopause. C. Lack of menstruation may be indicative of pregnancy. D. Cyclic menstruation extends between menarche and menopause. Choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
why: The first menstruation at puberty is menarche, not menopause, so B is false. A, C and D are correct statements.

q: Vital capacity of lung is _______.
