why: Vital capacity is the maximum air that can be breathed out after a maximal inspiration: ERV + TV + IRV.

q: Match List I with List II. List I: A. P-wave; B. Q-wave; C. QRS complex; D. T-wave  List II: I. Beginning of systole; II. Repolarisation of ventricles; III. Depolarisation of atria; IV. Depolarisation of ventricles. Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
why: P-wave is atrial depolarisation, the QRS complex is ventricular depolarisation (Q marks the beginning of systole), and the T-wave is ventricular repolarisation.

q: Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion A and the other is labelled as Reason R. Assertion A: Amniocentesis for sex determination is one of the strategies of Reproductive and Child Health Care Programme. Reason R: Ban on amniocentesis checks increasing menace of female foeticide. In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
opts: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true and R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.
why: Amniocentesis for sex determination is banned, not promoted, under the RCH programme, so A is false. The ban does help check female foeticide, so R is true.

q: Once the undigested and unabsorbed substances enter the caecum, their backflow is prevented by-
why: The ileo-caecal valve between the ileum and caecum prevents backflow of material from the large intestine into the small intestine.

q: Match List I with List II. List I: A. Gene 'a'; B. Gene 'y'; C. Gene 'i'; D. Gene 'z'  List II: I. β-galactosidase; II. Transacetylase; III. Permease; IV. Repressor protein. Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
why: In the lac operon, z codes for β-galactosidase, y for permease, a for transacetylase and i for the repressor protein.

q: Match List I with List II. List I (Cells): A. Peptic cells; B. Goblet cells; C. Oxyntic cells; D. Hepatic cells  List II (Secretion): I. Mucus; II. Bile juice; III. Proenzyme pepsinogen; IV. HCl and intrinsic factor for absorption of vitamin B₁₂. Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
why: Peptic (chief) cells secrete pepsinogen, goblet cells mucus, oxyntic (parietal) cells HCl and intrinsic factor, and hepatic cells bile.

q: Which of the following functions is carried out by cytoskeleton in a cell?
why: NCERT states that the cytoskeleton's functions include mechanical support, motility and maintenance of cell shape. Of the options, motility is the one listed.

q: Given below are statements: one is labelled as Assertion A and the other is labelled as Reason R. Assertion A: Nephrons are of two types: Cortical & Juxta medullary, based on their relative position in cortex and medulla. Reason R: Juxta medullary nephrons have short loop of Henle whereas, cortical nephrons have longer loop of Henle. In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
opts: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true and R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.
why: Nephrons are indeed cortical and juxtamedullary, so A is true. Juxtamedullary nephrons have long loops of Henle and cortical nephrons short ones, so R is reversed and false.

q: Given below are two statements: Statement I: Electrostatic precipitator is most widely used in thermal power plant. Statement II: Electrostatic precipitator in thermal power plant removes ionising radiations. In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
opts: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
Statement I incorrect but Statement II is correct.
why: Electrostatic precipitators are the most widely used device in thermal power plants, removing over 99% of particulate matter, not ionising radiations. So I is correct and II is incorrect.

q: Broad palm with single palm crease is visible in a person suffering from-
why: Down's syndrome (trisomy 21) features a broad flat face, furrowed tongue and a broad palm with a single palmar crease.

q: Radial symmetry is NOT found in adults of phylum _______.
why: Ctenophores and coelenterates are radially symmetrical, and adult echinoderms are radially symmetrical. Hemichordates are bilaterally symmetrical.

q: In which blood corpuscles, the HIV undergoes replication and produces progeny viruses?
why: HIV enters helper T lymphocytes (TH cells), uses reverse transcriptase to make viral DNA and replicates there, producing progeny viruses.

q: Which of the following is not a cloning vector?
why: BAC, YAC and pBR322 are cloning vectors. A probe is a labelled DNA or RNA fragment used to detect a complementary sequence.

q: Match List I with List II. List I: A. Logistic growth; B. Exponential growth; C. Expanding age pyramid; D. Stable age pyramid  List II: I. Unlimited resource availability condition; II. Limited resource availability condition; III. The percent individuals of pre-reproductive age is largest followed by reproductive and post reproductive age groups; IV. The percent individuals of pre-reproductives and reproductive age group are same. Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
why: Logistic growth occurs with limited resources and exponential growth with unlimited resources. An expanding pyramid has most individuals pre-reproductive; a stable pyramid has pre-reproductive and reproductive groups about equal.

q: Select the correct statements with reference to chordates. A. Presence of a mid-dorsal, solid and double nerve cord. B. Presence of closed circulatory system. C. Presence of paired pharyngeal gillslits. D. Presence of dorsal heart E. Triploblastic pseudocoelomate animals. Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
why: Chordates have a dorsal, hollow, single nerve cord (A false), a ventral heart (D false), and are coelomate (E false). They have a closed circulatory system and paired pharyngeal gill slits, so B and C are correct.

q: The parts of human brain that helps in regulation of sexual behaviour, expression of excitement, pleasure, rage, fear etc. are :
why: The limbic system together with the hypothalamus regulates sexual behaviour and emotional expression such as excitement, pleasure, rage and fear.

q: The unique mammalian characteristics are:
opts: hairs, tympanic membrane and mammary glands
pinna, monocondylic skull and mammary glands
why: NCERT lists mammary glands, hair and external ears (pinnae) as the unique characters of mammals. Tympanic membrane is found in other vertebrates and mammals have a dicondylic skull.

q: Which of the following are NOT under the control of thyroid hormone? A. Maintenance of water and electrolyte balance B. Regulation of basal metabolic rate C. Normal rhythm of sleep-wake cycle D. Development of immune system E. Support the process of R.B.Cs formation. Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
why: Thyroid hormones regulate BMR, support RBC formation and help maintain water and electrolyte balance. The sleep-wake rhythm (melatonin) and immune system development are not thyroid functions.

q: Select the correct statements. A. Tetrad formation is seen during Leptotene. B. During Anaphase, the centromeres split and chromatids separate. C. Terminalization takes place during Pachytene. D. Nucleolus, Golgi complex and ER are reformed during Telophase. E. Crossing over takes place between sister chromatids of homologous chromosome. Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
why: Tetrads are seen at pachytene (A false), terminalization occurs in diakinesis (C false), and crossing over is between non-sister chromatids (E false). B and D are correct.

q: Match List I with List II. List I: A. Mast cells; B. Inner surface of bronchiole; C. Blood; D. Tubular parts of nephron  List II: I. Ciliated epithelium; II. Areolar connective tissue; III. Cuboidal epithelium; IV. specialised connective tissue. Choose the correct answer from the options give below:
why: Mast cells are found in areolar connective tissue, bronchioles are lined by ciliated epithelium, blood is a specialised connective tissue and nephron tubules have cuboidal epithelium.

q: Which of the following is characteristic feature of cockroach regarding sexual dimorphism ?
opts: Dark brown body colour and anal cerci
why: Anal styles are present only in male cockroaches, whereas anal cerci occur in both sexes, so anal styles show sexual dimorphism.

q: Which one of the following is the sequence on corresponding coding strand, if the sequence on mRNA formed is as follows 5' AUCGAUCGAUCGAUCGAUCG AUCG AUCG 3'?
why: The coding strand has the same sequence as the mRNA (with T in place of U) and the same 5' to 3' polarity, giving 5' ATCGATCG... 3'.

q: In cockroach, excretion is brought about by- A. Phallic gland B. Urecose gland C. Nephrocytes D. Fat body E. Collaterial glands. Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
why: Besides Malpighian tubules, cockroach excretion involves urecose glands, nephrocytes and fat body. Phallic and collaterial glands are reproductive glands.

q: Given below are two statements: Statement I: During G₀ phase of cell cycle, the cell is metabolically inactive. Statement II: The centrosome undergoes duplication during S phase of interphase. In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
opts: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.
why: Cells in G₀ (quiescent) are metabolically active but do not divide, so Statement I is wrong. The centrosome duplicates in S phase, so Statement II is correct.

q: Which of the following statements are correct? A. An excessive loss of body fluid from the body switches off osmoreceptors. B. ADH facilitates water reabsorption to prevent diuresis. C. ANF causes vasodilation. D. ADH causes increase in blood pressure. E. ADH is responsible for decrease in GFR. Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
why: Fluid loss activates (not switches off) osmoreceptors, so A is false. ADH promotes water reabsorption and constricts vessels raising blood pressure; ANF causes vasodilation. ADH does not decrease GFR per NCERT, so E is false.

q: Which of the following statements are correct ? A. Basophils are most abundant cells of the total WBCs B. Basophils secrete histamine, serotonin and heparin C. Basophils are involved in inflammatory response D. Basophils have kidney shaped nucleus E. Basophils are agranulocytes. Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
why: Neutrophils (not basophils) are most abundant WBCs, basophils have a lobed nucleus and are granulocytes. Basophils secrete histamine, serotonin and heparin and take part in inflammatory reactions.

q: In a uniform magnetic field of 0.049 T, a magnetic needle performs 20 complete oscillations in 5 seconds. The moment of inertia of the needle is 9.8 × 10⁻⁶ kg m². If the magnitude of the magnetic moment of the needle is x × 10⁻⁵ Am², then the value of 'x' is:
A logic circuit provides the output Y as per the following truth table: (A, B, Y) = (0, 0, 1), (0, 1, 0), (1, 0, 1), (1, 1, 0). The expression for the output Y is:
why: Y = 1 exactly when B = 0 and Y = 0 when B = 1, independent of A. Hence Y = B̄ (NOT of B).

q: A thin flat circular disc of radius 4.5 cm is placed gently over the surface of water. If surface tension of water is 0.07 N m⁻¹, then the excess force required to take it away from the surface is:
why: Excess force = surface tension × length of contact line = T × 2πr = 0.07 × 2π × 0.045 ≈ 1.98 × 10⁻² N = 19.8 mN.

q: In a vernier callipers, (N + 1) divisions of vernier scale coincide with N divisions of main scale. If 1 MSD represents 0.1 mm, the vernier constant (in cm) is:
why: Vernier constant = 1 MSD / (number of vernier divisions) = 0.1 mm/(N+1) = 0.01 cm/(N+1) = 1/(100(N+1)) cm.

q: The maximum elongation of a steel wire of 1 m length if the elastic limit of steel and its Young's modulus are 8 × 10⁸ N m⁻² and 2 × 10¹¹ N m⁻², respectively, is:
why: Maximum strain = elastic limit / Y = 8×10⁸ / 2×10¹¹ = 4×10⁻³. Elongation = strain × L = 4×10⁻³ × 1 m = 4 mm.

q: Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion A and the other is labelled as Reason R. Assertion A: The potential (V) at any axial point, at 2 m distance (r) from the centre of the dipole of dipole moment vector P of magnitude, 4 × 10⁻⁶ C m, is ±9 × 10³ V. (Take 1/(4πε₀) = 9 × 10⁹ SI units) Reason R: V = ±2P/(4πε₀r²), where r is the distance of any axial point, situated at 2 m from the centre of the dipole. In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
opts: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true and R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.
why: Axial potential is V = ±P/(4πε₀r²) = 9×10⁹ × 4×10⁻⁶ / 4 = ±9×10³ V, so A is true. R contains an extra factor 2 and is false.

q: An unpolarised light beam strikes a glass surface at Brewster's angle. Then:
opts: The reflected light will be partially polarised.
The refracted light will be completely polarised.
Both the reflected and refracted light will be completely polarised.
The reflected light will be completely polarised but the refracted light will be partially polarised.
why: At Brewster's angle the reflected ray is completely plane polarised (perpendicular to the plane of incidence), while the refracted ray is only partially polarised.

q: A tightly wound 100 turns coil of radius 10 cm carries a current of 7 A. The magnitude of the magnetic field at the centre of the coil is (Take permeability of free space as 4π × 10⁻⁷ SI units):

Match List-I with List-II. List-I (Material): A. Diamagnetic; B. Ferromagnetic; C. Paramagnetic; D. Non-magnetic.  List-II (Susceptibility χ): I. χ = 0; II. 0 > χ ≥ −1; III. χ ≫ 1; IV. 0 < χ < ε (a small positive number).
why: Diamagnetic materials have small negative χ (0 > χ ≥ −1), ferromagnetic have very large positive χ, paramagnetic have small positive χ, and a non-magnetic material has χ = 0.

q: A bob is whirled in a horizontal plane by means of a string with an initial speed of ω rpm. The tension in the string is T. If speed becomes 2ω while keeping the same radius, the tension in the string becomes:
why: Tension supplies the centripetal force: T = mrω². Doubling ω at the same radius multiplies T by 2² = 4, giving 4T.

q: A wire of length ℓ and resistance 100 Ω is divided into 10 equal parts. The first 5 parts are connected in series while the next 5 parts are connected in parallel. The two combinations are again connected in series. The resistance of this final combination is:
why: Each part is 10 Ω. Five in series = 50 Ω. Five in parallel = 10/5 = 2 Ω. The two in series give 50 + 2 = 52 Ω.

topic: Dual nature of radiation and matter
q: If c is the velocity of light in free space, the correct statements about photon among the following are: A. The energy of a photon is E = hν. B. The velocity of a photon is c. C. The momentum of a photon, p = hν/c. D. In a photon-electron collision, both total energy and total momentum are conserved. E. Photon possesses positive charge.
opts: A, B, C and D only
why: A photon has energy hν, speed c and momentum hν/c, and energy and momentum are both conserved in collisions. A photon is electrically neutral, so E is false.

q: At any instant of time t, the displacement of any particle is given by 2t − 1 (SI unit) under the influence of force of 5 N. The value of instantaneous power is (in SI unit):
why: Velocity = d(2t − 1)/dt = 2 m/s (constant). Power P = F·v = 5 × 2 = 10 W.

q: A particle moving with uniform speed in a circular path maintains:
why: The speed is constant but the direction of velocity changes continuously, so velocity varies. The centripetal acceleration has constant magnitude but its direction keeps changing, so acceleration also varies.

q: If the monochromatic source in Young's double slit experiment is replaced by white light, then:
opts: There will be a central dark fringe surrounded by a few coloured fringes
There will be a central bright white fringe surrounded by a few coloured fringes
All bright fringes will be of equal width
why: At the centre the path difference is zero for all colours, so all colours give a bright fringe and combine to white. Away from the centre the fringes of different colours (different widths) separate and appear coloured.

q: If x = 5 sin(πt + π/3) m represents the motion of a particle executing simple harmonic motion, the amplitude and time period of motion, respectively, are:
why: Compare with x = A sin(ωt + φ): A = 5 m and ω = π rad/s. Time period T = 2π/ω = 2 s.

q: The moment of inertia of a thin rod about an axis passing through its midpoint and perpendicular to the rod is 2400 g cm². The length of the 400 g rod is nearly:
In an ideal transformer, the turns ratio is N_P/N_S = 1/2. The ratio V_S : V_P is equal to (the symbols carry their usual meaning):
why: For an ideal transformer V_S/V_P = N_S/N_P = 2/1, so V_S : V_P = 2 : 1.

q: The quantities which have the same dimensions as those of solid angle are:
why: Solid angle (steradian) is a ratio of area to area, so it is dimensionless. Strain and plane angle are also dimensionless; stress, arc length and angular speed are not.

q: In the nuclear emission stated below, the mass number and atomic number of the product Q, respectively, are: ²⁹⁰₈₂X →(α) Y →(e⁺) Z →(β⁻) P →(e⁻) Q
why: α emission: A 290 → 286, Z 82 → 80. e⁺ emission: Z 80 → 79. β⁻ emission: Z 79 → 80. e⁻ (β⁻) emission: Z 80 → 81. Mass number stays 286, so Q is (286, 81).

q: The mass of a planet is 1/10th that of the earth and its diameter is half that of the earth. The acceleration due to gravity on that planet is:

Two bodies A and B of same mass undergo completely inelastic one dimensional collision. The body A moves with velocity v₁ while body B is at rest before collision. The velocity of the system after collision is v₂. The ratio v₁ : v₂ is:
why: Momentum conservation: m v₁ = (m + m) v₂, so v₂ = v₁/2 and v₁ : v₂ = 2 : 1.

q: A small telescope has an objective of focal length 140 cm and an eye piece of focal length 5.0 cm. The magnifying power of the telescope for viewing a distant object is:
why: For a telescope in normal adjustment, m = f_o/f_e = 140/5 = 28.

q: The minimum energy required to launch a satellite of mass m from the surface of earth of mass M and radius R in a circular orbit at an altitude of 2R from the surface of the earth is:
why: Orbit radius r = 3R, total energy in orbit = −GMm/(2r) = −GMm/6R. Initial energy = −GMm/R. Minimum energy = −GMm/6R + GMm/R = 5GMm/6R.

topic: Thermal properties and elasticity of matter
q: A metallic bar of Young's modulus, 0.5 × 10¹¹ N/m² and coefficient of linear thermal expansion 10⁻⁵ °C⁻¹, length 1 m and area of cross-section 10⁻³ m² is heated from 0°C to 100°C without expansion or bending. The compressive force developed in it is:

A sheet is placed on a horizontal surface in front of a strong magnetic pole. A force is needed to: A. hold the sheet there if it is magnetic. B. hold the sheet there if it is non-magnetic. C. move the sheet away from the pole with uniform velocity if it is conducting. D. move the sheet away from the pole with uniform velocity if it is both, non-conducting and non-polar.
why: A magnetic sheet is attracted, so a force is needed to hold it (A). A conducting sheet moved in the field develops eddy currents which oppose motion, so a force is needed (C). A non-magnetic sheet feels no force (B) and a non-conducting non-polar sheet has no eddy currents (D).

q: If the plates of a parallel plate capacitor connected to a battery are moved close to each other, then: A. the charge stored in it, increases. B. the energy stored in it, decreases. C. its capacitance increases. D. the ratio of charge to its potential remains the same. E. the product of charge and voltage increases.
why: V is fixed by the battery. C = ε₀A/d increases as d decreases, so Q = CV increases, and U = ½CV² and QV both increase. Q/V = C changes, so D is false and B is false.

q: Two heaters A and B have power ratings of 1 kW and 2 kW, respectively. Those two are first connected in series and then in parallel to a fixed power source. The ratio of power outputs for these two cases is:
why: Take V² = 2000: R_A = 2, R_B = 1 (in suitable units). Series power = V²/(R_A + R_B) = 2000/3. Parallel power = 1 kW + 2 kW = 3000. Ratio = (2000/3)/3000 = 2 : 9.

q: If the mass of the bob in a simple pendulum is increased to thrice its original mass and its length is made half its original length, then the new time period of oscillation is x/2 times its original time period. Then the value of x is:
why: T = 2π√(L/g) does not depend on mass. New T = 2π√(L/2g) = T/√2. So x/2 = 1/√2 and x = √2.

q: An iron bar of length L has magnetic moment M. It is bent at the middle of its length such that the two arms make an angle 60° with each other. The magnetic moment of this new magnet is:
why: M = m L, with m the pole strength. After bending, each arm has length L/2 and the two poles are separated by 2 × (L/2) sin 30° = L/2. New moment = m × L/2 = M/2.

q: The property which is not of an electromagnetic wave travelling in free space is that:
opts: The energy density in electric field is equal to energy density in magnetic field
They travel with a speed equal to 1/√(μ₀ε₀)
They originate from charges moving with uniform speed
why: Electromagnetic waves are produced by accelerated (oscillating) charges, not by charges moving with uniform speed. The other three statements are true of EM waves.

q: A force defined by F = αt² + βt acts on a particle at a given time t. The factor which is dimensionless, if α and β are constants, is:
why: Each term has the dimensions of force, so [α] = F T⁻² and [β] = F T⁻¹. Then αt/β = (F T⁻¹)/(F T⁻¹) is dimensionless, whereas βt/α has dimension T².

q: A parallel plate capacitor is charged by connecting it to a battery through a resistor. If I is the current in the circuit, then in the gap between the plates:
opts: Displacement current of magnitude equal to I flows in the same direction as I
Displacement current of magnitude equal to I flows in a direction opposite to that of I
Displacement current of magnitude greater than I flows but can be in any direction
why: The displacement current ε₀ dΦE/dt between the plates equals the conduction current I and is in the same direction, which keeps the total current continuous.

q: Fehling's solution 'A' is:
opts: alkaline solution of sodium potassium tartrate (Rochelle's salt)
why: Fehling's solution A is aqueous copper sulphate; Fehling's solution B is alkaline sodium potassium tartrate (Rochelle's salt).

q: Match List I with List II. List I (Molecule): A. ethane; B. ethene; C. carbon molecule, C₂; D. ethyne.  List II (Number and types of bonds between two carbon atoms): I. one σ-bond and two π-bonds; II. two π-bonds; III. one σ-bond; IV. one σ-bond and one π-bond. Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
why: Ethane has a C–C single bond (one σ). Ethene has one σ and one π. C₂ has two π bonds (MO theory). Ethyne has one σ and two π bonds. So A-III, B-IV, C-II, D-I.

q: For the reaction 2A ⇌ B + C, K_C = 4 × 10⁻³. At a given time, the composition of reaction mixture is [A] = [B] = [C] = 2 × 10⁻³ M. Then, which of the following is correct?
opts: Reaction has a tendency to go in forward direction.
Reaction has a tendency to go in backward direction.
Reaction has gone to completion in forward direction.
why: Q_c = [B][C]/[A]² = (2×10⁻³)²/(2×10⁻³)² = 1, which is greater than K_c = 4×10⁻³. Since Q_c > K_c, the reaction proceeds backward.

q: Match List I with List II. List I (Process): A. Isothermal process; B. Isochoric process; C. Isobaric process; D. Adiabatic process.  List II (Conditions): I. No heat exchange; II. Carried out at constant temperature; III. Carried out at constant volume; IV. Carried out at constant pressure. Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
why: Isothermal means constant temperature (II), isochoric means constant volume (III), isobaric means constant pressure (IV), adiabatic means no heat exchange (I).

q: Given below are two statements: Statement I: Aniline does not undergo Friedel-Crafts alkylation reaction. Statement II: Aniline cannot be prepared through Gabriel synthesis.
opts: Both statement I and statement II are true
Both statement I and statement II are false
Statement I is correct but statement II is false
Statement I is incorrect but statement II is true
why: The NH₂ group of aniline forms a salt with AlCl₃ and deactivates the ring, so Friedel-Crafts fails. Gabriel synthesis needs an alkyl halide; aryl halides do not undergo nucleophilic substitution with phthalimide, so aromatic primary amines cannot be made this way.

q: 'Spin only' magnetic moment is same for which of the following ions? A. Ti³⁺ B. Cr²⁺ C. Mn²⁺ D. Fe²⁺ E. Sc³⁺
why: Spin-only moment depends on unpaired electrons: Ti³⁺ d¹ (1), Cr²⁺ d⁴ (4), Mn²⁺ d⁵ (5), Fe²⁺ d⁶ (4), Sc³⁺ d⁰ (0). Cr²⁺ and Fe²⁺ both have 4.

q: Arrange the following elements in increasing order of first ionization enthalpy. Li, Be, B, C, N
why: Ionization enthalpy generally rises across a period, but Be (filled 2s) is higher than B (2p electron is easier to remove). Order: Li < B < Be < C < N.

q: 1 gram of sodium hydroxide was treated with 25 mL of 0.75 M HCl solution, the mass of sodium hydroxide left unreacted is equal to:
why: NaOH = 1/40 mol = 25 mmol; HCl = 25 × 0.75 = 18.75 mmol. NaOH left = 6.25 mmol × 40 mg/mmol = 250 mg.

q: Match List I with List II. List I (Conversion): A. 1 mol of H₂O to O₂; B. 1 mol of MnO₄⁻ to Mn²⁺; C. 1.5 mol of Ca from molten CaCl₂; D. 1 mol of FeO to Fe₂O₃  List II (Number of Faraday required): I. 3F; II. 2F; III. 1F; IV. 5F. Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
why: H₂O → ½O₂ needs 2F; MnO₄⁻ → Mn²⁺ needs 5F; 1.5 mol Ca²⁺ → Ca needs 3F; FeO → ½Fe₂O₃ needs 1F. So A-II, B-IV, C-I, D-III.

q: The Henry's law constant (K_H) values of three gases (A, B, C) in water are 145, 2 × 10⁻⁵ and 35 kbar, respectively. The solubility of these gases in water follows the order:
why: Solubility is inversely proportional to Henry's constant (p = K_H x). Smallest K_H (B) is most soluble, then C (35), then A (145): B > C > A.

q: On heating, some solid substances change from solid to vapor state without passing through liquid state. The technique used for the purification of such solid substances based on the above principle is known as:
why: Direct solid to vapour change on heating is sublimation, and the technique used to purify such solids is sublimation.

q: Given below are two statements: Statement I: Both [Co(NH₃)₆]³⁺ and [CoF₆]³⁻ complexes are octahedral but differ in their magnetic behaviour. Statement II: [Co(NH₃)₆]³⁺ is diamagnetic whereas [CoF₆]³⁻ is paramagnetic.
opts: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
why: NH₃ is a strong-field ligand: Co³⁺ (d⁶) is low spin, t₂g⁶, diamagnetic. F⁻ is weak-field: high spin t₂g⁴eg², 4 unpaired electrons, paramagnetic. Both statements are true.

q: The E° value for the Mn³⁺/Mn²⁺ couple is more positive than that of Cr³⁺/Cr²⁺ or Fe³⁺/Fe²⁺ due to change of
why: Mn³⁺ (d⁴) reduces to Mn²⁺ (d⁵, half-filled and extra stable), so the reduction is very favourable and E° is highly positive.

q: Activation energy of any chemical reaction can be calculated if one knows the value of:
opts: orientation of reactant molecules during collision
rate constant at two different temperatures
why: From log(k₂/k₁) = (Eₐ/2.303R)(1/T₁ − 1/T₂), Eₐ follows from rate constants at two temperatures.

q: Given below are two statements: Statement I: The boiling point of three isomeric pentanes follows the order n-pentane > isopentane > neopentane. Statement II: When branching increases, the molecule attains a shape of sphere. This results in smaller surface area for contact, due to which the intermolecular forces between the spherical molecules are weak, thereby lowering the boiling point. In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
opts: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
why: Boiling points: n-pentane (309 K) > isopentane (301 K) > neopentane (283 K). Branching makes the molecule more spherical with less surface area, so van der Waals forces weaken. Both correct.

q: A compound with a molecular formula of C₆H₁₄ has two tertiary carbons. Its IUPAC name is:
why: 2,3-Dimethylbutane, (CH₃)₂CH–CH(CH₃)₂, has two CH carbons each bonded to three carbons (two tertiary carbons). 2-Methylpentane has only one.

q: The energy of an electron in the ground state (n = 1) for He⁺ ion is -x J, then that for an electron in n = 2 state for Be³⁺ ion in J is:
why: Eₙ ∝ −Z²/n². For He⁺, n = 1: Z²/n² = 4 gives −x. For Be³⁺, n = 2: 16/4 = 4, so energy is also −x.

q: Which reaction is NOT a redox reaction?
why: BaCl₂ + Na₂SO₄ → BaSO₄ + 2NaCl is a double displacement (precipitation) reaction with no change in oxidation numbers.

q: Match List I with List II. List I (Compound): A. NH₃; B. BrF₅; C. XeF₄; D. SF₆  List II (Shape/geometry): I. Trigonal Pyramidal; II. Square Planar; III. Octahedral; IV. Square Pyramidal
why: NH₃ is trigonal pyramidal, BrF₅ square pyramidal, XeF₄ square planar, SF₆ octahedral: A-I, B-IV, C-II, D-III.

q: Given below are two statements: Statement I: The boiling point of hydrides of Group 16 elements follow the order H₂O > H₂Te > H₂Se > H₂S. Statement II: On the basis of molecular mass, H₂O is expected to have a lower boiling point than the other members of the group but due to the presence of extensive H-bonding in H₂O, it has a higher boiling point. In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
opts: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
why: Boiling points: H₂O (373 K) > H₂Te (232 K) > H₂Se (231 K) > H₂S (213 K). Water's anomalously high value is due to extensive hydrogen bonding. Both true.

topic: Some basic concepts of chemistry mole concept
q: The highest number of helium atoms is in:
why: 4 mol = 4 Nₐ atoms; 4 u = 1 atom; 3 g = 0.75 mol; 2.271098 L at STP = 0.1 mol. 4 mol is the largest.

q: The reagents with which glucose does not react to give the corresponding tests/products are: A. Tollen's reagent B. Schiff's reagent C. HCN D. NH₂OH E. NaHSO₃
why: Glucose exists mainly in the cyclic hemiacetal form with little free CHO, so it does not give Schiff's test or the NaHSO₃ addition product. It reacts with Tollens', HCN and NH₂OH.

q: In which of the following processes entropy increases? A. A liquid evaporates to vapour. B. Temperature of a crystalline solid lowered from 130 K to 0 K. C. 2NaHCO₃(s) → Na₂CO₃(s) + CO₂(g) + H₂O(g) D. Cl₂(g) → 2Cl(g). Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
why: Entropy rises when disorder increases: evaporation, gas formation (C), and one gas molecule to two atoms (D). Cooling a solid to 0 K lowers entropy.

q: Among Group 16 elements, which one does NOT show -2 oxidation state?
why: Po is the most metallic member of the group and prefers +2 and +4 states; it does not show the −2 state.

q: Arrange the following elements in increasing order of electronegativity: N, O, F, C, Si. Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
why: Electronegativity increases across a period and decreases down a group: Si (1.8) < C (2.5) < N (3.0) < O (3.5) < F (4.0).

q: The pair of lanthanoid ions which are diamagnetic is:
why: Ce⁴⁺ is 4f⁰ and Yb²⁺ is 4f¹⁴, both with no unpaired electrons. Ce³⁺ (4f¹), Eu²⁺ (4f⁷), Gd³⁺ (4f⁷), Eu³⁺ (4f⁶), Pm³⁺ and Sm³⁺ are paramagnetic.

q: The work done during reversible isothermal expansion of one mole of hydrogen gas at 25°C from pressure of 20 atmosphere to 10 atmosphere is: (Given R = 2.0 cal K⁻¹ mol⁻¹)
why: w = −2.303 nRT log(P₁/P₂) = −2.303 × 1 × 2 × 298 × log 2 ≈ −413.14 cal (negative sign: work done by the system on expansion, as in the usual NCERT convention).

q: The products A and B obtained in the following reactions, respectively, are: 3ROH + PCl₃ → 3RCl + A; ROH + PCl₅ → RCl + HCl + B
why: PCl₃ with alcohols gives alkyl chloride and phosphorous acid (H₃PO₃); PCl₅ gives alkyl chloride, HCl and POCl₃.

q: Identify the major product C formed in the following reaction sequence: CH₃CH₂CH₂OH →(NaCN) A →(OH⁻) B →(NaOH, Br₂) C
why: A is butanenitrile (CH₃CH₂CH₂CN), partial hydrolysis with OH⁻ gives butanamide (B). Hofmann bromamide degradation (NaOH, Br₂) removes one carbon, giving propylamine.

q: A compound X contains 32% of A, 20% of B and remaining percentage of C. Then, the empirical formula of X is: (Given atomic masses of A = 64; B = 40; C = 32 u)
The rate of a reaction quadruples when temperature changes from 27°C to 57°C. Calculate the energy of activation. Given: R = 8.314 J K⁻¹ mol⁻¹, log 4 = 0.6021
During the preparation of Mohr's salt solution (Ferrous ammonium sulphate), which of the following acid is added to prevent hydrolysis of Fe²⁺ ion?
why: Dilute sulphuric acid suppresses hydrolysis of Fe²⁺ and shares the sulphate ion with the salt. HCl and HNO₃ would add foreign anions, and HNO₃ would also oxidise Fe²⁺.

q: Mass in grams of copper deposited by passing 9.6487 A current through a voltmeter containing copper sulphate solution for 100 seconds is (Given: Molar mass of Cu = 63 g/mol, 1 F = 96487 C)

Given below are two statements: Statement I: [Co(NH₃)₆]³⁺ is a homoleptic complex whereas [Co(NH₃)₄Cl₂]⁺ is a heteroleptic complex. Statement II: Complex [Co(NH₃)₆]³⁺ has only one kind of ligands but [Co(NH₃)₄Cl₂]⁺ has more than one kind of ligands.
opts: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
why: Homoleptic complexes have one kind of ligand (NH₃ only); heteroleptic ones have more than one kind (NH₃ and Cl⁻). Both statements are true.

q: Identify the correct answer.
opts: Three resonance structures can be drawn for ozone
Dipole moment of NF₃ is greater than that of NH₃.
Three canonical forms can be drawn for CO₃²⁻ ion.
why: Ozone has two resonance structures; BF₃ is planar symmetric (zero dipole); NF₃ has a smaller dipole than NH₃ because N–F and lone-pair dipoles oppose. CO₃²⁻ has three canonical forms.

q: The plot of osmotic pressure (Π) vs concentration (mol L⁻¹) for a solution gives a straight line with slope 25.73 L bar mol⁻¹. The temperature at which the osmotic pressure measurement is done is: Use R = 8.314 L bar mol⁻¹ K⁻¹, log 4 = 0.6021.
Which of the following are required for the dark reaction of photosynthesis? A. Light B. Chlorophyll C. CO₂ D. ATP E. NADPH Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
why: The dark (Calvin cycle) reaction needs CO₂ as the substrate and the ATP and NADPH made in the light reaction. It does not directly need light or chlorophyll.

q: Match List I with List II. List I: A. Two or more alternative forms of a gene; B. Cross of F₁ progeny with homozygous recessive parent; C. Cross of F₁ progeny with any of the parents; D. Number of chromosome sets in plant. List II: I. Back cross; II. Ploidy; III. Allele; IV. Test cross. Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
why: Alternative forms of a gene are alleles; F₁ × homozygous recessive is a test cross; F₁ × a parent is a back cross; number of chromosome sets is ploidy.

q: A transcription unit in DNA is defined primarily by the three regions in DNA and these are with respect to upstream and down stream end:
why: A transcription unit consists of a promoter (upstream), the structural gene and a terminator (downstream).

q: A pink flowered Snapdragon plant was crossed with a red flowered Snapdragon plant. What type of phenotype/s is/are expected in the progeny?
opts: Red flowered as well as pink flowered plants
Red, Pink as well as white flowered plants
why: Snapdragon shows incomplete dominance: pink = Rr and red = RR. Rr × RR gives 1 RR (red) : 1 Rr (pink).

q: Inhibition of Succinic dehydrogenase enzyme by malonate is a classical example of:
why: Malonate resembles the substrate succinate in structure and competes for the active site of succinic dehydrogenase, so it is competitive inhibition.

q: Spindle fibers attach to kinetochores of chromosomes during:
why: Spindle fibres attach to the kinetochores and chromosomes align on the metaphase plate during metaphase (NCERT: the chromosomes are moved to the spindle equator).

q: Tropical regions show greatest level of species richness because: A. Tropical latitudes have remained relatively undisturbed for millions of years, hence more time was available for species diversification. B. Tropical environments are more seasonal. C. More solar energy is available in tropics. D. Constant environments promote niche specialization. E. Tropical environments are constant and predictable. Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
opts: A, C, D and E only
why: NCERT gives three reasons: long undisturbed evolutionary time, less seasonal, constant and predictable environments promoting niche specialisation, and more solar energy (productivity). B is false because the tropics are less seasonal.

q: The equation of Verhulst-Pearl logistic growth is dN/dt = rN[(K − N)/K]. From this equation, K indicates:
why: In the logistic equation K is the carrying capacity, the maximum population size the environment can support; r is the intrinsic rate of natural increase.

q: Identify the set of correct statements: A. The flowers of Vallisneria are colourful and produce nectar. B. The flowers of water lily are not pollinated by water. C. In most water-pollinated species, the pollen grains are protected from wetting. D. Pollen grains of some hydrophytes are long and ribbon like. E. In some hydrophytes, the pollen grains are carried passively inside water. Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
opts: A, B, C and D only
A, C, D and E only
B, C, D and E only
why: Vallisneria flowers are small, not colourful, and produce no nectar, so A is false. Water lily is insect or air pollinated, so B is true. C, D and E are true statements about water pollination.

q: How many molecules of ATP and NADPH are required for every molecule of CO₂ fixed in the Calvin cycle?
opts: 2 molecules of ATP and 3 molecules of NADPH
2 molecules of ATP and 2 molecules of NADPH
3 molecules of ATP and 3 molecules of NADPH
3 molecules of ATP and 2 molecules of NADPH
why: Fixing 3 CO₂ needs 9 ATP and 6 NADPH, so each CO₂ needs 3 ATP and 2 NADPH.

q: These are regarded as major causes of biodiversity loss: A. Over exploitation B. Co-extinction C. Mutation D. Habitat loss and fragmentation E. Migration Choose the correct option:
opts: A, B, C and D only
why: The 'evil quartet' consists of habitat loss and fragmentation, over-exploitation, alien species invasions and co-extinctions. Mutation and migration are not causes.

q: Formation of interfascicular cambium from fully developed parenchyma cells is an example for:
why: Mature parenchyma cells regaining the ability to divide to form interfascicular cambium is dedifferentiation.

q: The capacity to generate a whole plant from any cell of the plant is called:
why: Totipotency is the ability of any plant cell to regenerate a whole plant.

q: The lactose present in the growth medium of bacteria is transported to the cell by the action of:
why: In the lac operon, permease (product of lacY) increases permeability of the cell to lactose; beta-galactosidase hydrolyses it.

q: Hind III always cuts DNA molecules at a particular point called recognition sequence and it consists of:
why: Hind III is a type II restriction endonuclease with a palindromic recognition sequence of 6 base pairs (A^AGCTT).

q: Given below are two statements: Statement I: Chromosomes become gradually visible under light microscope during leptotene stage. Statement II: The beginning of diplotene stage is recognized by dissolution of synaptonemal complex.
opts: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
why: In leptotene the chromosomes become gradually visible; diplotene begins with dissolution of the synaptonemal complex and the bivalents separate except at chiasmata. Both are true.

q: List of endangered species was released by:
why: IUCN publishes the Red List of threatened species.

q: Match List I with List II. List-I: A. Rhizopus; B. Ustilago; C. Puccinia; D. Agaricus. List-II: I. Mushroom; II. Smut fungus; III. Bread mould; IV. Rust fungus. Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
why: Rhizopus is bread mould, Ustilago causes smut, Puccinia causes rust and Agaricus is the mushroom.

q: Given below are two statements: Statement I: Bt toxins are insect group specific and coded by a gene cry IAc. Statement II: Bt toxin exists as inactive protoxin in Bacillus thuringiensis. However, after ingestion by the insect the inactive protoxin gets converted into active form due to acidic pH of the insect gut.
opts: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
why: Bt toxins are insect-group specific and cryIAc targets cotton bollworms, so I is true. The protoxin is activated by the alkaline pH of the insect gut, not acidic, so II is false.

q: Given below are two statements: Statement I: Parenchyma is living but collenchyma is dead tissue. Statement II: Gymnosperms lack xylem vessels but presence of xylem vessels is the characteristic of angiosperms.
opts: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
why: Collenchyma is a living tissue, so I is false. Gymnosperms lack vessels (they have tracheids) while vessels are characteristic of angiosperms, so II is true.

q: Which one of the following can be explained on the basis of Mendel's Law of Dominance? A. Out of one pair of factors one is dominant and the other is recessive. B. Alleles do not show any expression and both the characters appear as such in F₂ generation. C. Factors occur in pairs in normal diploid plants. D. The discrete unit controlling a particular character is called factor. E. The expression of only one of the parental characters is found in a monohybrid cross. Choose the correct option:
opts: A, C, D and E only
A, B, C, D and E
why: The law of dominance covers factors occurring in pairs, one dominant and one recessive, the unit being a factor, and only one parental character expressed in F₁. B describes codominance or non-blending, not dominance.

q: Which of the following is an example of actinomorphic flower?
why: Datura has radial symmetry (actinomorphic). Cassia, Pisum and Sesbania have zygomorphic (bilaterally symmetrical) flowers.

q: In a plant, black seed color (BB/Bb) is dominant over white seed color (bb). In order to find out the genotype of the black seed plant, with which of the following genotype will you cross it?
why: A test cross uses the homozygous recessive parent (bb). If all progeny are black the plant is BB; if black and white appear in 1:1 it is Bb.

q: The cofactor of the enzyme carboxypeptidase is:
why: Carboxypeptidase is a metalloenzyme that needs zinc as its cofactor. Niacin, flavin and haem are components of other coenzymes or prosthetic groups.

q: Auxin is used by gardeners to prepare weed-free lawns. But no damage is caused to grass as auxin:
opts: promotes abscission of mature leaves only
does not affect mature monocotyledonous plants
can help in cell division in grasses, to produce growth
why: 2,4-D is a selective weedicide that kills dicot weeds but does not affect mature monocotyledonous plants such as grasses.

q: Match List I with List II. List I: A. Clostridium butylicum; B. Saccharomyces cerevisiae; C. Trichoderma polysporum; D. Streptococcus sp.  List II: I. Ethanol; II. Streptokinase; III. Butyric acid; IV. Cyclosporin-A. Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
why: Clostridium butylicum gives butyric acid, Saccharomyces gives ethanol, Trichoderma polysporum gives cyclosporin-A and Streptococcus gives streptokinase: A-III, B-I, C-IV, D-II.

q: Bulliform cells are responsible for:
opts: Inward curling of leaves in monocots.
Protecting the plant from salt stress.
Providing large spaces for storage of sugars.
why: Bulliform cells are large, empty, colourless cells on the upper epidermis of grass leaves. When they lose water the leaf curls inward, which minimises water loss.

q: Lecithin, a small molecular weight organic compound found in living tissues, is an example of:
why: Lecithin is a phospholipid, a lipid containing phosphorus and a phosphorylated organic (choline) compound.

q: Which one of the following is not a criterion for classification of fungi?
why: Fungi are classified on the basis of morphology of mycelium, mode of spore formation and fruiting bodies. Mode of nutrition is not used as a criterion because all fungi are heterotrophic.

q: Spraying sugarcane crop with which of the following plant growth regulators, increases the length of stem, thus increasing the yield?
why: Gibberellins cause elongation of internodes. Spraying them on sugarcane increases stem length and so the sugar yield.

q: Identify the step in tricarboxylic acid cycle, which does not involve oxidation of substrate.
why: Succinyl-CoA → succinic acid is substrate-level phosphorylation (GTP formed) with no NADH or FADH₂ produced, so there is no oxidation. The other steps involve dehydrogenation.

q: Which of the following are fused in somatic hybridization involving two varieties of plants?
why: In somatic hybridization, protoplasts (cells with the cell wall removed) from two varieties are fused to form a hybrid.

q: The DNA present in chloroplast is:
why: Chloroplasts, like mitochondria, contain small circular double-stranded DNA.

q: Match List I with List II. List I: A. Robert May; B. Alexander von Humboldt; C. Paul Ehrlich; D. David Tilman.  List II: I. Species-Area relationship; II. Long term ecosystem experiment using outdoor plots; III. Global species diversity at about 7 million; IV. Rivet popper hypothesis. Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
why: Robert May estimated about 7 million species, Humboldt described the species-area relationship, Ehrlich proposed the rivet popper hypothesis and Tilman did long-term outdoor plot experiments: A-III, B-I, C-IV, D-II.

q: Read the following statements and choose the set of correct statements: In the members of Phaeophyceae, A. Asexual reproduction occurs usually by biflagellate zoospores. B. Sexual reproduction is by oogamous method only. C. Stored food is in the form of carbohydrates which is either mannitol or laminarin. D. The major pigments found are chlorophyll a, c and carotenoids and xanthophyll. E. Vegetative cells have a cellulosic wall, usually covered on the outside by gelatinous coating of algin.
opts: A, B, C and D only
B, C, D and E only
A, C, D and E only
A, B, C and E only
why: Statement B is wrong because sexual reproduction in brown algae may be isogamous, anisogamous or oogamous. A, C, D and E are correct.

q: Given below are two statements: Statement I: In C3 plants, some O₂ binds to RuBisCO, hence CO₂ fixation is decreased. Statement II: In C4 plants, mesophyll cells show very little photorespiration while bundle sheath cells do not show photorespiration. Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
opts: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
why: Statement I is true: O₂ competes with CO₂ for RuBisCO in C3 plants. Statement II is false: in C4 plants RuBisCO is present only in bundle sheath cells, which have high CO₂, and mesophyll cells lack RuBisCO, so photorespiration is absent.

q: Which of the following statement is correct regarding the process of replication in E.coli?
opts: The DNA dependent DNA polymerase catalyzes polymerization in one direction that is 3' → 5'
The DNA dependent RNA polymerase catalyzes polymerization in one direction, that is 5' → 3'
The DNA dependent DNA polymerase catalyzes polymerization in 5' → 3' as well as 3' → 5' direction
The DNA dependent DNA polymerase catalyzes polymerization in 5' → 3' direction
why: DNA polymerase adds nucleotides only to the 3' end, so polymerization is always 5' → 3'. Option 2 is about RNA polymerase, which does not carry out replication.

q: Match List I with List II. List I: A. Citric acid cycle; B. Glycolysis; C. Electron transport system; D. Proton gradient.  List II: I. Cytoplasm; II. Mitochondrial matrix; III. Intermembrane space of mitochondria; IV. Inner mitochondrial membrane. Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
why: The citric acid cycle occurs in the matrix, glycolysis in the cytoplasm, the electron transport system on the inner membrane, and the proton gradient builds up in the intermembrane space: A-II, B-I, C-IV, D-III.

q: Match List I with List II. List I (Types of Stamens): A. Monadelphous; B. Diadelphous; C. Polyadelphous; D. Epiphyllous.  List II (Example): I. Citrus; II. Pea; III. Lily; IV. China-rose.
why: China-rose is monadelphous, pea is diadelphous, Citrus is polyadelphous and lily is epiphyllous: A-IV, B-II, C-I, D-III.

q: Match List I with List II. List I: A. Frederick Griffith; B. Francois Jacob & Jacque Monod; C. Har Gobind Khorana; D. Meselson & Stahl.  List II: I. Genetic code; II. Semi-conservative mode of DNA replication; III. Transformation; IV. Lac operon. Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
why: Griffith showed transformation, Jacob and Monod proposed the lac operon, Khorana worked on the genetic code, and Meselson and Stahl showed semi-conservative replication: A-III, B-IV, C-I, D-II.

q: Match List-I with List-II. List I: A. GLUT-4; B. Insulin; C. Trypsin; D. Collagen.  List II: I. Hormone; II. Enzyme; III. Intercellular ground substance; IV. Enables glucose transport into cells. Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
why: GLUT-4 enables glucose transport into cells, insulin is a hormone, trypsin is an enzyme and collagen is part of the intercellular ground substance: A-IV, B-I, C-II, D-III.

q: Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion A and the other is labelled as Reason R: Assertion A: FSH acts upon ovarian follicles in female and Leydig cells in male. Reason R: Growing ovarian follicles secrete estrogen in female while interstitial cells secrete androgen in male human being. Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
opts: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
why: In males FSH acts on Sertoli cells, while LH acts on Leydig (interstitial) cells, so A is false. R is true.

q: Match List I with List II. List I: A. Pons; B. Hypothalamus; C. Medulla; D. Cerebellum.  List II: I. Provides additional space for Neurons, regulates posture and balance; II. Controls respiration and gastric secretions; III. Connects different regions of the brain; IV. Neuro secretory cells. Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
why: Pons connects different brain regions, the hypothalamus has neurosecretory cells, the medulla controls respiration and gastric secretions, and the cerebellum regulates posture and balance: A-III, B-IV, C-II, D-I.

q: Which of the following is not a steroid hormone?
why: Glucagon is a peptide hormone. Cortisol, testosterone and progesterone are steroid hormones derived from cholesterol.

q: Which of the following is not a component of Fallopian tube?
why: The Fallopian tube consists of the infundibulum, ampulla and isthmus. The fundus is part of the uterus.

q: The flippers of the Penguins and Dolphins are the example of the:
why: Flippers of penguins (birds) and dolphins (mammals) are analogous structures: different origins but similar function and form, which is convergent evolution.

q: Match List I with List II. List-I: A. Lipase; B. Nuclease; C. Protease; D. Amylase.  List-II: I. Peptide bond; II. Ester bond; III. Glycosidic bond; IV. Phosphodiester bond.
why: Lipase breaks ester bonds in fats, nuclease breaks phosphodiester bonds in nucleic acids, protease breaks peptide bonds and amylase breaks glycosidic bonds in starch. So A-II, B-IV, C-I, D-III.

q: The "Ti plasmid" of Agrobacterium tumefaciens stands for:
why: Ti plasmid of Agrobacterium tumefaciens is the tumour inducing plasmid; its T-DNA causes crown gall tumours and is used as a vector in plants.

q: Match List I with List II. List I: A. Axoneme; B. Cartwheel pattern; C. Crista; D. Satellite.  List II: I. Centriole; II. Cilia and flagella; III. Chromosome; IV. Mitochondria.
why: Axoneme is the core of cilia and flagella; the cartwheel pattern is seen in centrioles; cristae are folds of the inner mitochondrial membrane; a satellite is part of a chromosome. So A-II, B-I, C-IV, D-III.

q: Which one of the following factors will not affect the Hardy-Weinberg equilibrium?
why: Hardy-Weinberg equilibrium is disturbed by gene flow (migration), genetic drift, mutation, recombination and natural selection. A constant gene pool is the condition for equilibrium, so it does not affect it.

q: Given below are two statements: Statement I: In the nephron, the descending limb of loop of Henle is impermeable to water and permeable to electrolytes. Statement II: The proximal convoluted tubule is lined by simple columnar brush border epithelium and increases the surface area for reabsorption.
opts: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
why: The descending limb is permeable to water and almost impermeable to electrolytes, so Statement I is false. The PCT is lined by simple cuboidal brush border epithelium, not columnar, so Statement II is false.

q: Match List I with List II. List I: A. α-1 antitrypsin; B. Cry IAb; C. Cry IAc; D. Enzyme replacement therapy.  List II: I. Cotton bollworm; II. ADA deficiency; III. Emphysema; IV. Corn borer.
why: α-1 antitrypsin is used against emphysema; Cry IAb kills corn borer; Cry IAc kills cotton bollworm; enzyme replacement therapy treats ADA deficiency. So A-III, B-IV, C-I, D-II.

q: Following are the stages of cell division: A. Gap 2 phase B. Cytokinesis C. Synthesis phase D. Karyokinesis E. Gap 1 phase. Choose the correct sequence of stages from the options given below:
why: The cell cycle runs G1 (E), S (C), G2 (A), then karyokinesis (D) and finally cytokinesis (B): E-C-A-D-B.

q: In both sexes of cockroach, a pair of jointed filamentous structures called anal cerci are present on:
why: Anal cerci are a pair of jointed filamentous structures on the 10th abdominal segment in both male and female cockroaches. Anal styles occur only in males on the 9th segment.

q: Match List I with List II. List I: A. Down's syndrome; B. α-Thalassemia; C. β-Thalassemia; D. Klinefelter's syndrome.  List II: I. 11th chromosome; II. X chromosome; III. 21st chromosome; IV. 16th chromosome.
why: Down's syndrome is trisomy of chromosome 21; α-thalassemia is linked to chromosome 16; β-thalassemia to chromosome 11; Klinefelter's syndrome has an extra X chromosome (XXY). So A-III, B-IV, C-I, D-II.

q: Which of the following is not a natural/traditional contraceptive method?
why: Coitus interruptus, periodic abstinence and lactational amenorrhea are natural methods. Vaults are barrier devices (like diaphragms and cervical caps), not natural methods.

q: Match List I with List II. List I: A. Typhoid; B. Leishmaniasis; C. Ringworm; D. Filariasis.  List II: I. Fungus; II. Nematode; III. Protozoa; IV. Bacteria.
why: Typhoid is caused by a bacterium (Salmonella typhi), leishmaniasis by a protozoan, ringworm by fungi and filariasis by a nematode (Wuchereria). So A-IV, B-III, C-I, D-II.

q: Match List I with List II. List I: A. Pleurobrachia; B. Radula; C. Stomochord; D. Air bladder.  List II: I. Mollusca; II. Ctenophora; III. Osteichthyes; IV. Hemichordata.
why: Pleurobrachia is a ctenophore; radula is a feature of molluscs; stomochord is found in hemichordates; air bladder is found in bony fishes (Osteichthyes). So A-II, B-I, C-IV, D-III.

q: Match List I with List II. List I: A. Common cold; B. Haemozoin; C. Widal test; D. Allergy.  List II: I. Plasmodium; II. Typhoid; III. Rhinoviruses; IV. Dust mites.
why: Common cold is caused by rhinoviruses; haemozoin is the toxin released from Plasmodium; the Widal test is used to diagnose typhoid; dust mites are a common allergen. So A-III, B-I, C-II, D-IV.

q: Given below are two statements: Statement I: The presence or absence of hymen is not a reliable indicator of virginity. Statement II: The hymen is torn during the first coitus only. In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
opts: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
why: The hymen can be torn by a sudden fall, sports, tampon use or horse riding, and may persist after coitus, so it is not a reliable indicator (I true). It is not torn only during first coitus (II false).

q: Following are the stages of pathway for conduction of an action potential through the heart: A. AV bundle B. Purkinje fibres C. AV node D. Bundle branches E. SA node. Choose the correct sequence of pathway from the options given below
why: The impulse starts at the SA node, passes to the AV node, then the AV bundle, the bundle branches and finally the Purkinje fibres: E-C-A-D-B.

q: Given below are some stages of human evolution. Arrange them in correct sequence (Past to Recent): A. Homo habilis B. Homo sapiens C. Homo neanderthalensis D. Homo erectus. Choose the correct sequence of human evolution from the options given below:
why: Homo habilis (about 2 mya) came first, then Homo erectus (1.5 mya), then Neanderthals (about 100,000 to 40,000 years ago), and Homo sapiens is the most recent: A-D-C-B.

q: Match List I with List II. List I (Sub Phases of Prophase I): A. Diakinesis; B. Pachytene; C. Zygotene; D. Leptotene.  List II (Specific Characters): I. Synaptonemal complex formation; II. Completion of terminalisation of chiasmata; III. Chromosomes look like thin threads; IV. Appearance of recombination nodules.
why: Leptotene: chromosomes appear as thin threads; zygotene: synaptonemal complex forms; pachytene: recombination nodules appear and crossing over occurs; diakinesis: terminalisation of chiasmata is completed. So A-II, B-IV, C-I, D-III.

q: Which of the following statements is incorrect?
opts: A bio-reactor provides optimal growth conditions for achieving the desired product.
Most commonly used bio-reactors are of stirring type.
Bio-reactors are used to produce small scale bacterial cultures.
Bio-reactors have an agitator system, an oxygen delivery system, and foam control system.
why: Bio-reactors are vessels for large-scale production of products in large volumes (100-1000 litres), not small-scale cultures, which are made in flasks. So statement (C) is incorrect.

q: Consider the following statements: A. Annelids are true coelomates B. Poriferans are pseudocoelomates C. Aschelminthes are acoelomates D. Platyhelminthes are pseudocoelomates. Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
why: Annelids are true coelomates (A correct). Poriferans are acoelomates with no true body cavity, Aschelminthes are pseudocoelomates and Platyhelminthes are acoelomates, so B, C and D are wrong.

q: Which one is the correct product of DNA dependent RNA polymerase to the given template? DNA Template: 3'TACATGGCAAATATCCATTCA5'
why: RNA is complementary and antiparallel to the template with U replacing T, so the mRNA is 5'AUGUACCGUUUAUAGGUAAGU3'. Option 4 has T (DNA), options 2 and 3 do not start with AUG, so option 1 is the closest and only valid RNA starting with AUG.

q: Given below are two statements: One is labelled as Assertion A and the other is labelled as Reason R: Assertion A: Breast-feeding during initial period of infant growth is recommended by doctors for bringing a healthy baby. Reason R: Colostrum contains several antibodies absolutely essential to develop resistance for the new born baby.
opts: Both A and R are correct and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are correct but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is correct but R is not correct
A is not correct but R is correct
why: Colostrum, the first milk, contains antibodies (IgA) that give the newborn passive immunity, which is why early breast-feeding is recommended. R explains A.

q: Match List I with List II. List I: A. Fibrous joints; B. Cartilaginous joints; C. Hinge joints; D. Ball and socket joints.  List II: I. Adjacent vertebrae, limited movement; II. Humerus and Pectoral girdle, rotational movement; III. Skull, don't allow any movement; IV. Knee, help in locomotion.
why: Fibrous joints (skull sutures) allow no movement; cartilaginous joints between vertebrae allow limited movement; hinge joints (knee) help locomotion; ball and socket (shoulder) allows rotation. So A-III, B-I, C-IV, D-II.

q: Match List I with List II. List I: A. Pterophyllum; B. Myxine; C. Pristis; D. Exocoetus.  List II: I. Hag fish; II. Saw fish; III. Angel fish; IV. Flying fish.
why: Pterophyllum is angel fish, Myxine is hag fish, Pristis is saw fish and Exocoetus is flying fish. So A-III, B-I, C-II, D-IV.

q: Match List I with List II. List I: A. Cocaine; B. Heroin; C. Morphine; D. Marijuana.  List II: I. Effective sedative in surgery; II. Cannabis sativa; III. Erythroxylum; IV. Papaver somniferum.
why: Cocaine comes from Erythroxylum coca; heroin (diacetylmorphine) is derived from morphine of Papaver somniferum; morphine is a sedative and painkiller used in surgery; marijuana comes from Cannabis sativa. So A-III, B-IV, C-I, D-II.

q: Which of the following are Autoimmune disorders? A. Myasthenia gravis B. Rheumatoid arthritis C. Gout D. Muscular dystrophy E. Systemic Lupus Erythematosus (SLE). Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
why: Myasthenia gravis, rheumatoid arthritis and SLE are autoimmune. Gout is a metabolic disorder (uric acid deposits) and muscular dystrophy is genetic.

q: Match List I with List II: List I: A. Exophthalmic goiter; B. Acromegaly; C. Cushing's syndrome; D. Cretinism  List II: I. Excess secretion of cortisol, moon face & hyperglycemia.; II. Hypo-secretion of thyroid hormone and stunted growth.; III. Hyper secretion of thyroid hormone & protruding eye balls.; IV. Excessive secretion of growth hormone. Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
why: Exophthalmic goiter (Graves' disease) = thyroid hormone excess with protruding eyes; acromegaly = excess growth hormone in adults; Cushing's = excess cortisol; cretinism = thyroid hormone deficiency in infancy.

q: Given below are two statements: Statement I: The cerebral hemispheres are connected by nerve tract known as corpus callosum. Statement II: The brain stem consists of the medulla oblongata, pons and cerebrum.
opts: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.
why: The corpus callosum joins the two cerebral hemispheres. The brain stem consists of the midbrain, pons and medulla oblongata, not the cerebrum.

q: Match List I with List II: List I: A. RNA polymerase III; B. Termination of transcription; C. Splicing of Exons; D. TATA box  List II: I. snRNPs; II. Promotor; III. Rho factor; IV. SnRNAs, tRNA Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
why: RNA polymerase III transcribes tRNA and snRNAs; Rho factor terminates transcription; snRNPs form the spliceosome that splices exons; the TATA box is part of the promoter.

q: Match List I with List II: List I: A. Mesozoic Era; B. Proterozoic Era; C. Cenozoic Era; D. Paleozoic Era  List II: I. Lower invertebrates; II. Fish & Amphibia; III. Birds & Reptiles; IV. Mammals Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
why: Mesozoic was the age of reptiles (and early birds), Proterozoic saw lower invertebrates, Cenozoic is the age of mammals, and Paleozoic had fishes and amphibians.

q: As per ABO blood grouping system, the blood group of father is B⁺, mother is A⁺ and child is O⁺. Their respective genotype can be: 1. IᴮI/IAi/ii (that is Bi / Ai / ii)  2. IᴮIᴮ / IAIA / ii  3. IAIB / iIA / IBi  4. IAi / IBi / IAi  5. iIBi / IA / IAIB (as printed, garbled) Choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below :
why: The child is O (ii), so each parent must carry i: father IBi (group B) and mother IAi (group A). Homozygous parents (option 2) cannot give an ii child, so only genotype set 1 is possible.

q: Match List I with List II related to the digestive system of a cockroach: List I: A. The structures used for storing of food; B. Ring of 6-8 blind tubules at junction of foregut and midgut; C. Ring of 100-150 yellow coloured thin filaments at junction of midgut and hindgut; D. The structures used for grinding the food.  List II: I. Gizzard; II. Gastric Caeca; III. Malpighian tubules; IV. Crop Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
why: The crop stores food, gastric caeca are 6-8 blind tubules at the foregut-midgut junction, Malpighian tubules (100-150) lie at the midgut-hindgut junction, and the gizzard grinds food.

q: Regarding catalytic cycle of an enzyme action, select the correct sequential steps: A. Substrate enzyme complex formation B. Free enzyme ready to bind with another substrate C. Release of products D. Chemical bonds of the substrate broken E. Substrate binding to active site
why: The substrate binds the active site (E), forming the ES complex (A), bonds are broken (D), products are released (C), and the free enzyme is ready again (B).

q: The following are the statements about non-chordates: A. Pharynx is perforated by gill slits. B. Notochord is absent. C. Central nervous system is dorsal. D. Heart is dorsal if present. E. Post anal tail is absent.
why: Non-chordates lack a notochord, gill slits and a post-anal tail; their heart, if present, is dorsal, and the nerve cord is ventral (not dorsal). So B, D and E are correct.

q: Given below are two statements: Statement I: Bone marrow is the main lymphoid organ where all blood cells including lymphocytes are produced. Statement II: Both bone marrow and thymus provide microenvironments for the development and maturation of T-lymphocytes.
opts: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.
why: Bone marrow produces all blood cells including lymphocytes. Bone marrow and thymus are the primary lymphoid organs providing microenvironments for lymphocyte development and maturation, as stated in NCERT.

q: Match List I with List II: List I: A. P wave; B. QRS complex; C. T wave; D. T-P gap  List II: I. Heart muscles are electrically silent.; II. Depolarisation of ventricles.; III. Depolarisation of atria.; IV. Repolarisation of ventricles. Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
why: P wave is atrial depolarisation, QRS is ventricular depolarisation, T wave is ventricular repolarisation, and the T-P gap is the electrically silent interval.

q: Given below are two statements: Statement I: Gause's competitive exclusion principle states that two closely related species competing for different resources cannot exist indefinitely. Statement II: According to Gause's principle, during competition, the inferior will be eliminated. This may be true if resources are limiting. In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below :
opts: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
Statement I is false but Statement II is true.
why: Gause's principle applies to closely related species competing for the same (limiting) resources, so Statement I (different resources) is false. Statement II is true.

q: Choose the correct statement given below regarding juxta medullary nephron.
opts: Juxta medullary nephrons are located in the columns of Bertini.
Renal corpuscle of juxta medullary nephron lies in the outer portion of the renal medulla.
Loop of Henle of juxta medullary nephron runs deep into medulla.
Juxta medullary nephrons outnumber the cortical nephrons.
why: Juxtamedullary nephrons have long loops of Henle that extend deep into the medulla; their corpuscles lie in the cortex near the medulla, and cortical nephrons are the more numerous type.

q: Match List I with List II: List I: A. Unicellular glandular epithelium; B. Compound epithelium; C. Multicellular glandular epithelium; D. Endocrine glandular epithelium  List II: I. Salivary glands; II. Pancreas; III. Goblet cells of alimentary canal; IV. Moist surface of buccal cavity Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
why: Goblet cells are unicellular glands; compound (stratified) epithelium lines the moist buccal cavity; salivary glands are multicellular exocrine glands; the pancreas has endocrine glandular tissue.

q: A particle of mass m is moving around the origin with a constant force F pulling it towards the origin. If Bohr model is used to describe its motion, the radius r of the nth orbit and the particle's speed v in the orbit depend on n as
why: F = mv²/r and mvr = nħ give v = nħ/(mr). Then F = n²ħ²/(m r³), so r³ ∝ n², r ∝ n^(2/3). Hence v ∝ n/r ∝ n^(1/3).

q: In some appropriate units, time (t) and position (x) relation of a moving particle is given by t = x² + x. The acceleration of the particle is

A model for quantized motion of an electron in a uniform magnetic field B states that the flux passing through the orbit of the electron is n(h/e) where n is an integer, h is Planck's constant and e is electron's charge. According to the model, the magnetic moment of an electron in its lowest energy state will be (m is the mass of the electron)
why: Lowest state n = 1: B·πr² = h/e. Orbit radius r = mv/(eB), so angular momentum L = mvr = eBr² = h/π. Magnetic moment μ = (e/2m)L = eh/(2πm).

q: A microscope has an objective of focal length 2 cm, eyepiece of focal length 4 cm and the tube length of 40 cm. If the distance of distinct vision of eye is 25 cm, the magnification in the microscope is
why: For a compound microscope, m ≈ (L/f_o)(D/f_e) = (40/2)(25/4) = 20 × 6.25 = 125.

q: There are two inclined surfaces of equal length (L) and same angle of inclination 45° with the horizontal. One of them is rough and the other is perfectly smooth. A given body takes 2 times as much time to slide down on rough surface than on the smooth surface. The coefficient of kinetic friction (μk) between the object and the rough surface is close to
why: From L = ½at², doubling the time means a_rough = a_smooth/4. So g sin45° – μg cos45° = (g sin45°)/4, giving 1 – μ = 1/4, μ = 0.75.

q: A uniform rod of mass 20 kg and length 5 m leans against a smooth vertical wall making an angle of 60° with it. The other end rests on a rough horizontal floor. The friction force that the floor exerts on the rod is (take g = 10 m/s²)
why: Torque about the floor end: W(L/2) sin60° = N_wall·L cos60°, so N_wall = (W/2) tan60° = 100√3 N. Friction balances the wall's normal force, so f = 100√3 N.

q: Two identical charged conducting spheres A and B have their centres separated by a certain distance. Charge on each sphere is q and the force of repulsion between them is F. A third identical uncharged conducting sphere is brought in contact with sphere A first and then with B and finally removed from both. New force of repulsion between spheres A and B (Radii of A and B are negligible compared to the distance of separation so that for calculating force between them they can be considered as point charges) is best given as :
why: After touching A: A = q/2. Then touching B: B = (q + q/2)/2 = 3q/4. New force = k(q/2)(3q/4)/r² = (3/8)F.

q: Two cities X and Y are connected by a regular bus service with a bus leaving in either direction every T min. A girl is driving scooty with a speed of 60 km/h in the direction X to Y notices that a bus goes past her every 30 minutes in the direction of her motion, and every 10 minutes in the opposite direction. Choose the correct option for the period T of the bus service and the speed (assumed constant) of the buses.
why: With bus speed v, spacing = vT. Same direction: (v – 60)(30) = vT. Opposite: (v + 60)(10) = vT. Equating: 30v – 1800 = 10v + 600, v = 120 km/h. Then T = 10(180)/120 = 15 min.

q: A container has two chambers of volumes V₁ = 2 litres and V₂ = 3 litres separated by a partition made of a thermal insulator. The chambers contains n₁ = 5 and n₂ = 4 moles of ideal gas at pressures p₁ = 1 atm and p₂ = 2 atm, respectively. When the partition is removed, the mixture attains an equilibrium pressure of :
why: T₁ = p₁V₁/(n₁R) = 0.4/R, T₂ = p₂V₂/(n₂R) = 1.5/R (atm·L units). No heat exchange, so n₁T₁ + n₂T₂ = (n₁+n₂)T gives 2 + 6 = 9T, T = 8/(9R). Then p = (9)(8/9)/(5) = 1.6 atm.

topic: Bohr model and de Broglie wavelength
q: De-Broglie wavelength of an electron orbiting in the n = 2 state of hydrogen atom is close to (Given Bohr radius = 0.052 nm)
why: 2πr_n = nλ, so λ = 2πr₂/2 = π r₂. r₂ = 4 × 0.052 = 0.208 nm, so λ = π × 0.208 ≈ 0.65 nm, closest to 0.67 nm.

q: To an ac power supply of 220 V at 50 Hz, a resistor of 20 Ω, a capacitor of reactance 25 Ω and an inductor of reactance 45 Ω are connected in series. The corresponding current in the circuit and the phase angle between the current and the voltage is, respectively -
A pipe open at both ends has a fundamental frequency f in air. The pipe is now dipped vertically in a water drum to half of its length. The fundamental frequency of the air column is now equal to :
why: Open pipe: f = v/(2L). Dipped to half length it becomes a closed pipe of length L/2, with fundamental v/(4·L/2) = v/(2L) = f.

q: Two identical point masses P and Q, suspended from two separate massless springs of spring constants k₁ and k₂, respectively, oscillate vertically. If their maximum speeds are the same, the ratio (A_Q/A_P) of the amplitude A_Q of mass Q to the amplitude A_P of mass P is:
why: v_max = Aω = A√(k/m). Equal speeds and equal mass give A_P√k₁ = A_Q√k₂, so A_Q/A_P = √(k₁/k₂).

q: An oxygen cylinder of volume 30 litre has 18.20 moles of oxygen. After some oxygen is withdrawn from the cylinder, its gauge pressure drops to 11 atmospheric pressure at temperature 27°C. The mass of the oxygen withdrawn from the cylinder is nearly equal to: [Given, R = 100/12 J mol⁻¹K⁻¹, and molecular mass of O₂ = 32, 1 atm pressure = 1.01 × 10⁵ N/m²]
why: Gauge 11 atm means absolute pressure 12 atm = 1.212 × 10⁶ Pa. n = PV/RT = (1.212×10⁶ × 0.03)/((100/12)×300) ≈ 14.54 mol. Withdrawn = 18.20 – 14.54 ≈ 3.66 mol, mass ≈ 3.66 × 32 ≈ 0.117 kg, closest to 0.116 kg.

q: In a certain camera, a combination of four similar thin convex lenses are arranged axially in contact. Then the power of the combination and the total magnification in comparison to the power (p) and magnification (m) for each lens will be, respectively –
why: Powers of thin lenses in contact add: P = 4p. Magnifications of successive lenses multiply: total m⁴.

q: Two gases A and B are filled at the same pressure in separate cylinders with movable pistons of radius r_A and r_B, respectively. On supplying an equal amount of heat to both the systems reversibly under constant pressure, the pistons of gas A and B are displaced by 16 cm and 9 cm, respectively. If the change in their internal energy is the same, then the ratio r_A/r_B is equal to
why: Q = ΔU + W with equal Q and equal ΔU means equal work W = PΔV. So πr_A²(16) = πr_B²(9), r_A²/r_B² = 9/16, r_A/r_B = 3/4.

q: A balloon is made of a material of surface tension S and its inflation outlet (from where gas is filled in it) has small area A. It is filled with a gas of density ρ and takes a spherical shape of radius R. When the gas is allowed to flow freely out of it, its radius r changes from R to 0 (zero) in time T. If the speed v(r) of gas coming out of the balloon depends on r as r^a and T ∝ S^α A^β ρ^γ R^δ then
why: Excess pressure ∝ S/r and v ≈ √(2ΔP/ρ) ∝ (S/ρr)^(1/2), so a = –1/2. Volume flow: r² dr/dt ∝ –A v ∝ –A S^(1/2)ρ^(-1/2) r^(-1/2), so T ∝ R^(7/2) S^(-1/2) A^(-1) ρ^(1/2).

q: A physical quantity P is related to four observations a, b, c and d as follows: P = a³b²/(c√d). The percentage errors of measurement in a, b, c and d are 1%, 3%, 2%, and 4% respectively. The percentage error in the quantity P is

topic: System of particles and rotational motion
q: The Sun rotates around its centre once in 27 days. What will be the period of revolution if the Sun were to expand to twice its present radius without any external influence? Assume the Sun to be a sphere of uniform density.
why: Angular momentum is conserved: Iω = constant with I ∝ MR². Doubling R makes I four times, so ω falls to 1/4 and the period becomes 4 × 27 = 108 days.

q: The radius of Martian orbit around the Sun is about 4 times the radius of the orbit of Mercury. The Martian year is 687 Earth days. Then which of the following is the length of 1 year on Mercury ?
why: Kepler's third law: T² ∝ r³, so T_Mars/T_Mercury = 4^(3/2) = 8. T_Mercury = 687/8 ≈ 86 days, closest to 88 days.

q: A wire of resistance R is cut into 8 equal pieces. From these pieces two equivalent resistances are made by adding four of these together in parallel. Then these two sets are added in series. The net effective resistance of the combination is :
why: Each piece is R/8. Four in parallel give (R/8)/4 = R/32. Two such sets in series give R/16.

topic: Dual nature of matter and radiation
q: A photon and an electron (mass m) have the same energy E. The ratio (λ_photon/λ_electron) of their de Broglie wavelengths is: (c is the speed of light)
why: λ_photon = hc/E and λ_electron = h/√(2mE). The ratio is (hc/E)·√(2mE)/h = c√(2m/E).

q: An electron (mass 9×10⁻³¹ kg and charge 1.6×10⁻¹⁹ C) moving with speed c/100 (c = speed of light) is injected into a magnetic field B of magnitude 9×10⁻⁴ T perpendicular to its direction of motion.
