We wish to apply an uniform electric field E together with the magnetic field so that the electron does not deflect from its path. Then (speed of light c = 3×10⁸ ms⁻¹)
opts: E is parallel to B and its magnitude is 27×10² V m⁻¹
E is parallel to B and its magnitude is 27×10⁴ V m⁻¹
E is perpendicular to B and its magnitude is 27×10⁴ V m⁻¹
E is perpendicular to B and its magnitude is 27×10² V m⁻¹
why: For no deflection qE = qvB, with E perpendicular to both v and B. v = 3×10⁶ m/s, so E = vB = 3×10⁶ × 9×10⁻⁴ = 2.7×10³ = 27×10² V/m.

q: The electric field in a plane electromagnetic wave is given by E_z = 60 cos(5x + 1.5×10⁹ t) V/m. Then expression for the corresponding magnetic field is (here subscripts denote the direction of the field) :
why: The wave speed is ω/k = 1.5×10⁹/5 = 3×10⁸ m/s, travelling along –x. B₀ = E₀/c = 60/(3×10⁸) = 2×10⁻⁷ T, in phase with E. E × B must point along –x; with E along z, B is along y.

q: A body weighs 48 N on the surface of the earth. The gravitational force experienced by the body due to the earth at a height equal to one-third the radius of the earth from its surface is :
why: g ∝ 1/r². At height R/3, r = 4R/3, so the force = 48 × (R/(4R/3))² = 48 × 9/16 = 27 N.

q: An unpolarized light beam travelling in air is incident on a medium of refractive index 1.73 at Brewster's angle. Then-
opts: both reflected and transmitted light are perfectly polarized with angles of reflection and refraction close to 60° and 30°, respectively.
transmitted light is completely polarized with angle of refraction close to 30°
reflected light is completely polarized and the angle of reflection is close to 60°
reflected light is partially polarized and the angle of reflection is close to 30°
why: Brewster's law: tan i_p = 1.73 = √3, so i_p = 60°. At this angle the reflected light is completely polarized while the transmitted light is only partially polarized; refraction angle is 30°.

q: The plates of a parallel plate capacitor are separated by d. Two slabs of different dielectric constant K₁ and K₂ with thickness 3d/8 and d/2, respectively, are inserted in the capacitor. Due to this, the capacitance becomes two times larger than when there is nothing between the plates. If K₁ = 1.25 K₂, the value of K₁ is :
why: C = ε₀A/[d – t₁ – t₂ + t₁/K₁ + t₂/K₂] = 2ε₀A/d, so d/8 + 3d/(8K₁) + d/(2K₂) = d/2. With K₂ = K₁/1.25 this gives 0.375/K₁ + 0.625/K₁ = 0.375, so K₁ = 1/0.375 ≈ 2.66.

q: Consider the diameter of a spherical object being measured with the help of a Vernier callipers. Suppose its 10 Vernier Scale Divisions (V.S.D.) are equal to its 9 Main Scale Divisions (M.S.D.). The least division in the M.S. is 0.1 cm and the zero of V.S. is at x = 0.1 cm when the jaws of Vernier callipers are closed. If the main scale reading for the diameter is M = 5 cm and the number of coinciding vernier division is 8, the measured diameter after zero error correction, is
why: Least count = 0.1 cm/10 = 0.01 cm. Observed reading = 5 + 8 × 0.01 = 5.08 cm. Zero error is +0.1 cm (zero of vernier sits at 0.1 cm when closed), so corrected diameter = 5.08 – 0.1 = 4.98 cm.

q: A 2 amp current is flowing through two different small circular copper coils having radii ratio 1:2. The ratio of their respective magnetic moments will be
why: Magnetic moment M = I·πr². With equal current, M ∝ r², so the ratio is 1² : 2² = 1:4.

q: The correct order of decreasing acidity of the following aliphatic acids is :
why: Alkyl groups are electron-donating (+I) and destabilise the carboxylate anion, so acidity falls as the number and size of alkyl groups increase: HCOOH is strongest and (CH₃)₃CCOOH weakest.

topic: Practical organic chemistry detection of elements
q: Which one of the following reactions does NOT belong to “Lassaigne’s test”?
why: Lassaigne's test fuses the organic compound with sodium to give NaX, NaCN and Na₂S. The reduction of CuO by carbon is a test for carbon in other detection methods, not part of the sodium fusion extract.

q: If the rate constant of a reaction is 0.03 s⁻¹, how much time does it take for 7.2 mol L⁻¹ concentration of the reactant to get reduced to 0.9 mol L⁻¹? (Given: log 2 = 0.301)
why: First order: t = (2.303/k) log([A]₀/[A]) = (2.303/0.03) × log 8 = 76.8 × 0.903 ≈ 69.3 s. (7.2 → 0.9 is three half-lives of 23.1 s each.)

q: Given below are two statements : Statement I : A hypothetical diatomic molecule with bond order zero is quite stable. Statement II : As bond order increases, the bond length increases. In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below :
opts: Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
why: Bond order zero means no net bonding, so the molecule is not stable. Bond length decreases as bond order increases. Both statements are false.

topic: Colligative properties elevation of boiling point
q: Which of the following aqueous solution will exhibit highest boiling point?
why: Elevation of boiling point depends on i × C: Na₂SO₄ = 3 × 0.01 = 0.03; glucose = 0.015; urea = 0.01; KNO₃ = 2 × 0.01 = 0.02. Na₂SO₄ is highest.

q: Consider the following compounds : KO₂, H₂O₂ and H₂SO₄. The oxidation states of the underlined elements (K in KO₂, O in H₂O₂, S in H₂SO₄) in them are, respectively,
why: K is +1 (alkali metal). In H₂O₂ each O is −1 (peroxide). In H₂SO₄: 2(+1) + S + 4(−2) = 0 gives S = +6.

q: Match List - I with List - II. List-I: A. Haber process; B. Wacker oxidation; C. Wilkinson catalyst; D. Ziegler catalyst. List-II: I. Fe catalyst; II. PdCl₂; III. [(PPh₃)₃RhCl]; IV. TiCl₄ with Al(CH₃)₃. Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
why: Haber process uses Fe; Wacker oxidation uses PdCl₂; Wilkinson's catalyst is [(PPh₃)₃RhCl]; Ziegler-Natta catalyst is TiCl₄ with Al(CH₃)₃.

q: Given below are two statements : Statement I : Like nitrogen that can form ammonia, arsenic can form arsine. Statement II : Antimony cannot form antimony pentoxide. In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below :
opts: Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
why: Arsenic forms arsine (AsH₃), so Statement I is correct. Antimony does form the pentoxide Sb₂O₅ (+5 state), so Statement II is incorrect.

q: Match List - I with List - II. List-I: A. XeO₃; B. XeF₂; C. XeOF₄; D. XeF₆. List-II: I. sp³d; linear; II. sp³; pyramidal; III. sp³d³; distorted octahedral; IV. sp³d²; square pyramidal. Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
why: XeO₃ is sp³ pyramidal; XeF₂ is sp³d linear; XeOF₄ is sp³d² square pyramidal; XeF₆ is sp³d³ distorted octahedral.

q: How many products (including stereoisomers) are expected from monochlorination of the following compound? (CH₃)₂CH–CH₂–CH₃ (2-methylbutane)
why: 2-Methylbutane has four types of H: Cl at C1 gives 1-chloro-2-methylbutane (chiral, 2 stereoisomers); at C2 gives 2-chloro-2-methylbutane (1); at C3 gives 2-chloro-3-methylbutane (chiral, 2); at C4 gives 1-chloro-3-methylbutane (1). Total = 6.

q: Which of the following statements are true? A. Unlike Ga that has a very high melting point, Cs has a very low melting point. B. On Pauling scale, the electronegativity values of N and Cl are not the same. C. Ar, K⁺, Cl⁻, Ca²⁺, and S²⁻ are all isoelectronic species. D. The correct order of the first ionization enthalpies of Na, Mg, Al, and Si is Si > Al > Mg > Na. E. The atomic radius of Cs is greater than that of Li and Rb. Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
why: Ga has a low melting point (about 303 K), so A is false; N and Cl both have electronegativity 3.0, so B is false; all species in C have 18 electrons; the correct IE order is Si > Mg > Al > Na, so D is false; Cs > Rb > Li in size, so E is true.

q: The standard heat of formation, in kcal/mol of Ba²⁺ is : [Given : standard heat of formation of SO₄²⁻ ion (aq) = −216 kcal/mol, standard heat of crystallisation of BaSO₄(s) = −4.5 kcal/mol, standard heat of formation of BaSO₄(s) = −349 kcal/mol]
why: Ba²⁺(aq) + SO₄²⁻(aq) → BaSO₄(s) has ΔH = −4.5. So ΔHf(BaSO₄) = ΔHf(Ba²⁺) + ΔHf(SO₄²⁻) − 4.5, giving −349 = x − 216 − 4.5 and x = −128.5 kcal/mol.

q: Match List - I with List - II. List-I (Example): A. Humidity; B. Alloys; C. Amalgams; D. Smoke. List-II (Type of Solution): I. Solid in solid; II. Liquid in gas; III. Solid in gas; IV. Liquid in solid. Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
why: Humidity is liquid (water) in gas; alloys are solid in solid; amalgams are liquid (Hg) in solid; smoke is solid particles in gas.

q: Sugar ‘X’ A. is found in honey. B. is a keto sugar. C. exists in α and β - anomeric forms. D. is laevorotatory. ‘X’ is :
why: D-Fructose is present in honey, is a ketohexose, exists in α and β anomeric forms and is laevorotatory (−92.4°). Sucrose has no free anomeric carbon and glucose is an aldose.

q: Total number of possible isomers (both structural as well as stereoisomers) of cyclic ethers of molecular formula C₄H₈O is :
why: Tetrahydrofuran (1); 2-methyloxetane (2 enantiomers) and 3-methyloxetane (1); 2-ethyloxirane (2); 2,2-dimethyloxirane (1); 2,3-dimethyloxirane (cis plus 2 trans enantiomers = 3). Total = 1 + 3 + 2 + 1 + 3 = 10.

q: For the reaction A(g) ⇌ 2B(g), the backward reaction rate constant is higher than the forward reaction rate constant by a factor of 2500, at 1000 K. [Given : R = 0.0831 L atm mol⁻¹ K⁻¹] K_P for the reaction at 1000 K is
The ratio of the wavelengths of the light absorbed by a Hydrogen atom when it undergoes n = 2 → n = 3 and n = 4 → n = 6 transitions, respectively, is

If the molar conductivity (Λm) of a 0.050 mol L⁻¹ solution of a monobasic weak acid is 90 S cm² mol⁻¹, its extent (degree) of dissociation will be [Assume Λ°₊ = 349.6 S cm² mol⁻¹ and Λ°₋ = 50.4 S cm² mol⁻¹.]
why: Λ°m = 349.6 + 50.4 = 400 S cm² mol⁻¹. Degree of dissociation α = Λm/Λ°m = 90/400 = 0.225.

q: 5 moles of liquid X and 10 moles of liquid Y make a solution having a vapour pressure of 70 torr. The vapour pressures of pure X and Y are 63 torr and 78 torr respectively. Which of the following is true regarding the described solution?
opts: The solution has volume greater than the sum of individual volumes.
why: Ideal vapour pressure = (5/15)(63) + (10/15)(78) = 21 + 52 = 73 torr. The observed 70 torr is lower, so there is negative deviation (and volume is less than the sum).

topic: Some basic concepts of chemistry mole concept
q: Among the following, choose the ones with equal number of atoms. A. 212 g of Na₂CO₃ (s) [molar mass = 106 g] B. 248 g of Na₂O (s) [molar mass = 62 g] C. 240 g of NaOH (s) [molar mass = 40 g] D. 12 g of H₂ (g) [molar mass = 2 g] E. 220 g of CO₂(g) [molar mass = 44 g] Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
why: Moles of atoms: A = 2 × 6 = 12; B = 4 × 3 = 12; C = 6 × 3 = 18; D = 6 × 2 = 12; E = 5 × 3 = 15. A, B and D are equal.

q: Which of the following are paramagnetic? A. [NiCl₄]²⁻ B. Ni(CO)₄ C. [Ni(CN)₄]²⁻ D. [Ni(H₂O)₆]²⁺ E. Ni(PPh₃)₄ Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
why: [NiCl₄]²⁻ (tetrahedral, Ni²⁺ d⁸ with weak field) and [Ni(H₂O)₆]²⁺ (octahedral) have 2 unpaired electrons. Ni(CO)₄ and Ni(PPh₃)₄ are Ni(0) d¹⁰, and [Ni(CN)₄]²⁻ is square planar, so all are diamagnetic.

q: If the half-life (t₁/₂) for a first order reaction is 1 minute, then the time required for 99.9% completion of the reaction is closest to :
Energy and radius of first Bohr orbit of He⁺ and Li²⁺ are [Given R_H = 2.18 × 10⁻¹⁸ J, a₀ = 52.9 pm]
Dalton’s Atomic theory could not explain which of the following?
why: Dalton's theory explained the laws of conservation of mass, constant proportion and multiple proportion, but could not explain Gay-Lussac's law of gaseous volumes.

q: Identify the correct orders against the property mentioned. A. H₂O > NH₃ > CHCl₃ – dipole moment B. XeF₄ > XeO₃ > XeF₂ – number of lone pairs on central atom C. O–H > C–H > N–O – bond length D. N₂ > O₂ > H₂ – bond enthalpy Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
why: Dipole moments: H₂O 1.85 > NH₃ 1.47 > CHCl₃ 1.04 (A true). Lone pairs: XeF₂ 3, XeF₄ 2, XeO₃ 1 (B false). Bond length: N–O > C–H > O–H (C false). Bond enthalpy: N₂ 946 > O₂ 498 > H₂ 436 (D true).

q: Match List I with List II. List I (Name of Vitamin): A. Vitamin B₁₂; B. Vitamin D; C. Vitamin B₂; D. Vitamin B₆. List II (Deficiency disease): I. Cheilosis; II. Convulsions; III. Rickets; IV. Pernicious anaemia. Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
why: Vitamin B₁₂ deficiency causes pernicious anaemia; vitamin D deficiency causes rickets; vitamin B₂ (riboflavin) deficiency causes cheilosis; vitamin B₆ deficiency causes convulsions.

q: The correct order of decreasing basic strength of the given amines is
why: Aliphatic amines are stronger bases than aromatic ones, and the secondary N-ethylethanamine is stronger than primary ethanamine in aqueous solution. N-methylaniline (pKb about 9.2) is slightly more basic than aniline (pKb about 9.4) due to the +I effect of CH₃.

q: The correct order of the wavelength of light absorbed by the following complexes is, A. [Co(NH₃)₆]³⁺ B. [Co(CN)₆]³⁻ C. [Cu(H₂O)₄]²⁺ D. [Ti(H₂O)₆]³⁺ Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
why: Larger crystal field splitting Δ means shorter wavelength absorbed. Δ order: [Co(CN)₆]³⁻ > [Co(NH₃)₆]³⁺ > [Ti(H₂O)₆]³⁺ > [Cu(H₂O)₄]²⁺ (CN⁻ strongest field; Cu²⁺ aqua has small Δ). So λ: B < A < D < C.

q: Match List I with List II. List I (Mixture): A. CHCl₃ + C₆H₅NH₂; B. Crude oil in petroleum industry; C. Glycerol from spent-lye; D. Aniline - water. List II (Method of Separation): I. Distillation under reduced pressure; II. Steam distillation; III. Fractional distillation; IV. Simple distillation. Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
why: CHCl₃ and aniline differ widely in boiling points: simple distillation. Crude oil: fractional distillation. Glycerol from spent lye: distillation under reduced pressure. Aniline in water: steam distillation.

q: Which among the following electronic configurations belong to main group elements? A. [Ne]3s¹ B. [Ar]3d³4s² C. [Kr]4d¹⁰5s²5p⁵ D. [Ar]3d¹⁰4s¹ E. [Rn]5f⁰6d²7s² Choose the correct option given below :
why: A is Na (s-block) and C is I (p-block): main group. B is V, D is Cu and E is Rf, which are d-block transition elements.

q: Which one of the following compounds can exist as cis-trans isomers?
why: Cis-trans isomerism needs two different substituents on each of two ring carbons or double-bond carbons. 1,2-Dimethylcyclohexane qualifies; the others have identical groups on one carbon.

q: Phosphoric acid ionizes in three steps with their ionization constant values Ka1, Ka2 and Ka3 respectively, while K is the overall ionization constant. Which of the following statements are true? A. log K = log Ka1 + log Ka2 + log Ka3 B. H₃PO₄ is a stronger acid than H₂PO₄⁻ and HPO₄²⁻. C. Ka1 > Ka2 > Ka3 D. Ka1 = (Ka3 + Ka2)/2 Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
why: K = Ka1 × Ka2 × Ka3 so A is true. Each successive ionization is harder (Ka1 > Ka2 > Ka3), so B and C are true, and D has no basis.

q: Match List I with List II. List I (Ion): A. Co²⁺; B. Mg²⁺; C. Pb²⁺; D. Al³⁺. List II (Group Number in Cation Analysis): I. Group-I; II. Group-III; III. Group-IV; IV. Group-VI. Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
why: Co²⁺ is Group IV, Mg²⁺ is Group VI, Pb²⁺ is Group I (as PbCl₂) and Al³⁺ is Group III.

q: Higher yield of NO in N₂(g) + O₂(g) ⇌ 2NO(g) can be obtained at [ΔH of the reaction = + 180.7 kJ mol⁻¹] A. higher temperature B. lower temperature C. higher concentration of N₂ D. higher concentration of O₂ Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
why: The reaction is endothermic, so a higher temperature favours NO. Increasing the concentration of the reactants N₂ or O₂ also shifts the equilibrium forward (Le Chatelier's principle).

q: Given below are two statements: Statement I: Benzenediazonium salt is prepared by the reaction of aniline with nitrous acid at 273 - 278 K. It decomposes easily in the dry state. Statement II: Insertion of iodine into the benzene ring is difficult and hence iodobenzene is prepared through the reaction of benzenediazonium salt with KI. In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
opts: Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
why: Diazotisation of aniline with HNO₂ at 273-278 K gives the diazonium salt, which is unstable and explosive when dry. Direct iodination is reversible and difficult, so ArN₂⁺ + KI → ArI is used. Both statements are correct.

q: The protein portion of an enzyme is called:
why: The protein part of a conjugate enzyme is the apoenzyme; the non-protein part is the cofactor. Apoenzyme + cofactor = holoenzyme.

q: Given below are two statements: Statement I: The primary source of energy in an ecosystem is solar energy. Statement II: The rate of production of organic matter during photosynthesis in an ecosystem is called net primary productivity (NPP). In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
opts: Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
why: Solar energy is the primary energy source, so Statement I is correct. The rate of organic matter production in photosynthesis is gross primary productivity (GPP); NPP = GPP - respiratory losses, so Statement II is incorrect.

q: Assertion (A): A typical unfertilised, angiosperm embryo sac at maturity is 8 nucleate and 7-celled. Reason (R): The egg apparatus has 2 polar nuclei. In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
opts: A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
why: The embryo sac is 8-nucleate and 7-celled, so A is true. The egg apparatus has two synergids and one egg cell; the two polar nuclei lie in the central cell, so R is false.

q: Neoplastic characteristics of cells refer to: A. A mass of proliferating cell B. Rapid growth of cells C. Invasion and damage to the surrounding tissue D. Those confined to original location. Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
why: Neoplastic (cancerous) cells proliferate rapidly as a mass and invade and damage surrounding tissue. Being confined to the original location is a feature of benign tumours, so D is wrong.

q: Which one of the following is the characteristic feature of gymnosperms?
why: Gymnos means naked: gymnosperm ovules are not enclosed in an ovary, so the seeds are naked.

q: Match List - I with List - II. List I: A. Progesterone; B. Relaxin; C. Melanocyte stimulating hormone; D. Catecholamines. List II: I. Pars intermedia; II. Ovary; III. Adrenal Medulla; IV. Corpus luteum. Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
why: Progesterone comes from the corpus luteum, relaxin from the ovary, MSH from the pars intermedia and catecholamines from the adrenal medulla.

q: Which chromosome in the human genome has the highest number of genes?
why: Human Genome Project data: chromosome 1 has the most genes (2968) while Y has the fewest (231).

q: Which of the following statements about RuBisCO is true?
opts: It is an enzyme involved in the photolysis of water.
It catalyzes the carboxylation of RuBP.
It is active only in the dark.
It has higher affinity for oxygen than carbon dioxide.
why: RuBisCO catalyses carboxylation of RuBP with CO₂ to form 3-PGA. It is not involved in water photolysis, is not dark-only, and has higher affinity for CO₂ than O₂ (it has oxygenase activity at high O₂).

q: The first menstruation is called:
why: The first menstrual cycle at puberty is menarche; cessation at about 50 years is menopause.

q: Which of the following genetically engineered organisms was used by Eli Lilly to prepare human insulin?
why: Eli Lilly produced human insulin (Humulin) using the bacterium E. coli carrying the A and B chain genes.

q: Assertion (A): All vertebrates are chordates but all chordates are not vertebrate. Reason (R): The members of subphylum vertebrata possess notochord during the embryonic period, the notochord is replaced by a cartilaginous or bony vertebral column in adults. In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
opts: A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
why: All vertebrates have a notochord at some stage so are chordates, while urochordates and cephalochordates are chordates without a vertebral column. R explains why vertebrates are chordates, so both are true and R explains A.

q: What is the main function of the spindle fibers during mitosis?
why: Spindle fibres attach to kinetochores and pull sister chromatids to opposite poles during anaphase.

q: Match List I with List II. List-I: A. Alfred Hershey and Martha Chase; B. Euchromatin; C. Frederick Griffith; D. Heterochromatin. List-II: I. Streptococcus pneumoniae; II. Densely packed and dark-stained; III. Loosely packed and light-stained; IV. DNA as genetic material confirmation. Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
why: Hershey-Chase confirmed DNA as genetic material; euchromatin is loosely packed and light-stained; Griffith used Streptococcus pneumoniae; heterochromatin is densely packed and dark-stained.

q: Match List I with List II. List I: A. Adenosine; B. Adenylic acid; C. Adenine; D. Alanine. List II: I. Nitrogen base; II. Nucleotide; III. Nucleoside; IV. Amino acid. Choose the option with all correct matches.
why: Adenosine is a nucleoside, adenylic acid (AMP) a nucleotide, adenine a nitrogen base and alanine an amino acid.

q: In frog, the Renal portal system is a special venous connection that acts to link:
opts: Kidney and lower part of body
why: The renal portal vein carries blood from the lower part of the body (hind limbs) to the kidneys, in addition to the hepatic portal system linking intestine and liver.

q: Which of the following are the post-transcriptional events in an eukaryotic cell? A. Transport of pre-mRNA to cytoplasm prior to splicing. B. Removal of introns and joining of exons. C. Addition of methyl group at 5' end of hnRNA. D. Addition of adenine residues at 3' end of hnRNA. E. Base pairing of two complementary RNAs. Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
why: hnRNA processing consists of splicing (B), 5' capping with methyl guanosine (C) and 3' poly-A tailing (D). Splicing occurs before export to the cytoplasm, so A is wrong; E is not a processing step.

q: Polymerase chain reaction (PCR) amplifies DNA following the equation.
why: Each PCR cycle doubles the DNA, so after n cycles one copy gives 2ⁿ copies.

q: Assertion (A): Both wind and water pollinated flowers are not very colourful and do not produce nectar. Reason (R): The flowers produce enormous amount of pollen grains in wind and water pollinated flowers. In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
opts: A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
why: Abiotic-pollinated flowers lack colour and nectar, and they do produce huge amounts of pollen, so both are true. However, the large pollen output does not explain the absence of colour and nectar.

q: Epiphytes that are growing on a mango branch is an example of which of the following?
why: The epiphyte benefits by getting support while the mango tree is neither harmed nor benefited: commensalism.

q: Frogs respire in water by skin and buccal cavity and on land by skin, buccal cavity and lungs. Choose the correct answer from the following:
opts: The statement is false for water but true for land
The statement is false for both the environment
The statement is true for water but false for land
The statement is true for both the environment
why: In water frogs respire only through the skin (cutaneous respiration), so buccal cavity is not involved there; on land they use skin, buccal cavity and lungs. The statement is false for water but true for land.

q: Consider the following statements regarding function of adrenal medullary hormones: A. It causes pupilary constriction B. It is a hyperglycemic hormone C. It causes piloerection D. It increases strength of heart contraction. Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
why: Adrenaline and noradrenaline cause pupillary dilation (not constriction), raise blood glucose, cause piloerection and increase the force of heart contraction. So B, C and D are correct.

q: Read the following statements on plant growth and development. A. Parthenocarpy can be induced by auxins. B. Plant growth regulators can be involved in promotion as well as inhibition of growth. C. Dedifferentiation is a pre-requisite for re-differentiation. D. Abscisic acid is a plant growth promoter. E. Apical dominance promotes the growth of lateral buds. Choose the option with all correct statements.
why: Auxins induce parthenocarpy, PGRs can promote or inhibit growth, and dedifferentiation precedes redifferentiation. ABA is an inhibitor, and apical dominance inhibits lateral buds, so D and E are wrong.

q: Which of the following hormones released from the pituitary is actually synthesized in the hypothalamus?
why: ADH and oxytocin are made in hypothalamic neurons and stored and released from the posterior pituitary. FSH, ACTH and LH are synthesised in the anterior pituitary.

q: Which of the following is an example of non-distilled alcoholic beverage produced by yeast?
why: Wine and beer are produced by fermentation without distillation; whisky, brandy and rum are distilled.

q: What is the pattern of inheritance for polygenic trait?
why: Polygenic traits (such as height or skin colour) are controlled by several genes with additive effects and show continuous variation, which does not follow a simple Mendelian pattern.

q: Match List I with List II. List I: A. Head; B. Middle piece; C. Acrosome; D. Tail. List II: I. Enzymes; II. Sperm motility; III. Energy; IV. Genetic material. Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
why: The head holds the nucleus (genetic material), the middle piece has mitochondria (energy), the acrosome has enzymes, and the tail gives motility.

q: Which of the following is an example of a zygomorphic flower?
why: Pea (and Cassia, Gulmohar) has zygomorphic flowers; chilli, petunia and datura are actinomorphic.

q: Which of following organisms cannot fix nitrogen? A. Azotobacter B. Oscillatoria C. Anabaena D. Volvox E. Nostoc. Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
why: Azotobacter, Oscillatoria, Anabaena and Nostoc are nitrogen fixers; Volvox is a green alga and cannot fix nitrogen.

q: Which one of the following is an example of ex-situ conservation?
why: Ex-situ conservation takes organisms out of their habitat, as in zoos, botanical gardens and seed banks. The others are in-situ.

q: Who is known as the father of Ecology in India?
why: Ramdeo Misra is regarded as the father of ecology in India.

q: Given below are two statements: Statement I: In the RNA world, RNA is considered the first genetic material evolved to carry out essential life processes. RNA acts as a genetic material and also as a catalyst for some important biochemical reactions in living systems. Being reactive, RNA is unstable. Statement II: DNA evolved from RNA and is a more stable genetic material. Its double helical strands being complementary, resist changes by evolving repairing mechanism. In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
opts: Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
why: Both statements match NCERT: RNA is catalytic but unstable, and DNA is more stable due to its complementary strands and repair mechanisms.

q: Given below are two statements: Statement I: Transfer RNAs and ribosomal RNA do not interact with mRNA. Statement II: RNA interference (RNAi) takes place in all eukaryotic organisms as a method of cellular defence. In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
opts: Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
why: tRNA reads mRNA codons by anticodon pairing and rRNA is part of the ribosome that binds mRNA, so Statement I is false. RNAi is a cellular defence in all eukaryotes, so Statement II is true.

q: Match List - I with List - II. List - I: A. Heart; B. Kidney; C. Gastro-intestinal tract; D. Adrenal Cortex. List - II: I. Erythropoietin; II. Aldosterone; III. Atrial natriuretic factor; IV. Secretin. Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
why: The heart secretes ANF, the kidney erythropoietin, the GI tract secretin, and the adrenal cortex aldosterone.

q: All living members of the class Cyclostomata are:
why: NCERT: all living cyclostomes (lampreys and hagfishes) are ectoparasites on some fishes.

q: Streptokinase produced by bacterium Streptococcus is used for:
why: Streptokinase is a clot buster used to dissolve clots in the blood vessels of patients with myocardial infarction.

q: Role of the water vascular system in Echinoderms is: A. Respiration and Locomotion B. Excretion and Locomotion C. Capture and transport of food D. Digestion and Respiration E. Digestion and Excretion. Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
why: The water vascular system helps in locomotion, capture and transport of food and respiration. So A and C are correct.

q: Match List I with List II. List I: A. Pteridophyte; B. Bryophyte; C. Angiosperm; D. Gymnosperm. List II: I. Salvia; II. Ginkgo; III. Polytrichum; IV. Salvinia. Choose the option with all correct matches.
why: Salvinia is a pteridophyte (heterosporous fern), Polytrichum a moss, Salvia an angiosperm and Ginkgo a gymnosperm.

q: Which are correct: A. Computed tomography and magnetic resonance imaging detect cancers of internal organs. B. Chemotherapeutics drugs are used to kill non-cancerous cells. C. α-interferon activate the cancer patients' immune system and helps in destroying the tumour. D. Chemotherapeutic drugs are biological response modifiers. E. In the case of leukaemia blood cell counts are decreased. Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
why: CT and MRI detect internal cancers (A) and α-interferon activates the immune system (C). Chemotherapy kills cancerous cells, biological response modifiers are interferons and not chemotherapeutic drugs, and leukaemia increases white blood cell counts.

q: What are the potential drawbacks in adoption of the IVF method? A. High fatality risk to mother B. Expensive instruments and reagents C. Husband/wife necessary for being donors D. Less adoption of orphans E. Not available in India F. Possibility that the early embryo does not survive. Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
opts: A, B, C, E, F only
why: IVF needs expensive instruments and reagents, it may reduce adoption of orphans, and early embryos may fail to survive. It is not highly fatal, donors are not required to be spouses, and it is available in India.

q: Consider the following: A. The reductive division for the human female gametogenesis starts earlier than that of the male gametogenesis. B. The gap between the first meiotic division and the second meiotic division is much shorter for males compared to females. C. The first polar body is associated with the formation of the primary oocyte. D. Luteinizing Hormone (LH) surge leads to disintegration of the endometrium and onset of menstrual bleeding. Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
why: Female meiosis starts in the foetus, whereas male meiosis starts at puberty, and the interval between meiosis I and II is much longer in females. The first polar body forms from the primary oocyte division to give the secondary oocyte, and the LH surge causes ovulation, not menstruation. So A and B are true.

q: In bryophytes, the gemmae help in which one of the following?
why: Gemmae are green multicellular buds in gemma cups of Marchantia that detach and grow into new plants: asexual reproduction.

q: Assertion (A): The primary function of the Golgi apparatus is to package the materials made by the endoplasmic reticulum and deliver it to intracellular targets and outside the cell. Reason (R): Vesicles containing materials made by the endoplasmic reticulum fuse with the cis face of the Golgi apparatus, and they are modified and released from the trans face of the Golgi apparatus. In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
opts: A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
why: The Golgi receives ER vesicles at the cis face and dispatches modified material from the trans face. R describes exactly how packaging and delivery occur, so it explains A.

q: Which one of the following statements refers to Reductionist Biology?
opts: Chemical approach to study and understand living organisms.
Behavioural approach to study and understand living organisms.
Physico-chemical approach to study and understand living organisms.
Physiological approach to study and understand living organisms.
why: Reductionist biology explains living organisms by reducing them to physico-chemical processes of molecules; the other approaches are holistic or organismal.

q: After maturation, in primary lymphoid organs, the lymphocytes migrate for interaction with antigens with secondary lymphoid organ(s) / tissue(s) like: A. thymus B. bone marrow C. spleen D. lymph nodes E. Peyer's patches. Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
why: Thymus and bone marrow are primary lymphoid organs; spleen, lymph nodes and Peyer's patches (MALT) are secondary lymphoid organs.

q: Match List I with List II. List I: A. The Evil Quartet; B. Ex situ conservation; C. Lantana camara; D. Dodo.  List II: I. Cryopreservation; II. Alien species invasion; III. Causes of biodiversity losses; IV. Extinction. Choose the option with all correct matches.
why: The Evil Quartet lists causes of biodiversity loss; cryopreservation is an ex situ method; Lantana camara is an alien invasive species; the Dodo is extinct.

q: How many meiotic and mitotic divisions need to occur for the development of a mature female gametophyte from the megaspore mother cell in an angiosperm plant?
why: The megaspore mother cell divides once by meiosis to give megaspores; the functional megaspore undergoes 3 successive mitoses to form the 8-nucleate, 7-celled embryo sac.

q: Which of the following type of immunity is present at the time of birth and is a non-specific type of defence in the human body?
why: Innate immunity is inborn and non-specific (barriers, phagocytes, etc.); the others are acquired and specific.

q: Given below are two statements: One is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R). Assertion (A): Cells of the tapetum possess dense cytoplasm and generally have more than one nucleus. Reason (R): Presence of more than one nucleus in the tapetum increases the efficiency of nourishing the developing microspore mother cells. In light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
opts: A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
why: Tapetal cells are multinucleate with dense cytoplasm, which makes them efficient in nourishing the developing pollen; R explains A.

q: From the statements given below choose the correct option: A. The eukaryotic ribosomes are 80S and prokaryotic ribosomes are 70S. B. Each ribosome has two sub-units. C. The two sub-units of 80S ribosome are 60S and 40S while that of 70S are 50S and 30S. D. The two sub-units of 80S ribosome are 60S and 20S and that of 70S are 50S and 20S. E. The two sub-units of 80S are 60S and 30S and that of 70S are 50S and 30S.
why: Eukaryotic 80S = 60S + 40S and prokaryotic 70S = 50S + 30S, each with two subunits; so A, B and C are true.

q: Which one of the following enzymes contains 'Haem' as the prosthetic group?
why: Catalase has a haem prosthetic group; succinate dehydrogenase has FAD, carbonic anhydrase has zinc and RuBisCO has Mg²⁺ as cofactor.

q: What is the name of the blood vessel that carries deoxygenated blood from the body to the heart in a frog?
why: In frog, the sinus venosus receives deoxygenated blood from the body through the vena cava (pre- and post-caval veins) and passes it to the right atrium.

q: Given below are the stages in the life cycle of pteridophytes. Arrange the following stages in the correct sequence. A. Prothallus stage B. Meiosis in spore mother cells C. Fertilisation D. Formation of archegonia and antheridia in gametophyte. E. Transfer of antherozoids to the archegonia in presence of water. Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
why: Spore mother cells undergo meiosis to give spores, which grow into the prothallus; it forms archegonia and antheridia; antherozoids swim to the archegonia; fertilisation follows.

q: The blue and white selectable markers have been developed which differentiate recombinant colonies from non-recombinant colonies on the basis of their ability to produce colour in the presence of a chromogenic substrate. Given below are two statements about this method: Statement I: The blue coloured colonies have DNA insert in the plasmid and they are identified as recombinant colonies. Statement II: The colonies without blue colour have DNA insert in the plasmid and are identified as recombinant colonies. In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
opts: Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
why: Insertion of foreign DNA inactivates the lacZ gene (β-galactosidase), so recombinant colonies stay white; blue colonies are non-recombinant.

q: Which of the following microbes is NOT involved in the preparation of household products? A. Aspergillus niger B. Lactobacillus C. Trichoderma polysporum D. Saccharomyces cerevisiae E. Propionibacterium sharmanii. Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
why: Lactobacillus (curd), Saccharomyces (bread, dough) and Propionibacterium (Swiss cheese) are used in households; Aspergillus niger (citric acid) and Trichoderma polysporum (cyclosporin A) are industrial.

q: Silencing of specific mRNA is possible via RNAi because of -
why: RNA interference uses a double-stranded RNA complementary to the target mRNA, which binds and silences it.

q: The complex II of mitochondrial electron transport chain is also known as
why: Complex I is NADH dehydrogenase, II is succinate dehydrogenase, III is cytochrome bc₁ and IV is cytochrome c oxidase.

q: While trying to find out the characteristic of a newly found animal, a researcher did the histology of adult animal and observed a cavity with presence of mesodermal tissue towards the body wall but no mesodermal tissue was observed towards the alimentary canal. What could be the possible coelome of that animal?
why: In a pseudocoelom the mesoderm is present only as scattered pouches on the body wall side and not lining the gut.

q: Given below are two statements: Statement I: In a floral formula ⊕ stands for zygomorphic nature of the flower, and G (underlined) stands for inferior ovary. Statement II: In a floral formula ⊕ stands for actinomorphic nature of the flower and G (underlined) stands for superior ovary. In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
opts: Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
why: ⊕ denotes actinomorphic and % (or ↓) zygomorphic; G with a line below denotes superior ovary and G with a line above inferior ovary.

q: Given below are two statements: Statement I: In ecosystem, there is unidirectional flow of energy of sun from producers to consumers. Statement II: Ecosystems are exempted from 2nd law of thermodynamics. In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
opts: Statement I is correct but statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but statement II is correct
Both statement I and statement II are correct
Both statement I and statement II are incorrect
why: Energy flows one way from the sun through producers to consumers. Ecosystems are not exempt from the 2nd law; they need a continuous energy input to stay organised.

q: Which of the following is the unit of productivity of an Ecosystem?
why: Productivity is a rate, expressed as g m⁻² yr⁻¹ or (kcal m⁻²) yr⁻¹; biomass or standing crop is in g m⁻² or kcal m⁻².

q: In the seeds of cereals, the outer covering of endosperm separates the embryo by a protein-rich layer called :
why: In cereal grains the endosperm is surrounded by a protein-rich aleurone layer that separates it from the embryo.

q: Match List I with List II. List I: A. Chlorophyll a; B. Chlorophyll b; C. Xanthophylls; D. Carotenoids.  List II: I. Yellow-green; II. Yellow; III. Blue-green; IV. Yellow to Yellow-orange. Choose the option with all correct matches.
why: Chlorophyll a is bright or blue-green, chlorophyll b yellow-green, xanthophylls yellow and carotenoids yellow to yellow-orange.

q: Who proposed that the genetic code for amino acids should be made up of three nucleotides?
why: George Gamow argued that 4 bases must code for 20 amino acids and proposed a triplet code (4³ = 64).

q: Histones are enriched with -
why: Histones are rich in the basic amino acids lysine and arginine, which carry positive charges and bind the negatively charged DNA.

q: Which of the following enzyme(s) are NOT essential for gene cloning? A. Restriction enzymes B. DNA ligase C. DNA mutase D. DNA recombinase E. DNA polymerase. Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
why: Gene cloning needs restriction enzymes to cut and DNA ligase to join; DNA mutase and DNA recombinase are not part of the standard cloning procedure.

q: A specialised membranous structure in a prokaryotic cell which helps in cell wall formation, DNA replication and respiration is :
why: Mesosomes are infoldings of the plasma membrane in prokaryotes that help in cell wall formation, DNA replication and respiration.

q: Which factor is important for termination of transcription?
why: The rho (ρ) factor binds the RNA polymerase and causes termination; sigma factor is for initiation.

q: Which of the following statement is correct about location of the male frog copulatory pad ?
opts: First digit of the fore limb
First and Second digit of fore limb
why: Male frogs have copulatory pads on the first digit of the forelimbs, used to clasp the female during amplexus.

q: Identify the statement that is NOT correct.
opts: Antigen binding site is located at C-terminal region of antibody molecules.
Constant region of heavy and light chains are located at C-terminus of antibody molecules.
Each antibody has two light and two heavy chains.
The heavy and light chains are held together by disulfide bonds.
why: The antigen-binding (variable) region is at the N-terminal end; the constant regions are at the C-terminus.

q: Match List I with List II. List I: A. Scutellum; B. Non-albuminous seed; C. Epiblast; D. Perisperm.  List II: I. Persistent nucellus; II. Cotyledon of Monocot seed; III. Groundnut; IV. Rudimentary cotyledon. Choose the option with all correct matches.
why: Scutellum is the monocot cotyledon, groundnut is non-albuminous, epiblast is a rudimentary cotyledon, and perisperm is persistent nucellus.

q: Find the statement that is NOT correct with regard to the structure of monocot stem.
opts: Vascular bundles are conjoint and closed.
why: In a monocot stem the hypodermis is sclerenchymatous (parenchymatous hypodermis is a dicot feature); the other statements are correct.

q: Twins are born to a family that lives next door to you. The twins are a boy and a girl. Which of the following must be true?
opts: They were conceived through in vitro fertilization.
why: Monozygotic twins are always of the same sex, so a boy and a girl must have come from two separate zygotes, i.e. fraternal twins.

q: Sweet potato and potato represent a certain type of evolution. Select the correct combination of terms to explain the evolution.
why: Sweet potato is a root and potato is a stem tuber; they have similar function but different origin, so they are analogous structures from convergent evolution.

q: Which one of the following phytohormones promotes nutrient mobilization which helps in the delay of leaf senescence in plants?
why: Cytokinins promote nutrient mobilisation and delay senescence of leaves.

q: Why can't insulin be given orally to diabetic patients?
opts: Human body will elicit strong immune response
It will be digested in Gastro-Intestinal (GI) tract
why: Insulin is a protein, so oral doses are digested by proteases in the GI tract; it must be injected.

q: Name the class of enzyme that usually catalyze the following reaction: S – G + S# → S + S# – G. Where, G → a group other than hydrogen, S → a substrate, S# → another substrate
why: Transfer of a group G between substrates is catalysed by transferases.

q: Given below are two statements: Statement I: The DNA fragments extracted from gel electrophoresis can be used in construction of recombinant DNA. Statement II: Smaller size DNA fragments are observed near anode and larger fragments are found near the wells in an agarose gel. In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
opts: Statement I is correct but statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but statement II is correct
Both statement I and statement II are correct
Both statement I and statement II are incorrect
why: DNA bands can be eluted from the gel and used for cloning. DNA is negatively charged and moves to the anode, with smaller fragments travelling farther.

q: The correct sequence of events in the life cycle of bryophytes is A. Fusion of antherozoid with egg. B. Attachment of gametophyte to substratum. C. Reduction division to produce haploid spores. D. Formation of sporophyte. E. Release of antherozoids into water. Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
why: The gametophyte attaches, antherozoids are released and fuse with the egg, the zygote forms the sporophyte, and meiosis in it gives spores.

q: Genes R and Y follow independent assortment. If RRYY produce round yellow seeds and rryy produce wrinkled green seeds, what will be the phenotypic ratio of the F2 generation?
why: A dihybrid cross with independent assortment gives 9 : 3 : 3 : 1 in the F2.

q: Each of the following characteristics represent a Kingdom proposed by Whittaker. Arrange the following in increasing order of complexity of body organization. A. Multicellular heterotrophs with cell wall made of chitin. B. Heterotrophs with tissue/organ/organ system level of body organization. C. Prokaryotes with cell wall made of polysaccharides and amino acids. D. Eukaryotic autotrophs with tissue/organ level of body organization. E. Eukaryotes with cellular body organization. Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
why: C is Monera, E is Protista, A is Fungi, D is Plantae (tissue/organ level) and B is Animalia (organ system level).

q: Match List - I with List - II. List - I: A. Centromere; B. Cilium; C. Cristae; D. Cell membrane.  List - II: I. Mitochondrion; II. Cell division; III. Cell movement; IV. Phospholipid Bilayer. Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
why: Centromere functions in cell division, cilia in movement, cristae are folds of the mitochondrion, and the cell membrane is a phospholipid bilayer.

q: Which one of the following equations represents the Verhulst-Pearl Logistic Growth of population?
why: The logistic growth equation is dN/dt = rN(K − N)/K, where K is the carrying capacity.

q: Match List - I with List - II. List - I: A. Emphysema; B. Angina Pectoris; C. Glomerulonephritis; D. Tetany.  List - II: I. Rapid spasms in muscle due to low Ca⁺⁺ in body fluid; II. Damaged alveolar walls and decreased respiratory surface; III. Acute chest pain when not enough oxygen is reaching to heart muscle; IV. Inflammation of glomeruli of kidney. Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
why: Emphysema damages alveolar walls, angina causes chest pain from low oxygen to the heart, glomerulonephritis is inflammation of glomeruli, and tetany is spasm from low Ca²⁺.

q: Cardiac activities of the heart are regulated by : A. Nodal tissue B. A special neural centre in the medulla oblongata C. Adrenal medullary hormones D. Adrenal cortical hormones. Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
why: The nodal tissue (SAN) is autorhythmic, the medulla's cardiac centre acts via ANS, and adrenal medullary hormones (adrenaline) raise heart rate; adrenal cortical hormones do not regulate cardiac activity.

q: A room heater is rated 400 W, 220 V. If the supply voltage drops to 200 V, what will be the power consumed (approximately) ?
why: R = V²/P = 220²/400 = 121 Ω (constant). New power = 200²/121 ≈ 331 W.

q: The angular speed of a flywheel is increased from 600 rpm to 1200 rpm in 10 s. The number of revolutions completed by the flywheel during this time is :
why: Uniform angular acceleration: average speed = (600 + 1200)/2 = 900 rpm = 15 rev/s. Revolutions = 15 × 10 = 150.

q: The sum of kinetic energy and potential energy of a simple pendulum bob is 0.02 joule. The speed of the simple pendulum bob at equilibrium position is approximately : (Consider mass of the bob = 20 g)
why: At the equilibrium position all the energy is kinetic: ½mv² = 0.02 J with m = 0.02 kg, so v² = 2 and v ≈ 1.41 m/s.

q: A 100-turn closely wound circular coil of radius 5 cm has a magnetic field of 3.14 × 10⁻³ T at its centre. The current flowing through the coil, and the magnitude of the magnetic moment of this coil are, respectively : (Take μ₀ = 4π × 10⁻⁷ T m/A)
why: B = μ₀NI/2r gives I = 3.14×10⁻³ × 0.1 /(4π×10⁻⁷ × 100) = 2.5 A. Magnetic moment M = NIA = 100 × 2.5 × π(0.05)² ≈ 2 A m².

q: A submarine is designed to withstand an absolute pressure of 100 atm. How deep can it go below the water surface ? (Consider the density of water = 1000 kg m⁻³, 1 atm = 1 × 10⁵ Pa and gravitational acceleration g = 10 m s⁻²)
why: Absolute pressure = P₀ + ρgh, so ρgh = 99 atm = 9.9×10⁶ Pa. h = 9.9×10⁶/(1000 × 10) = 990 m.

topic: Dual nature of radiation and matter
q: Match List I with List II : List I: A. E = hν; B. Diffraction and Interference; C. λ = h/p; D. Compton effect  List II: I. de Broglie wavelength; II. Particle nature of light; III. Wave nature of light; IV. Energy of photon. Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
why: E = hν is the photon energy; diffraction and interference show wave nature; λ = h/p is the de Broglie wavelength; Compton effect shows particle nature of light.

q: Match List I with List II : List I: A. Young's Modulus; B. Compressibility; C. Bulk Modulus; D. Poisson's Ratio  List II: I. (Δd/ΔL)(L/d); II. FL/(A(ΔL)); III. −(1/ΔP)(ΔV/V); IV. −P(V/ΔV). Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
why: Young's modulus = FL/(AΔL); compressibility = 1/B = −(1/ΔP)(ΔV/V); bulk modulus = −PV/ΔV; Poisson's ratio = lateral strain/longitudinal strain = (Δd/d)/(ΔL/L).

q: The amount of work done to raise a mass 'm' from the surface of the Earth to a height equal to the radius of the Earth 'R', will be :
why: W = ΔU = GMm(1/R − 1/2R) = GMm/2R. Since GM = gR², W = mgR/2.

q: When a ruler falls vertically, 5 different persons catch it with different reaction times. (g = 9.8 m s⁻²) A. Person A has reaction time of 0.20 s. B. Person B has reaction time of 0.22 s. C. Person C has reaction time of 0.18 s. D. Person D has reaction time of 0.19 s. E. Person E has reaction time of 0.21 s. What is the correct order of the distance travelled by the ruler for each person ?
why: The ruler falls from rest, so d = ½gt², larger for longer reaction time. Times: B 0.22 > E 0.21 > A 0.20 > D 0.19 > C 0.18, so B > E > A > D > C.

q: The power of a crane, which lifts a mass of 1000 kg to a height of 20 m in 10 s is : (g = 9.8 m/s²)

Consider two uncharged capacitors of equal capacitance 200 pF. One of them is charged by a 100 V supply and disconnected. Now this capacitor is connected to the uncharged capacitor. The amount of electrostatic energy lost in the process is :
why: Initial energy = ½CV² = ½ × 200×10⁻¹² × 10⁴ = 1×10⁻⁶ J. After sharing charge equally, the final energy is half of this, so the loss is 0.5 × 10⁻⁶ J.

q: An ac circuit contains a resistance of 1 kΩ, a capacitor of 0.1 μF and an inductor of 1 mH connected in series. The resonance frequency of the circuit is approximately :
An electric heater supplies heat to a system at a rate of 100 W. If the system performs work at a rate of 75 J/s, then the rate at which internal energy increases will be :
why: First law: dU/dt = dQ/dt − dW/dt = 100 − 75 = 25 W.

q: The peak value of an alternating current is 5 A and frequency is 60 Hz. How long will the current, starting from zero, take to reach the peak value ?
why: Current reaches its peak in a quarter cycle: t = T/4 = 1/(4 × 60) = 1/240 s.

q: In Young's double slit experiment, using monochromatic light of wavelength λ, the intensity of light at a point on the screen where the path difference is λ, is K units. The intensity of light at a point where the path difference is λ/3 will be :
why: Path difference λ gives phase 2π, so K = I_max. For λ/3, φ = 2π/3 and I = I_max cos²(φ/2) = K cos²60° = K/4.

q: Four statements are given (A is mass number) : A. The volume of a nucleus is proportional to A^(1/3). B. The volume of a nucleus is proportional to A. C. The difference in mass of an atom and its nucleus is called the mass defect. D. The difference in mass of a nucleus and its constituents is called the mass defect. Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
opts: A and D are true, but B and C are false
B and D are true, but A and C are false
B and C are true, but A and D are false
A and C are true, but B and D are false
why: Nuclear radius R ∝ A^(1/3), so volume ∝ A (B true, A false). Mass defect is the difference between the mass of the constituent nucleons and the nucleus (D true, C false).

q: In interference and diffraction, the light energy is redistributed. If it reduces in one region, producing a dark fringe, it increases in another region, producing a bright fringe. A. As there is no gain or loss of energy, these phenomena are consistent with the principle of conservation of energy. B. Diffraction and interference are characteristics exhibited only by light waves. Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
opts: A is false, but B is true
A is true, but B is false
A is true and B is also true
Both A and B are false
why: Energy is only redistributed, so A is true. Interference and diffraction are shown by all waves (sound, water, matter waves), not only light, so B is false.

topic: Current electricity cells and internal resistance
q: A resistor is connected to a battery of 12 V emf and internal resistance 2 Ω. If the current in the circuit is 0.6 A, the terminal voltage of the battery is :

Savitha, a XI standard student, while conducting an experiment to determine the effective length of a simple pendulum L, notes down the data of time taken to complete 30 oscillations as 60 s and hence calculates the length of the simple pendulum as : (Take π² = 9.8, and g = 9.8 m/s²)

Which of the following statements are correct ? A. Inside a conductor, the electrostatic field is zero. B. Electric field at the surface of a charged conductor does not depend on its surface charge density. C. The interior of a charged conductor can have no excess charge in the static situation. D. At the surface of a charged conductor, the electrostatic field must be normal to the surface at every point. E. The electrostatic potential is zero everywhere inside a charged conductor. Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
why: Inside a conductor E = 0, no excess charge in the interior, and field at the surface is normal. At the surface E = σ/ε₀ depends on σ (B false), and the potential is constant, not zero (E false).

q: Two statements are given below : A. When the forward bias voltage across a p-n junction diode increases above a certain threshold voltage, the diode current increases significantly. B. This current is called reverse saturation current. Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
opts: Both Statements A and B are true
Both Statements A and B are false
Statement A is true, but Statement B is false
Statement A is false, but Statement B is true
why: Above the threshold (knee) voltage the forward current rises sharply, so A is true. Reverse saturation current is the small current under reverse bias, so B is false.

q: In a concave lens, a ray of light emanating from the object parallel to the principal axis of the lens, after refraction :
opts: passes through the second principal focus.
appears to diverge from the first principal focus.
passes through 2F, which is the radius of curvature of the lens.
emerges parallel to the principal axis.
why: A concave lens diverges a ray parallel to the axis so that it appears to come from the principal focus on the incident (object) side, the first principal focus.

q: An unknown nucleus has a nuclear density of 2.29 × 10¹⁷ kg/m³ and mass of 19.926 × 10⁻²⁷ kg. Its mass number A is approximately : (Take R₀ = 1.2 × 10⁻¹⁵ m, 4π = 12.56)
why: Mass = density × (4/3)πR₀³A: (4/3)π(1.2×10⁻¹⁵)³ = 7.24×10⁻⁴⁵ m³, times 2.29×10¹⁷ gives 1.657×10⁻²⁷ kg per nucleon. A = 19.926/1.657 ≈ 12.

q: A galvanometer of resistance 100 Ω gives full scale deflection for a current of 1 mA. It is converted into an ammeter of range 0 – 10 A. The shunt required is :

For a travelling harmonic wave y(x, t) = 2.0 cos 2π(10 t − 0.0080 x + 0.35), where x and y are in cm and t in s. The phase difference between oscillatory motion of two points separated by a distance of 0.5 m is :

A box of mass 15 kg is kept on the floor of a stationary trolley. The coefficient of static friction between the box and the trolley is 0.12. Keeping the box in stationary state over the trolley, the maximum acceleration with which the trolley can be moved horizontally in m s⁻² is : (g = 10 m/s²)
why: Friction provides the acceleration: a_max = μg = 0.12 × 10 = 1.2 m/s².

topic: Kinetic theory of gases rms speed
q: A flask contains argon and chlorine in the ratio of 2 : 1 by mass. The temperature of the mixture is 27°C. The ratio of root mean square speed of the molecules of the two gases (v_rms of Ar / v_rms of Cl) is : (Atomic mass of argon = 40.0 u and molecular mass of chlorine = 70.0 u)
why: v_rms ∝ 1/√M at the same temperature, so ratio = √(70/40) = √(7/4) = √7/2. The mass ratio does not matter.

q: Match List I with List II : List I (Electromagnetic wave): A. Microwave; B. Visible light; C. Gamma rays; D. Infra-red rays  List II (Production): I. Electrons in atoms emit light when they move from a higher energy level to a lower energy level; II. Radioactive decay of nucleus; III. Vibration of atoms and molecules; IV. Klystron valve or magnetron valve. Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
why: Microwaves come from klystron or magnetron valves; visible light from atomic transitions; gamma rays from radioactive decay of nuclei; infrared from vibrations of atoms and molecules.

topic: Laws of motion vector addition of forces
q: The magnitude and direction of the acceleration produced in a body of mass 5 kg when two mutually perpendicular forces 8 N and 6 N act on it, are respectively :
opts: 2 m s⁻²; tan⁻¹(3/4) with 8 N force
2 m s⁻²; tan⁻¹(4/3) with 8 N force
2 m s⁻²; tan⁻¹(3/4) with 6 N force
20 m s⁻²; tan⁻¹(4/3) with 8 N force
why: Resultant F = √(8² + 6²) = 10 N, so a = 10/5 = 2 m/s². Its angle with the 8 N force is tan⁻¹(6/8) = tan⁻¹(3/4).

q: For a metal of work function 6.6 eV, which of the following wavelengths of incident radiation does not give rise to the photoelectric effect ? (Take Planck's constant as 6.6 × 10⁻³⁴ J s)
why: Threshold wavelength λ₀ = hc/φ = 1240 eV nm / 6.6 eV ≈ 188 nm. Radiation of wavelength greater than 188 nm (200 nm) cannot eject electrons.

q: The speed of light in vacuum is taken as unity. If light takes 6 min 40 s to reach the Earth from the Sun, the distance between the Sun and the Earth in new unit is :
why: With c = 1 unit, distance = c × t = 1 × (6 × 60 + 40) = 400 units.

q: A rectangular wire loop of sides 8 cm and 3 cm with a small cut, is moving out of a region of uniform magnetic field of magnitude 0.3 T directed normal to the plane of the loop. The emf developed across the cut, if the velocity of the loop is 2 cm s⁻¹, in a direction normal to the shorter side of the loop, will be :
why: Moving normal to the shorter side, the 3 cm side cuts the field: emf = Blv = 0.3 × 0.03 × 0.02 = 1.8 × 10⁻⁴ V.

q: In a vernier callipers, 20 VSD coincide with 16 MSD (each division of length 1 mm). The least count of the vernier callipers is :
why: 1 VSD = 16/20 = 0.8 mm. Least count = 1 MSD − 1 VSD = 1 − 0.8 = 0.2 mm = 0.02 cm.

q: In the first excited state of hydrogen atom, the radial energy of its electron is −3.4 eV. The radial distance of the electron from the hydrogen nucleus in this case is approximately : (Take 1 eV = 1.6 × 10⁻¹⁹ J, e = 1.6 × 10⁻¹⁹ C and 1/(4πε₀) = 9 × 10⁹ N m²/C²)
why: For the electron orbit |E| = ke²/2r, so r = ke²/(2|E|) = 9×10⁹ × (1.6×10⁻¹⁹)² /(2 × 3.4 × 1.6×10⁻¹⁹) ≈ 2.1 × 10⁻¹⁰ m.

q: Match List I with List II : List I (Complex/Ion): A. [Pt(Cl₂)(NH₃)₂]; B. [Co(NH₃)₆]Cl₃; C. [NiCl₄]²⁻; D. [Fe(CO)₅]  List II (Shape/geometry): I. Octahedral; II. Trigonal bipyramidal; III. Square planar; IV. Tetrahedral. Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
why: Pt(II) d⁸ is square planar; Co(III) with six NH₃ is octahedral; Ni(II) with weak field Cl⁻ is tetrahedral; Fe(CO)₅ is trigonal bipyramidal (dsp³).

q: At 298 K, a certain buffer solution contains equal concentrations of X⁻ and HX, K_b for X⁻ is 10⁻¹⁰. What is the pH of this buffer solution ?
why: K_a of HX = K_w/K_b = 10⁻¹⁴/10⁻¹⁰ = 10⁻⁴. For equal [X⁻] and [HX], pH = pK_a = 4.

q: Given below are certain reactions. Identify the reaction for which K_p ≠ K_c.
why: K_p = K_c(RT)^Δn, so they differ only when Δn ≠ 0. Only N₂ + 3H₂ ⇌ 2NH₃ has Δn = 2 − 4 = −2.

q: Consider the following reaction : 2A (g) + B (g) → 2D (g)  ΔU° = − 10 kJ mol⁻¹ and ΔS° = − 44 J K⁻¹ at 298 K. Identify the correct option with ΔG° for the reaction and spontaneity of the reaction at 298 K. (Given : R = 8.31 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹)
why: Δn_g = 2 − 3 = −1, so ΔH = ΔU + Δn RT = −10 − 2.476 = −12.476 kJ. ΔG = ΔH − TΔS = −12.476 + 298 × 0.044 = +0.636 kJ/mol, positive so non-spontaneous.

q: Given below is an expression for the rate constant of a first order reaction occurring at a certain temperature, T (K). ln k = 14.34 − (1.25 × 10⁴)/T. The energy of activation in kcal mol⁻¹ for the reaction is : (Given : k in s⁻¹, R = 1.987 cal mol⁻¹ K⁻¹)
why: ln k = ln A − Ea/RT, so Ea/R = 1.25 × 10⁴ K and Ea = 1.25×10⁴ × 1.987 = 24837 cal ≈ 24.84 kcal/mol.

q: Select the reagents that reduce nitriles to primary amines : A. (i) LiAlH₄; (ii) H₂O  B. Sn + HCl  C. H₂/Ni  D. Na(Hg)/C₂H₅OH  E. Br₂/aq. NaOH. Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
why: Nitriles are reduced to primary amines by LiAlH₄, catalytic hydrogenation (H₂/Ni) and Na/alcohol (Na(Hg)/C₂H₅OH). Sn + HCl (Stephen reduction) stops at the aldehyde stage and Br₂/NaOH is the Hofmann reagent for amides.

q: The correct statement with regard to the secondary structure of DNA/RNA is :
opts: DNA possesses a double strand helix structure and contains thymine as one of the four bases.
DNA possesses a single strand helix structure and contains uracil as one of the four bases.
RNA possesses a double strand helix structure and contains uracil as one of the four bases.
RNA possesses a single strand helix structure and contains thymine as one of the four bases.
why: DNA is a double-stranded helix whose bases are A, G, C and thymine. RNA is single stranded and has uracil in place of thymine.

q: During Lassaigne's test, the elements present in an organic compound are converted from :
why: Fusing the compound with sodium converts covalently bonded N, S and halogens into ionic species (NaCN, Na₂S, NaX) that can be detected in the extract.

q: Mixture of chloroform and acetone forms a solution with negative deviation from Raoult's law due to :
opts: stronger intermolecular forces between chloroform molecules than those between chloroform and acetone molecules.
formation of hydrogen bonding between acetone and chloroform.
increase in escaping tendency of molecules of each component.
why: The H of CHCl₃ hydrogen-bonds with the C=O oxygen of acetone, so A-B attractions exceed A-A and B-B ones. The escaping tendency falls and the vapour pressure is lower than expected (negative deviation).

q: In a test tube containing a salt, a few drops of dilute H₂SO₄ was added, which gave colourless vapours having the smell of vinegar. The vapours turned the blue litmus paper red. Identify the correct anion from the following :
why: Acetates with dilute H₂SO₄ liberate acetic acid vapours with a vinegar smell, which are acidic and turn blue litmus red. CO₂ is odourless and H₂S smells of rotten eggs.

q: Identify the correct statement about ClF₃ from the following options :
opts: It has T-shaped geometry with three lone pairs on Cl atom.
It has T-shaped geometry with two lone pairs on Cl atom.
It has a trigonal pyramidal geometry with two lone pairs on Cl atom.
It has a planar trigonal geometry with two lone pairs on Cl atom.
why: Cl in ClF₃ has 3 bond pairs and 2 lone pairs (sp³d). The lone pairs sit in equatorial positions, giving a T-shaped molecule.

q: Match List I with List II : List I (Complex): A. [Pt(NH₃)₂Cl₂]; B. [Co(en)₃]³⁺; C. [Co(NH₃)₅NO₂]Cl₂; D. [Cr(H₂O)₆]Cl₃  List II (Type of isomerism): I. Optical; II. Solvate; III. Geometrical; IV. Linkage. Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
why: Square planar [Pt(NH₃)₂Cl₂] shows cis-trans (geometrical) isomerism. [Co(en)₃]³⁺ is optically active. NO₂⁻ is ambidentate, so [Co(NH₃)₅NO₂]Cl₂ shows linkage isomerism. [Cr(H₂O)₆]Cl₃ shows solvate (hydrate) isomerism.

q: The number of chlorine atoms present in the organic products X and Y of the following reactions, respectively, are : Benzene + 6Cl₂ (Anhydrous AlCl₃, dark, cold) → X ; Benzene + 3Cl₂ (UV, 500 K) → Y
why: With excess Cl₂ and AlCl₃ in the dark, all six H atoms are substituted to give hexachlorobenzene, C₆Cl₆ (6 Cl). Under UV, 3Cl₂ adds to benzene to give benzene hexachloride, C₆H₆Cl₆ (6 Cl).

q: Identify the incorrect statement from the following :
opts: Phosphorus, arsenic and antimony show catenation property.
P(C₂H₅)₃ and As(C₂H₅)₃ form dπ-dπ bond with transition metals.
Nitrogen can form dπ-pπ bond with oxygen.
Nitrogen can form pπ-pπ multiple bonds with itself.
why: Nitrogen has no d-orbitals in its valence shell, so it cannot form dπ-pπ bonds. It forms pπ-pπ bonds (with O and with itself).

q: At a certain temperature, T (K), during a process, 500 J is absorbed by the system and work of 200 J is done by the system. Then change in internal energy of the system is :
why: ΔU = q + w with q = +500 J and w = -200 J (work done by the system), so ΔU = 500 - 200 = 300 J.

q: The correct IUPAC name of the following compound is : CH₃–CH₂–CH(CH₂CH₃)–CH₂–CH(CH₃)–CH₂–CH₃ (an ethyl group is on the third carbon and a methyl group on the fifth carbon of a seven-carbon chain)
why: The longest chain has 7 carbons (heptane) with substituents at 3 and 5 from either end. Alphabetical order gives ethyl the lower locant, so the name is 3-ethyl-5-methylheptane.

q: In the following reaction sequence, X and Z, respectively are : CH₃CH₂CH₂–OH + PCl₅ → CH₃CH₂CH₂Cl + X + HCl ; CH₃CH₂CH₂Cl --(alc. KOH, Δ)--> Y ; Y --(HBr, (C₆H₅CO)₂O₂)--> Z
why: PCl₅ with an alcohol gives the alkyl chloride, POCl₃ and HCl, so X = POCl₃. Alc. KOH gives propene (Y). HBr with peroxide adds by the anti-Markovnikov (Kharasch) route to give 1-bromopropane.

q: When 1 dm³ of CO₂ gas is passed over hot coke, the volume of gaseous mixture after complete reaction at STP becomes 1·4 dm³. The composition of the gaseous mixture at STP is :
opts: 0·6 dm³ of CO, 0·8 dm³ of CO₂
0·8 dm³ of CO, 0·8 dm³ of CO₂
0·6 dm³ of CO, 0·4 dm³ of CO₂
0·8 dm³ of CO, 0·6 dm³ of CO₂
why: CO₂ + C → 2CO. If x dm³ of CO₂ reacts, the total volume is (1 - x) + 2x = 1 + x = 1.4, so x = 0.4. This gives CO = 0.8 dm³ and CO₂ = 0.6 dm³.

q: Match List I with List II : List I (Order of reaction): A. Zero order; B. First order; C. Second order; D. Third order  List II (Unit of rate constant): I. mol⁻¹ L s⁻¹; II. mol⁻² L² s⁻¹; III. s⁻¹; IV. mol L⁻¹ s⁻¹. Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
why: The unit of k is (mol L⁻¹)¹⁻ⁿ s⁻¹. This gives mol L⁻¹ s⁻¹ for zero order, s⁻¹ for first order, mol⁻¹ L s⁻¹ for second order and mol⁻² L² s⁻¹ for third order.

q: The correct order of increasing metallic character of Na, Be, P, Mg and Si is :
why: Metallic character falls across a period and rises down a group. P < Si (non-metal side), Be is a weak metal, Mg is more metallic than Be, and Na is the most metallic.

q: The number of hydrogen atoms present in 5·4 g of urea is : (Given : Molar mass of urea : 60 g mol⁻¹, N_A : 6·022 × 10²³ particles mol⁻¹)
why: Moles of urea = 5.4/60 = 0.09. Each CO(NH₂)₂ has 4 H atoms, so H atoms = 0.09 × 4 × 6.022×10²³ = 2.168×10²³.

q: In a qualitative analysis, Bi³⁺ is detected by appearance of precipitate of BiO(OH)(s). Calculate pH when the following equilibrium exists at 298 K : BiO(OH)(s) ⇌ BiO⁺(aq) + OH⁻(aq), K = 4 × 10⁻¹⁰ (Given : log 2 = 0·3010)

Match List I with List II : List I: A. cumene (isopropylbenzene) → phenol; B. CH₃COOH → CH₃CH₂OH; C. CH₃CH₂CH₂OH → CH₃–CH(OH)–CH₃; D. benzene → phenol  List II: I. (i) oleum; (ii) NaOH, Δ; (iii) H⁺; II. (i) O₂; (ii) H₂O/H⁺; III. (i) CH₃OH, H⁺; (ii) H₂, catalyst; IV. (i) conc. H₂SO₄, Δ; (ii) H⁺/H₂O. Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
why: Cumene → phenol uses O₂ then H₂O/H⁺ (cumene process). CH₃COOH is esterified and then hydrogenated to ethanol. Propan-1-ol is dehydrated to propene and then hydrated (Markovnikov) to propan-2-ol. Benzene → phenol uses sulphonation with oleum, then NaOH fusion, then H⁺.

q: A bulb is rated at 150 watt, converting 8% energy into light. If energy of one photon is 4·42 × 10⁻¹⁹ J, how many photons are emitted by the bulb per second ?
why: Light power = 0.08 × 150 = 12 W = 12 J/s. Number of photons per second = 12 / 4.42×10⁻¹⁹ = 2.71×10¹⁹.

q: The pair of molecules that are metamers among the following is :
why: Metamers have the same molecular formula and functional group but different alkyl groups on either side of it. Methyl propyl ether and diethyl ether (both C₄H₁₀O) are metamers.

q: Identify the correct statements : A. The molality of 2·5 g of ethanoic acid (Molar mass : 60 g mol⁻¹) in 75 g of benzene solution is 0·556 m. B. The molarity of a solution containing 5 g of NaOH (molar mass : 40 g mol⁻¹) in 450 mL of solution is 0·278 M at 298 K. C. Aquatic species are more comfortable in cold water. D. The solubility of gas increases with decrease in pressure. E. For a binary mixture of A and B, the number of moles of A and B are n_A and n_B respectively. The mole fraction of B will be x_B = n_A/(n_A + n_B). Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
why: A: (2.5/60)/0.075 kg = 0.556 m (true). B: (5/40)/0.45 L = 0.278 M (true). C: gas solubility is higher in cold water, so more dissolved O₂ (true). D is false (solubility rises with pressure). E is false because x_B = n_B/(n_A + n_B).

q: Which one of the following is an ambidentate ligand ?
why: Thiocyanate (SCN⁻) can bind through S or N, so it is ambidentate. Oxalate and en are bidentate and EDTA is hexadentate.

q: The functional group that can be identified through phthalein dye test is :
why: Phenols heated with phthalic anhydride and conc. H₂SO₄ give phenolphthalein, which turns pink in alkali. This is the phthalein dye test for phenols.

q: Match List I with List II : List I: A. C₂H₄; B. C₂H₂; C. CH₄; D. NH₃  List II: I. 3 σ bonds, 2 π bonds; II. 3 σ bonds, one lone pair; III. 4 σ bonds; IV. 5 σ bonds, 1 π bond. Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
why: C₂H₄ has 5 σ and 1 π bond. C₂H₂ has 3 σ and 2 π. CH₄ has 4 σ. NH₃ has 3 σ and one lone pair.

q: A solution of copper sulphate is electrolysed for 10 minutes with current of 1·5 amperes. The mass of copper deposited at cathode is : (Given : Molar mass of Cu = 63 g mol⁻¹; 1 F = 96487 C mol⁻¹)

Match List I with List II : List I (Quantum Numbers 'n' and 'l'): A. n = 2, l = 1; B. n = 4, l = 0; C. n = 5, l = 3; D. n = 3, l = 2  List II (Orbital): I. 3d; II. 2p; III. 4s; IV. 5f. Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
why: l = 0, 1, 2, 3 correspond to s, p, d, f. So (2,1) is 2p, (4,0) is 4s, (5,3) is 5f and (3,2) is 3d.

q: The major product Z formed in the following sequence of reactions is : C₂H₆ --(Cl₂, UV light)--> (monochlorinated product) --(NH₃)--> Y --((i) NaNO₂/HCl; (ii) H₂O)--> Z
why: Ethane gives C₂H₅Cl, and ammonolysis gives ethylamine (Y). Aliphatic primary amines react with HNO₂ (NaNO₂/HCl) via an unstable diazonium salt to give the alcohol, C₂H₅OH.

q: Although +3 oxidation state is most common in lanthanoids, cerium still shows +4 oxidation state because :
opts: After losing one more electron, it acquires 4f¹⁴ electronic configuration.
Its nearest inert gas is Radon.
After losing one more electron, it acquires 4f⁰ electronic configuration.
why: Ce (4f¹5d¹6s²) loses four electrons to give Ce⁴⁺ with the empty, stable 4f⁰ configuration (noble gas Xe core). Its atomic number is 58 and its nearest inert gas is xenon.

q: Methane reacts with steam at 1273 K in the presence of nickel catalyst to form :
why: Steam reforming: CH₄ + H₂O → CO + 3H₂ at 1273 K over Ni, which gives water gas / syngas (a source of dihydrogen).

q: Identify the incorrect statement from the following :
opts: The order of catenation property of Group 14 elements is C >> Si > Ge ≈ Sn.
Carbon has the ability to form pπ-pπ multiple bond with itself.
ECl₃ (E = B and Al) is a monomer when E = B and a dimer when E = Al.
why: Oxygen is not restricted to -2: it shows -1 (peroxides), -1/2 (superoxides) and +2 (OF₂). The other three statements are correct.

q: Identify the incorrect statement from the following :
opts: The largest and the smallest species among Mg, Mg²⁺, Al and Al³⁺ are Mg²⁺, respectively.
The IUPAC name of the element with atomic number 107 is Unnilseptium.
The similarity in behaviour of Li with Mg is referred to as 'diagonal relationship'.
The oxidation state and covalency of Al in [AlCl(H₂O)₅]²⁺ are 3 and 6 respectively.
why: A cation is smaller than its atom and a larger charge gives a smaller ion, so Mg (not Mg²⁺) is the largest and Al³⁺ the smallest. Statements 2, 3 and 4 are correct (Z = 107 is Uns; Al is +3 with 6 donor atoms).

q: The following two reactions give the same foul smelling product Z. C₂H₅Cl --(X)--> Z ; C₂H₅CONH₂ --(Br₂, NaOH)--> Y --(CHCl₃/ethanolic KOH, Δ)--> Z. X and Z, respectively, are :
why: Hofmann bromamide gives C₂H₅NH₂ (Y), and the carbylamine test with CHCl₃/KOH gives the foul-smelling ethyl isocyanide, C₂H₅NC. Covalent AgCN reacts with C₂H₅Cl through N to give the same isocyanide.

q: The calculated 'spin-only' magnetic moment of Ti²⁺ (3d²) is :
why: Ti²⁺ (3d²) has n = 2 unpaired electrons. μ = √(n(n+2)) = √8 = 2.84 BM.

q: Match List I with List II : List I (Transition metal/compound/complex): A. V₂O₅; B. Fe; C. PdCl₂; D. Ni complex  List II (Catalytic Role): I. Preparation of ammonia from N₂/H₂ mixture; II. Polymerisation of alkynes; III. Preparation of H₂SO₄ from SO₂; IV. Oxidation of ethyne to ethanal. Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
why: V₂O₅ catalyses the contact process (SO₂ → SO₃ for H₂SO₄), Fe is the Haber process catalyst, PdCl₂ is the Wacker catalyst (ethene/ethyne to ethanal), and Ni complexes polymerise alkynes.

q: Two products X and Y are formed in the following reaction sequence. Benzene + CH₃Cl --(Anhydr. AlCl₃)--> W --(dil. HNO₃ + dil. H₂SO₄, warm)--> X + Y. The suitable method that can be used for the separation of products X and Y is :
why: Friedel-Crafts methylation gives toluene (W), and nitration gives a mixture of o- and p-nitrotoluene. These are liquids with different boiling points (about 222 °C and 238 °C), so they are separated by fractional distillation.

q: Match List I with List II : List I: A. Genetically modified organism; B. Thermostable DNA polymerase; C. Ti plasmid; D. pBR322  List II: I. Agrobacterium tumefaciens; II. Bt cotton; III. Thermus aquaticus; IV. Escherichia coli. Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
why: Bt cotton is a GMO, Taq polymerase comes from Thermus aquaticus, the Ti plasmid belongs to Agrobacterium tumefaciens, and pBR322 is an E. coli cloning vector.

q: Exploring molecular, genetic and species-level diversity for products of economic importance is called :
why: Bioprospecting is the exploration of biodiversity (molecules, genes, species) for commercially valuable products. Biofortification is breeding crops for higher nutrient content.

q: Which of the following statements are true with reference to the sex-determination in honeybees ? A. An offspring formed from the union of a sperm and an egg, develops as a female (queen or worker). B. An unfertilized egg develops as a male by parthenogenesis. C. A male has half the number of chromosomes than that of a female. D. Males produce sperms by meiosis. E. Honeybees have a haplodiploid sex-determination system. Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
opts: A, B, C and E only
A, B, C and D only
B, C, D and E only
A, B, D and E only
