why: Honeybees are haplodiploid: fertilised eggs (2n = 32) give females and unfertilised eggs (n = 16) give males by parthenogenesis. Drones are already haploid, so they produce sperm by mitosis, not meiosis, which makes D false.

q: Match List I with List II : List I (Growth Regulator): A. 2,4-D; B. GA₃; C. Kinetin; D. ABA  List II (Function/Effect): I. Brewing industry; II. Stimulation of stomatal closure; III. Herbicide; IV. Nutrient mobilisation. Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
why: 2,4-D is a synthetic auxin used as a herbicide, GA₃ is used in the brewing industry (malting), kinetin (a cytokinin) helps nutrient mobilisation and delays senescence, and ABA stimulates stomatal closure.

q: In racemose inflorescence, ______.
opts: flowers are borne in an acropetal succession
the main axis terminates in a flower
why: In racemose inflorescence the main axis has unlimited growth and flowers are borne laterally in acropetal order (youngest at the apex). Termination in a flower is a feature of cymose inflorescence.

q: Since the origin and diversification of life on Earth, there have been five episodes of mass extinction of species. How is the sixth extinction, which is in progress, different from the previous episodes ?
opts: The current species extinction rates are far lower than those in previous episodes.
The present species extinction rates are 100 to 1000 times faster than in the pre-human times.
The present net species extinction rate is zero.
The current species extinction rate is nearly 10 times faster than that in previous episodes.
why: NCERT states that the current extinction rate is estimated to be 100 to 1000 times faster than in pre-human times, largely due to human activities.

q: Alpha-helix is found in which level of protein structure ?
why: The α-helix and β-pleated sheet are patterns of regular folding of the polypeptide backbone, held by hydrogen bonds. They are the secondary structure.

q: The enzyme required for carboxylation in the Calvin cycle is :
why: In the Calvin cycle RuBisCO (RuBP carboxylase-oxygenase) fixes CO₂ onto RuBP to form two molecules of 3-PGA. PEP carboxylase works in the C₄ mesophyll.

q: Arrange the following in the correct developmental sequence related to microsporogenesis : A. Microspore tetrads B. Sporogenous tissue C. Pollen grains D. Pollen mother cells. Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
why: Sporogenous tissue → pollen mother cells (microspore mother cells) → meiosis gives microspore tetrads → microspores mature into pollen grains: B, D, A, C.

q: Which of the following statements are not true regarding restriction endonucleases ? A. They are called molecular scissors. B. These are the enzymes responsible for restricting the growth of bacteriophages in E. coli. C. They cut the DNA only at the centre of the palindromic sites. D. They remove nucleotides only from the ends of DNA fragments. E. They recognise specific palindromic base-pair sequences. Choose the answer from the options given below :
why: Restriction endonucleases cut within the DNA at a specific palindromic site, but not at the exact centre: they cut each strand a little away from the centre, leaving sticky ends (C is false). Removing nucleotides from the ends is the job of exonucleases (D is false). A, B and E are true.

q: In the lac operon, the z gene codes for :
why: In the lac operon, z codes for β-galactosidase, y for permease and a for transacetylase. The repressor is coded by the i gene.

q: Match List I with List II : List I (Phase of cell cycle): A. G₁ phase; B. S phase; C. G₂ phase; D. M phase  List II (Activity): I. Actual cell division occurs; II. Cell is metabolically active and continuously grows but does not replicate its DNA; III. Synthesis of DNA occurs and the amount of DNA per cell doubles; IV. Proteins are synthesized while cell growth continues. Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
why: G₁ is the growth phase without DNA replication, S is DNA synthesis (DNA content doubles), G₂ is protein synthesis and growth in preparation for mitosis, and M is the actual cell division.

q: 2 (C₅₁H₉₈O₆) + 145 O₂ → 102 CO₂ + 98 H₂O + energy. The Respiratory Quotient (RQ) of a biomolecule used for respiration, as per the above equation, would be :
why: RQ = CO₂ evolved / O₂ consumed = 102/145 = 0.70. This is the value for a fat (tripalmitin), which falls between 0.5 and 0.95.

q: Which one of the following is not a characteristic of plant cells in the phase of elongation ?
why: Large conspicuous nuclei, dense cytoplasm and thin walls are features of the meristematic phase. In the elongation phase the cells enlarge, form large vacuoles and deposit new wall material.

q: Arrange the following steps of somatic hybridisation in a correct sequence. A. Digestion of cell walls. B. Isolation of naked protoplasts. C. Fusion of protoplasts to get hybrid protoplast. D. Isolation of single cells from two different varieties of plants. E. Growing of hybrid protoplast to form a new plant. Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
why: Single cells are isolated (D), cell walls digested (A), naked protoplasts isolated (B), fused (C), and the hybrid is cultured into a plant (E).

q: Match List I with List II. List I: A. Conjunctive tissue; B. Casparian strips; C. Subsidiary cells; D. Starch sheath.  List II: I. Specialised cells in the vicinity of guard cells; II. Endodermal cells rich in starch; III. Tissue between xylem and phloem; IV. Endodermal cells with suberin deposition. Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
why: Conjunctive tissue lies between xylem and phloem; Casparian strips are suberin bands in endodermis; subsidiary cells surround guard cells; the starch sheath is the starch-rich endodermis.

q: In angiosperms, root hairs arise from which one of the following regions of the root ?
why: Root hairs are outgrowths of epidermal cells in the region of maturation.

q: Which of the following floral formula is the correct floral formula of Solanaceae family ?
opts: ⊕ ⚥ K(5) C(5)⌒A5 G̲(2)  (arc joining C(5) and A5, i.e. epipetalous)
⊕ ⚥ K5 C(5)⌒A5 G̲(2)  (arc joining C(5) and A5, i.e. epipetalous)
why: Solanaceae has gamosepalous calyx K(5), gamopetalous corolla C(5) with epipetalous stamens (arc joining C and A) A5, and superior bicarpellary syncarpous ovary G̲(2).

q: Which one of the following is a triploid cell ?
why: The primary endosperm cell (3n) forms when a male gamete fuses with the two polar nuclei of the diploid central cell.

q: Match List I with List II. List I: A. Decomposition; B. Detritus; C. Mineralisation; D. Humification.  List II: I. Accumulation of dark coloured amorphous colloidal substance; II. Release of inorganic nutrients by the activity of microbes in soil; III. Breaking down of complex organic matter into inorganic substances; IV. Dead remains of plants and animals including fecal matter. Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
why: Decomposition breaks complex matter into inorganic substances; detritus is dead remains; mineralisation releases inorganic nutrients; humification forms dark colloidal humus.

q: The main criteria used for Five Kingdom Classification proposed by R.H. Whittaker (1969) included : A. Cell structure B. Body organization C. Presence of flagellum D. Reproduction E. Phylogenetic relationships. Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
opts: A, B, C, D and E
A, B, D and E only
why: Whittaker used cell structure, body organisation, mode of nutrition, reproduction and phylogenetic relationships; presence of flagellum was not a criterion.

q: "The Evil Quartet" of biodiversity loss includes which of the following ?
opts: Over-exploitation; Alien species invasions; Soil pollution; Co-extinctions
Habitat loss and fragmentation; Air pollution; Water pollution; Co-extinctions
Habitat loss and fragmentation; over-exploitation; Alien species invasions; Co-extinctions
Over-exploitation; Alien species invasions; Air pollution; Co-extinctions
why: The Evil Quartet comprises habitat loss and fragmentation, over-exploitation, alien species invasions and co-extinctions.

q: Arrange the following steps of DNA fingerprinting in a correct sequence. A. Isolation of DNA and its digestion by restriction endonucleases. B. Hybridisation using a labelled VNTR probe. C. Transferring of separated DNA fragments to synthetic membranes. D. Detection of hybridised DNA fragments by autoradiography. E. Separation of DNA fragments by electrophoresis. Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
why: Isolate and digest DNA (A), separate by electrophoresis (E), blot onto membrane (C), hybridise with VNTR probe (B), detect by autoradiography (D).

q: Which one of the following types of pollination brings genetically different types of pollen grains to the stigma ?
why: Xenogamy transfers pollen from a different plant (genetically different); geitonogamy, cleistogamy and autogamy involve genetically similar pollen.

q: Which of the following is an in situ conservation method ?
why: In situ conservation protects species in their natural habitats, e.g. sacred groves, national parks; seed banks, botanical gardens and safari parks are ex situ.

q: Heterophyllous development in response to environment is an example of which of the following phenomena ?
why: Plasticity is the ability of plants to follow different pathways in response to environment or life phases, e.g. heterophylly in cotton, coriander and larkspur.

q: Match List I with List II. List I: A. Productivity; B. Net primary productivity; C. Gross primary productivity; D. Secondary productivity.  List II: I. Gross primary productivity minus respiration losses; II. Rate of formation of new organic matter by consumers; III. Rate of biomass production; IV. Rate of production of organic matter during photosynthesis. Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
why: Productivity is the rate of biomass production; NPP = GPP minus respiration; GPP is the rate of organic matter production in photosynthesis; secondary productivity is formation of new organic matter by consumers.

q: Which of the following statements are correct regarding amino acids ? A. They are substituted methanes. B. Serine is an aromatic amino acid. C. Valine is a neutral amino acid. D. Lysine is an acidic amino acid. Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
why: Amino acids are substituted methanes; valine is neutral. Serine is a hydroxyl (non-aromatic) amino acid and lysine is basic.

q: In which one of the following, the ovules are not enclosed by an ovary wall and remain exposed ?
why: Pinus is a gymnosperm with naked ovules; Wolffia is an angiosperm, while Funaria and Selaginella do not form ovules at all.

q: Which of the following statements are correct with reference to packaging of DNA helix ? A. Histones are organized to form a unit of eight molecules called histone octamer. B. Histones are negatively charged basic proteins. C. Histones are rich in the basic amino acid residues - lysine and arginine. D. The positively charged DNA is wrapped around the histone octamer to form nucleosome. E. The packaging of chromatin at higher levels requires an additional set of proteins called non-histone chromosomal proteins. Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
why: Histones are positively charged basic proteins rich in lysine and arginine, forming an octamer around which negatively charged DNA wraps; so B and D are wrong, A, C and E are right.

q: Match List I with List II. List I (Placentation): A. Marginal; B. Axile; C. Parietal; D. Basal.  List II (Example): I. Mustard; II. Pea; III. Marigold; IV. Lemon. Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
why: Pea has marginal, lemon axile, mustard parietal and marigold basal placentation.

q: Which one of the following is the site for active ribosomal RNA synthesis ?
why: The nucleolus is the non-membranous nuclear region where rRNA is actively synthesised.

q: The main function of bulliform cells in grasses is :
opts: to minimize water loss during water stress.
to make the leaf impermeable to fungal spores.
why: Bulliform cells lose turgor in water stress, making the leaf curl inwards and minimising water loss.

q: Which of the following statements are correct ? A. The Amazon rainforest being cut and cleared for cultivation of soyabeans is an example of habitat loss. B. Steller's sea cow and passenger pigeon became extinct due to over-exploitation by humans. C. The Nile perch introduced into Lake Victoria in East Africa helped in population growth of cichlid fish in the lake. D. Water hyacinth is an invasive species. E. When a species becomes extinct, the plant and animal species associated with it are not affected. Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
why: Nile perch led to extinction of cichlids (C false) and extinction of one species affects associated species (E false); A, B and D are correct.

q: Which one of the following statements is not true about the universal rules of binomial nomenclature ?
opts: The first word in the biological name represents the specific epithet, while the second component denotes the genus.
The specific epithet in the biological name starts with a small letter.
Both the words in a biological name, when handwritten, are separately underlined or printed in italics.
Biological names are generally in Latin.
why: The first word is the genus and the second the specific epithet, so statement (1) is reversed and untrue.

q: Which one of the following disorders is caused by the substitution of Glutamic acid (Glu) by Valine (Val) at the sixth position of the beta globin chain of the haemoglobin molecule ?
why: A single base substitution (GAG to GUG) replaces Glu with Val at position 6 of the β-globin chain, causing sickle-cell anaemia.

q: Find the incorrect statement(s) about photosynthesis from the following : A. The water splitting complex is associated with PS I. B. C₄ plants use the C₃ pathway of CO₂ fixation as the main biosynthetic pathway. C. In C₄ plants, photorespiration does not occur. D. C₃ plants exhibit 'Kranz' anatomy. E. ATP synthesis in chloroplast occurs through chemiosmosis.
why: The water splitting complex is on the PS II side (A false) and Kranz anatomy is a feature of C₄ plants, not C₃ (D false).

q: Match List I with List II. List I: A. Trypsin; B. Morphine; C. Concanavalin A; D. Collagen.  List II: I. Intercellular ground substance; II. Lectin; III. Enzyme; IV. Alkaloid. Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
why: Trypsin is an enzyme, morphine an alkaloid, concanavalin A a lectin and collagen the most abundant protein of intercellular ground substance.

q: Identify the correct statements about biomolecules. A. Lipids are generally water soluble. B. Proteins are polypeptides. C. Polysaccharides are long chains of sugars. D. Adenine and guanine are substituted pyrimidines. E. Almost all enzymes are proteins. Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
why: Lipids are water insoluble, and adenine and guanine are substituted purines; B, C and E are correct.

q: Match List I with List II. List I: A. Incomplete dominance; B. Co-dominance; C. Pleiotropy; D. Polygenic inheritance.  List II: I. Human skin colour; II. Inheritance of flower colour in Antirrhinum sp.; III. Phenylketonuria disease in humans; IV. ABO blood groups. Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
why: Antirrhinum flower colour shows incomplete dominance, ABO groups co-dominance, phenylketonuria is pleiotropic, and skin colour is polygenic.

q: Identify the correct sequence of steps in each cycle of Polymerase Chain Reaction :
why: Each PCR cycle is denaturation of DNA, annealing of primers, then extension by Taq polymerase.

q: How many ATP and NADPH molecules are required to make one molecule of glucose through the Calvin pathway ?
why: Fixing 6 CO₂ needs 18 ATP and 12 NADPH (3 ATP and 2 NADPH per CO₂).

q: Match List I with List II. List I (Process): A. Glycolysis; B. ETS; C. Accumulation of protons; D. Krebs' cycle.  List II (Location): I. Inner mitochondrial membrane; II. Mitochondrial matrix; III. Cytoplasm; IV. Intermembrane space. Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
why: Glycolysis occurs in cytoplasm, ETS on inner membrane, protons accumulate in the intermembrane space and the Krebs' cycle is in the matrix.

q: Which of the following statements are correct with respect to DNA separation, isolation and visualization ? A. The cutting of DNA is done by molecular scissors. B. The DNA fragments separate according to their size in an agarose gel, upon electrophoresis. C. The separated DNA fragments can be seen without staining when exposed to UV light. D. The separated DNA fragments, when stained with ethidium bromide, can be seen in visible light. Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
why: Restriction enzymes (molecular scissors) cut DNA and fragments separate by size; DNA must be stained with ethidium bromide and seen under UV, not visible light.

q: What is the probability of having children with 'O' blood group, where both mother and father are heterozygous for 'A' and 'B' blood group, respectively ?
why: IAi × IBi gives IAIB, IAi, IBi and ii in equal proportions, so ii (O group) is 1/4 = 25%.

q: Match List I with List II. List I: A. Molluscs; B. Reptiles; C. Adult amphibians; D. Amoeba.  List II: I. Pulmonary respiration only; II. Branchial respiration; III. Cellular respiration; IV. Pulmonary and Cutaneous respiration. Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
why: Molluscs respire through gills, reptiles through lungs only, adult amphibians through lungs and skin, and Amoeba by cellular (surface) respiration.

q: Insertion of a foreign DNA at a BamHI site in an E. coli cloning vector pBR322 results in the loss of antibiotic resistance towards :
why: The BamHI site lies within the tetracycline resistance gene (tetR), so insertion inactivates tetracycline resistance only.

q: What is the reason behind production of large holes in 'Swiss Cheese' ?
opts: The production of large amount of CO₂ and H₂ by Trichoderma polysporum
The production of large amount of CO₂ and H₂ by lactic acid bacteria called Lactobacillus
The production of large amount of CO₂ by Propionibacterium sharmanii
The production of large amount of CO₂ by Clostridium butylicum
why: Propionibacterium sharmanii releases large amounts of CO₂, forming the big holes in Swiss cheese.

q: Which of the following is not an example of convergent evolution ?
opts: Fore limbs of whales and bats
why: Forelimbs of whales and bats are homologous structures (divergent evolution); the others are analogous.

q: Non-membrane bound cell organelles found in both prokaryotic and eukaryotic cells are ______.
why: Ribosomes are non-membranous and occur in both cell types; centrosomes are absent in prokaryotes and the others are membrane-bound.

q: Ecological pyramids represent the relationship between the organisms at different trophic levels and they are generally inverted for :
opts: Pyramid of energy in pond ecosystem
why: The biomass pyramid in the sea is generally inverted because phytoplankton biomass is small compared with zooplankton and fish; grassland pyramids are upright and the energy pyramid is never inverted.

q: Arrange the following events occurring in Renin-Angiotensin mechanism in the correct order : A. Increase in blood pressure and Glomerular filtration rate. B. Reabsorption of Na⁺ and water from distal parts of tubule due to Aldosterone. C. Fall in Glomerular filtration rate. D. Vasoconstriction by Angiotensin II and release of Aldosterone. E. Renin converts Angiotensinogen into Angiotensin I, followed by Angiotensin II. Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
why: Fall in GFR (C) triggers renin release converting angiotensinogen to angiotensin II (E), causing vasoconstriction and aldosterone release (D), Na⁺ and water reabsorption (B) and raised BP and GFR (A).

q: Choose the correct statements regarding population interactions between two species. A. In both parasitism and commensalism, only one species benefits and the other species is harmed. B. Both species benefit in mutualism. C. Both species benefit in commensalism. D. In parasitism, only one species benefits and the other is harmed. E. In amensalism, one species is harmed and the other is unaffected. Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
why: Mutualism is +/+, parasitism +/-, amensalism -/0 and commensalism +/0; so A and C are wrong.

q: In which animal do haploid cells divide mitotically to produce gametes ?
why: Male honey bees (drones) develop parthenogenetically and are haploid, so they produce sperm by mitosis.

q: In humans, respiration occurs in the following steps. Arrange these steps in the correct order. A. Diffusion of O₂ and CO₂ between blood and tissues. B. Diffusion of O₂ and CO₂ across alveolar membrane. C. Pulmonary ventilation by which atmospheric air is drawn in and CO₂ rich alveolar air is released out. D. Cellular respiration. E. Transport of gases by the blood. Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
why: The sequence is ventilation (C), alveolar diffusion (B), blood transport (E), tissue diffusion (A) and cellular respiration (D).

q: The following reaction depicts the activity of a particular class of enzymes : Substrate: two adjacent carbons C-C with group X on one carbon and group Y on the other; in the presence of E it gives X-Y + C=C (products). Identify the enzyme class 'E' from the following options :
why: Enzymes that remove groups (X-Y) from a substrate by means other than hydrolysis, leaving a double bond, are lyases.

q: Match List I with List II. List I (Bioactive molecules): A. Streptokinase; B. Statins; C. Lipases; D. Cyclosporin A.  List II (Importance): I. Immunosuppressive agent; II. Removal of clots from the blood vessels; III. Blood cholesterol-lowering agent; IV. Detergent formulations. Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
why: Streptokinase is a clot buster, statins lower cholesterol, lipases are used in detergents and cyclosporin A is an immunosuppressant.

q: Which of the following equations depicts Verhulst-Pearl logistic population growth ?
why: The logistic equation is dN/dt = rN(K − N)/K, where K is the carrying capacity.

q: Arrange the following cell layers/structures around the female gamete, from outer to inner side : A. Zona pellucida B. Perivitelline space C. Corona radiata D. Plasma membrane of ovum. Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
why: From outside inwards: corona radiata, zona pellucida, perivitelline space, then the plasma membrane of the ovum.

q: Which one of the following is an appropriate example of 'sexual deceit' ?
why: The Ophrys flower mimics a female bee in shape, colour and scent, so male bees pseudo-copulate and pollinate it.

q: Match List I with List II related to muscular/skeletal system : List I: A. Tetany; B. Arthritis; C. Myasthenia gravis; D. Muscular dystrophy.  List II: I. Inflammation of joints; II. Autoimmune disorder affecting neuromuscular junction; III. Wild contraction in muscle due to low Ca⁺⁺ in body fluid; IV. Progressive degeneration of skeletal muscle. Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
why: Tetany is caused by low Ca⁺⁺, arthritis is joint inflammation, myasthenia gravis is autoimmune at the neuromuscular junction, and muscular dystrophy is progressive muscle degeneration.

q: Select the correct statements regarding cell membrane in eukaryotic cell. A. Membrane of human RBCs has approximately 52% protein. B. Major phospholipids are arranged in a bilayer. C. Extensions of the plasma membrane into the cell form mesosomes. D. Tails towards the inner part of lipids are hydrophobic and thus protected from aqueous medium. E. Glycocalyx is present on the outer surface of the plasma membrane. Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
why: Mesosomes are infoldings of prokaryotic (bacterial) membranes, so C is wrong; the other statements describe the lipid bilayer and membrane composition correctly, and the only option excluding C is A, B and D.

q: Choose the correct statements regarding cell organelles and their inclusions. A. The endomembrane system includes Golgi complex, endoplasmic reticulum and mitochondria. B. Rough endoplasmic reticulum bears ribosomes on its surface. C. Both mitochondria and plastids have circular DNA. D. A network of microtubules, microfilaments and intermediate filaments present in the cytoplasm is called cytoskeleton. E. Mitochondrion is a single membrane-bound structure. Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
why: Mitochondria are double-membrane organelles outside the endomembrane system (A and E false); RER carries ribosomes, mitochondria and plastids have circular DNA and the cytoskeleton is that filament network.

q: The toxin proteins isolated from Bacillus thuringiensis, coded by which of the following genes would control cotton bollworms and corn borer, respectively ?
why: cryIAc and cryIIAb control cotton bollworms, while cryIAb controls corn borer; so cotton bollworm and corn borer are cryIAc and cryIAb respectively.

q: The JGA (Juxta Glomerular Apparatus) is a special sensitive region formed by cellular modifications in ________ related to the same nephron.
opts: Proximal convoluted tubule and efferent renal arteriole
Distal convoluted tubule and efferent renal arteriole
Distal convoluted tubule and afferent renal arteriole
Proximal convoluted tubule and afferent renal arteriole
why: The JGA is formed by modified cells of the distal convoluted tubule and the afferent arteriole at the location of their contact.

q: Choose the correct statements regarding frog's anatomy : A. Hepatic portal system is the special venous connection between liver and intestine. B. There are twelve pairs of cranial nerves arising from the brain. C. The ureters and oviducts open separately into the cloaca in female frogs. D. Hind-brain consists of cerebellum, medulla oblongata and optic lobes. E. Sinus venosus joins the right atrium of heart.
why: Frogs have ten pairs of cranial nerves (B false) and optic lobes belong to the mid-brain (D false); A, C and E are correct.

q: Match List I with List II : List I: A. Cortisol; B. Aldosterone; C. Cholecystokinin; D. Progesterone.  List II: I. Stimulates the formation of alveoli in mammary glands; II. Produces anti-inflammatory reactions; III. Stimulates reabsorption of Na⁺ and water from renal tubule; IV. Stimulates secretion of pancreatic enzymes and bile juice
why: Cortisol is anti-inflammatory, aldosterone promotes Na⁺ and water reabsorption, CCK stimulates pancreatic enzymes and bile, progesterone supports alveoli formation in mammary glands.

q: The sixth mutant codon of beta globin gene causing polymerization of Haemoglobin and change in RBC shape is ________.
why: In sickle-cell anaemia the sixth codon GAG (glutamic acid) changes to GUG (valine) in the beta globin mRNA.

q: Male frogs can be distinguished from female frogs due to the presence of A. Bulging eyes B. Vocal sacs C. Webbed digits in feet D. Copulatory pad on first digit of fore limbs E. Olive green-coloured skin with dark irregular spots
why: Sexual dimorphism in frogs: males have vocal sacs and a copulatory pad on the first digit of the forelimbs, which females lack.

q: The human protein named α-1-antitrypsin, obtained from transgenic animals, is used for the treatment of ________
why: α-1-antitrypsin is used to treat emphysema.

q: Match List I (Drug) with List II (Effect) : A. Nicotine; B. Morphine; C. Heroin; D. Cocaine.  List II: I. Causes sense of euphoria and increased energy; II. Stimulates adrenal gland to release catecholamines into blood circulation; III. Effective sedative and painkiller; IV. A depressant; slows down body function
why: Nicotine stimulates adrenal release of catecholamines; morphine is a sedative and painkiller; heroin (smack) is a depressant slowing body function; cocaine causes euphoria and increased energy.

q: The WBC count of a person's blood sample is 8000/cu.mm. How many eosinophils and lymphocytes would be in the same blood sample approximately ?
why: Eosinophils are 2-3% of WBCs (160-240) and lymphocytes 20-25% (1600-2000) of 8000.

q: Match List I with List II with respect to chronology of evolution of life forms : A. About 65 mya; B. About 500 mya; C. About 350 mya; D. About 320 mya.  List II: I. Jawless fish probably evolved; II. The dinosaurs suddenly disappeared from the earth; III. Seaweeds and few plants probably existed; IV. Invertebrates were formed and became active
why: Per the NCERT geological timeline, dinosaurs vanished about 65 mya, invertebrates formed about 500 mya, jawless fish evolved about 350 mya and seaweeds and few plants existed about 320 mya.

q: Match List I with List II : A. Progestasert; B. Multiload 375; C. Diaphragm; D. Saheli.  List II: I. Barrier made of rubber used by females; II. Oral contraceptive; III. Hormone releasing IUD; IV. Copper releasing IUD
why: Progestasert is a hormone-releasing IUD, Multiload 375 releases copper, the diaphragm is a rubber barrier and Saheli is an oral contraceptive pill.

q: The following are the stages of life cycle of Plasmodium. Arrange the stages in the proper order. A. The parasites reproduce asexually in RBCs, bursting the cells. B. The parasites reproduce asexually in liver cells, bursting the cells and releasing into blood. C. Gametocytes develop in RBCs. D. Sporozoites reach the liver through the blood. E. Female mosquito injects sporozoites into humans during bite.
why: Sporozoites are injected (E), reach the liver (D), multiply there (B), then multiply in RBCs (A) and gametocytes develop (C).

q: Match List I with List II related to embryonic development at various months of pregnancy : A. The foetus movement starts and hair appears on the head; B. The foetus develops limbs and digits; C. The foetus develops external genital organs; D. The foetus body is covered with fine hair; eyelids separate and eyelashes are formed.  List II: I. 24 weeks of pregnancy; II. 20 weeks of pregnancy; III. 8 weeks of pregnancy; IV. 12 weeks of pregnancy
why: Limbs and digits form by the end of 2 months (8 weeks), genitals by 12 weeks, first movements and head hair by the 5th month (20 weeks), fine body hair and eyelashes by 24 weeks.

q: The flightless bird with forelimbs modified as paddle-like structures suited for swimming is known as :
why: Aptenodytes (penguin) is a flightless bird whose forelimbs are paddle-like for swimming.

q: Select the Incorrect statements from the following : A. Digestive system in Platyhelminthes is incomplete. B. Bilateral symmetry is a characteristic feature of adult Echinoderms. C. Pseudocoelom is possessed by Aschelminthes. D. Notochord is persistent throughout life in the class Chondrichthyes. E. Members of class Reptilia maintain a constant body temperature.
why: Adult echinoderms are radially symmetrical (B incorrect) and reptiles are poikilothermic (E incorrect); A and C are correct, so B and E are the incorrect pair offered.

q: A group of researchers procured some fish-like animals and upon investigation the following characters were observed : A. Endoskeleton was made of cartilage. B. Ectoparasitic; as they were found attached on fish skin with their circular sucking mouth. C. Paired fins and scales were absent, but 7 pairs of gill slits were present. Which of the following species of animals did they consider to fit best with these characters ?
why: Petromyzon (lamprey), a cyclostome, is an ectoparasite with a circular sucking mouth, no paired fins or scales and 6-7 pairs of gill slits.

q: Choose the correct statements regarding muscle contraction. A. A motor neuron carries a signal sent by the Central Nervous System (CNS) to the sarcolemma of the muscle fibre. B. The neural signal generates an action potential which causes the release of Ca⁺⁺ into sarcoplasm. C. Increase in Ca⁺⁺ inactivates the actin for breaking cross bridges. D. Actin binds to the myosin head to form a cross bridge. E. Shortening of sarcomere takes place, by pulling actin filaments towards the centre of 'A' band.
opts: A, B, D and E only
why: Increased Ca⁺⁺ activates actin by exposing myosin-binding sites on it, so C is false; A, B, D and E describe the sliding filament mechanism correctly.

q: Choose the correct statement regarding GIFT to overcome infertility.
opts: Ova collected from a female donor are transferred to the uterus of an infertile female.
Early embryos with up to 8 blastomeres are transferred into the fallopian tube of an infertile female.
Early embryos with up to 8 blastomeres are transferred to the uterus of an infertile female.
It is the transfer of an ovum collected from a donor into the fallopian tube of another female who cannot produce ovum but can provide suitable environment for fertilization and development.
why: GIFT (gamete intra-fallopian transfer) transfers a donor ovum into the fallopian tube of a female who cannot produce ova but can support fertilisation and development.

q: Which of the following statements are correct with reference to human endoskeleton ? A. Human skull is monocondylic. B. The joint between any two adjoining vertebrae is a cartilaginous joint. C. In human beings, the number of cervical vertebrae is seven. D. All ribs except the last 2 pairs are bicephalic. E. The occipital bone of skull is articulated with atlas vertebra.
why: The human skull is dicondylic (A false) and all ribs are bicephalic, so D is false; vertebral joints are cartilaginous, there are seven cervical vertebrae and the occipital condyles articulate with the atlas.

q: Spermatogonia undergo a series of cell divisions to produce sperms. Select the correct statements from the following : A. Spermatogonia always undergo meiotic cell division. B. Primary spermatocytes divide mitotically to produce secondary spermatocytes. C. Secondary spermatocytes, through their second meiotic division, produce haploid spermatids. D. Spermatids produce spermatozoa through mitosis. E. Spermatids transform into spermatozoa by spermiogenesis.
why: Spermatogonia divide mitotically, primary spermatocytes undergo meiosis I, secondary spermatocytes meiosis II giving spermatids, which transform into sperm by spermiogenesis (no division); only C and E are correct.

q: Select the incorrect statements with reference to Rh grouping. A. Erythroblastosis foetalis is a condition observed having foetus with Rh⁻ᵛᵉ blood and mother with Rh⁺ᵛᵉ blood. B. Rh antigen is observed on RBCs in the majority of human beings. C. Before blood transfusion, Rh group should also be matched. D. Rh incompatibility is observed when a pregnant mother is Rh⁻ᵛᵉ and the foetus is Rh⁺ᵛᵉ. E. Erythroblastosis foetalis can be avoided by administering anti-Rh antibodies to the mother immediately after the delivery of the second child.
why: The condition arises with an Rh⁻ mother and Rh⁺ foetus (A incorrect), and anti-Rh antibodies are given right after the delivery of the first child (E incorrect).

q: Select the set of fishes which belong to the class Osteichthyes.
opts: Saw fish, Fighting fish and Dog fish
Flying fish, Angel fish and Fighting fish
why: Flying fish, angel fish and fighting fish are bony fishes; saw fish and dog fish are cartilaginous, and cuttlefish, starfish and devil fish (ray or octopus) are not Osteichthyes.

q: In a population of a grasshopper species, the chromosome number of some members is 23 and some other members possess 24 chromosomes. The 23 and 24 chromosome-bearing members in this species are ________.
why: Grasshoppers show XO sex determination: males have one X (23) and females have XX (24).

q: Evolution of human appears parallel to the progressive development of brain and language skills. As such, the evolution of individual species in the sequence of their appearance is :
opts: Ramapithecus → Homo habilis → Homo erectus → Neanderthal → Homo sapiens
Neanderthal → Ramapithecus → Homo habilis → Homo erectus → Homo sapiens
Homo habilis → Homo erectus → Ramapithecus → Neanderthal → Homo sapiens
Homo sapiens → Ramapithecus → Homo habilis → Neanderthal → Homo erectus
why: The sequence is Ramapithecus, Homo habilis, Homo erectus, Neanderthal, then Homo sapiens.

q: The specific receptors for neurotransmitters in a synapse are present on ________.
why: Neurotransmitters released from the pre-synaptic neuron bind to specific receptors on the post-synaptic membrane.

q: Match List I (Respiratory Volume) with List II (Capacity in mL) : A. ERV (Expiratory Reserve Volume); B. RV (Residual Volume); C. IRV (Inspiratory Reserve Volume); D. TV (Tidal Volume).  List II: I. 2500 - 3000 mL; II. 500 mL; III. 1000 - 1100 mL; IV. 1100 - 1200 mL
why: ERV is 1000-1100 mL, RV 1100-1200 mL, IRV 2500-3000 mL and TV about 500 mL.
